lines.zh: 走进博物馆，游客将通过虚拟体验看到自由女神头部内部的样子。他们还有机会看到雕像创作者弗雷德里克·奥古斯特·巴托尔迪工作室的复原场景。

lines.en: Museum visitors also will see the 1,600-kilogram torch that lit up New York Harbor for nearly 100 years. It was replaced in 1985.
lines.zh: 博物馆游客还会看到那支 1600 公斤重、照亮纽约港近 100 年的火炬。它在 1985 年被替换了下来。

lines.en: On top of the Statue of Liberty Museum, visitors can have a good look at New York's Lower Manhattan area. Nicholas Garrison says the museum "tries to be inspirational unto itself as its own object…while being respectful to the buildings that are here."
lines.zh: 在自由女神像博物馆顶上，游客可以好好看看纽约曼哈顿下城。尼古拉斯·加里森说，这座博物馆“力求作为一件独立的作品本身就鼓舞人心……同时尊重这里已有的建筑”。

lines.en: I'm Jonathan Evans.
lines.zh: 我是乔纳森·埃文斯。

qs.q: Who gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
qs.why: "The statue was a gift from the people of France."

qs.q: Why can only about 20 percent of visitors go inside the statue?
qs.why: "because of limited space."

qs.q: What old object will the museum show?
qs.why: "the 1,600-kilogram torch that lit up New York Harbor for nearly 100 years."

lessons.title: Old Medicines Preserved in US Apothecary Museum
lessons.zh: 美国老药铺博物馆里的古老药物
lessons.sum: 弗吉尼亚州亚历山德里亚的斯泰布勒-利德比特药铺从 1792 年营业到 1933 年，华盛顿夫妇也曾是顾客。如今它是一座博物馆，展出放血工具、能“对付狼人”的乌头草，以及早年当药卖、含可卡因的可口可乐。

lines.en: In earlier times, healers and health workers used strangely-named plants for medicinal purposes. Plants with names such as dragon's blood, mandrake root and devil's snare could be bought at a drugstore called an apothecary.
lines.zh: 过去，治病的人和医务工作者用一些名字奇怪的植物来治病。“龙血”、曼德拉草根、“魔鬼网”这样名字的植物，可以在一种叫“药铺”（apothecary）的药店买到。

lines.en: Today, one of the best preserved apothecaries in the United States has been turned into a museum in Alexandria, Virginia. The museum provides interesting examples of medicines used before the development of modern drugs.
lines.zh: 如今，美国保存最完好的药铺之一，在弗吉尼亚州亚历山德里亚被改成了一座博物馆。博物馆展示了现代药物出现之前人们使用的药物，很有意思。

lines.en: The Stabler-Leadbeater Apothecary served customers for more than 140 years, from 1792 to 1933. When the business failed, the store and its contents were bought. It was redesigned to look as it had in the 18th century. In 1939, it reopened as a museum.
lines.zh: 斯泰布勒-利德比特药铺从 1792 年到 1933 年为顾客服务了 140 多年。生意失败后，有人买下了药铺和里面的东西，把它重新布置成 18 世纪的样子。1939 年，它作为博物馆重新开放。

lines.en: Lauren Gleason supervises the museum.
lines.zh: 劳伦·格利森负责管理这座博物馆。

lines.en: "A lot of the medicines that people would have been purchasing here were probably for minor ailments, rashes, skin conditions, the flu, a headache."
lines.zh: “人们在这里买的药，很多大概是治小病的，比如皮疹、皮肤病、流感、头痛。”

lines.en: The apothecary has many thousands of objects. Some seem strange now, like the bloodletting tools. They were used to take blood from patients in hopes of removing their sickness as well. The treatment was often harmful, however, and ended in the late 19th century.
lines.zh: 药铺里有成千上万件物品。有些现在看来很奇怪，比如放血工具。人们曾用它们给病人放血，希望把病也一起排出去。不过这种疗法往往有害，到 19 世纪后期就不用了。

lines.en: Many famous people visited the apothecary while it was still a business, including America's first president. George Washington and his wife Martha lived nearby in the early 1800s at their home of Mount Vernon.
lines.zh: 药铺还在营业时，有许多名人来过，包括美国第一任总统。19 世纪初，乔治·华盛顿和妻子玛莎就住在附近的弗农山庄。

lines.en: But the apothecary had more than medicine.
lines.zh: 不过药铺里卖的不只是药。

lines.en: "Lots of other chemicals like paints, dyes and perfumes, would have been made and sold here."
lines.zh: “很多别的化学品，比如油漆、染料和香水，也会在这里制作和出售。”

lines.en: And, she said, customers could also buy baby bottles, writing instruments, and even clothes-making machines at the store.
lines.zh: 她说，顾客还可以在店里买到奶瓶、书写工具，甚至缝纫机。

lines.en: One bottle at the store holds a poison that was once used to ease pain. The drug called aconite comes from the wolfsbane plant. In earlier times, wolfsbane was thought to help control violence by imaginary creatures known as werewolves. In folklore, a werewolf is a human that changes into a wolf during full moons. Jim Williams works at the apothecary.
lines.zh: 店里有一个瓶子装着一种曾被用来止痛的毒药。这种叫乌头碱的药来自乌头草（wolfsbane，“狼毒”）。过去人们认为乌头草能帮助控制一种叫狼人的虚构生物的暴力。在民间传说中，狼人是在满月时变成狼的人。吉姆·威廉斯在药铺工作。

lines.en: "So if you're having werewolf trouble, it will get you through to the next full moon."
lines.zh: “所以，如果你被狼人困扰，它能帮你撑到下一个满月。”

lines.en: Williams added that wolfsbane would also be used to treat pain in human joints.
lines.zh: 威廉斯补充说，乌头草也被用来治疗人的关节疼痛。

lines.en: Visitor Christine Zapata from California said she was especially interested in the former store's different plants.
lines.zh: 来自加利福尼亚的游客克里斯汀·萨帕塔说，她对这家老店的各种植物特别感兴趣。

lines.en: "Using all these different herbs and plant-based medicines that are coming back now, for me that's most interesting for me since I work in the cannabis industry."
lines.zh: “这些各种各样的草药和植物药现在又回来了，对我来说这是最有意思的，因为我在大麻行业工作。”

lines.en: One box at the apothecary used to contain bottles of Coca-Cola. The drinks were first sold in the late 1800s as medicine believed to cure conditions like tiredness and headaches. However, Coca-Cola at that time contained the drug cocaine and could be addictive.
lines.zh: 药铺里有个箱子过去装着可口可乐。19 世纪后期，这种饮料最初是作为药出售的，人们相信它能治疲劳和头痛。不过，那时的可口可乐含有毒品可卡因，可能使人上瘾。

lines.en: Some treatments fell into disuse after it became known they were poisonous. But we continue to depend on many medicines found in the apothecary to heal injuries and cure disease.
lines.zh: 有些疗法在人们知道它们有毒后就不再使用了。但我们今天仍然依靠药铺里的许多药物来治伤治病。

lines.en: I'm Jonathan Evans.
lines.zh: 我是乔纳森·埃文斯。

qs.q: What is an apothecary?
qs.why: "a drugstore called an apothecary."

qs.q: Which famous people lived near the apothecary?
qs.why: "George Washington and his wife Martha lived nearby."

qs.q: Why was early Coca-Cola sold?
opts: as medicine for tiredness and headaches
as a sweet soda for children
qs.a: as medicine for tiredness and headaches
qs.why: "first sold in the late 1800s as medicine."

lessons.title: West Virginia Cook-off Celebrates Unusual Foods
lessons.zh: 西弗吉尼亚的“奇特食物”烹饪大赛
lessons.sum: 每年九月最后一个周末，西弗吉尼亚州小镇马林顿举办“路杀烹饪大赛”：海龟汤、鳄鱼肉秋葵浓汤、熊肉辣豆汤……至少 25% 的肉必须是野味。这个阿巴拉契亚山区的节日每年吸引上万人，给当地带来约 200 万美元收入。

lines.en: Would you like to try turtle soup? How about a thicker, richer-tasting gumbo made with alligator meat? Or perhaps you would like a helping of chili made with bear meat.
lines.zh: 你想尝尝海龟汤吗？用鳄鱼肉做的更浓稠、味道更浓郁的秋葵浓汤怎么样？或者来一份熊肉做的辣豆汤？

lines.en: Foods like these might sound very appealing to some Americans, but not everyone. They were just a few of the unusual foods available at the West Virginia Roadkill Cook-off. The cook-off festival takes place each year in Pocahontas County, West Virginia.
lines.zh: 这类食物对有些美国人来说也许很诱人，但不是对每个人。它们只是西弗吉尼亚“路杀烹饪大赛”上的几样奇特食物。这个烹饪节每年在西弗吉尼亚州波卡洪塔斯县举行。

lines.en: Since 1991, the event has been held in the Appalachian Mountains in the small town of Marlinton. The cook-off is a celebration of food dishes Americans normally do not find in a restaurant. All the dishes are made with roadkill, meaning animals found on the side of the road after being struck by a car or truck.
lines.zh: 自 1991 年以来，这项活动一直在阿巴拉契亚山区的小镇马林顿举行。烹饪大赛庆祝的是美国人平时在餐馆里吃不到的菜。所有菜都用“路杀”做——也就是被汽车或卡车撞死在路边的动物。

lines.en: Anyone can sign up to prepare food for the event. But at least 25 percent of the meat must be "wild," meaning it came from either hunting or killing an animal, and not from a store.
lines.zh: 任何人都可以报名为活动做菜。但至少 25% 的肉必须是“野生”的，也就是来自打猎或宰杀的动物，而不是商店买的。

lines.en: This year, some of the dishes had names like "Drunken Deer in the Headlights" and "Hillbilly Mardi Gras Alligator and Turtle Gumbo."
lines.zh: 今年有些菜的名字是“车灯前的醉鹿”和“山里人狂欢节鳄鱼海龟秋葵浓汤”。

lines.en: Ben Wilfong is vice president of the Pocahontas County Chamber of Commerce, the organization that finances the roadkill cook-off. He says the event started as simply an autumn harvest festival.
lines.zh: 本·威尔丰是波卡洪塔斯县商会的副会长，商会为路杀烹饪大赛提供资金。他说，这项活动最初只是一个秋收节。

lines.en: "Being Appalachia, and the wild game and history and culture, they decided to start the roadkill cook-off portion," Wilfong noted. "Its meaning is to cook something that you could possibly find on the side of the road …which is wildlife and part of Appalachian culture."
lines.zh: “这里是阿巴拉契亚，有野味，有历史和文化，所以他们决定开设路杀烹饪大赛这个部分，”威尔丰说，“它的意义是做一些你可能在路边找到的东西……也就是野生动物，这是阿巴拉契亚文化的一部分。”

lines.en: Wilfong said that people normally start planning a year before the cook-off to make sure they have enough wild meat. But he said the cooks never know exactly what kind of food they will prepare until a few weeks before the festival, and there are always surprises. In recent years, festival goers have enjoyed meat from pheasant, opossum, snake, and even iguana.
lines.zh: 威尔丰说，人们通常提前一年就开始准备，确保有足够的野味。但他说，厨师们直到节日前几个星期才确切知道要做什么菜，而且总有惊喜。近年来，参加节日的人吃过雉鸡、负鼠、蛇，甚至鬣蜥的肉。

lines.en: Bill Jordan, president of the chamber of commerce, said the idea for the event came from a book called "West Virginian Roadkill Cook-off." It was written by a West Virginian named Jeff Everball.
lines.zh: 商会会长比尔·乔丹说，这个活动的想法来自一本叫《西弗吉尼亚路杀烹饪大赛》的书，作者是西弗吉尼亚人杰夫·埃弗鲍尔。

lines.en: It did not take a long time for the cook-off to become popular.
lines.zh: 烹饪大赛没过多久就火了。

lines.en: "Eighty percent of the people here are not local, they are from Oklahoma, Texas, and Kansas," said Jordan. He added that people from as far away as India and Germany have traveled to Marlinton for the festival. They come for the chance to try out food they have never had before.
lines.zh: “这里 80% 的人不是本地人，他们来自俄克拉何马、德克萨斯和堪萨斯。”乔丹说。他还说，有人甚至从印度和德国远道来马林顿参加节日，就为了有机会尝尝从没吃过的食物。

lines.en: While the festival is known as the "roadkill" cook-off, many of the cooks get their meat from hunting or businesses that sell unusual kinds of meats.
lines.zh: 虽然这个节日叫“路杀”烹饪大赛，但很多厨师的肉其实来自打猎或卖特殊肉类的商家。

lines.en: Wilfong noted that it is illegal in West Virginia to pick up animals you kill with a vehicle unless one gets approval from the local government. However, that does not mean the festival never has food dishes from actual roadkill.
lines.zh: 威尔丰指出，在西弗吉尼亚，除非得到地方政府批准，捡拾被车撞死的动物是违法的。不过这并不意味着节日上从来没有真正用路杀做的菜。

lines.en: "One year," Jordan said, "a guy showed up that morning unregistered with a deer on the back of his truck that he had just hit that morning and wanted to cook it."
lines.zh: “有一年，”乔丹说，“一个家伙早上没报名就来了，卡车后面放着一头他当天早上刚撞到的鹿，想拿来做菜。”

lines.en: There is more to the festival than just unusual foods. You can also find hundreds of arts and craft dealers who sell their work. There is also a biscuit baking competition, and even a "Roadkill Queen" beauty competition.
lines.zh: 这个节日不只有奇特的食物。你还能看到几百个卖自己作品的手工艺品商贩。还有烤小圆面包比赛，甚至还有“路杀皇后”选美比赛。

lines.en: The festival is not just about having a good time either. It is also a money-making event for Marlinton and Pocahontas County.
lines.zh: 这个节日也不只是为了玩得开心。它也是马林顿和波卡洪塔斯县的一项创收活动。

lines.en: "It's close to a $2 million economic impact," says Wilfong. "The population of Pocahontas County is just slightly over 8,500 people, and they get about 12,000 for the event."
lines.zh: “它带来的经济效益接近 200 万美元，”威尔丰说，“波卡洪塔斯县的人口只有 8500 多人，而活动能吸引约 12000 人。”

lines.en: Wilfong added that the festival provides money for all businesses in the area, such as fuel businesses, hotels, store owners and restaurants.
lines.zh: 威尔丰补充说，这个节日给当地所有行业都带来了收入，比如加油站、旅馆、商店和餐馆。

lines.en: For local people, it also is a great way to get involved in the community.
lines.zh: 对当地人来说，这也是参与社区活动的好方式。

lines.en: Angela Lester and Peggie Stahl, from a group called the Youth Health Service, were taking part for their second time. They made a chili with a combination of venison and bear meat, which won first place at the festival this year.
lines.zh: 来自“青少年健康服务”组织的安吉拉·莱斯特和佩吉·斯塔尔是第二次参加。她们做了一道鹿肉加熊肉的辣豆汤，在今年的节日上得了第一名。

lines.en: Lester said they decided to compete as a way to get involved with their community, and because it was a lot of fun.
lines.zh: 莱斯特说，她们决定参赛是为了参与社区活动，而且非常好玩。

lines.en: Lester said they got their bear meat mostly from hunting, "But we've all come up on bear that has been hit by a vehicle. I just hit a deer the other day by accident."
lines.zh: 莱斯特说，她们的熊肉大多来自打猎，“不过我们都碰到过被车撞的熊。前几天我就不小心撞了一头鹿。”

lines.en: The Roadkill Cook-off festival is held every year on the last weekend of September. Cooking directions for some of the winning dishes from earlier years can be found in the "Roadkill Cookbook," which can be found on the Pocahontas County website.
lines.zh: 路杀烹饪大赛每年九月的最后一个周末举行。往年一些获奖菜的做法可以在《路杀食谱》里找到，这本食谱在波卡洪塔斯县的网站上可以看到。

lines.en: I'm Rick Hindman. And I'm Dorothy Gundy.
lines.zh: 我是里克·欣德曼。我是多萝西·冈迪。

qs.q: What must at least 25 percent of the meat be?
qs.why: "at least 25 percent of the meat must be 'wild.'"

qs.q: Where do most people at the festival come from?
qs.why: "Eighty percent of the people here are not local."

qs.q: What won first place this year?
opts: chili with venison and bear meat
qs.a: chili with venison and bear meat
qs.why: "They made a chili with a combination of venison and bear meat, which won first place."

lessons.title: New Bakery, Old Baking Method
lessons.zh: 新面包店，老做法
lessons.sum: 乔纳森·贝索尼曾在塞内加尔的沙漠村庄生活，后来爱上了烘焙。他在华盛顿开了面包店 Seylou（曼丁哥语“鹰”的意思），从本地农民那里买约 20 种有机谷物，在店里自己磨粉，用全谷物做面包和糕点。

lines.en: Jonathan Bethony uses his experiences in West Africa and other places to bring the ancient art of bread-making to Washington, D.C.
lines.zh: 乔纳森·贝索尼利用他在西非和其他地方的经历，把古老的面包制作艺术带到了华盛顿。

lines.en: His bakery, Seylou, is different from most bakeries around the country. Bakers there grind whole grains in their own mill. They also buy their grains from local farmers.
lines.zh: 他的面包店 Seylou 和全国大多数面包店不一样。那里的面包师用自己的磨坊研磨全谷物，还从本地农民那里买谷物。

lines.en: More than 15 years ago, Bethony visited Senegal to learn West African drumming. During his time living in a small desert village, he became interested in working with local farmers. He wanted to help local people who were struggling to get enough food.
lines.zh: 15 年多前，贝索尼去塞内加尔学习西非鼓。他住在一个沙漠小村庄的那段时间，对和当地农民合作产生了兴趣。他想帮助那些难以填饱肚子的当地人。

lines.en: When he came back to the U.S., Bethony began working in restaurants and discovered a love for baking.
lines.zh: 回到美国后，贝索尼开始在餐馆工作，发现自己热爱烘焙。

lines.en: Later, Bethony started working for the Washington State University's Bread Lab. There, he developed new ways of using many kinds of locally grown wheat, without wasting any of their components.
lines.zh: 后来，贝索尼开始在华盛顿州立大学的“面包实验室”工作。在那里，他开发了使用多种本地小麦、又不浪费其任何部分的新方法。

lines.en: For Bethony, having his own bakery was the next step in using the skills he had learned and developed over many years. In November, he opened his bakery and called it Seylou, which means "eagle" in the West African language of Mandinka.
lines.zh: 对贝索尼来说，拥有自己的面包店，是运用他多年来学到和发展的技能的下一步。11 月，他开了自己的面包店，取名 Seylou，在西非曼丁哥语里是“鹰”的意思。

lines.en: At Seylou, it is important to use local ingredients. They get all of their grain fresh from local farmers. Bethony uses about 20 different kinds of organic grains in making his bread.
lines.zh: 在 Seylou，使用本地原料很重要。他们所有的谷物都是从本地农民那里新鲜采购的。贝索尼做面包用大约 20 种不同的有机谷物。

lines.en: He said, "We use several varieties of wheat alone, and about 3 different ryes…Our mission here is to use what they call underutilized grains, which is important to grow in the organic system."
lines.zh: 他说：“光是小麦我们就用好几个品种，还有大约 3 种黑麦……我们在这里的使命是使用所谓‘未被充分利用’的谷物，这对有机种植体系很重要。”

lines.en: Bethony adds that a lot of the soil in the area has been damaged from growing tobacco. He said growing millet helps bring life back to the soil.
lines.zh: 贝索尼还说，这一带很多土壤因为种植烟草而受损。他说，种小米能帮助土壤恢复生机。

lines.en: Bethony is one of only a small number of bakers around the United States who mill their grains on-site, meaning at the bakery. This has caught the attention of food and environment reporter Sam Fromartz, who has written a book about bread called, "In Search of the Perfect Loaf."
lines.zh: 贝索尼是全美少数几个在店里——也就是在面包店现场——磨粉的面包师之一。这引起了食品与环境记者萨姆·弗罗马茨的注意，他写过一本关于面包的书，叫《寻找完美的面包》。

lines.en: He says knowing how to mill and knowing which grains to use is what gives each kind of bread its individual taste and feel.
lines.zh: 他说，知道怎么磨粉、知道用哪些谷物，是让每种面包都有独特味道和口感的关键。

lines.en: Fromartz said, "When you start baking with grains from particular farmers, the grains will be different in each farm. So, Jonathan, in a sense, is adjusting each batch of grain that he mills. So, he's kind of mixing and matching and playing with his ingredients"
lines.zh: 弗罗马茨说：“当你开始用特定农民的谷物烘焙时，每个农场的谷物都会不一样。所以从某种意义上说，乔纳森在调整他磨的每一批谷物。他在搭配、组合、摆弄他的原料。”

lines.en: He said that Bethony is part of a developing movement in the American food industry. More bakers are returning to "old food ways" by trying to bake with whole grains.
lines.zh: 他说，贝索尼是美国食品业一个正在发展的运动的一部分：越来越多的面包师尝试用全谷物烘焙，回归“传统的饮食方式”。

lines.en: One-hundred percent organic whole grain is not only for making bread. Seylou also makes pastries using whole grains.
lines.zh: 百分之百有机全谷物不只用来做面包，Seylou 还用全谷物做糕点。

lines.en: Bethony said his work is easy because he surrounds himself with like-minded people, like his pastry chef, Charbel Abrache.
lines.zh: 贝索尼说，他的工作很轻松，因为身边都是志同道合的人，比如他的糕点师查贝尔·阿布拉什。

lines.en: But, Bethony said Seylou would not work without the support of his business partner and wife, Jessica Azees.
lines.zh: 不过贝索尼说，没有他的生意伙伴兼妻子杰西卡·阿齐兹的支持，Seylou 就办不起来。

lines.en: Seylou's baked products are rich in natural minerals and vitamins, but the taste is what brings people back to the store. This makes Bethony happy, because he wants people to eat food that is healthy for them, but still enjoyable.
lines.zh: Seylou 的烘焙产品富含天然矿物质和维生素，但让人们一再光顾的是它的味道。这让贝索尼很高兴，因为他希望人们吃到既健康又好吃的食物。

lines.en: "When you're going to a pastry shop or a bakery, there is excitement…I don't want to take away any of this experience," Bethony said.
lines.zh: “去糕点店或面包店时，人们会很兴奋……我不想夺走这种体验。”贝索尼说。

lines.en: I'm Phil Dierking.
lines.zh: 我是菲尔·迪尔金。

qs.q: What makes Seylou different from most bakeries?
qs.why: "Bakers there grind whole grains in their own mill."

qs.q: What does "Seylou" mean?
qs.why: "which means 'eagle' in the West African language of Mandinka."

qs.q: Why did Bethony first go to Senegal?
qs.why: "Bethony visited Senegal to learn West African drumming."

lessons.title: The Crazy Success Behind 'John's Crazy Socks'
lessons.zh: “约翰的疯狂袜子”的成功故事
lessons.sum: 纽约长岛的约翰·克罗宁生来患有唐氏综合征，高中毕业后没上大学，而是和父亲一起开了一家卖彩色“疯狂袜子”的公司。公司创造了 35 个工作岗位，其中 18 个给了残障人士，营收超过 400 万美元，还为慈善机构募捐。

lines.en: After graduating from high school, many young people are excited to go off to college. But not all. Some may want to skip college and jump right into a business.
lines.zh: 高中毕业后，很多年轻人都兴奋地去上大学，但不是所有人。有些人可能想跳过大学，直接去做生意。

lines.en: That was the case with John Cronin from Long Island, New York. He did not dream of going to college. He dreamed of going into business with his father. But they did not know what kind of business.
lines.zh: 纽约长岛的约翰·克罗宁就是这样。他梦想的不是上大学，而是和父亲一起做生意。可他们不知道做什么生意。

lines.en: John Cronin told Money magazine that he thought about starting a food truck. But, there was one problem. Neither he nor his father can cook.
lines.zh: 约翰·克罗宁对《金钱》杂志说，他想过开一辆餐车。可是有一个问题：他和父亲都不会做饭。

lines.en: After some thinking, the father-son team decided to go into business making a product the younger Cronin loves: socks!
lines.zh: 想了一阵子后，这对父子决定做小克罗宁最喜欢的一样东西：袜子！

lines.en: Mark, John's father, says his son has always loved colorful, wild socks. So, they created John's Crazy Socks Company.
lines.zh: 约翰的父亲马克说，儿子一直喜欢色彩鲜艳、花样疯狂的袜子。于是他们创办了“约翰的疯狂袜子”公司。

lines.en: The younger Cronin explains what he loves about his work.
lines.zh: 小克罗宁讲了他喜欢自己工作的哪些地方。

lines.en: "I want to sell crazy socks. Why socks? Because it's fun; it's colorful. I like to be creative, and I want to see wonderful things here." (Mark) "You're a talented guy!" (John) "Yes, I am."
lines.zh: “我想卖疯狂的袜子。为什么是袜子？因为好玩，色彩丰富。我喜欢有创意，我想在这里看到美好的东西。”（马克）“你是个有才华的家伙！”（约翰）“是的，我是。”

lines.en: John was born with Down Syndrome, a genetic disorder that causes learning disabilities and developmental delays. But that has not stopped him from gaining major success in the business world.
lines.zh: 约翰生来患有唐氏综合征，这是一种导致学习障碍和发育迟缓的遗传病。但这并没有阻止他在商界取得巨大成功。

lines.en: Since launching John's Crazy Socks, father and son have been crazy busy making crazy money. But their business also helps others with disabilities.
lines.zh: 自从创办“约翰的疯狂袜子”以来，父子俩忙得“疯狂”，赚钱也赚得“疯狂”。他们的生意还帮助了其他残障人士。

lines.en: "We've been able to create 35 jobs —18 of those are held by people with differing abilities. We've raised over $135,000 for our charity partners."
lines.zh: “我们已经创造了 35 个工作岗位——其中 18 个由不同能力的人担任。我们为慈善合作伙伴募集了 13.5 万多美元。”

lines.en: The father and son divide the duties of the business.
lines.zh: 父子俩分工经营。

lines.en: John works on sock design but he is also the face of the company. This means he represents the company on its advertising used to help sell the product and on the packaging of the product. Mark takes care of the books, managing money, supplies and hiring.
lines.zh: 约翰负责设计袜子，同时也是公司的“门面”。也就是说，在帮助推销产品的广告上和产品包装上，都由他代表公司。马克负责管账，管理资金、货品和招聘。

lines.en: John and Mark try to make each sock purchase personal. So, they hand-carry orders to customers in the Long Island area. But for those who live farther, John sends a personal note with each order he sends.
lines.zh: 约翰和马克努力让每一笔袜子订单都带着个人的温度。所以他们亲手把订单送给长岛地区的顾客。对住得更远的顾客，约翰会在寄出的每份订单里附上一张亲笔便条。

lines.en: (Mark) "What's our mission?"
lines.zh: （马克）“我们的使命是什么？”

lines.en: (John) "Our mission is to spread happiness."
lines.zh: （约翰）“我们的使命是传播快乐。”

lines.en: (Mark) "Our customers are happy. We have over 10,000 online reviews — 96 percent of those are five-star reviews — and we've done a lot of work, a lot of business. We've shipped over 115,000 orders and earned over $4 million in revenue."
lines.zh: （马克）“我们的顾客很开心。我们有一万多条在线评价——其中 96% 是五星好评——我们做了大量工作、大量生意。我们寄出了 11.5 万多份订单，营收超过 400 万美元。”

lines.en: Five percent of John's profits goes to the Special Olympics. The company also gives to the National Down Syndrome Society and the Association for Children with Down Syndrome.
lines.zh: 约翰利润的 5% 捐给特殊奥林匹克运动会。公司还向全国唐氏综合征协会和唐氏综合征儿童协会捐款。

lines.en: John Cronin is living his dream; spreading happiness, one pair of crazy socks at a time.
lines.zh: 约翰·克罗宁正在实现他的梦想：一双疯狂的袜子接一双疯狂的袜子地传播快乐。

lines.en: I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: Why didn't John and his father start a food truck?
qs.why: "Neither he nor his father can cook."

qs.q: What is the company's mission?
qs.why: "Our mission is to spread happiness."

qs.q: How many of the 35 jobs are held by people with differing abilities?
qs.why: "18 of those are held by people with differing abilities."

lessons.title: Appalachian Music Celebrates Modern Culture, Immigrant Past
lessons.zh: 阿巴拉契亚音乐：移民的过去与今天的文化
lessons.sum: 18 世纪，爱尔兰、苏格兰、德国移民来到美国东部的阿巴拉契亚山区，他们的音乐和非洲奴隶的音乐融合，形成了“老时光音乐”。它用小提琴、班卓琴、吉他演奏，靠耳朵代代相传，至今仍凝聚着山区社区。

lines.en: "To me the difference between a violin, and a fiddle, is that a violin never had a beer spilled on it... That is the difference."
lines.zh: “在我看来，小提琴（violin）和‘乡村提琴’（fiddle）的区别是，violin 上从没洒过啤酒……这就是区别。”

lines.en: Will Fanning laughs at his joke as he rocks on his chair outside his home in Mingo, West Virginia. Fanning is a musician and hotel owner born in Ireland. But now he lives deep in the Appalachian Mountains of the United States.
lines.zh: 威尔·范宁坐在西弗吉尼亚州明戈家门外的摇椅上，被自己的笑话逗笑了。范宁是个音乐人和旅馆老板，出生在爱尔兰，如今却住在美国阿巴拉契亚山脉的深处。

lines.en: "The Irish nearly every day have a song and play music," said Fanning. "So that tradition is kind of bred into me. My family, every weekend we'd play music at the house."
lines.zh: “爱尔兰人几乎每天都唱歌、弹琴，”范宁说，“所以这个传统可以说是从小就融进了我的血液。我们家每个周末都在家里演奏音乐。”

lines.en: Like Fanning, many in the area continue the traditions from their families' immigrant history including a kind of music called old-time.
lines.zh: 和范宁一样，这一带的许多人延续着家族移民史中的传统，其中包括一种叫“老时光”（old-time）的音乐。

lines.en: Old-time music comes from the Appalachian Mountains, a 2,400-kilometer-long system of mountains along the eastern part of the United States.
lines.zh: 老时光音乐来自阿巴拉契亚山脉，这是一条沿美国东部绵延 2400 公里的山脉。

lines.en: In the 18th century, many Europeans from Ireland, Scotland, and Germany arrived in the area to begin new lives.
lines.zh: 18 世纪，许多来自爱尔兰、苏格兰和德国的欧洲人来到这一地区开始新生活。

lines.en: The U.S. was now their home, but these Appalachian communities continued the European music and dance traditions they loved. Over time, the music mixed with that of African slaves and became its own. It is called old-time music.
lines.zh: 美国成了他们的家，但这些阿巴拉契亚社区延续了他们热爱的欧洲音乐和舞蹈传统。随着时间推移，这种音乐和非洲奴隶的音乐融合，形成了自己的风格，叫作老时光音乐。

lines.en: Gerry Milnes is a musician and folklorist from Elkins, West Virginia. He says the culture of the Appalachian people has survived throughout time because they lived far from other groups.
lines.zh: 格里·米尔恩斯是西弗吉尼亚州埃尔金斯的音乐人和民俗学者。他说，阿巴拉契亚人的文化能一直保存下来，是因为他们住得离其他群体很远。

lines.en: "The sort of earliest culture that arrived here in that period has really maintained those old traditions. It's both dialect, and music and customs and traditions and folk ways of all kinds… have a particular Appalachian sensibility to them."
lines.zh: “那个时期最早来到这里的文化，确实保留了那些古老的传统。方言、音乐、风俗、传统和各种民间生活方式……都带着一种特别的阿巴拉契亚气质。”

lines.en: The instruments used to make old-time music usually include guitar, banjo, fiddle, mandolin and bass.
lines.zh: 演奏老时光音乐的乐器通常有吉他、班卓琴、乡村提琴、曼陀林和贝斯。

lines.en: "Old time music -- you can hear fiddle tunes that have been played pretty much the same way for a couple hundred years," Milnes said.
lines.zh: “老时光音乐——你能听到一些提琴曲，几百年来演奏方式几乎没变过。”米尔恩斯说。

lines.en: Professional musician John Lilly, of Charleston, West Virginia, plays old-time and country music. He says the earliest purpose of the music was for dancing. Life in the mountains was hard work. Music and dancing provided Appalachians a much needed break from the labors of the day.
lines.zh: 西弗吉尼亚州查尔斯顿的职业音乐人约翰·利利演奏老时光音乐和乡村音乐。他说，这种音乐最早的用途是伴舞。山区生活很辛苦，音乐和舞蹈让阿巴拉契亚人从一天的劳作中得到急需的休息。

lines.en: And it brought members of different generations together. Emily Miller, another local West Virginian musician, says that in small Appalachian towns in the past, there was always an old fiddler or musician in the neighborhood. Young people would study the art under him or her.
lines.zh: 它还把不同代的人聚在一起。另一位西弗吉尼亚本地音乐人埃米莉·米勒说，过去在阿巴拉契亚的小镇上，街坊里总有一位老提琴手或音乐人，年轻人会跟着他或她学艺。

lines.en: Richard Heffner, a musician from Lewisburg, West Virginia, is in the Black Mountain Bluegrass Boys Band. He says his community often enjoyed music in groups.
lines.zh: 来自西弗吉尼亚州刘易斯堡的音乐人理查德·赫夫纳是“黑山蓝草男孩乐队”的成员。他说，他所在的社区常常一群人一起享受音乐。

lines.en: "A lot of the people, they would just meet at their houses, move the furniture back, and dance in the living room, and, like I say, roll up the rug… and that still goes on in our family!"
lines.zh: “很多人就在自己家里聚会，把家具挪开，在客厅里跳舞，就像我说的，把地毯卷起来……我们家现在还这样！”

lines.en: High school student Silas Riley and his sister Hazel are learning to banjo. Old-time music is learned by ear, Silas said.
lines.zh: 高中生塞拉斯·赖利和他的妹妹黑兹尔在学弹班卓琴。塞拉斯说，老时光音乐是靠耳朵学的。

lines.en: "It's a lot harder than other music. There's no written stuff, no written notes, so you have to learn it all by listening to it and trying to reproduce the sound," Silas said
lines.zh: “它比其他音乐难多了。没有写下来的东西，没有乐谱，所以你得全靠听，然后努力把声音弹出来。”塞拉斯说。

lines.en: Silas adds that old-time musicians might not read music, but they can still easily put a song together.
lines.zh: 塞拉斯补充说，老时光音乐人也许不识谱，但他们照样能轻松地把一首曲子弹出来。

lines.en: "You can just listen to it and then play it," he said.
lines.zh: “你听一听就能弹。”他说。

lines.en: Old-time songs are records of history. Some called "spirituals" are based in the Christian religion. Others are American civil war songs. And, many are about the life and land that surround the songwriter, says Heffner.
lines.zh: 赫夫纳说，老时光歌曲是历史的记录。有些叫“灵歌”，以基督教为基础；有些是美国南北战争时期的歌；还有很多是关于写歌人周围的生活和土地的。

lines.en: "Some of the words of the songs have so much to do with the area. The hills, mountains, streams, and rivers, the old log cabin, and real gruesome ones about murder and things like that," Heffner said.
lines.zh: “有些歌词跟这一带关系太密切了：丘陵、山脉、小溪、河流、老木屋，还有真正可怕的关于谋杀之类的歌。”赫夫纳说。

lines.en: But some of the earliest songs go back to the music's European roots.
lines.zh: 不过一些最早的歌曲可以追溯到这种音乐的欧洲根源。

lines.en: Patrick O'Flaherty was born in Ireland, but now lives in Lewisburg, West Virginia. He owns an Irish restaurant there and plays Irish music in his band, The Poor Claires.
lines.zh: 帕特里克·奥弗莱厄蒂出生在爱尔兰，现在住在西弗吉尼亚州刘易斯堡。他在那里开了一家爱尔兰餐馆，还在他的乐队“可怜的克莱尔们”里演奏爱尔兰音乐。

lines.en: O'Flaherty says that when he hears old-time music, he recognizes songs that he heard growing up in Ireland.
lines.zh: 奥弗莱厄蒂说，他听老时光音乐时，能认出他在爱尔兰长大时听过的歌。

lines.en: "Lots of the tunes of the old timey music and the bluegrass, you hear the Scottish reels and Scottish jigs, or the Irish reels and Irish jigs and … I can nearly tell where that came from. The root is there."
lines.zh: “很多老时光音乐和蓝草音乐的曲子里，你能听到苏格兰里尔舞曲和苏格兰吉格舞曲，或者爱尔兰里尔舞曲和吉格舞曲……我几乎能说出它们是从哪里来的。根就在那里。”

lines.en: Reels and jigs are forms of music and dance.
lines.zh: 里尔舞和吉格舞是两种音乐和舞蹈形式。

lines.en: It is a sunny day at the Augusta Heritage Festival in West Virginia.
lines.zh: 西弗吉尼亚的奥古斯塔传统文化节上，阳光明媚。

lines.en: "The first thing you ever learn on the clawhammer banjo is the basic strum… And the way to hold your hand, if you've ever like, I usually tell people how they hold an axe, like you're splitting wood or something, that's how you hold your hand. After you learn that, you can just really play anything..."
lines.zh: “学爪锤式班卓琴，第一件事就是学基本的拨弦……手的姿势嘛，我通常告诉别人，就像握斧子劈柴那样握，手就是这样放的。学会这个以后，你就真的什么都能弹了……”

lines.en: Trevor Hammons is describing how to play the banjo.
lines.zh: 特雷弗·哈蒙斯在讲怎么弹班卓琴。

lines.en: The Hammons family is an important part of old-time music in West Virginia. They came from Kentucky, and settled in the area just before the Civil War. Hammonds' family musicians wrote many of the songs that people play in West Virginia today.
lines.zh: 哈蒙斯家族是西弗吉尼亚老时光音乐的重要组成部分。他们来自肯塔基州，在南北战争前不久在这一带定居。哈蒙斯家族的音乐人写了很多今天西弗吉尼亚人仍在演奏的歌。

lines.en: Trevor is in high school, and first became interested in music after listening to an album that had a photo of his great-grandfather, Lee Hammons, on the cover. Trevor quickly learned to play the banjo. His style is often compared to that of his great-grandfather's.
lines.zh: 特雷弗在上高中。他最初对音乐感兴趣，是因为听了一张封面上印着他曾祖父李·哈蒙斯照片的专辑。特雷弗很快学会了弹班卓琴，他的风格常被拿来和曾祖父相比。

lines.en: "They say my hand is just like his," Trevor said. "People say it's like I'm his shadow or something."
lines.zh: “他们说我的手跟他一模一样，”特雷弗说，“人们说我就像他的影子什么的。”

lines.en: What he likes best about the old-time music culture is its hopefulness.
lines.zh: 他最喜欢老时光音乐文化的，是它充满希望。

lines.en: "With this music, you never really meet a person with negativity," Trevor says. "They all kind of are like a big family, a special bond you get when you sit around and jam and play."
lines.zh: “玩这种音乐，你几乎碰不到消极的人，”特雷弗说，“他们就像一个大家庭，大家坐在一起即兴合奏的时候，会产生一种特别的纽带。”

lines.en: These days, old-time music is not often heard over the radio. But it still lives on strongly in the communities where it came from.
lines.zh: 如今，电台里不常听到老时光音乐了。但在它的发源地社区里，它依然生生不息。

lines.en: Organizations like the Mountain Music Trail have created a record of events and places people can visit to experience this rich part of American history.
lines.zh: “山区音乐之路”这样的组织整理了一份活动和地点清单，人们可以去那里体验美国历史中这丰富的一部分。

lines.en: A history, that Miller says is important to the identity of the people.
lines.zh: 米勒说，这段历史对这里的人的身份认同很重要。

lines.en: "So I think that there's a real pride in what the people of Appalachia have made together… And the music specifically is just something that everyone kind of identifies with. This region has hard times, we've been going through economic transition, but this music has stuck with us through it all"
lines.zh: “所以我觉得阿巴拉契亚人对他们共同创造的东西真的很自豪……尤其是音乐，大家都认同它。这个地区经历过艰难时期，我们一直在经历经济转型，但这种音乐一路陪伴着我们。”

lines.en: I'm Phil Dierking. And I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是菲尔·迪尔金。我是凯蒂·韦弗。

qs.q: Where does old-time music come from?
qs.why: "Old-time music comes from the Appalachian Mountains."

qs.q: How is old-time music learned?
qs.why: "Old-time music is learned by ear."

qs.q: What was the earliest purpose of the music?
qs.why: "the earliest purpose of the music was for dancing."

lessons.title: Pierogi Dumpling Project Brings Volunteers Together
lessons.zh: “饺子项目”把志愿者聚在一起
lessons.sum: 俄亥俄州克利夫兰附近一座乌克兰天主教堂里，奥莲娜和志愿者们每周手工包几百公斤东欧饺子（pierogi），卖给附近居民和餐馆，为教堂筹款。从周一做酸菜馅到周四捏饺子，这个项目也让大家成了一家人。

lines.en: Chinese steamed buns. Italian ravioli. Indian samosas. No matter where you live, chances are there is a local dumpling – a small mass of dough usually cooked with meat and vegetables inside.
lines.zh: 中国的包子，意大利的饺子（ravioli），印度的萨莫萨三角饺。不管你住在哪里，当地很可能都有一种“饺子”——一小团面皮，里面通常包着肉和蔬菜煮熟。

lines.en: Today, we are talking about the pierogi, a dumpling from Eastern Europe. Traditional pierogi fillings include potatoes, sauerkraut, cheese and even fruit.
lines.zh: 今天我们来聊聊 pierogi，一种来自东欧的饺子。传统的馅有土豆、酸菜、奶酪，甚至水果。

lines.en: Olena Apostoluk is an American of Ukrainian-English descent. She has been making pierogis for 17 years.
lines.zh: 奥莲娜·阿波斯托卢克是乌克兰和英国血统的美国人。她包 pierogi 已经 17 年了。

lines.en: "We call it 'pyrohy' but really, it's 'varenyky' because you are boiling it. So, Americanized it's 'pierogis, pyrogis' -- depends on where you come from."
lines.zh: “我们叫它 pyrohy，不过其实应该叫 varenyky，因为是煮的。美国化了以后就叫 pierogis、pyrogis——看你是从哪里来的。”

lines.en: Olena operates a volunteer food project out of the St. Josaphat Ukrainian Catholic Cathedral near Cleveland, Ohio. It is called the Pierogi Project. It raises money to help pay the cost of operating the church.
lines.zh: 奥莲娜在俄亥俄州克利夫兰附近的圣约沙法乌克兰天主教大教堂经营一个志愿者食品项目，叫“饺子项目”。它筹集资金，帮助支付教堂的运营费用。

lines.en: Olena and her team prepare and sell 130 to 180 kilograms of pierogis to the public every Thursday and Friday. During the Christian holidays of Lent and Christmas, they make and sell about 600 kilograms of pierogis each week.
lines.zh: 奥莲娜和她的团队每周四、周五制作并向公众出售 130 到 180 公斤饺子。在基督教的大斋节和圣诞节期间，他们每周要做、要卖大约 600 公斤。

lines.en: "The people who buy pierogis are regular people that have been buying pierogis from us for many years. Or a lot of people are word-of-mouth. I do have a handful of restaurants and bars that buy from me."
lines.zh: “来买饺子的是常客，他们从我们这儿买了很多年了。也有很多人是口口相传来的。还有几家餐馆和酒吧从我这儿进货。”

lines.en: Making hundreds and sometimes thousands of pierogis by hand each week is a lot of work. Olena prepares for the task by completing a special job each day. On Monday, the sauerkraut filling is prepared. The mixture arrives in a large container. Olena rinses it in water and then presses the water out. She adds spices, and then forms the filling into small balls.
lines.zh: 每周手工包几百个、有时几千个饺子，是个大工程。奥莲娜每天完成一项专门的工作来做准备。星期一准备酸菜馅：酸菜装在一个大容器里送来，奥莲娜用水冲洗，再把水挤干，加入香料，然后把馅捏成小球。

lines.en: On Tuesday, the potato filling is prepared. Olena uses only potatoes that cook well in water: the Russet Norkotah or Burbank from the state of Idaho. She and her team hand peel, cook, and smash about 20 kilograms of potatoes or more. The cheese filling is also prepared on Tuesday.
lines.zh: 星期二准备土豆馅。奥莲娜只用适合水煮的土豆：爱达荷州的褐皮诺科塔或伯班克土豆。她和团队手工削皮、煮熟、捣碎大约 20 公斤甚至更多土豆。奶酪馅也在星期二准备。

lines.en: On Wednesday, Olena prepares the dumpling dough.
lines.zh: 星期三，奥莲娜准备饺子皮的面团。

lines.en: "The dough recipe was given to me by my mother-in-law. Everybody has their own little dough recipe but mine works for me. It's nice and soft. The customers that come in, they really like our dough."
lines.zh: “面团的配方是我婆婆给我的。每个人都有自己的小配方，不过我的对我很管用。它又软又好。来买的顾客都很喜欢我们的面皮。”

lines.en: For the dough, Olena mixes about 10 kilograms of flour with water, milk and salt in an electric mixing bowl for about 20 minutes. She knows from touch when the dough is ready to cool.
lines.zh: 做面团时，奥莲娜把大约 10 公斤面粉和水、牛奶、盐放进电动搅拌盆，搅大约 20 分钟。她用手一摸就知道面团什么时候可以放凉了。

lines.en: Early on Thursday, the whole team comes together for the final stage of the pierogi production.
lines.zh: 星期四一早，整个团队聚在一起，完成饺子制作的最后一步。

lines.en: "The dough is rolled out and then after it's rolled out there's a roller that will cut the rounds. The ladies over there, they are pinching. We call it pinching pierogis. So, they are just taking the dough rounds and making sure that they are closed, so that when we cook them, they don't open up."
lines.zh: “把面团擀开，擀开以后用一个滚刀切出圆片。那边的女士们在捏。我们管这叫‘捏饺子’。她们拿起圆面片，确保把口捏紧，这样煮的时候就不会破。”

lines.en: After the pierogis are put together, they are boiled, and then packaged. At 8 in the morning, the first pierogis go on sale.
lines.zh: 饺子包好后，先煮熟，再包装。早上 8 点，第一批饺子开卖。

lines.en: Linda Hupert has been working on the Pierogi Project for about four years. Before that, her mother was a volunteer. But now, she says she doesn't have much family left.
lines.zh: 琳达·休珀特参加“饺子项目”大约四年了。在那之前，她的母亲是这里的志愿者。可现在，她说她没剩多少家人了。

lines.en: So, my family has become the people here at church. So, that's my extended family.
lines.zh: “所以，我的家人就成了教堂里的这些人。这是我的大家庭。”

lines.en: The Pierogi Project does more than make pierogis for the community.
lines.zh: “饺子项目”为社区做的不只是饺子。

lines.en: It brings people together.
lines.zh: 它把人们聚在了一起。

lines.en: I'm Dorothy Gundy.
lines.zh: 我是多萝西·冈迪。

qs.q: Why does the Pierogi Project sell dumplings?
opts: to raise money for the church
qs.a: to raise money for the church
qs.why: "It raises money to help pay the cost of operating the church."

qs.q: What is prepared on Monday?
qs.why: "On Monday, the sauerkraut filling is prepared."

qs.q: What does Linda Hupert say about the people at the church?
qs.why: "that's my extended family."

lessons.title: Supporting National Parks Through the Arts
lessons.zh: 用艺术支持国家公园
lessons.sum: 美国国家公园管理局的“驻园艺术家”项目让画家、作家、摄影师和音乐人在国家公园住上几周进行创作。画家罗莎莉在大雾山公园画真菌、昆虫和同步闪光的萤火虫；音乐人戴维在人迹罕至的罗亚尔岛写了 16 首歌。

lines.en: Artist Rosalie Haizlett starts every day by opening a map of the Great Smokey Mountains National Park. Over breakfast, she plans her walk for the day. She packs food and a sketch book, and then leaves for her walk in the woods.
lines.zh: 艺术家罗莎莉·海兹利特每天一开始，都会打开一张大雾山国家公园的地图。吃早饭时，她规划当天的徒步路线。她带上食物和速写本，然后出发去林中漫步。

lines.en: Haizlett spends all day exploring the park and sketching what she sees. At the end of the day she returns to her cabin, and starts painting pictures based on the sketches.
lines.zh: 海兹利特整天在公园里探索，把看到的东西画下来。傍晚她回到小木屋，根据速写开始画画。

lines.en: Haizlett has been doing this since the beginning of June as part of the United States National Park Service's Artist-in-Residence program, or A.I.R.
lines.zh: 从 6 月初开始，海兹利特就一直这样做，这是美国国家公园管理局“驻园艺术家”（A.I.R.）项目的一部分。

lines.en: Artists have been important to American national parks for a long time. In the 1870s, an art movement called the Hudson River School, documented natural America from the northeastern coast to the Wild West.
lines.zh: 长期以来，艺术家对美国国家公园一直很重要。19 世纪 70 年代，一个叫“哈德逊河画派”的艺术运动，记录了从东北海岸到狂野西部的美国自然风光。

lines.en: During that same time, the work of American painter Thomas Moran helped persuade the U.S. Congress to create the country's first national park: Yellowstone, in the western state of Wyoming.
lines.zh: 同一时期，美国画家托马斯·莫兰的作品帮助说服美国国会建立了第一座国家公园：位于西部怀俄明州的黄石国家公园。

lines.en: Since 1969, the National Park Service has provided artists the chance to be officially involved with American parks, through A.I.R.
lines.zh: 自 1969 年以来，国家公园管理局通过 A.I.R. 项目，给艺术家们提供正式参与美国公园工作的机会。

lines.en: Chris Amidon supervises the resident artist program at Isle Royale National Park in Michigan.
lines.zh: 克里斯·阿米登负责密歇根州罗亚尔岛国家公园的驻园艺术家项目。

lines.en: "It's about connecting to the next generation to art and the public with the landscapes of the national parks."
lines.zh: “这是要让下一代与艺术相连，让公众与国家公园的风景相连。”

lines.en: Resident artists spend two to four weeks in a park. Artists of all kinds may take part, including painters, writers, photographers and musicians. The artists spend their time working on art inspired by their surroundings. They also agree to donate at least one artwork to the park.
lines.zh: 驻园艺术家在公园里待两到四周。各类艺术家都可以参加，包括画家、作家、摄影师和音乐人。艺术家们利用这段时间创作受周围环境启发的作品，并同意至少捐给公园一件作品。

lines.en: Currently, NPS runs 47 artist-in-residence programs in 30 different states.
lines.zh: 目前，国家公园管理局在 30 个州开展了 47 个驻园艺术家项目。

lines.en: Amidon said one NPS goal is to bring new people from a mix of age groups and ethnicities to the parks. The A.I.R. program is important for "building a bridge" between the parks and the public, he said.
lines.zh: 阿米登说，国家公园管理局的一个目标，是把不同年龄、不同族裔的新游客带到公园来。他说，A.I.R. 项目对在公园和公众之间“架起一座桥梁”很重要。

lines.en: Haizlett said it was her childhood growing up in an artistic family in the Appalachian Mountains of West Virginia that led to her career as an artist.
lines.zh: 海兹利特说，她在西弗吉尼亚阿巴拉契亚山区一个艺术之家长大的童年，让她走上了艺术家的道路。

lines.en: The painter says she is most inspired by small forms of life in nature, such as fungi, insects, and animals.
lines.zh: 这位画家说，最能激发她灵感的是大自然中的小生命，比如真菌、昆虫和动物。

lines.en: "I've always really enjoyed the stories of things that are underrepresented."
lines.zh: “我一直很喜欢那些很少被人关注的事物的故事。”

lines.en: Haizlett says she is combining her paintings and drawings created in the Smokies to make a jigsaw puzzle. It will show the many species of fungi and insects in the park.
lines.zh: 海兹利特说，她正把在大雾山创作的绘画和素描组合成一幅拼图，展示公园里的许多种真菌和昆虫。

lines.en: One of Haizlett's favorite experiences at the park so far was the light show produced during the synchronous firefly season. The insects fill the woods. As night falls they begin to light up and off as part of the reproduction process. Within moments, they are all flashing at the same time.
lines.zh: 到目前为止，海兹利特在公园里最喜欢的经历之一，是同步萤火虫季节的灯光秀。萤火虫布满树林，夜幕降临时，它们开始一闪一闪，这是繁殖过程的一部分。片刻之间，它们全都同时闪烁起来。

lines.en: Haizlett created an artistic workbook for children that explains how the bugs do this and why.
lines.zh: 海兹利特为孩子们制作了一本艺术练习册，解释萤火虫怎么做到这一点、为什么这样做。

lines.en: Haizlett believes that the residency program helps show the national parks in a new way that can appeal to different people.
lines.zh: 海兹利特认为，驻园项目有助于以一种新方式展示国家公园，吸引不同的人。

lines.en: "So many artists are inspired by nature, but sometimes people that aren't artists don't see their sources of inspiration as clearly. They make the art more real to people and that I think adds value to the National Parks."
lines.zh: “很多艺术家都从大自然中获得灵感，但不是艺术家的人有时看不清灵感的来源。艺术家让艺术对人们来说更真实，我觉得这为国家公园增添了价值。”

lines.en: The Great Smokey Mountains National Park is the most visited park in the U.S. It receives over 11.3 million visitors every year. Its Artist-in-Residence program is one of the largest.
lines.zh: 大雾山国家公园是美国游客最多的国家公园，每年接待 1130 多万游客。它的驻园艺术家项目也是规模最大的之一。

lines.en: Sheridan Roberts is the park's coordinator of volunteers. "Parks and the arts are both things that we need," she says. But, it can be hard to find the financial support they require. So, Sheridan adds, "we should both hold hands when we can."
lines.zh: 谢里登·罗伯茨是该公园的志愿者协调员。“公园和艺术都是我们需要的东西。”她说。但两者都很难找到所需的资金支持。所以谢里登补充说：“只要可能，我们就应该携手合作。”

lines.en: As a National Parks Service Artist-in-Residence, Haizlett also teaches at local art schools, as well as for Job Corps, a government program offering job skills training to young adults.
lines.zh: 作为国家公园管理局的驻园艺术家，海兹利特还在当地艺术学校以及“职业团”任教。“职业团”是一个为年轻人提供职业技能培训的政府项目。

lines.en: This relationship with the local art community is another important part of the A-I-R program. They partner for art projects and choosing A-I-R candidates.
lines.zh: 与当地艺术界的这种关系，是 A.I.R. 项目的另一个重要部分。他们合作开展艺术项目，并共同挑选驻园艺术家人选。

lines.en: Not all of the A.I.R. art is visual.
lines.zh: 并不是所有 A.I.R. 的艺术都是视觉艺术。

lines.en: David Huckfelt is a musician and member of the band The Pines. While his band was taking a break last September, he entered the resident artist program on Isle Royale National Park.
lines.zh: 戴维·哈克菲尔特是一位音乐人，也是乐队“松树”的成员。去年 9 月乐队休息时，他参加了罗亚尔岛国家公园的驻园艺术家项目。

lines.en: The group of islands found in Lake Superior is the least visited National Park in the states. Huckfelt seemed to enjoy that quality.
lines.zh: 这组位于苏必利尔湖中的岛屿，是美国游客最少的国家公园。哈克菲尔特似乎很享受这一点。

lines.en: "It contains pretty much all of the most necessary aspects for an artist these days: solitude, national beauty, very low expense, and the ability to really immerse yourself in the history and geography of our national parks."
lines.zh: “它几乎具备了如今一个艺术家最需要的一切：清静、国家级的美景、极低的花费，以及能真正沉浸在国家公园的历史和地理之中。”

lines.en: Huckfelt wrote 16 songs inspired by his experience at Isle Royale. He recorded them for a new album when he returned home to Minnesota. It is his first solo music project.
lines.zh: 哈克菲尔特受罗亚尔岛经历的启发，写了 16 首歌。回到明尼苏达的家后，他把这些歌录成了一张新专辑。这是他的第一个个人音乐项目。

lines.en: While at the national park he also performed concerts for visitors, and took video recordings in the park. He plans to use those recordings to create a music video for one of the new songs. He will donate the video to the park.
lines.zh: 在国家公园期间，他还为游客举办音乐会，并在园内拍摄视频。他打算用这些视频为其中一首新歌制作音乐录影带，并把它捐给公园。

lines.en: Huckfelt says it is important for people to experience the parks. After all, he said, "We own these parks…they're taxpayer funded."
lines.zh: 哈克菲尔特说，人们亲身体验公园很重要。他说，毕竟“这些公园是我们的……是纳税人出钱建的”。

lines.en: Sheridan Roberts of the Great Smokey Mountains National Park agrees.
lines.zh: 大雾山国家公园的谢里登·罗伯茨同意这个看法。

lines.en: "The national park system would not have existed today had it not been for creative visionaries," She said. "Writers, photographers, painters… it was artists and volunteers who began the movement that introduced the national park system in this country."
lines.zh: “要不是那些富有创造力的远见者，国家公园系统今天就不会存在，”她说，“作家、摄影师、画家……是艺术家和志愿者发起了这场运动，在这个国家引入了国家公园系统。”

lines.en: I'm Phil Dierking. And I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是菲尔·迪尔金。我是凯蒂·韦弗。

qs.q: What must resident artists give the park?
qs.why: "They also agree to donate at least one artwork to the park."

qs.q: Which is the most visited national park in the US?
qs.why: "The Great Smokey Mountains National Park is the most visited park in the U.S."

qs.q: What did David Huckfelt create at Isle Royale?
qs.why: "Huckfelt wrote 16 songs inspired by his experience at Isle Royale."

lessons.title: 12-Year-Old Entrepreneur Skates Into Success
lessons.zh: 12 岁的滑板小老板
lessons.sum: 加州圣克莱门特的 12 岁男孩卡森苦于滑板放不进学校储物柜，于是把回收的旧滑板改成方形小滑板，能装进背包和柜子。他不想做家务挣冲浪课的钱，就卖起了 Lockerboard，两年卖出约 700 块，每卖一块捐一美元保护海洋。

lines.en: Carson Kropfl is an inventor, business owner and environmental activist.
lines.zh: 卡森·克罗普夫尔是一位发明家、企业主和环保活动人士。

lines.en: He enjoys the excitement of surfing. In addition to riding the waves, he likes riding his skateboard. Kropfl is a very hard-working 12-year-old.
lines.zh: 他喜欢冲浪的刺激。除了冲浪，他还喜欢玩滑板。克罗普夫尔是个非常勤奋的 12 岁孩子。

lines.en: You heard right. The San Clemente, California, boy just completed seventh grade. And, school had a lot to do with the creation of his company.
lines.zh: 你没听错。这个来自加州圣克莱门特的男孩刚读完七年级。而他的公司能创办起来，和学校有很大关系。

lines.en: His story is proof that necessity is truly the mother of invention. Carson had enjoyed skating for years. He liked to use his skateboard to go to places, including school. But over time, he grew increasingly frustrated that he had no place to store his board once he arrived.
lines.zh: 他的故事证明了“需要是发明之母”。卡森玩滑板好多年了，喜欢踩着滑板去各个地方，包括上学。可是时间一长，他越来越苦恼：到了学校，滑板没地方放。

lines.en: As a student, he could not change the size of his locker. But he realized he might be able to change the shape of his skateboard. And, from that small desire, a business was born.
lines.zh: 作为学生，他没法改变储物柜的大小，但他意识到，也许可以改变滑板的形状。就这样，一个小小的愿望催生了一门生意。

lines.en: "I have a skateboard company called Lockerboard and what I do is, I take recycled skateboard decks and reshape them to fit inside of backpacks and lockers."
lines.zh: “我有一家滑板公司叫 Lockerboard（储物柜滑板）。我做的是，把回收的滑板板面重新切割成能放进背包和储物柜的形状。”

lines.en: Carson first just made a shorter skateboard in the shape of a square for himself.
lines.zh: 卡森起初只是给自己做了一块更短的方形滑板。

lines.en: "But then my parents told me I had to clean and do chores to pay for my surf contest and surf lessons. But I hate to clean, so I asked them if I could try selling my Lockerboards instead."
lines.zh: “可后来我爸妈说，我得打扫卫生、做家务来挣冲浪比赛和冲浪课的钱。可我讨厌打扫，所以我问他们，能不能改成卖我的储物柜滑板。”

lines.en: Carson's parents not only said yes, they agreed to help him make it happen. They searched around for the best tools for creating skateboards. But he says one tool made his mother a little nervous.
lines.zh: 卡森的父母不但同意了，还答应帮他实现。他们四处寻找做滑板最好的工具。不过他说，有一样工具让他妈妈有点紧张。

lines.en: "Then we used a table saw but my Mom didn't like that because I was making skateboards by myself. And my Mom was like, 'I'm not sure if this is safe,' and my Dad was like, 'its perfectly fine!' And, then a board shot back and hit him straight in the stomach..."
lines.zh: “后来我们用了台锯，可我妈不喜欢，因为我自己一个人做滑板。我妈说，‘我不确定这样安不安全’，我爸说，‘完全没问题！’结果一块板子弹回来，正好打在他肚子上……”

lines.en: Carson made his first sales in the room where students ate at his school. He put a few skateboards on a table and his schoolmates started buying them up.
lines.zh: 卡森的第一笔生意是在学校的餐厅里做成的。他在桌上摆了几块滑板，同学们就开始抢着买。

lines.en: Within months, Carson had an agreement with a manufacturer. The young man says he has now sold about 700 skateboards in under two years of operation.
lines.zh: 几个月内，卡森就和一家制造商签了协议。这个小伙子说，不到两年时间里，他已经卖出了大约 700 块滑板。

lines.en: His skateboards come in a number of shapes and designs. Each one costs around $100. But not all the profit goes to Carson. Some money goes to a non profit group that supports the health and well-being of a place close to his heart.
lines.zh: 他的滑板有好几种形状和设计，每块大约 100 美元。但利润并不全归卡森，有一部分钱捐给了一个非营利组织，这个组织守护着一个他心中珍爱的地方的健康。

lines.en: "I donate one dollar for every Lockerboard sold to Ocean Unite because they're focused on ocean conservation."
lines.zh: “每卖出一块储物柜滑板，我就给‘海洋联合’捐一美元，因为他们专注于海洋保护。”

lines.en: Carson's hometown of San Clemente sits along a beautiful coastal area of the Pacific Ocean. And Carson, the surfer, wants the ocean to stay that way.
lines.zh: 卡森的家乡圣克莱门特坐落在太平洋美丽的海岸边。作为冲浪者，卡森希望大海永远这样美丽。

lines.en: The young business owner says he is not exactly sure what he will do when he grows up. But he sure will stay busy.
lines.zh: 这位年轻的老板说，他还不太确定长大后要做什么，但他肯定会一直忙下去。

lines.en: "I kinda want to be doing what I'm doing now -- being an entrepreneur. If it's not Lockerboard, I'm pretty positive I'm going to be creating something. And, I'm going to be an activist traveling the world, supporting ocean conservation and how we could help our earth. And, traveling the world, skating and surfing, because I am an athlete."
lines.zh: “我有点想继续做我现在做的事——当一个创业者。就算不是储物柜滑板，我很确定我也会去创造点什么。我还要当一名环保活动人士，周游世界，支持海洋保护，想办法帮助我们的地球。还要周游世界去滑板、冲浪，因为我是一名运动员。”

lines.en: I'm Dorothy Gundy.
lines.zh: 我是多萝西·冈迪。

qs.q: Why did Carson make a new kind of skateboard?
opts: His skateboard did not fit in his school locker.
qs.a: His skateboard did not fit in his school locker.
qs.why: "he had no place to store his board once he arrived."

qs.q: Why did Carson start selling Lockerboards?
opts: He hates cleaning and doing chores.
qs.a: He hates cleaning and doing chores.
qs.why: "But I hate to clean, so I asked them if I could try selling my Lockerboards instead."

qs.q: What does he do with one dollar from every sale?
opts: He gives it to ocean conservation.
qs.a: He gives it to ocean conservation.
qs.why: "I donate one dollar for every Lockerboard sold to Ocean Unite."

lessons.title: 1 in 4 Americans Have Not Visited Famous US Places
lessons.zh: 四分之一的美国人没去过本地名胜
lessons.sum: 一项调查发现，25% 的美国人从没去过自己城市的标志性景点，只有三分之一去过尼亚加拉大瀑布，28% 去过大峡谷。主要原因是没钱、没时间、交通不便。美国人最想去的是大峡谷、黄石公园和自由女神像。

lines.en: A new study suggests many Americans have not visited the most popular places of interest around the country or even in their hometown.
lines.zh: 一项新研究表明，许多美国人没去过全国最受欢迎的名胜，甚至没去过自己家乡的。

lines.en: The study found that 25 percent of Americans have yet to visit "iconic landmarks" in their own cities. Twenty-three percent said they had not visited any of the nation's natural wonders, famous buildings or historic battlefields.
lines.zh: 研究发现，25% 的美国人还没去过自己城市的“标志性地标”。23% 的人说，他们从没去过国内的任何自然奇观、著名建筑或历史战场。

lines.en: The study was a project of the research service OnePoll and Zipcar, a car-sharing company.
lines.zh: 这项研究由调查机构 OnePoll 和汽车共享公司 Zipcar 共同开展。

lines.en: Researchers questioned 2,000 Americans. Only 33 percent of them said they had been to Niagara Falls and just 28 percent had been to Arizona's Grand Canyon. The study showed that only 30 percent had been to New York's Empire State Building. Only 22 percent had ever visited the National Mall in Washington, D.C.
lines.zh: 研究人员调查了 2000 名美国人。其中只有 33% 说去过尼亚加拉大瀑布，只有 28% 去过亚利桑那州的大峡谷。研究显示，只有 30% 的人去过纽约的帝国大厦，只有 22% 去过华盛顿的国家广场。

lines.en: Many Americans say they would like to travel more. More than half of those questioned said they would like to get out more. Forty-nine percent reported being "creatures of habit." By that, they mean they generally do the same things in the same way. That would leave little time to visit local or national landmarks.
lines.zh: 许多美国人说他们想多出去旅行。超过一半的受访者说想多出去走走。49% 的人说自己是“习惯的动物”，意思是他们通常用同样的方式做同样的事。这样就没什么时间去参观本地或全国的地标了。

lines.en: The researchers found that the main reasons keeping Americans from exploring their cities or the country were money, lack of time and a lack of good transportation.
lines.zh: 研究人员发现，阻碍美国人探索自己的城市或国家的主要原因是钱、缺少时间和缺少便利的交通。

lines.en: On social media, one Twitter user reacting to the study named a few reasons for not visiting famous places. The writer noted that "most of us don't get paid days off, get punished for taking a day off, or simply can't afford to visit anything or go anywhere anymore."
lines.zh: 在社交媒体上，一位推特用户回应这项研究，列举了几个没去名胜的原因。这位用户写道：“我们大多数人没有带薪假，请一天假就会受罚，或者根本负担不起去参观任何地方、去任何地方了。”

lines.en: The Twitter user added, "Childcare costs more than College, College Loans costs more than a mortgage payment, and jobs don't even pay for one of those things."
lines.zh: 这位推特用户还说：“托儿费比上大学还贵，助学贷款比房贷还多，而工作挣的钱连其中一样都付不起。”

lines.en: The study found that three of the places Americans wanted to visit were Grand Canyon National Park, Yellowstone National Park and the Statue of Liberty.
lines.zh: 研究发现，美国人想去的地方中有三个是大峡谷国家公园、黄石国家公园和自由女神像。

lines.en: The researchers also found that, on average, Americans go to a new coffee shop every five months, and a new restaurant every four months. They also spent time at a lake or near the ocean once every six months, and go to a park every five months.
lines.zh: 研究人员还发现，平均来看，美国人每五个月去一家新咖啡店，每四个月去一家新餐馆。他们每六个月去一次湖边或海边，每五个月去一次公园。

lines.en: I'm Jonathan Evans.
lines.zh: 我是乔纳森·埃文斯。

qs.q: What percent of Americans have not visited landmarks in their own cities?
qs.why: "25 percent of Americans have yet to visit 'iconic landmarks' in their own cities."

qs.q: What are the main reasons people do not explore?
qs.why: "money, lack of time and a lack of good transportation."

qs.q: What does "creature of habit" mean?
opts: someone who does the same things the same way
a person who travels a lot
qs.a: someone who does the same things the same way
qs.why: "they generally do the same things in the same way."

lessons.title: Immigrant from Laos Finds Success with Washington Restaurant
lessons.zh: 老挝移民在华盛顿开餐馆获得成功
lessons.sum: 森·卢昂拉特七岁就开始做饭，跟外婆学厨艺。1981 年她随家人逃离老挝，在泰国难民营学会了各地老挝菜，后来移民美国。2014 年她在华盛顿开了第一家老挝餐馆“糯米篮”，还获得了詹姆斯·比尔德奖提名。

lines.en: Seng Luangrath has been cooking since she was seven years old.
lines.zh: 森·卢昂拉特从七岁起就开始做饭。

lines.en: "Cooking is my passion. When I cook, I put 100 percent of my heart and soul into what I am making."
lines.zh: “做饭是我的热爱。我做饭的时候，会把百分之百的心和灵魂放进我做的东西里。”

lines.en: Seng Luangrath learned many of her skills from her grandmother in Laos.
lines.zh: 森·卢昂拉特的很多手艺是在老挝跟外婆学的。

lines.en: Now, she operates a popular restaurant in Washington, D.C. She spoke to VOA recently about her life and cooking.
lines.zh: 如今，她在华盛顿经营着一家很受欢迎的餐馆。她最近接受 VOA 采访，讲述了她的人生和烹饪。

lines.en: "My mom was too busy working. So I had to cook for my three other siblings. I remember it was a joy for me to learn, to observe whatever my grandmother will give me an assignment to do."
lines.zh: “我妈妈忙着工作，所以我得给另外三个弟弟妹妹做饭。我记得，观察学习外婆交给我的任何任务，对我来说都是一种快乐。”

lines.en: Her family fled Laos in 1981 as the country struggled with the effects of the Vietnam War. They went to Thailand, where they spent two years at a refugee camp. There she learned to prepare different kinds of food.
lines.zh: 1981 年，在老挝饱受越南战争影响之际，她的家人逃离了老挝。他们去了泰国，在难民营里待了两年。在那里，她学会了做各种不同的食物。

lines.en: "I was 12 years old. I learned how to cook from my neighbors. We have neighbors from all over Laos. So, I got myself exposed to different types of Lao cooking."
lines.zh: “我当时 12 岁。我跟邻居们学做饭。我们的邻居来自老挝各地，所以我接触到了各种不同的老挝菜。”

lines.en: Then, her family moved to the U.S. West Coast and settled in the San Francisco Bay area.
lines.zh: 后来，她的家人搬到美国西海岸，在旧金山湾区定居。

lines.en: Seng Luangrath was the oldest child. She continued to cook for the family while her parents had jobs and worked long hours.
lines.zh: 森·卢昂拉特是家里的老大。父母上班、工作时间很长，她就一直为家人做饭。

lines.en: Many years later, she has taken that experience and used it to launch the first Lao restaurant in Washington.
lines.zh: 多年以后，她利用这段经历，在华盛顿开了第一家老挝餐馆。

lines.en: Chef Seng, as she is called, opened her restaurant in 2014. At the time, Lao food was unknown in the D.C. area.
lines.zh: 人们称她“森大厨”，她在 2014 年开了这家餐馆。那时，华盛顿地区的人还不知道老挝菜。

lines.en: She started in the restaurant business by working at a Thai eatery just outside Washington. Once that business was profitable, she began to offer its customers some Lao dishes.
lines.zh: 她最初在华盛顿郊外的一家泰国餐馆工作，进入餐饮业。那家店开始赚钱后，她就开始给顾客提供一些老挝菜。

lines.en: She said few of the people who come to her restaurant know about Lao dishes or even where Laos is.
lines.zh: 她说，来她餐馆的人很少有人了解老挝菜，甚至不知道老挝在哪儿。

lines.en: So, she has to teach Americans about the food and her homeland.
lines.zh: 所以，她得给美国人讲讲老挝的食物和她的家乡。

lines.en: Lao food, or cuisine, is different from other cooking traditions in Southeast Asia. But it is also the same as the cuisine of northeastern Thailand, an area called Isan. It was once was part of Laos.
lines.zh: 老挝菜和东南亚其他烹饪传统不同，但和泰国东北部一个叫伊桑的地区的菜是一样的。伊桑曾经是老挝的一部分。

lines.en: On her website, Chef Seng says people in the Isan area speak a form of the Lao language and they eat many of the same foods, including sticky rice. She says the Lao probably eat more sticky rice than any other people in the world. It also helps explain the name of her restaurant, Thip Khao.
lines.zh: 森大厨在她的网站上说，伊桑地区的人说一种老挝语，吃很多同样的食物，包括糯米。她说，老挝人吃的糯米可能比世界上任何民族都多。这也解释了她餐馆的名字——Thip Khao。

lines.en: "Thip Khao means a basket, a vessel that hold stick rice. It's a part of Lao culture. If you go to Lao households, you're always going to see Thip Khao. It's a basket that is also meaningful for our Lao culture as well."
lines.zh: “Thip Khao 是一种篮子，一种装糯米的容器。它是老挝文化的一部分。如果你去老挝人家里，总能看到 Thip Khao。这个篮子对我们老挝文化也很有意义。”

lines.en: An important part of her success is the fresh taste of her dishes. There are some herbs and vegetables that she cannot find in stores near Washington. So she grows them at home.
lines.zh: 她成功的一个重要原因是菜肴新鲜的味道。有些香草和蔬菜在华盛顿附近的商店里买不到，所以她在家里自己种。

lines.en: She said an example of this is Kaffir lime leaves, which she adds to salads.
lines.zh: 她说，一个例子是她加在沙拉里的卡菲尔青柠叶。

lines.en: The restaurant industry also has noticed Seng's work. She said she was surprised to learn that her business was nominated as one of the 50 best new restaurants in America by the food magazine Bon Appétit. The nomination came less than one year after her eatery opened.
lines.zh: 餐饮业也注意到了森的成就。她说，得知自己的餐馆被美食杂志《好胃口》提名为全美 50 家最佳新餐馆之一时，她很惊讶。那时她的餐馆开张还不到一年。

lines.en: And this year, Seng was nominated as a Best Chef – Mid-Atlantic semifinalist for a restaurant industry award: the James Beard Award. She also was nominated last year.
lines.zh: 今年，森被提名为餐饮业大奖“詹姆斯·比尔德奖”中大西洋地区最佳厨师半决赛候选人。去年她也获得了提名。

lines.en: However, the biggest award, Seng said, is doing what she loves. She said cooking makes her happy and is an important part of her life.
lines.zh: 不过森说，最大的奖励是做自己热爱的事。她说，做饭让她快乐，是她生活中重要的一部分。

lines.en: I'm Mario Ritter.
lines.zh: 我是马里奥·里特。

qs.q: Who taught Seng Luangrath to cook?
qs.why: "Seng Luangrath learned many of her skills from her grandmother in Laos."

qs.q: What does "Thip Khao" mean?
opts: a basket that holds sticky rice
qs.a: a basket that holds sticky rice
qs.why: "Thip Khao means a basket, a vessel that hold stick rice."

qs.q: Why does she grow some herbs at home?
opts: She cannot find them in stores near Washington.
qs.a: She cannot find them in stores near Washington.
qs.why: "There are some herbs and vegetables that she cannot find in stores near Washington."

lessons.title: Washington's Bike Party Wheels Keep Rolling
lessons.zh: 华盛顿的自行车派对
lessons.sum: 每个月，几百名骑手在华盛顿杜邦圆环集合，穿着花哨的服装在夜色中骑车穿城，音响自行车一路放音乐，中途停在公园跳舞交友。这个全由志愿者组织的“自行车派对”让人感到：这座城市不只有西装领带。

lines.en: It is 10:30 on a warm May night in Washington, D.C. Emily Skeels and a few friends are outside talking and laughing. One friend plays music from a wireless device.
lines.zh: 华盛顿，五月一个温暖的夜晚，10 点 30 分。埃米莉·斯基尔斯和几个朋友在户外说说笑笑，一个朋友用无线设备放着音乐。

lines.en: Skeels and friends have just finished a bicycle ride around the city on an event called D.C. Bike Party.
lines.zh: 斯基尔斯和朋友们刚刚参加完一场叫“华盛顿自行车派对”的活动，骑车绕城一圈。

lines.en: Each month, hundreds of cyclists take to the city's streets for this highly imaginative group ride. They meet at Dupont Circle and roll onto the road in colorful clothing as the sun sets. Event volunteers lead the adventure.
lines.zh: 每个月，几百名骑手涌上城市街头，参加这场充满想象力的集体骑行。他们在杜邦圆环集合，穿着色彩鲜艳的衣服，在日落时分骑上马路。活动志愿者在前面带路。

lines.en: Skeels, who has lived in D.C. for many years, tells VOA what she likes about Bike Party.
lines.zh: 斯基尔斯在华盛顿住了很多年，她向 VOA 讲述了自己喜欢“自行车派对”的地方。

lines.en: "I love bikes and I love biking on streets without traffic and all of my friends go and the weather's really nice right now."
lines.zh: “我爱自行车，爱在没有车流的街上骑车，我的朋友们都去，而且现在天气很好。”

lines.en: Technically, there is traffic, but the huge group finds safety in numbers. And that's not all they find.
lines.zh: 严格来说，路上还是有车的，但这么一大群人，人多就安全。他们找到的还不止安全。

lines.en: The name "Bike Party" is just right, since this is more of a celebration on wheels than a usual cycling event.
lines.zh: “自行车派对”这个名字恰如其分，因为这与其说是一场普通的骑行活动，不如说是一场车轮上的庆典。

lines.en: For one, it happens at night. And, there's music – lots of it. For example, longtime event volunteer Danny Lesh brings along his "sound bike" – a bicycle with an oversized speaker system attached.
lines.zh: 首先，它在晚上举行。还有音乐——很多很多音乐。比如，长期参与的志愿者丹尼·莱什会带上他的“音响自行车”——一辆装着超大音响系统的自行车。

lines.en: Lesh built the system in 2012. He says he "had a good feeling that great music" could build a following for a community bike ride in DC. He was right.
lines.zh: 莱什在 2012 年组装了这套系统。他说他“有种感觉，好音乐”能让华盛顿的社区骑行吸引一批追随者。他说对了。

lines.en: Each month, he makes music playlists that fit with the event themes. Tonight, Lesh played funk music for the event's Photon Funk Ride, in honor of the city's yearly Funk Parade.
lines.zh: 每个月，他都会制作符合活动主题的音乐歌单。今晚，莱什为活动的“光子放克骑行”播放放克音乐，向这座城市一年一度的放克游行致敬。

lines.en: And then there are the costumes. Many riders dress in creative, brightly colored clothing to go with the themes. In October, for example, they dress up for Halloween.
lines.zh: 还有服装。许多骑手穿上配合主题、富有创意、色彩鲜艳的衣服。比如十月，他们会装扮起来过万圣节。

lines.en: Washington, D.C. native Will Bien Duggan seriously regrets missing one Halloween ride a few years ago. It was a rainy, cold night. But, Bike Party still went on. The event led cyclists to a party with live music at the Congressional Cemetery.
lines.zh: 华盛顿本地人威尔·比安·达根非常后悔几年前错过了一次万圣节骑行。那天晚上又冷又下雨，可自行车派对照常进行，活动把骑手们带到了国会公墓的一场有现场音乐的派对上。

lines.en: "I saw the video of everyone coming into it and it was just something otherworldly and I realized that only in D.C. and only with Bike Party could you ever have that kind of experience."
lines.zh: “我看了大家骑进去的视频，那简直如梦似幻。我意识到，只有在华盛顿、只有和自行车派对一起，才可能有那样的体验。”

lines.en: Along with exciting themes, music and clothing, the party ride also brings out some very inventive bicycles.
lines.zh: 除了精彩的主题、音乐和服装，派对骑行还带来了一些非常有创意的自行车。

lines.en: Event founder Lia Seremetis, a California native, says the creativity of the riders is always wonderful. Over the years, she has seen all kinds of bikes on Bike Party, including a penny-farthing and a one-wheeled vehicle called a unicycle.
lines.zh: 活动创始人、加州人莉娅·塞雷梅蒂斯说，骑手们的创造力总是令人惊叹。多年来，她在自行车派对上见过各种各样的车，包括前轮巨大的“高轮自行车”和一种叫独轮车的单轮车。

lines.en: In addition, every month, she says, a group of people on rollerblades take part and bring their own disco ball.
lines.zh: 她说，另外，每个月都有一群穿直排轮滑鞋的人参加，还带着他们自己的迪斯科球。

lines.en: "So, it just…never ends. People are truly amazing."
lines.zh: “所以，它就是……没完没了。人们真的太了不起了。”

lines.en: Some that take part in Bike Party do not use any wheels at all, says Los Angeles native and dog lover, Marla Larrave. She was excited to see a four-legged participant on a recent ride.
lines.zh: 洛杉矶人、爱狗人士玛拉·拉拉韦说，有些参加自行车派对的人根本不用轮子。她在最近一次骑行中看到一位四条腿的参与者，很兴奋。

lines.en: "And, there was a dog -- a little dog that was running the whole time alongside all the cyclists with his human. That was super cute."
lines.zh: “有一只狗——一只小狗，一直跟着主人在骑手们旁边跑。超级可爱。”

lines.en: Larrave met Skeels through Bike Party and says the event is her favorite thing to do in DC.
lines.zh: 拉拉韦是通过自行车派对认识斯基尔斯的。她说这个活动是她在华盛顿最喜欢做的事。

lines.en: "You know, I've got friends that I've made at Bike Party and then their friends become my friends too."
lines.zh: “你知道吗，我在自行车派对上交了朋友，然后他们的朋友也成了我的朋友。”

lines.en: About halfway through every Bike Party, riders stop at a park. They set down their bicycles and talk, laugh, make new friends, eat, drink, listen to music. And, of course, they dance.
lines.zh: 每次自行车派对骑到一半左右，骑手们会在一个公园停下来。他们放下自行车，聊天、说笑、交新朋友、吃喝、听音乐。当然，还要跳舞。

lines.en: Larrave loves the musicality. She says last month's ride took the group to a park filled with Japanese cherry trees.
lines.zh: 拉拉韦很喜欢这里的音乐氛围。她说上个月的骑行把大家带到了一个种满日本樱花树的公园。

lines.en: "It was just beautiful riding through the park and seeing all those trees."
lines.zh: “骑车穿过公园、看着那些树，真是太美了。”

lines.en: Then, Brazilian music began to play and people danced by the trees.
lines.zh: 接着，巴西音乐响起，人们在树旁跳起了舞。

lines.en: Seremetis was sad to leave behind the big group bikes rides from her hometown of San Jose, California. So, in 2012, two years after she moved to D.C., she started the D.C. Bike Party.
lines.zh: 塞雷梅蒂斯离开家乡加州圣何塞时，很舍不得那里的大型集体骑行。所以 2012 年，她搬到华盛顿两年后，创办了华盛顿自行车派对。

lines.en: She says, as free-spirited as the ride is, event volunteers work hard to make sure it operates smoothly each month. It is all volunteer-organized. About 30 people put the event together to make sure it is safe and responsible.
lines.zh: 她说，尽管这个骑行活动自由奔放，活动志愿者每个月都努力确保它顺利进行。活动完全由志愿者组织，大约 30 个人一起筹办，确保它安全、负责任。

lines.en: "I like to say that we take having fun very seriously."
lines.zh: “我喜欢说，我们非常认真地对待玩乐这件事。”

lines.en: Bien Duggan says there is a special connectedness among those in the bicycle community around the world. A few years ago, he spent 14 months on a bicycle tour through South America. On many nights, cyclists opened their homes for him to stay the night.
lines.zh: 比安·达根说，世界各地的自行车爱好者之间有一种特别的联系。几年前，他骑车在南美洲旅行了 14 个月。很多个晚上，当地骑手都敞开家门让他留宿。

lines.en: Bien Duggan says he feels a similar sense of unity on rides with the Bike Party.
lines.zh: 比安·达根说，他在自行车派对的骑行中也感受到类似的团结。

lines.en: He says it offers "...a sense of community and a good reminder that the whole city isn't just suit-and-tie and that's a really great feeling."
lines.zh: 他说，它带来了“……一种社区感，也很好地提醒我们，整座城市并不只有西装领带，那感觉真的很棒”。

lines.en: I'm Alice Bryant.
lines.zh: 我是艾丽斯·布莱恩特。

qs.q: Where do the Bike Party riders meet?
qs.why: "They meet at Dupont Circle."

qs.q: What is a "sound bike"?
opts: a bicycle with a big speaker system
qs.a: a bicycle with a big speaker system
qs.why: "a bicycle with an oversized speaker system attached."

qs.q: Who organizes the event?
qs.why: "It is all volunteer-organized."

gloss: 超凡脱俗的，如梦似幻的
西装领带（指严肃的上班族）

lessons.title: US Museum Shows History of Teeth and Dentist Tools
lessons.zh: 美国牙科博物馆：牙齿与牙医工具的历史
lessons.sum: 巴尔的摩的国家牙科博物馆收藏 4 万多件藏品：早期牙医诊所、像刑具一样的老工具、维多利亚女王牙医的金珍珠器械，还有华盛顿总统的假牙——它们不是木头做的，而是动物骨头做的。

lines.en: Most people do not look forward to going to the dentist. But they might actually enjoy visiting an American museum that explores the history of teeth and dentistry.
lines.zh: 大多数人都不期待去看牙医。但他们也许会喜欢参观一座探索牙齿和牙科历史的美国博物馆。

lines.en: The Dr. Samuel D. Harris National Museum of Dentistry is at the University of Maryland in Baltimore. It was the world's first college to train dentists. A man named G.V. Black was one of the founders of modern U.S. dentistry in the 1800s.
lines.zh: 塞缪尔·D·哈里斯博士国家牙科博物馆位于巴尔的摩的马里兰大学。马里兰大学是世界上第一所培养牙医的学院。一位叫 G.V. 布莱克的人是 19 世纪美国现代牙科的奠基人之一。

lines.en: Visitors to the museum can look at a reproduction of Black's dentist office. When he treated patients, he had no electricity for light. So his office, like many others, had large windows. Chairs for patients often faced south to help dentists work by sunlight.
lines.zh: 博物馆的参观者可以看到布莱克牙科诊所的复原场景。他给病人治疗时没有电灯照明，所以他的诊所和其他许多诊所一样有大窗户。病人的椅子通常朝南，帮助牙医借着阳光工作。

lines.en: Patrick Cutter is a researcher at the museum.
lines.zh: 帕特里克·卡特是这家博物馆的研究员。

lines.en: "What we're looking at here is kind of an early idea of what a dentist office would have looked like. But most of the time a dentist would have actually just been a traveling dentist, so he would have went from town square to town square."
lines.zh: “我们在这里看到的，大致是早期牙医诊所的样子。不过大多数时候，牙医其实是流动的，他会从一个镇广场走到另一个镇广场。”

lines.en: With more than 40,000 items, the museum contains one of the largest dental collections in the world. Visitors can see some of the tools used by early dentists to work on patients. Some of the old equipment looks more like torture devices than dental instruments.
lines.zh: 博物馆有 4 万多件藏品，是世界上最大的牙科收藏之一。参观者可以看到早期牙医给病人治牙用的一些工具。有些老设备看起来更像刑具，而不是牙科器械。

lines.en: Others shown seem fit for kings and queens. For example, Queen Victoria's dentist used instruments made of gold and pearls.
lines.zh: 另一些展品似乎配得上国王和王后。比如，维多利亚女王的牙医用的器械是用金子和珍珠做的。

lines.en: The museum shows many examples of false teeth, along with explanations about the kinds of materials used to make them.
lines.zh: 博物馆展出了许多假牙，并介绍了制作假牙用的各种材料。

lines.en: One of the most popular areas shows a set of false teeth once worn by America's first president, George Washington. But the museum corrects a widely believed story that Washington's false teeth were wooden. They were actually made of animal bone.
lines.zh: 最受欢迎的展区之一，展出了美国第一任总统乔治·华盛顿戴过的一副假牙。不过博物馆纠正了一个流传很广的说法：华盛顿的假牙是木头做的。其实它们是用动物骨头做的。

lines.en: Historians believe the false teeth made it difficult for Washington to eat and speak. They say this is likely why his second inaugural speech contained just 135 words – the shortest in history.
lines.zh: 历史学家认为，假牙让华盛顿吃饭、说话都很困难。他们说，这可能就是为什么他的第二次就职演说只有 135 个词——历史上最短的一次。

lines.en: Some early tools used to clean teeth were also made from animal parts, the museum's Patrick Cutter explains.
lines.zh: 博物馆的帕特里克·卡特解释说，一些早期清洁牙齿的工具也是用动物身体的部位做的。

lines.en: "Some of the older toothbrushes that were actually made out of animal bone."
lines.zh: “一些比较老的牙刷其实是用动物骨头做的。”

lines.en: The cleaning end of the brushes often came from the hair of cows or other animals. The museum also shows teeth from a mix of animals and notes how they are different from human teeth.
lines.zh: 牙刷的刷毛常常来自牛或其他动物的毛。博物馆还展出了各种动物的牙齿，并说明它们和人类牙齿有什么不同。

lines.en: In addition, visitors can explore how teeth have long been used to solve mysteries and crimes. And, they can see the history of tooth replacement and learn about new technology that could grow replacement teeth.
lines.zh: 此外，参观者还可以了解牙齿长期以来如何被用来破解谜团和案件。他们还可以看到补牙、换牙的历史，了解一种可能让人长出新牙的新技术。

lines.en: One part of the museum, called Mouthpower, contains large toothbrushes and mouths. The models show how bacteria can damage the teeth and let people practice cleaning methods.
lines.zh: 博物馆有一个叫“口腔力量”的展区，有巨大的牙刷和嘴巴模型。这些模型展示了细菌如何损坏牙齿，还让人练习清洁牙齿的方法。

lines.en: While visitors to this unusual museum might at times feel like they are in a dentist office, the experience is sure to be a lot more pleasant.
lines.zh: 虽然来这座不寻常博物馆的参观者有时会觉得像在牙医诊所里，但这段体验肯定愉快得多。

qs.q: What were George Washington's false teeth made of?
qs.why: "They were actually made of animal bone."

qs.q: Why did early dentist chairs face south?
qs.why: "Chairs for patients often faced south to help dentists work by sunlight."

qs.q: Why might Washington's second inaugural speech be so short?
opts: His false teeth made speaking difficult.
qs.a: His false teeth made speaking difficult.
qs.why: "the false teeth made it difficult for Washington to eat and speak."

lessons.title: Americans Go Crazy for Ramps in the Spring
lessons.zh: 美国人春天为野韭葱疯狂
lessons.sum: 野韭葱（ramps）是北美东部山区的一种野生植物，味道像大蒜和洋葱，每年春天只长几周。它在阿巴拉契亚山区有悠久历史，如今成了纽约、华盛顿高档餐馆的抢手货，过度采挖也让它面临消失的危险。

lines.en: The spring season brings warm weather, flowers and other changes for people to enjoy.
lines.zh: 春天带来了温暖的天气、鲜花，还有其他让人享受的变化。

lines.en: For some restaurant chefs, the most exciting spring arrival is ramps.
lines.zh: 对一些餐馆厨师来说，春天最令人兴奋的到来是野韭葱（ramps）。

lines.en: Every spring, restaurants across the United States compete to be the first to offer the seasonal vegetable.
lines.zh: 每年春天，全美各地的餐馆都争着第一个推出这种时令蔬菜。

lines.en: The excitement has even created a ramps black market in Canada.
lines.zh: 这股热潮甚至在加拿大催生了一个野韭葱黑市。

lines.en: So, what is the great appeal of ramps? Maybe you have never even heard of them.
lines.zh: 那么，野韭葱到底有什么魅力？也许你都没听说过它。

lines.en: Ramps, or allium tricoccum, are a wild plant native to the eastern mountains of North America. They are one of the first plants that grow in the spring, usually between April and May. They are part of the same family as leeks and shallots. They are recognized by their red stem, and two long and broad green leaves.
lines.zh: 野韭葱，学名 allium tricoccum，是一种原产于北美东部山区的野生植物。它是春天最早长出来的植物之一，通常在四五月间。它和韭葱、红葱头同属一科，特征是红色的茎和两片又长又宽的绿叶。

lines.en: They are also famous for their strong taste, similar to garlic, and other onions.
lines.zh: 它也以浓烈的味道出名，类似大蒜和其他洋葱。

lines.en: Ramps are not as well-known as other vegetables, but they have a long history in the United States.
lines.zh: 野韭葱不如其他蔬菜那么有名，但它在美国有着悠久的历史。

lines.en: In the Appalachian Mountains, ramps have been an important food for a long time. During spring, it is common for small towns in the Appalachian area to hold large ramp dinners for the community.
lines.zh: 在阿巴拉契亚山区，野韭葱长期以来都是一种重要的食物。春天，阿巴拉契亚地区的小镇常常为社区举办盛大的野韭葱晚宴。

lines.en: David Townsend owns the Mountain Roots Market and Restaurant, in Weston, West Virginia. He uses ramps every year, spending as much as a couple thousand dollars buying the plants.
lines.zh: 戴维·汤森在西弗吉尼亚州韦斯顿经营“山根市场和餐馆”。他每年都用野韭葱，花在买这种植物上的钱多达几千美元。

lines.en: Townsend told us he uses the vegetable in many ways. At his restaurant, for example, he might make ramp burgers. He also likes to mix ramps with potatoes and egg dishes. And he dries them for seasonings.
lines.zh: 汤森告诉我们，他用这种蔬菜做很多菜。比如在他的餐馆里，他可能做野韭葱汉堡。他还喜欢把野韭葱和土豆、鸡蛋菜混在一起，还会把它晒干做调料。

lines.en: Townsend says you can also enjoy ramps fried, pickled, and even raw.
lines.zh: 汤森说，野韭葱也可以炸着吃、腌着吃，甚至生吃。

lines.en: However, others might not enjoy the effect of ramps on your breath.
lines.zh: 不过，别人可能不喜欢野韭葱对你口气的影响。

lines.en: Townsend says, "The joke was that if you eat raw ramps, and you go to school, you would get kicked out of school because you stink."
lines.zh: 汤森说：“有个笑话说，如果你吃了生野韭葱去上学，你会被赶出学校，因为你太臭了。”

lines.en: One reason the plant is popular is that it grows in the wild.
lines.zh: 这种植物受欢迎的一个原因是它长在野外。

lines.en: It is difficult to grow ramp crops on farms. Most restaurants get their supply from foragers. They are people who gather ramps by searching forests for patches, areas where they grow.
lines.zh: 在农场里种野韭葱很难。大多数餐馆的货源来自“采集者”，也就是在森林里搜寻野韭葱生长的地块来采挖的人。

lines.en: Townsend said the competitive market for the plant means that when someone finds a patch, they do not tell others where it is.
lines.zh: 汤森说，这种植物的市场竞争激烈，所以有人找到一片野韭葱时，不会告诉别人在哪里。

lines.en: In the past, ramps were mostly eaten in small towns in the areas where they grew. However, over the last 10 years, ramps' popularity has grown quickly. They are now a highly-desired vegetable for many nice restaurants in cities like New York and Washington D.C.
lines.zh: 过去，野韭葱主要在它生长地区的小镇上被人吃。但在过去 10 年里，野韭葱的人气迅速上升。如今它是纽约、华盛顿这类城市许多高档餐馆极想要的蔬菜。

lines.en: Adam Harvey is the chef at Little Coco's, an Italian restaurant in Washington D.C. He has been using ramps on his pizzas for about the last 10 years.
lines.zh: 亚当·哈维是华盛顿意大利餐馆 Little Coco's 的主厨。过去大约 10 年里，他一直在比萨上用野韭葱。

lines.en: When spring comes, Harvey says, chefs around the country get excited for the arrival of the plant. They try to prepare it in as many ways as possible, and try to include as many choices as possible.
lines.zh: 哈维说，春天一到，全国的厨师都为这种植物的到来而兴奋。他们想方设法用尽可能多的方式做它，尽量在菜单上多加几道。

lines.en: "It's one of those things where people go a little crazy," Harvey said. He adds that the popularity of ramps in nicer restaurants is a combination of several things.
lines.zh: “这种东西会让人有点疯狂。”哈维说。他补充说，野韭葱在高档餐馆受欢迎，是几个因素共同作用的结果。

lines.en: "First, it has a really great flavor that is very individual… and second, it's wild. It has such a short season, and you can't get them all the time." Harvey said.
lines.zh: “第一，它的味道真的很棒，很独特……第二，它是野生的。它的季节太短了，不是什么时候都能买到。”哈维说。

lines.en: Harvey also noted that many chefs want to keep their restaurant offerings seasonal. Ramps are the first "green thing" to grow after the winter, he said, so cooks feel a pull to use them.
lines.zh: 哈维还指出，很多厨师希望菜单保持时令性。他说，野韭葱是冬天过后最早长出来的“绿色东西”，所以厨师们很想用它。

lines.en: Harvey said that his favorite way to cook ramps is to pickle the bulb, or bottom of the plant.
lines.zh: 哈维说，他最喜欢的做法是把鳞茎——也就是植物的底部——腌起来。

lines.en: Ramps have a short season. Within a few weeks of full growth, the plant is done for the year. This short life cycle is partly responsible for their popularity. And that popularity could lead to their disappearance from Earth.
lines.zh: 野韭葱的季节很短。完全长成几周之内，它这一年的生长就结束了。这么短的生命周期是它受欢迎的部分原因。而这种受欢迎可能导致它从地球上消失。

lines.en: Townsend said, "A lot of the public places where ramps are [grown]… have been over-dug… because of the amount of money that a person can make off them." He added that people who sell ramps to restaurants in New York can sometimes make as much as $20 for half a kilogram.
lines.zh: 汤森说：“很多公共场所里长野韭葱的地方……都被挖得太过了……因为靠它能赚很多钱。”他补充说，把野韭葱卖给纽约餐馆的人，有时半公斤能卖到 20 美元。

lines.en: "In two-to-three months, you can make two-to-three thousand dollars," he said.
lines.zh: “两三个月里，你就能赚两三千美元。”他说。

lines.en: Townsend also said that not everyone who forages for ramps obeys the guidelines for protecting future growth.
lines.zh: 汤森还说，并不是每个采野韭葱的人都遵守保护未来生长的规定。

lines.en: Foragers are supposed to leave some ramps in the ground to re-populate the area for the next season. But, Townsend says, some foragers still dig up the entire patch.
lines.zh: 采集者本应在地里留下一些野韭葱，让它们下一季能重新长满这片地。但汤森说，有些采集者还是把整片都挖光了。

lines.en: In the province of Quebec, Canada, ramps are called "wild garlic." In 1995, the provincial government declared the plant a "vulnerable species" from over-harvesting. They also banned selling the plant to businesses.
lines.zh: 在加拿大魁北克省，野韭葱被称为“野蒜”。1995 年，省政府因为过度采集宣布它为“易危物种”，还禁止向商家出售这种植物。

lines.en: However, the demand for the plant has caused people to illegally harvest the plant in the neighboring province of Ontario. Canadian police deploy officers in the woods to watch for the illegal activity.
lines.zh: 然而，对这种植物的需求导致有人在邻近的安大略省非法采挖。加拿大警方派警员进入树林，监视这种非法活动。

lines.en: The season is short, but it has not ended yet. If you are in the right place, you still have time to try a taste of ramps yourself.
lines.zh: 季节很短，但还没结束。如果你在对的地方，还有时间亲自尝尝野韭葱的味道。

lines.en: I'm ­­­­­­­­­­­­­Phil Dierking.
lines.zh: 我是菲尔·迪尔金。

lines.en: And I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。

qs.q: What do ramps taste like?
qs.why: "their strong taste, similar to garlic, and other onions."

qs.q: Where do most restaurants get their ramps?
opts: from foragers who find them in forests
qs.a: from foragers who find them in forests
qs.why: "Most restaurants get their supply from foragers."

qs.q: Why did Quebec ban selling ramps to businesses?
qs.why: "declared the plant a 'vulnerable species' from over-harvesting."

lessons.title: Horses, Hats and Roses: The Kentucky Derby
lessons.zh: 马、帽子和玫瑰：肯塔基赛马会
lessons.sum: 肯塔基赛马会被称为“体育界最激动人心的两分钟”，是美国“三冠王”赛马系列的第一站。它既是体育赛事，也是文化盛会：观众盛装出席，女士们戴上夸张的帽子，冠军马披上红玫瑰，人们喝着薄荷朱利普酒。

lines.en: The most famous horse races in America begin on May 5 with the running of the 144th Kentucky Derby. It is the first of a three part championship series. The other two races are the Preakness in Maryland and the Belmont Stakes in New York.
lines.zh: 美国最著名的赛马比赛将于 5 月 5 日开始，届时将举行第 144 届肯塔基赛马会。这是三场冠军系列赛的第一场，另外两场是马里兰州的普瑞克尼斯锦标赛和纽约州的贝尔蒙特锦标赛。

lines.en: Win all three races and your horse is named a Triple Crown champion. It does not happen often. Only 12 horses have won the Triple Crown of Thoroughbred Racing. The first was Sir Barton in 1919. The most recent, almost 100 years later, was 2015 champion American Pharoah.
lines.zh: 三场全赢，你的马就被称为“三冠王”。这种事不常发生。只有 12 匹马赢得过纯种马赛的三冠王。第一匹是 1919 年的“巴顿爵士”，最近一匹是近 100 年后的 2015 年冠军“美国法老”。
