lines.en: The Kentucky Derby, in the southern city of Louisville, is the youngest of the three races. It is arguably the most famous horse race in the world. It is often called the "most exciting two minutes in sports."
lines.zh: 肯塔基赛马会在南方城市路易斯维尔举行，是三场比赛中历史最短的。它可以说是世界上最著名的赛马比赛，常被称为“体育界最激动人心的两分钟”。

lines.en: Millions of dollars are wagered on the Derby. And great wealth can be gained from breeding Derby winners.
lines.zh: 人们在肯塔基赛马会上下注几百万美元。培育赛马会冠军马也能带来巨额财富。

lines.en: Kentucky Derby competitors are three years old. They run for two kilometers around the Churchill Downs racetrack in Louisville. Derby runners can be male or female horses. Only males have ever won, so far.
lines.zh: 肯塔基赛马会的参赛马都是三岁。它们绕路易斯维尔的丘吉尔唐斯赛道跑两公里。参赛马可以是公马也可以是母马，不过到目前为止只有公马赢过。

lines.en: The famous Triple Crown winner Secretariat finished the Kentucky Derby faster than any horse, before or after him. His time in the 1973 race was 1 minute, 59.4 seconds. Only one other competitor has run the Derby in under two minutes. That horse, Monarchos, won the race in 2001. But, he did not break Secretariat's record.
lines.zh: 著名的三冠王“秘书处”跑完肯塔基赛马会的速度，比它之前和之后的任何一匹马都快。它在 1973 年比赛中的成绩是 1 分 59.4 秒。只有另一匹参赛马跑进过两分钟，那就是 2001 年的冠军“君主”，但它没能打破秘书处的纪录。

lines.en: Horse lovers, gamblers, the rich and the famous gather at Churchill Downs for the Kentucky Derby. It is as much a cultural celebration as it is a sporting event. And that celebration requires some preparation on the part of those attending.
lines.zh: 爱马人士、赌徒、富人和名人齐聚丘吉尔唐斯观看肯塔基赛马会。它既是一项体育赛事，也是一场文化庆典。而这场庆典需要参加者做些准备。

lines.en: The Kentucky Derby is outside. The race can get very dirty, with the horses kicking up mud and dust as they speed around the track. But, observers are expected to look their best. Many men wear suits. Many women wear beautiful spring dresses.
lines.zh: 肯塔基赛马会在户外举行。比赛可能会很脏，马在赛道上飞奔时会扬起泥土和灰尘。但观众要打扮得光鲜亮丽。很多男士穿西装，很多女士穿漂亮的春装。

lines.en: However, the critical piece of clothing goes on top of your head.
lines.zh: 不过，最关键的一件服饰是戴在头上的。

lines.en: Hats are almost a requirement at the Kentucky Derby. They come in all sizes, shapes and colors at the race. Women's hat styles vary greatly. They can include flowers, feathers, ribbons, jewels and more. You might even see a hat or two larger than the heads they top.
lines.zh: 在肯塔基赛马会上，帽子几乎是必需的。赛场上的帽子大小、形状、颜色各异。女士帽子的款式千变万化，可以装饰鲜花、羽毛、缎带、珠宝等等。你甚至可能看到一两顶比戴它的脑袋还大的帽子。

lines.en: The owners of the winning horse receive more than $1 million. More importantly, people will pay a lot of money to breed their horses with a Kentucky Derby winner.
lines.zh: 冠军马的主人会得到 100 多万美元。更重要的是，人们会花大价钱让自己的马和肯塔基赛马会冠军配种。

lines.en: And the horse? It gets flowers. As soon as the race is over, a spread of red roses is hung over the winning animal's neck. The tradition began in 1896. The red rose became the official Derby flower in 1904. And, about twenty years after that, the Kentucky Derby came to be known as the "Run for the Roses."
lines.zh: 那马呢？它得到的是花。比赛一结束，一大片红玫瑰就会挂在冠军马的脖子上。这个传统始于 1896 年，红玫瑰在 1904 年成为赛马会的官方用花。大约二十年后，肯塔基赛马会就有了“玫瑰之赛”的称号。

lines.en: Kentucky is famous for making the alcohol called bourbon. And Kentucky bourbon is the base of a famous Derby drink: the mint julep. It is served in a metal container to keep it very cold. It contains bourbon, sugar, mint leaves and ice.
lines.zh: 肯塔基以酿造一种叫波本的酒而闻名。肯塔基波本酒是一种著名的赛马会饮品——薄荷朱利普——的基酒。它盛在金属杯里，保持冰凉，由波本酒、糖、薄荷叶和冰块调成。

lines.en: The Kentucky Derby's official website says more than 120,000 mint juleps will be sold at Churchill Downs during the Derby weekend.
lines.zh: 肯塔基赛马会官网说，赛马会周末期间，丘吉尔唐斯将售出 12 万多杯薄荷朱利普。

lines.en: I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。

qs.q: What is the Kentucky Derby often called?
opts: "the most exciting two minutes in sports"
qs.a: "the most exciting two minutes in sports"
qs.why: "It is often called the 'most exciting two minutes in sports.'"

qs.q: What does the winning horse get?
qs.why: "a spread of red roses is hung over the winning animal's neck."

qs.q: What is almost a requirement for people at the Derby?
qs.why: "Hats are almost a requirement at the Kentucky Derby."

lessons.title: DC's National Arboretum: A Quieter Place for Cherry Blossoms
lessons.zh: 国家树木园：华盛顿赏樱的清静去处
lessons.sum: 每年春天一百多万人涌向潮汐湖赏樱，而 8 公里外的美国国家树木园清静得多。这里有 1000 多棵樱花树，科学家们培育杂交新品种，还克隆了 1912 年日本赠送的原始樱花树。

lines.en: Each year at the start of spring, more than 1 million people travel to Washington, D.C., for one major reason: the cherry blossoms.
lines.zh: 每年春天一开始，就有一百多万人为了一个主要原因来到华盛顿：樱花。

lines.en: Most of the travelers visit an area known as the Tidal Basin. During "peak bloom," the Tidal Basin is bursting with color. It is also bursting with people.
lines.zh: 大多数游客去一个叫潮汐湖的地方。“盛花期”时，潮汐湖色彩缤纷，也人山人海。

lines.en: But there is another, quieter way to enjoy Washington's cherry blossoms.
lines.zh: 不过，还有另一种更清静的方式欣赏华盛顿的樱花。

lines.en: About eight kilometers across town, you will find the United States National Arboretum, a huge public garden and research collection.
lines.zh: 在城市另一头大约八公里外，你会找到美国国家树木园，一座巨大的公共花园和研究收藏机构。

lines.en: The United States Congress established the Arboretum in 1927. Its aim is to use research and conservation to improve the appearance and environmental and economic value of plants.
lines.zh: 美国国会于 1927 年建立了国家树木园，目的是通过研究和保护，提升植物的观赏价值以及环境和经济价值。

lines.en: Cherry tree research is one of the Arboretum's specialties, says Margaret Pooler. She is the director of research. She and her team work on developing a larger base of cherry trees.
lines.zh: 研究主任玛格丽特·普勒说，樱花树研究是树木园的专长之一。她和团队致力于培育更多樱花树品种。

lines.en: "Most people know the Yoshino Cherries, they know the Kwanzan Cherries, the familiar one that you see down at the Tidal Basin. But what a lot of people don't realize is that there's so many other species that we can use to broaden the base of the cultivated plants that we see. So, that's what we're trying to do."
lines.zh: “大多数人知道染井吉野樱，知道关山樱，就是你在潮汐湖看到的那些熟悉的品种。但很多人没意识到，还有很多其他品种可以用来拓宽我们看到的栽培植物的基础。我们就是在做这件事。”

lines.en: Today, the Arboretum has more than 1,000 different cherry trees. Some are short and wide. Others grow tall. A few are "weeping" trees. Their long, flowering branches hang down near the ground.
lines.zh: 如今，树木园有 1000 多棵不同的樱花树。有的又矮又宽，有的长得很高，还有几棵是“垂枝”樱，开满花的长枝条垂到地面附近。

lines.en: Pooler showed VOA Learning English around the Arboretum's research field. In late March and early April, this wide, open space comes to life with flowering cherry trees. Some produce bright white blooms. Others are different shades of pink.
lines.zh: 普勒带 VOA 慢速英语参观了树木园的研究园地。三月底四月初，这片宽阔的空地因樱花盛开而充满生机。有的开出亮白的花，有的是深浅不同的粉色。

lines.en: Many of them are new species of cherry trees developed by Arboretum scientists themselves. They are "hybrid" cherry trees, Pooler explains.
lines.zh: 普勒解释说，其中许多是树木园科学家自己培育的樱花新品种，它们是“杂交”樱花树。

lines.en: "In our research program, we create hybrids. That is, we take pollen from one plant and put it on another plant to combine the best traits from both of those. And so, most of the plants here in our research field are various hybrids of that kind that we've created."
lines.zh: “在我们的研究项目中，我们培育杂交品种。也就是把一种植物的花粉授到另一种植物上，把两者最好的特性结合起来。所以我们研究园地里的大多数植物，都是我们培育的各种杂交品种。”

lines.en: Most of the hybrids are known only by number. But scientists have given some of hybrids names, such as Dream Catcher and First Lady. One cherry hybrid is called Helen Taft, in honor of the wife of former U.S. President William Howard Taft. She played an important role in bringing cherry trees to America.
lines.zh: 大多数杂交品种只有编号，但科学家给其中一些起了名字，比如“捕梦网”和“第一夫人”。有一种杂交樱叫“海伦·塔夫脱”，纪念美国前总统威廉·霍华德·塔夫脱的夫人，她在把樱花树引进美国方面发挥了重要作用。

lines.en: "The really, really good ones, those are the ones that we end up naming and we release to...the public to then grow and produce."
lines.zh: “真正、真正好的品种，我们最后会给它们命名，发布给……公众去种植和培育。”

lines.en: Pooler has worked on cherry trees at the Arboretum for more than 20 years. She lists two "weeping" trees as among her favorites there.
lines.zh: 普勒在树木园研究樱花树已经 20 多年了。她说那里有两棵“垂枝”樱是她的最爱。

lines.en: "I like them because they're just huge. I mean, they're just awesome trees. But I like them also because they tend to not bloom very long. When they're in bloom, they're just spectacular."
lines.zh: “我喜欢它们，因为它们太大了。我是说，它们真是令人惊叹的树。我喜欢它们也因为它们的花期往往不长。开花的时候，简直壮观极了。”

lines.en: The Arboretum has a self-guided tour of its cherry trees. People can use a small book to learn about the different species. The book describes about 35 kinds of cherries.
lines.zh: 树木园有樱花树自助游览路线。人们可以用一本小册子了解不同的品种，册子介绍了大约 35 种樱花。

lines.en: Among them are genetic matches of a few of the original trees that were planted at the Tidal Basin back in 1912. The trees were a gift to the United States from Japan.
lines.zh: 其中有几棵和 1912 年种在潮汐湖的原始樱花树基因相同。那些树是日本送给美国的礼物。

lines.en: "Very few of those original plants still exist there. We got involved with the National Park Service a few years ago to help propagate, or clone, some of those original plants. So we have some of those planted here."
lines.zh: “那些原始的樱花树现在还剩下很少。几年前，我们和国家公园管理局合作，帮助繁殖——也就是克隆——一些原始樱花树。所以我们这里也种了一些。”

lines.en: Antonio and Marlen are from Spain and now live in the state of Maryland. They visited the Arboretum with their two young children and had a picnic near one of the flowering trees. The family had gone to the Tidal Basin earlier that day to see the cherry blossoms, as well.
lines.zh: 安东尼奥和玛伦来自西班牙，现在住在马里兰州。他们带着两个年幼的孩子来到树木园，在一棵开花的树旁野餐。这家人那天早些时候也去潮汐湖看过樱花。

lines.en: "Here you see nature around, which is like, better...I prefer Arboretum than [to] Tidal Basin."
lines.zh: “在这里你能看到周围的大自然，感觉更好……比起潮汐湖，我更喜欢树木园。”

lines.en: Emily Kowalksi and Elisabeth Seburg had just arrived to Washington from Minnesota. They came straight from the airport to the Arboretum to see the cherry trees, Kowalski said.
lines.zh: 埃米莉·科瓦尔斯基和伊丽莎白·塞伯格刚从明尼苏达来到华盛顿。科瓦尔斯基说，她们一下飞机就直奔树木园来看樱花。

lines.en: "There's this one we just kind of walked up on and from afar, just the view from afar you can't even take a picture of it because it's just something you have to take in with your own eyes."
lines.zh: “有一棵我们刚走过去，从远处看——远处的景色你都没法拍照，因为那是你必须用自己的眼睛去欣赏的东西。”

lines.en: Whether at the Arboretum, Tidal Basin or elsewhere, cherry blossoms are a special part of life in America's capital. Along with being beautiful to look at, the trees are something Washingtonians can "count on" every year, Pooler says.
lines.zh: 无论是在树木园、潮汐湖还是别处，樱花都是美国首都生活中特别的一部分。普勒说，这些树不仅好看，还是华盛顿人每年都能“指望”的东西。

lines.en: "Even when the spring is late or drawn out or cold, or even when winter is freezing cold and our temperatures are terrible, we know, no matter what happens…even [when] things are happening in Washington politically…it doesn't matter. These cherries are going to bloom every year. We can totally count on them."
lines.zh: “就算春天来得晚、拖得长、天气冷，就算冬天冷得要命、气温很糟，我们知道，不管发生什么……就算华盛顿政坛风云变幻……都没关系。这些樱花每年都会开。我们完全可以指望它们。”

lines.en: I'm Ashley Thompson.
lines.zh: 我是阿什莉·汤普森。

qs.q: How many different cherry trees does the Arboretum have?
qs.why: "the Arboretum has more than 1,000 different cherry trees."

qs.q: What is a hybrid cherry tree?
opts: a tree that combines the best traits of two plants
qs.a: a tree that combines the best traits of two plants
qs.why: "we take pollen from one plant and put it on another plant to combine the best traits."

qs.q: Why do Antonio and Marlen prefer the Arboretum?
opts: They can see nature around them.
It is closer to the airport.
qs.a: They can see nature around them.
qs.why: "Here you see nature around, which is like, better."

gloss: 相配的东西；（genetic match）基因相同的

lessons.title: Everyone Gets to be Irish on Saint Patrick's Day
lessons.zh: 圣帕特里克节：人人都是爱尔兰人
lessons.sum: 3 月 17 日是爱尔兰的圣帕特里克节，最初是纪念把基督教带到爱尔兰的圣人的宗教节日。如今全世界都在庆祝：游行、绿色灯光、染绿的河水。绿啤酒、咸牛肉配卷心菜这些习俗其实是美国的爱尔兰人发明的。

lines.en: On March 17, people around the world celebrate the Irish holiday of Saint Patrick's Day.
lines.zh: 3 月 17 日，世界各地的人们都在庆祝爱尔兰节日——圣帕特里克节。

lines.en: It is a major holiday in Ireland, but the rest of the world has influenced its celebration as much as the Irish themselves.
lines.zh: 这是爱尔兰的一个重要节日，但世界其他地方对它庆祝方式的影响，和爱尔兰人自己一样大。

lines.en: Most Americans think of Saint Patrick's Day as a big party centered around drinking alcohol. But its beginnings in Ireland were religious, says Mike Cronin, a professor of Irish history with Boston College of Massachusetts.
lines.zh: 大多数美国人把圣帕特里克节看作一个以喝酒为中心的大派对。但马萨诸塞州波士顿学院的爱尔兰历史教授迈克·克罗宁说，这个节日在爱尔兰起源时是宗教性的。

lines.en: Ireland is a mostly Roman Catholic country. Saint Patrick lived in Ireland more than 2,000 years ago. He is widely considered to have established Christianity in the country.
lines.zh: 爱尔兰是一个以罗马天主教为主的国家。圣帕特里克生活在很久以前的爱尔兰（原文说“两千多年前”，史学界一般认为是公元 5 世纪）。人们普遍认为是他在这个国家确立了基督教。

lines.en: The Church honored him with a holy day in the 17th century. March 17 marks the date of his death.
lines.zh: 17 世纪，教会设立了一个圣日来纪念他。3 月 17 日是他去世的日子。

lines.en: St. Patrick, a Briton reportedly, is believed to have served in Ireland as a Catholic Bishop. One traditional story says that St. Patrick drove all the snakes out of Ireland.
lines.zh: 据说圣帕特里克是个不列颠人，在爱尔兰担任天主教主教。一个传统故事说，圣帕特里克把所有的蛇都赶出了爱尔兰。

lines.en: The average Irish person honored March 17 quietly. Attending church services was the main activity. In fact, most businesses that served alcohol would close in honor of the day.
lines.zh: 普通爱尔兰人过 3 月 17 日都很安静，主要活动是去教堂做礼拜。事实上，大多数卖酒的店铺都会为这一天关门。

lines.en: In the early 1900s, Ireland's government made St. Patrick's Day an official holiday. By the 1960s, towns across Ireland started celebrating the holiday with parades and music. In Ireland today,
lines.zh: 20 世纪初，爱尔兰政府把圣帕特里克节定为法定假日。到 20 世纪 60 年代，爱尔兰各地的城镇开始用游行和音乐庆祝这个节日。如今在爱尔兰，

lines.en: St. Patrick's Day is a four-day public celebration that includes parades, music, food, and games.
lines.zh: 圣帕特里克节是为期四天的公共庆典，有游行、音乐、美食和游戏。

lines.en: For Irish people living outside Ireland, Saint Patrick's Day became a chance to celebrate their Irish identity and culture.
lines.zh: 对住在爱尔兰以外的爱尔兰人来说，圣帕特里克节成了庆祝自己爱尔兰身份和文化的机会。

lines.en: "It's very much a day by which the Irish put themselves center stage," Cronin said.
lines.zh: “这确实是爱尔兰人让自己站上舞台中央的一天。”克罗宁说。

lines.en: Now, countries and cities around the world celebrate March 17 in creative ways.
lines.zh: 如今，世界各地的国家和城市都以富有创意的方式庆祝 3 月 17 日。

lines.en: Many countries hold Saint Patrick's Day parades. Famous monuments, including the Great Wall of China, the Colosseum in Rome, the Niagara Falls, and the Gateway of India in Mumbai will all be colored by green light for the day.
lines.zh: 许多国家举行圣帕特里克节游行。中国的长城、罗马斗兽场、尼亚加拉大瀑布、孟买的印度门等著名地标都会在这一天被绿色灯光照亮。

lines.en: The U.S. is especially famous for its Saint Patrick's Day celebrations. Many cities with large ethnic Irish communities, like Boston, New York and Chicago, hold parades and parties. Cities will also color local rivers green for the day.
lines.zh: 美国的圣帕特里克节庆祝活动尤其有名。波士顿、纽约、芝加哥等许多有大量爱尔兰裔社区的城市都会举行游行和派对。有的城市还会在这一天把当地的河水染成绿色。

lines.en: Ireland is known as the Emerald Isle. The country is covered in deep green grass.
lines.zh: 爱尔兰被称为“翡翠岛”，整个国家覆盖着深绿色的草地。

lines.en: Cronin says that the worldwide popularity of Saint Patrick's Day has helped the Irish government, which uses the holiday as a form of diplomacy.
lines.zh: 克罗宁说，圣帕特里克节在全世界的流行帮助了爱尔兰政府，政府把这个节日当作一种外交手段。

lines.en: "So what you have is this quite remarkable day where literally over much of the globe, everybody, whether they're Irish or not, the one thing they do know is the 17th of March is Saint Patrick's Day. And for a small island of 4.5 to 5 million people it's quite remarkable that they have that kind of soft power."
lines.zh: “所以这是非常了不起的一天：几乎在全球大部分地方，每个人，不管是不是爱尔兰人，他们都知道一件事，那就是 3 月 17 日是圣帕特里克节。对一个只有四五百万人口的小岛来说，拥有这样的软实力是非常了不起的。”

lines.en: However, Cronin says many modern Saint Patrick's Day traditions were invented by the Irish in America.
lines.zh: 不过克罗宁说，很多现代的圣帕特里克节传统是美国的爱尔兰人发明的。

lines.en: In the U.S. on Saint Patrick's Day, it is common for Americans to drink green beer or eat corned beef and cabbage.
lines.zh: 在美国，圣帕特里克节喝绿色啤酒、吃咸牛肉配卷心菜是很常见的。

lines.en: However, Cronin, says, many of these traditions are not really Irish.
lines.zh: 可是克罗宁说，这些传统中有很多其实并不是爱尔兰的。

lines.en: "You could walk around the streets of Dublin all day and not find any corned beef and cabbage," he said.
lines.zh: “你可以在都柏林街头走上一整天，也找不到一份咸牛肉配卷心菜。”他说。

lines.en: Neil O'Flaherty, an Irish citizen now living in the U.S., agrees.
lines.zh: 现在住在美国的爱尔兰公民尼尔·奥弗莱厄蒂也同意这一点。

lines.en: Growing up in a small town in Ireland, O'Flaherty remembers celebrating Saint Patrick's Day much differently than it is now.
lines.zh: 奥弗莱厄蒂在爱尔兰一个小镇长大。他记得那时过圣帕特里克节和现在很不一样。

lines.en: "Back then, for Catholic families, it was the day you had to go to church, you were required to go to Mass on that day. It had much more the feeling of a religious holiday than a public holiday."
lines.zh: “那时候，对天主教家庭来说，这是必须去教堂的日子，那天你必须去做弥撒。它更像一个宗教节日，而不是公共假日。”

lines.en: He also remembers everyone wearing small, three-leaf plant pieces, called shamrocks.
lines.zh: 他还记得每个人都戴着一小片三叶植物，叫三叶草。

lines.en: O'Flaherty said that he was surprised to see how much Saint Patrick's Day in the U.S. has become linked to drinking lots of beer or other alcoholic drinks.
lines.zh: 奥弗莱厄蒂说，看到美国的圣帕特里克节和大量喝啤酒或其他酒联系得这么紧密，他很惊讶。

lines.en: However, there are some Irish connections between drinking and Saint Patrick's Day.
lines.zh: 不过，喝酒和圣帕特里克节之间也确实有一些爱尔兰渊源。

lines.en: One tradition that does come from Ireland is called "drowning the shamrock." Cronin explains that this tradition involved taking the shamrock that people wore all day, and placing it in a glass of whiskey or beer before drinking it.
lines.zh: 有一个确实来自爱尔兰的传统叫“淹三叶草”。克罗宁解释说，这个传统是把人们戴了一整天的三叶草放进一杯威士忌或啤酒里，然后把酒喝掉。

lines.en: Professor Mike Cronin suggests it is not that important how people celebrate March 17. He calls Saint Patrick's Day "a day for everyone to be Irish."
lines.zh: 迈克·克罗宁教授认为，人们怎样庆祝 3 月 17 日并不那么重要。他称圣帕特里克节是“人人都能当爱尔兰人的一天”。

lines.en: I'm Kelly Jean Kelly.
lines.zh: 我是凯莉·琼·凯莉。

lines.en: And I'm Phil Dierking.
lines.zh: 我是菲尔·迪尔金。

qs.q: Why is March 17 Saint Patrick's Day?
opts: It marks the date of his death.
It is the first day of spring.
qs.a: It marks the date of his death.
qs.why: "March 17 marks the date of his death."

qs.q: Which tradition is not really Irish?
qs.why: "You could walk around the streets of Dublin all day and not find any corned beef and cabbage."

qs.q: What is "drowning the shamrock"?
opts: putting a shamrock in a drink before drinking it
throwing a shamrock in a river
qs.a: putting a shamrock in a drink before drinking it
qs.why: "placing it in a glass of whiskey or beer before drinking it."

lessons.title: Valentine's Day Is for Love
lessons.zh: 情人节：为爱而过
lessons.sum: 2 月 14 日情人节是庆祝爱情的日子，人们互送鲜花、糖果和贺卡，很多人选在这天订婚、结婚。它可能源于古罗马的牧神节，也和一位违抗皇帝禁婚令、秘密为恋人证婚的圣瓦伦丁有关。

lines.en: Valentine's Day celebrates love. It is a day to exchange flowers, candy, and greeting cards with your husband or wife, or someone else you desire. It is a popular day to become engaged and to get married.
lines.zh: 情人节是庆祝爱情的日子。在这一天，人们和丈夫、妻子或心仪的人互送鲜花、糖果和贺卡。这也是订婚和结婚的热门日子。

lines.en: Historians argue about the earliest roots of Valentine's Day. Many say it is linked to the ancient Roman festival of Lupercalia, which was observed on the 15th of February. That day celebrated the coming of spring and female fertility.
lines.zh: 历史学家对情人节最早的起源有争论。很多人说它和古罗马的牧神节有关，牧神节在 2 月 15 日，庆祝春天的到来和女性的生育能力。

lines.en: Then, around 1,500 years ago, Christians supposedly began to celebrate the feast day of St. Valentine on February 14.
lines.zh: 后来，大约 1500 年前，据说基督徒开始在 2 月 14 日庆祝圣瓦伦丁的纪念日。

lines.en: However, there are several Saint Valentines and several stories about them. One involves Valentine of Terni, a Christian clergyman. He was said to have violated the orders of Roman Emperor Claudius the 2nd.
lines.zh: 不过，叫圣瓦伦丁的圣人有好几位，关于他们的故事也有好几个。其中一个讲的是特尔尼的瓦伦丁，一位基督教神职人员。据说他违抗了罗马皇帝克劳狄二世的命令。

lines.en: Claudius was having trouble getting married men to serve as soldiers. So, he banned marriage. Valentine considered the ban immoral and secretly married young Christian lovers, anyway. When the Emperor learned of the actions, he ordered Valentine's death. The execution is said to have happened on February 14, around the year 300.
lines.zh: 克劳狄很难让已婚男子去当兵，于是他禁止结婚。瓦伦丁认为这个禁令不道德，还是偷偷为年轻的基督徒恋人主持婚礼。皇帝得知后，下令处死瓦伦丁。据说行刑发生在大约公元 300 年的 2 月 14 日。

lines.en: Some people say this is the reason the holiday is linked to love.
lines.zh: 有人说，这就是这个节日和爱情联系在一起的原因。

lines.en: The exchange of valentines, or written expressions of love, began in the 1500s. The tradition remains popular today. Valentine cards usually include images of hearts, flowers, or Cupid, the Roman god of love and desire. The cards also often include poems. One valentine from the year 1910 reads: "When we meet: The flowers look brighter, And all on earth seems sweet, My heart is always lighter, My darling, when we meet."
lines.zh: 互送 valentine——也就是写下的爱意表达——的习俗始于 16 世纪，至今仍很流行。情人节卡片上通常画着爱心、鲜花或丘比特——罗马神话中爱与欲望之神。卡片上也常有诗。一张 1910 年的情人节卡片上写着：“当我们相见：花儿更加鲜艳，人间万物都显得甜蜜，我的心总是更加轻快，我的爱人，当我们相见。”

lines.en: But Valentine's Day is not only for romance. It can also be a day to celebrate love of family and friends.
lines.zh: 不过，情人节不只属于浪漫。它也可以是庆祝亲情和友情的日子。

lines.en: I'm Dorothy Gundy.
lines.zh: 我是多萝西·冈迪。

qs.q: What do people exchange on Valentine's Day?
qs.why: "exchange flowers, candy, and greeting cards."

qs.q: Why did Emperor Claudius ban marriage?
opts: He had trouble getting married men to be soldiers.
qs.a: He had trouble getting married men to be soldiers.
qs.why: "Claudius was having trouble getting married men to serve as soldiers."

qs.q: Who is Cupid?
qs.why: "Cupid, the Roman god of love and desire."

lessons.title: Christmas Attractions Across America
lessons.zh: 美国各地的圣诞景点
lessons.sum: 纽约洛克菲勒中心的巨型圣诞树和第五大道橱窗，巴尔的摩 34 街的灯饰，新奥尔良橡树林的灯光节和午夜大餐，阿拉斯加“北极镇”的冰雕，印第安纳波利斯赛道上的灯展，洛杉矶的墨西哥“波萨达”游行，以及大峡谷的“极地特快”列车。

lines.en: Cities all across the United States are dressing up for the Christmas season with trees, lights and holiday magic. Today, we look at a few of them.
lines.zh: 美国各地的城市都用圣诞树、彩灯和节日魔法装扮起来，迎接圣诞季。今天我们来看看其中几个。

lines.en: In New York City, one of the best-known holiday attractions is Rockefeller Center's Christmas tree in Manhattan. The tree is lit during a public ceremony in late November. The city has displayed a large Christmas tree here since 1933. This year's tree is 23 meters tall and covered with 50,000 lights. A Swarovski crystal sits on top.
lines.zh: 在纽约市，最有名的节日景点之一是曼哈顿洛克菲勒中心的圣诞树。11 月底会举行公开的点灯仪式。自 1933 年起，纽约每年都在这里摆放一棵巨大的圣诞树。今年的树高 23 米，挂着 5 万盏灯，树顶是一颗施华洛世奇水晶星。

lines.en: Ornate window displays are another New York Christmas tradition. Large department stores along the famous shopping area of Fifth Avenue create imaginative displays during the holiday season.
lines.zh: 华丽的橱窗展示是纽约的另一个圣诞传统。著名购物区第五大道上的大百货公司，会在节日期间推出充满想象力的橱窗。

lines.en: Stores choose different themes every year. This year, for example, Saks Fifth Avenue's windows celebrate the 80th anniversary of the Disney film "Snow White and the Seven Dwarves." Another famed department store, Bergdorf Goodman, celebrates New York's diverse museums and cultural sites, such as the Philharmonic and the New York Historical Society.
lines.zh: 商店每年选择不同的主题。比如今年，萨克斯第五大道百货的橱窗庆祝迪士尼电影《白雪公主和七个小矮人》上映 80 周年。另一家著名百货公司波道夫·古德曼则展示纽约多样的博物馆和文化场所，比如纽约爱乐乐团和纽约历史学会。

lines.en: The Fifth Avenue windows are so popular that police use long ropes to set up controlled lines for the window viewing.
lines.zh: 第五大道的橱窗太受欢迎了，警察要用长绳子拉起排队通道，有序引导人们观看。

lines.en: Miracle on 34th Street is a well-known and beloved American Christmas movie. And there is actually a real Miracle on 34th Street – in Baltimore, Maryland.
lines.zh: 《34 街的奇迹》是一部有名的、深受喜爱的美国圣诞电影。而现实中真有一个“34 街的奇迹”——在马里兰州巴尔的摩。

lines.en: Every year, Baltimore residents along a block of 34th street put up an almost blindingly bright display of Christmas lights and decorations. Thousands of people visit the block to see the bright and colorful display of Christmas cheer, now in its 71st year.
lines.zh: 每年，巴尔的摩 34 街一个街区的居民都会挂起几乎亮得晃眼的圣诞彩灯和装饰。成千上万的人来这个街区观看这场色彩缤纷的圣诞欢乐展示，今年已是第 71 年。

lines.en: The event opened with an official lighting ceremony on November 25 and will continue through the holidays.
lines.zh: 活动在 11 月 25 日以正式的点灯仪式开幕，将持续整个节日期间。

lines.en: Every December, City Park in New Orleans, Louisiana, becomes a winter wonderland. It features more than 10 hectares of light displays, it's famous old oak trees wrapped in thousands of twinkling lights. More than 165,000 people visit the so-called Celebration in the Oaks each year.
lines.zh: 每年 12 月，路易斯安那州新奥尔良的城市公园都会变成冬季仙境。园内有 10 多公顷的灯光展，著名的古老橡树上缠满了成千上万闪烁的彩灯。每年有 16.5 万多人来参观这个所谓的“橡树林庆典”。

lines.en: New Orleans also celebrates its French Creole connection each holiday season with Reveillon dinners. Reveillon comes from the French word for "awakening." The 19th-century French Creole tradition began as a large meal eaten after midnight mass on Christmas Eve. The "reveillon" tradition is still alive in New Orleans' French Quarter. Restaurants there offer special Reveillon meals that include oysters and other seafood, meat, soup, dessert and more.
lines.zh: 每到节日季，新奥尔良还会用“雷韦永”晚餐来庆祝它与法国克里奥尔文化的渊源。Reveillon 来自法语“觉醒”一词。这个 19 世纪的法国克里奥尔传统，起初是平安夜午夜弥撒后吃的一顿大餐。这个传统在新奥尔良的法国区仍然盛行，那里的餐馆供应特别的雷韦永大餐，有牡蛎和其他海鲜、肉、汤、甜点等等。

lines.en: The icy North Pole is said to be the home of Santa Claus. So it is no surprise that the small Alaskan town with the same name is home to the world's largest Santa statue. It stands in front of Santa Claus House, the center of the town's Christmas activities.
lines.zh: 据说冰天雪地的北极是圣诞老人的家。所以，阿拉斯加一个同名的小镇（North Pole）拥有世界上最大的圣诞老人雕像，也就不奇怪了。雕像立在“圣诞老人之家”前面，这里是小镇圣诞活动的中心。

lines.en: While the town displays Christmas decorations all year round, it really comes alive in December. The North Pole Christmas in Ice contest brings ice artists from around the world to the town of 2,000 people. Visitors can slide down frozen slides and work their way through complex ice mazes.
lines.zh: 这个小镇一年四季都挂着圣诞装饰，但到了 12 月才真正热闹起来。“北极冰雕圣诞”比赛把世界各地的冰雕艺术家吸引到这个 2000 人的小镇。游客可以从冰滑梯上滑下来，在复杂的冰迷宫里穿行。

lines.en: The central U.S. city of Indianapolis, Indiana is famous for its yearly Indy 500 automobile race.
lines.zh: 美国中部城市印第安纳州印第安纳波利斯以一年一度的印第安纳波利斯 500 英里汽车赛出名。

lines.en: During the winter holiday season, the world-famous race track fills up with more than two million Christmas lights, 500 light displays and 40 holiday scenes. Visitors are permitted to drive their own cars on the speedway.
lines.zh: 冬季节日期间，这条世界闻名的赛道上挂满了 200 多万盏圣诞彩灯，有 500 个灯光展和 40 个节日场景。游客可以开着自己的车在赛道上行驶。

lines.en: A traditional Mexican festival takes place in Los Angeles, California. The nine-day Las Posadas celebration is one of the city's oldest Christmas events. Las Posadas can be found on Olvera Street, considered the first street of the city.
lines.zh: 一个传统的墨西哥节日在加州洛杉矶举行。为期九天的“波萨达”庆典是这座城市最古老的圣诞活动之一，在被认为是洛杉矶第一条街的奥尔韦拉街举行。

lines.en: The celebration commemorates the story of Mary and Joseph traveling from Nazareth to Bethlehem to prepare for Jesus' birth.
lines.zh: 这个庆典纪念的是玛丽亚和约瑟从拿撒勒前往伯利恒、准备迎接耶稣诞生的故事。

lines.en: Celebrations are held nightly from December 16 through December 24. The events include a candlelight parade. Children clothed to look like shepherds, angels, and Mary and Joseph lead the march, followed by worshipers. The public can also join the parade or just watch from the side. The group sings songs in English and Spanish as they walk.
lines.zh: 从 12 月 16 日到 24 日，每晚都有庆祝活动，包括烛光游行。打扮成牧羊人、天使以及玛丽亚和约瑟的孩子们走在队伍前面，后面跟着信众。公众也可以加入游行，或者在路边观看。队伍边走边用英语和西班牙语唱歌。

lines.en: "Posada" means "inn" or "shelter" in Spanish. During the parade, the marchers stop at stores along Olvera Street that pretend to be inns. They ask the business owners for shelter. The stores usually deny the request, often in song. Finally, one will say yes, and the marchers are admitted. Free hot drinks and sweet bread are served.
lines.zh: “Posada”在西班牙语里是“客栈”或“住处”的意思。游行时，队伍会在奥尔韦拉街上假扮成客栈的商店前停下，请店主让他们借宿。店主通常会拒绝，而且常常是用唱歌的方式。最后会有一家同意，队伍就被请进去。店里免费供应热饮和甜面包。

lines.en: Many scenic railways around the country offer train rides that center on Santa Claus and Christmas. In Arizona, the Grand Canyon Railway brings to life the classic children's book "Polar Express," written by Chris Van Allsburg. The train sets off from Williams, Arizona and travels for 90 minutes until it arrives at "Santa's Village," where Santa and his elves welcome the passengers. Santa and his helpers ride the train back to Williams with the children. Each child receives one a small bell as a gift.
lines.zh: 全国许多观光铁路都推出以圣诞老人和圣诞节为主题的火车之旅。在亚利桑那州，大峡谷铁路把克里斯·范·奥尔斯伯格的经典童书《极地特快》变成了现实。火车从亚利桑那州威廉斯出发，行驶 90 分钟后到达“圣诞老人村”，圣诞老人和小精灵们在那里欢迎乘客。圣诞老人和他的助手们会和孩子们一起坐火车回威廉斯，每个孩子都会得到一个小铃铛作为礼物。

lines.en: Does your city, town or village do something special for the holiday season?
lines.zh: 你所在的城市、小镇或村庄在节日季有什么特别的活动吗？

lines.en: I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。

lines.en: And I'm Ashley Thompson.
lines.zh: 我是阿什莉·汤普森。

qs.q: How tall is this year's Rockefeller Center tree?
qs.why: "This year's tree is 23 meters tall."

qs.q: What does "posada" mean in Spanish?
qs.why: "'Posada' means 'inn' or 'shelter' in Spanish."

qs.q: Where is the world's largest Santa statue?
qs.why: "the small Alaskan town with the same name is home to the world's largest Santa statue."

lessons.title: Santas Sharpen Their Skills at Michigan School
lessons.zh: 密歇根的圣诞老人学校
lessons.sum: 密歇根州米德兰的 CW 霍华德圣诞老人学校创办于 1937 年，是世界上历史最长的圣诞老人学校。每年有 250 多位“圣诞老人”来这里学习手语、驯鹿知识、化妆、接受采访，甚至报税。他们从不承诺孩子任何事，只说“尽力而为”。

lines.en: As soon as the Thanksgiving holiday is over, Santa Clauses start appearing everywhere – in shopping centers, supermarkets and other places.
lines.zh: 感恩节一过，圣诞老人就开始到处出现——在购物中心、超市和其他地方。

lines.en: It takes more than red clothing and a white beard to be a professional Santa. In fact, many aspiring Santas attend special classes.
lines.zh: 要成为职业圣诞老人，光有红衣服和白胡子可不够。事实上，许多想当圣诞老人的人都会去上专门的课程。

lines.en: The CW Howard Santa School is in Midland, Michigan. It is the longest continuously running Santa Claus School in the world. This year, it is celebrating its 80th anniversary.
lines.zh: CW 霍华德圣诞老人学校位于密歇根州米德兰，是世界上连续开办时间最长的圣诞老人学校。今年是它成立 80 周年。

lines.en: VOA recently visited the school.
lines.zh: VOA 最近走访了这所学校。

lines.en: More than 250 Santas have gathered at the school to prepare for their seasonal work. Charlie W. Howard was the Santa Claus in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade for 17 years. He started the school in 1937. Tom Valent is the school's current leader.
lines.zh: 250 多位圣诞老人聚集在学校，为季节性工作做准备。查理·W·霍华德曾连续 17 年在梅西百货感恩节大游行中扮演圣诞老人，他在 1937 年创办了这所学校。汤姆·瓦伦特是学校现任负责人。

lines.en: "At that time, there was a great need for good Santas, better Santas. Santas didn't portray the image that we want. Santa Claus stands for all good things and some of the gentlemen that were portraying that image weren't up to par then."
lines.zh: “那时候非常需要好的圣诞老人、更好的圣诞老人。当时的圣诞老人没有表现出我们想要的形象。圣诞老人代表一切美好的事物，而当时一些扮演这个形象的先生们并不达标。”

lines.en: The three-day Santa workshop teaches people "Santa sign language," facts about reindeer and clothing and make-up style. The future Santas also learn about the newest wish list toys, gain interview experience for radio and television and even get advice on how to do their business taxes.
lines.zh: 为期三天的圣诞老人培训班教人们“圣诞老人手语”、驯鹿知识、服装和化妆风格。未来的圣诞老人们还会了解最新的愿望清单玩具，获得接受电台和电视采访的经验，甚至得到如何为自己的生意报税的建议。

lines.en: Robert Davis has played Santa for 30 years. He has attended the school several times.
lines.zh: 罗伯特·戴维斯扮演圣诞老人已经 30 年了，他来过这所学校好几次。

lines.en: "I think no matter how good you are at whatever you choose to do, you can always be better. And not only does the school teach you so much, but when you interact with 250 fellow people who love the same thing you do, you learn something new every year."
lines.zh: “我认为，不管你选择做什么、做得多好，总能做得更好。学校不仅教你很多东西，而且和 250 位跟你热爱同样事情的人交流，每年你都会学到新东西。”

lines.en: The student Santas' headquarters is the Santa House. Tom Valent designed the house in 1986 to look like those made of gingerbread, a Christmas tradition.
lines.zh: 学员圣诞老人的大本营是“圣诞老人之家”。汤姆·瓦伦特在 1986 年设计了这座房子，让它看起来像姜饼屋——一种圣诞传统。

lines.en: Conservative estimates suggest 15,000 students have graduated from the Santa School. They come from all over North America, Europe, Africa, and Australia to study. This year, the school welcomed Santas from all 50 states as well as Canada, Denmark, New Zealand and Norway.
lines.zh: 保守估计，已有 1.5 万名学员从圣诞老人学校毕业。他们来自北美、欧洲、非洲和澳大利亚各地。今年，学校迎来了来自全美 50 个州以及加拿大、丹麦、新西兰和挪威的圣诞老人。

lines.en: Fred Ostaer is the only Norwegian Santa at the school this year. He is known as Oslo Santa. It is his eighth time at the school.
lines.zh: 弗雷德·奥斯塔尔是今年学校里唯一的挪威圣诞老人，人称“奥斯陆圣诞老人”。这是他第八次来这所学校。

lines.en: "I have been Santa this Christmas 65 years. I started to be a Santa when I was 12."
lines.zh: “到今年圣诞节，我当圣诞老人已经 65 年了。我 12 岁就开始当圣诞老人。”

lines.en: The Santas never claim to be the one and only "real" Santa. Instead they describe themselves as "the spirit of Christmas." At the school's opening-night activity, Santa Walk, they tell visiting children they are the "cousins of Santa."
lines.zh: 这些圣诞老人从不声称自己是唯一的“真”圣诞老人，而是称自己为“圣诞精神”。在学校开幕夜的“圣诞老人漫步”活动上，他们告诉来访的孩子们，自己是“圣诞老人的表兄弟”。

lines.en: Robert Davis says they also never promise children anything. Instead they say they will "try their best."
lines.zh: 罗伯特·戴维斯说，他们也从不向孩子们承诺任何事，而是说会“尽力而为”。

lines.en: "Anywhere I go, I try to make my contact and exchange with that child the very best that it can be because that could be that child's best five minutes of the year."
lines.zh: “不管我去哪儿，我都努力让我和孩子的接触和交流做到最好，因为那可能是那个孩子一年里最美好的五分钟。”

lines.en: After all, as founder Charles W. Howard liked to say, "He errs who thinks Santa enters through the chimney. Santa enters through the heart."
lines.zh: 毕竟，正如创始人查尔斯·W·霍华德常说的：“以为圣诞老人从烟囱进来的人错了。圣诞老人是从心里进来的。”

lines.en: I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。

qs.q: When did the Santa school start?
qs.why: "He started the school in 1937."

qs.q: What do these Santas call themselves?
qs.why: "they describe themselves as 'the spirit of Christmas.'"

qs.q: What do the Santas say instead of making promises?
qs.why: "Instead they say they will 'try their best.'"

lessons.title: What Is the History of the Presidential Turkey Pardon?
lessons.zh: 总统“赦免”火鸡的由来
lessons.sum: 每年感恩节前，美国总统都会在白宫“赦免”一只火鸡，让它免于上餐桌。关于起源说法很多：林肯的儿子泰德救下了宠物火鸡，杜鲁门被误认为是开创者，而第一位正式赦免火鸡的是肯尼迪总统。

lines.en: Every year, at a ceremony at the White House, the American president "pardons" a turkey.
lines.zh: 每年，美国总统都会在白宫的一个仪式上“赦免”一只火鸡。

lines.en: Instead of becoming part of a Thanksgiving dinner in the United States, the bird's life is saved.
lines.zh: 这只火鸡不会成为美国感恩节晚餐的一部分，它的命保住了。

lines.en: Stories on the origins of the presidential turkey "pardon" are numerous. Some of these stories date back to the presidency of Abraham Lincoln during the U.S. Civil War.
lines.zh: 关于总统赦免火鸡的起源，说法有很多。有些可以追溯到南北战争时期亚伯拉罕·林肯任总统的时候。

lines.en: Edward Lengel is the chief historian of the White House Historical Association.
lines.zh: 爱德华·伦格尔是白宫历史协会的首席历史学家。

lines.en: "He (the president) had a son named Ted, who joked with Abraham Lincoln about his pet turkey that he had, who was strolling around the voting booths in 1864. And Abraham Lincoln asked why he was strolling around. Is he (the turkey) here to vote?"
lines.zh: “他（总统）有个儿子叫泰德，泰德跟林肯开玩笑说起他的宠物火鸡，1864 年那只火鸡在投票站周围闲逛。林肯问它为什么在那儿闲逛，难道它（火鸡）是来投票的吗？”

lines.en: The boy answered that his turkey could not vote because he was too young.
lines.zh: 男孩回答说，他的火鸡不能投票，因为它年纪太小了。

lines.en: "Therefore," Lengel said, "Abraham Lincoln pardoned his turkey and forgave him the possibility of being killed for the Thanksgiving table."
lines.zh: “所以，”伦格尔说，“林肯赦免了他的火鸡，免得它被宰了端上感恩节餐桌。”

lines.en: Some people say a later president, Harry Truman, was the originator of the modern-day turkey pardon. But the Truman Library and Museum disputes this claim.
lines.zh: 有人说后来的哈里·杜鲁门总统是现代火鸡赦免仪式的首创者，但杜鲁门图书馆和博物馆对此提出了异议。

lines.en: According to the library's website, workers have found no evidence of "Truman pardoning a turkey that he received as a gift in 1947, or at any other time during his Presidency. "
lines.zh: 据该图书馆网站说，工作人员没有发现任何证据表明“杜鲁门赦免过他在 1947 年收到的礼物火鸡，或在他总统任期内的任何其他时候赦免过火鸡”。

lines.en: Almost 20 years after Truman's presidency, President John F. Kennedy decided to spare a turkey brought to the White House for the Thanksgiving meal. He reportedly said: 'No, I think I'll pardon this turkey and let it grow.'
lines.zh: 杜鲁门总统任期结束近 20 年后，约翰·F·肯尼迪总统决定放过一只为感恩节晚餐送到白宫的火鸡。据报道，他说：“不，我想我要赦免这只火鸡，让它长大吧。”

lines.en: Edward Lengel notes that Kennedy was the first president to give an official pardon.
lines.zh: 爱德华·伦格尔指出，肯尼迪是第一位正式赦免火鸡的总统。

lines.en: "We know that John F Kennedy definitely began this tradition and it has continued on and off ever since."
lines.zh: “我们知道，约翰·F·肯尼迪肯定开创了这一传统，此后它断断续续地一直延续下来。”

lines.en: After 1981, the custom of sending the pardoned turkey to a farm became accepted practice during the presidency of Ronald Reagan.
lines.zh: 1981 年以后，在罗纳德·里根任总统期间，把被赦免的火鸡送到农场养老成了公认的惯例。

lines.en: Even if the presidents pardon turkeys before Thanksgiving, they generally still eat a different turkey on the holiday.
lines.zh: 虽然总统在感恩节前赦免火鸡，但节日当天他们通常还是会吃另一只火鸡。

lines.en: The bird cooked for the president's meal is bought with his own money and prepared according to his taste and that of his family.
lines.zh: 总统晚餐吃的火鸡是用他自己的钱买的，按他和家人的口味烹制。

lines.en: I'm John Russell.
lines.zh: 我是约翰·拉塞尔。

qs.q: Which president was the first to give an official turkey pardon?
qs.why: "Kennedy was the first president to give an official pardon."

qs.q: Why couldn't Ted Lincoln's turkey vote?
qs.why: "his turkey could not vote because he was too young."

qs.q: Who pays for the turkey the president eats?
qs.why: "bought with his own money."

lessons.title: Immigrants in Ohio Create a Lively Food Culture
lessons.zh: 俄亥俄移民打造的美食文化
lessons.sum: 俄亥俄州哥伦布市有来自 40 多个国家的异国餐馆。“哥伦布美食探险”带游客去克利夫兰大道品尝印度、墨西哥、尼日利亚、越南和索马里菜。尼泊尔移民开的饺子馆 Momo Ghar 只有两张小桌，却是点评网站上的城里第一名。

lines.en: There are plenty of ways to see a city. Visits to historic homes, famous statues, and even ghost tours under the night sky are just a few.
lines.zh: 游览一座城市的方式有很多。参观历史故居、著名雕像，甚至在夜空下来一场“寻鬼之旅”，这些只是其中几种。

lines.en: But maybe only Columbus, Ohio, has tours designed for food lovers.
lines.zh: 但也许只有俄亥俄州哥伦布市有专为美食爱好者设计的游览。

lines.en: Bethia Woolf writes about food on her blog. In 2010, she launched Columbus Food Adventures, in part because of the city's immigrant groups. Immigrants represent nine percent of the total population.
lines.zh: 贝西娅·伍尔夫在她的博客上写美食。2010 年，她创办了“哥伦布美食探险”，部分原因是这座城市的移民群体。移民占当地总人口的 9%。

lines.en: Columbus Food Adventures can take you on a taco truck tour, with stops at food trucks specializing in Mexican cuisine. The business also offers German village tours and what Woolf calls the 'Alt Eats' tour.
lines.zh: “哥伦布美食探险”可以带你参加塔可餐车之旅，在专做墨西哥菜的餐车停下品尝。公司还提供德国村之旅，以及伍尔夫称为“另类美食”的游览。

lines.en: "This unique city tour centers on the thriving ethnic enclaves of north Cleveland Avenue, where much of Columbus' immigrant community lives, eats, and plays," notes the company's website.
lines.zh: 公司网站写道：“这个独特的城市游览以北克利夫兰大道繁荣的少数族裔聚居区为中心，哥伦布的很多移民都在这里生活、吃饭、娱乐。”

lines.en: Food lovers are guided to explore little-known ethnic restaurants, all within a short walk of one another.
lines.zh: 导游带着美食爱好者探访鲜为人知的异国餐馆，这些餐馆彼此相距都只有几步路。

lines.en: "We visit Indian, a Mexican bakery," Woolf explains. "We visit Nigerian, Vietnamese, and Somali (restaurants)." She says the company's tour guides make sure to tell people about the food they will eat.
lines.zh: “我们去印度餐馆、一家墨西哥面包店，”伍尔夫解释说，“我们还去尼日利亚、越南和索马里（餐馆）。”她说，公司的导游一定会给大家介绍要吃的食物。

lines.en: Columbus now has ethnic restaurants from more than 40 nationalities, and more are being added all the time.
lines.zh: 哥伦布现在有来自 40 多个国家的异国餐馆，而且还在不断增加。

lines.en: "We recently found a market that is offering Sudanese food," Woolf said. "Without leaving Columbus, you can explore all these different cuisines."
lines.zh: “我们最近发现了一家卖苏丹食物的市场，”伍尔夫说，“不用离开哥伦布，你就能探索所有这些不同的菜系。”

lines.en: Columbus Food Adventures tours are popular with visitors to Columbus and natives to the city.
lines.zh: “哥伦布美食探险”的游览很受外地游客和本地人欢迎。

lines.en: Gloria Chavez is a visitor from California.
lines.zh: 格洛丽亚·查韦斯是来自加利福尼亚的游客。

lines.en: "It's just a great way to try new foods and meet new people and learn about different cultures. It was great!"
lines.zh: “这是尝试新食物、认识新朋友、了解不同文化的好方法。太棒了！”

lines.en: For Brian Wolf and his wife, the tour is a guide to fine eating in his own city.
lines.zh: 对布赖恩·沃尔夫和他妻子来说，这个游览是他们自己城市的美食指南。

lines.en: "Now we will definitely come back to these restaurants because they're all within 10 minutes of where we live and all of them have been delicious."
lines.zh: “现在我们肯定会再来这些餐馆，因为它们离我们家都不到 10 分钟，而且每家都很好吃。”

lines.en: Momo Ghar
lines.zh: Momo Ghar（饺子屋）

lines.en: Momo Ghar was at one time one of the restaurants on the tour. Guides had to lead their groups inside an international market to get there. The Nepalese and Tibetan eatery had just two small tables and a counter close to where the food was prepared.
lines.zh: Momo Ghar 曾经是游览路线上的餐馆之一。导游得带着团队走进一个国际市场才能找到它。这家尼泊尔和西藏风味小馆只有两张小桌子和一个紧挨着厨房的柜台。

lines.en: But its appearance can fool most people. Momo Ghar is Yelp's No. 1 restaurant in Columbus.
lines.zh: 可它的外表会骗过大多数人。Momo Ghar 是点评网站 Yelp 上哥伦布排名第一的餐馆。

lines.en: Phuntso Lama is the owner of Momo Ghar.
lines.zh: 彭措·拉玛是 Momo Ghar 的老板。

lines.en: "Momo is dumpling. We make a lot of dumplings. We are making probably several thousand dumplings a day. We have to keep up with the demand."
lines.zh: “Momo 就是饺子。我们做很多饺子，大概每天要做几千个。我们得跟上需求。”

lines.en: A Nepalese immigrant, Lama says Momo is almost like a national dish in Nepal. She is happy that the tastes she brought from her native land are so popular in her new home.
lines.zh: 拉玛是尼泊尔移民，她说 momo 在尼泊尔几乎就像国菜。她很高兴自己从故乡带来的味道在新家这么受欢迎。

lines.en: Windi Noble of Columbus often stops by Momo Ghar.
lines.zh: 哥伦布的温迪·诺布尔经常来 Momo Ghar。

lines.en: "All those are flavorful and super tasty and filling and really cheap. So, it's a great affordable meal. That's why we keep coming back."
lines.zh: “这些都很有味道，超级好吃，吃得饱，还特别便宜。所以这是一顿很实惠的饭。这就是我们一再回来的原因。”

lines.en: The rise in immigrants to Columbus has also helped energize aging shopping centers as the newcomers open businesses and restaurants.
lines.zh: 来哥伦布的移民增多，也让老旧的购物中心重新焕发活力，因为新来的人在那里开店、开餐馆。

lines.en: Guadalupe Velasquez is assistant director for the city's Department of Neighborhoods. She told VOA that the central Ohio area is home to an estimated 150,000 to 200,000 immigrants and refugees. "The total local and state taxes paid by immigrants is $340 million," she said.
lines.zh: 瓜达卢佩·贝拉斯克斯是该市社区事务局的副局长。她告诉 VOA，俄亥俄州中部地区估计有 15 万到 20 万移民和难民。“移民缴纳的地方和州税总额达 3.4 亿美元。”她说。

lines.en: Lama is planning to expand her restaurant business.
lines.zh: 拉玛正计划扩大她的餐馆生意。

lines.en: "Employees, I have about 14 or 15 of them. The reason I have so many right now is I am training a lot of them because we are opening a second location."
lines.zh: “员工我大概有 14 到 15 个。我现在有这么多人，是因为我在培训很多人，我们要开第二家店了。”

lines.en: I'm Dorothy Gundy.
lines.zh: 我是多萝西·冈迪。

qs.q: How many nationalities of ethnic restaurants does Columbus have?
qs.why: "ethnic restaurants from more than 40 nationalities."

qs.q: What is a "momo"?
qs.why: "Momo is dumpling."

qs.q: Why does Windi Noble keep going to Momo Ghar?
opts: The food is tasty and cheap.
qs.a: The food is tasty and cheap.
qs.why: "super tasty and filling and really cheap."

lessons.title: Paw Paws, a Forgotten American Fruit, Become Popular Again
lessons.zh: 被遗忘的美国水果：泡泡果又流行了
lessons.sum: 泡泡果（paw paw）是美国原产的最大可食用水果，味道像香蕉、杏和芒果的混合，华盛顿和杰斐逊都很爱吃。它只在九十月间成熟两三周，摘下后两三天就会坏，所以从没进入商店。如今农民们办起“泡泡果节”，让它重回餐桌。

lines.en: Have you ever heard of a paw paw?
lines.zh: 你听说过泡泡果（paw paw）吗？

lines.en: If not, do not feel bad. Most Americans do not know of the fruit, although it is native to the United States.
lines.zh: 如果没听过，别难过。大多数美国人都不知道这种水果，尽管它原产于美国。

lines.en: Once, however, it was one of the most popular fruits in North America.
lines.zh: 不过，它曾经是北美最受欢迎的水果之一。

lines.en: Happily, those who love the paw paw are trying to return it to its former position in American foods.
lines.zh: 令人高兴的是，喜爱泡泡果的人们正努力让它重新回到美国饮食中原来的位置。

lines.en: A paw paw is a tropical-like fruit that grows on trees found all over the eastern United States. It's also the largest edible fruit native to the US.
lines.zh: 泡泡果是一种像热带水果的果子，长在遍布美国东部的树上。它也是美国原产的最大的可食用水果。

lines.en: It is similar to a typical mango in size. It has a dull green-colored skin, and a soft, almost-creamy orange inside.
lines.zh: 它的大小和普通芒果差不多，外皮是暗绿色的，里面是柔软、近乎奶油状的橙色果肉。

lines.en: Most people agree that the pawpaw tastes like a combination of a banana, an apricot and a mango. Most people are very surprised by its sweet taste.
lines.zh: 大多数人都认为泡泡果吃起来像香蕉、杏和芒果的混合。大多数人都对它的甜味感到很惊讶。

lines.en: At one time, it could be found as far west as Nebraska. It also grows along the East Coast from New York to Florida. The fruit has a very short harvest season, from two to three weeks in September and October.
lines.zh: 它曾经最西可以在内布拉斯加州找到，也沿东海岸从纽约一直生长到佛罗里达。这种水果的收获期非常短，只在九月和十月间的两到三周。

lines.en: The paw paw was an important food for Native Americans and even early European settlers.
lines.zh: 泡泡果是美洲原住民甚至早期欧洲移民的重要食物。

lines.en: Paw paws reportedly were a favorite treat of George Washington, the first U.S. president, who especially liked them cold. Thomas Jefferson, the third U.S. president, was also a fan of the fruit. He planted paw paws at Monticello, his home in Virginia. He also sent paw paw seeds to his friends in France. American explorers Lewis and Clark wrote in their journals about the paw paw.
lines.zh: 据说泡泡果是美国第一任总统乔治·华盛顿最喜欢的零食，他尤其喜欢冰过的。第三任总统托马斯·杰斐逊也是它的粉丝，他在弗吉尼亚州的家蒙蒂塞洛种了泡泡果，还把泡泡果种子寄给法国的朋友。美国探险家刘易斯和克拉克也在日记里写到了泡泡果。

lines.en: Today, paw paws remain popular in the Appalachian mountain area.
lines.zh: 如今，泡泡果在阿巴拉契亚山区仍然很受欢迎。

lines.en: The paw paw has never been sold commercially. The fruit requires a very special environment -- low, wet areas that sometimes flood.
lines.zh: 泡泡果从来没有在商店里出售过。这种水果需要非常特殊的环境——低洼潮湿、有时会被水淹的地方。

lines.en: In addition, the fruit is good to eat for only two to three days after harvesting. This makes it hard to sell anywhere distant from the paw paw tree it came from.
lines.zh: 此外，这种水果摘下后只有两三天好吃，所以很难运到离产地很远的地方去卖。

lines.en: Planters are again growing paw paw trees and harvesting the fruit. In several states farmers have organized "paw paw festivals" to reintroduce people to the food.
lines.zh: 种植者们又开始种泡泡果树、收获果子。好几个州的农民组织了“泡泡果节”，重新向人们介绍这种食物。

lines.en: At such a festival in Maryland recently, farmers displayed different products made with paw paws. There were paw paw jams, pies, gelato, and beer.
lines.zh: 最近在马里兰州的一个泡泡果节上，农民们展示了用泡泡果做的各种产品：泡泡果果酱、派、意式冰淇淋，还有啤酒。

lines.en: Michael Judd helped organize the Maryland paw paw festival.
lines.zh: 迈克尔·贾德帮助组织了马里兰州的泡泡果节。

lines.en: "It has that energy, and the people here today, there's an excitement, because they are trying something totally new but also exotic that grows here."
lines.zh: “它有那种活力。今天来的人都很兴奋，因为他们在尝试一种全新、带点异国风味、却又是本地生长的东西。”

lines.en: Farmers are trying to grow kinds of paw paw that will be easier to ship and sell commercially. Donna and Jim Davis are paw paw farmers in Westminster, Maryland. They told National Public Radio that they purchased their paw paw trees in the 1990s and now sell the fruit at farmers markets and online.
lines.zh: 农民们正努力种植更容易运输和商业销售的泡泡果品种。唐娜和吉姆·戴维斯是马里兰州威斯敏斯特的泡泡果农。他们告诉美国国家公共电台，他们在 20 世纪 90 年代买了泡泡果树，现在在农贸市场和网上卖这种水果。

lines.en: So, who knows? Maybe the paw paw will show up soon at a market near you.
lines.zh: 所以，谁知道呢？也许泡泡果很快就会出现在你家附近的市场上。

lines.en: I'm Phil Dierking
lines.zh: 我是菲尔·迪尔金。

qs.q: What does a paw paw taste like?
qs.why: "tastes like a combination of a banana, an apricot and a mango."

qs.q: Why has the paw paw never been sold commercially?
opts: It is good for only two to three days after harvest.
qs.a: It is good for only two to three days after harvest.
qs.why: "the fruit is good to eat for only two to three days after harvesting."

qs.q: Which president planted paw paws at Monticello?
qs.why: "He planted paw paws at Monticello."

lessons.title: Delta Blues: The Birth of American Music
lessons.zh: 三角洲布鲁斯：美国音乐的诞生
lessons.sum: 布鲁斯音乐 19 世纪末诞生于密西西比三角洲，源自非裔奴隶的灵歌和劳动号子，讲述生活的苦与乐。它的“AAB”歌词结构影响深远，摇滚、爵士、乡村、节奏布鲁斯和说唱都由它衍生。几位老布鲁斯乐手讲述了他们的人生和种族隔离的往事。

lines.en: "I look at blues as the way of life… it's a story, a story told with music."
lines.zh: “在我看来，布鲁斯是一种生活方式……它是一个故事，一个用音乐讲的故事。”

lines.en: That voice belongs to Jimmy "Duck" Holmes, a blues musician. He is sitting on an old chair in a dark corner of the Blue Front Cafe playing his guitar. Holmes's parents owned the restaurant and now it belongs to him.
lines.zh: 这个声音属于布鲁斯乐手吉米·“鸭子”·霍姆斯。他坐在“蓝色门面咖啡馆”昏暗角落的一把旧椅子上弹吉他。这家店原是霍姆斯父母开的，现在归他了。

lines.en: Photographs, vinyl records, and guitars cover its walls. The objects all speak to the 70-year-old artist's life and music. The smell of beer and sounds coming from the jukebox in the corner help create the perfect atmosphere for his history with the blues.
lines.zh: 墙上挂满了照片、黑胶唱片和吉他，每样东西都诉说着这位 70 岁艺术家的人生和音乐。啤酒的味道和角落里点唱机传出的声音，为他与布鲁斯的历史营造出完美的氛围。

lines.en: Blues music itself tells a story -- a story about America.
lines.zh: 布鲁斯音乐本身就在讲一个故事——一个关于美国的故事。

lines.en: When people think of American music, they probably think of rap or rock-and-roll or jazz. What many may not realize is that these "American" sounds are all tied to a common place.
lines.zh: 人们想到美国音乐时，可能会想到说唱、摇滚或爵士。很多人可能没意识到，这些“美国”声音都和一个共同的源头相连。

lines.en: That place is blues music.
lines.zh: 那个源头就是布鲁斯音乐。

lines.en: The blues was born in the Mississippi Delta area sometime in the late 1800s. The music is rooted in African American slave spiritual and work songs.
lines.zh: 布鲁斯在 19 世纪末的某个时候诞生于密西西比三角洲地区，根源是非裔美国奴隶的灵歌和劳动号子。

lines.en: Life was hard for black people in the U.S. Slavery technically had ended, but poverty and unjust laws kept people from full freedom. Some former slaves stayed in the South and continued to work on farms, often for their former owners. Much of the work was outside in the fields, in the unforgiving heat of the Mississippi sun.
lines.zh: 那时美国黑人的生活很艰难。奴隶制名义上已经结束，但贫困和不公正的法律让人们无法获得完全的自由。一些前奴隶留在南方继续在农场干活，常常还是给以前的主人干。很多活是在田里干的，头顶是密西西比无情的烈日。

lines.en: Roger Stolle is a Mississippi blues historian. He says a culture of singing helped people deal with the hardships. People sang spirituals at church and work songs in the fields to make the days go by. Over time, this music developed into what people now call "the blues."
lines.zh: 罗杰·斯托尔是密西西比布鲁斯历史学家。他说，唱歌的文化帮助人们熬过苦难。人们在教堂唱灵歌，在田里唱劳动号子来打发日子。随着时间推移，这种音乐发展成了今天人们所说的“布鲁斯”。

lines.en: As the blues grew in popularity, musicians began to perform around the Delta. Some, like B.B. King or John Lee Hooker, would travel to the city of Memphis, Tennessee, to establish professional music careers.
lines.zh: 随着布鲁斯越来越受欢迎，乐手们开始在三角洲各地演出。有些人，比如 B.B. 金和约翰·李·胡克，去了田纳西州孟菲斯市，开始职业音乐生涯。

lines.en: Blues is both American and foreign. Blues historian Scott Barretta says many elements of the blues -- including singing styles, rhythm, instrument playing, and pentatonic scale -- are African and were brought to the U.S. by those who had been enslaved.
lines.zh: 布鲁斯既是美国的，也是外来的。布鲁斯历史学家斯科特·巴雷塔说，布鲁斯的许多元素——包括演唱风格、节奏、乐器演奏和五声音阶——都来自非洲，是被奴役的人带到美国的。

lines.en: Baretta also notes the patterns to the lyrics.
lines.zh: 巴雷塔还指出了歌词的模式。

lines.en: "The blues follows an "A, A, B lyrical style…What we mean by that, is that when you perform the blues, you're often singing a verse, repeating the verse, and then there's an answer line. That's a style of music which we didn't really see before around 1900."
lines.zh: “布鲁斯遵循‘A、A、B’的歌词结构……意思是，唱布鲁斯时，你常常先唱一段，再重复这一段，然后是一句回答。这种音乐风格在 1900 年前后之前我们基本没见过。”

lines.en: When it comes to the words, many musicians sing about difficulties from their own life stories. Holmes is among them.
lines.zh: 说到歌词，很多乐手唱的是自己人生中的艰辛，霍姆斯就是其中之一。

lines.en: "I don't sing about lies, I tell the truth!...True blues, the lyrics are absolutely true. They sing about life experience. Sometimes good, sometimes bad, but they didn't lie."
lines.zh: “我不唱谎话，我讲真话！……真正的布鲁斯，歌词绝对是真的。他们唱人生经历，有时好，有时坏，但他们不撒谎。”

lines.en: Eighty-five-year-old blues musician Leo "Bud" Welch agrees.
lines.zh: 85 岁的布鲁斯乐手利奥·“巴德”·韦尔奇也这么认为。

lines.en: "Well the blues ain't nothing but some good man or woman feeling bad. It's about life."
lines.zh: “布鲁斯不过就是一个好男人或好女人心里难受。它讲的是生活。”

lines.en: Many blues musicians never gained fame. Often they were farmworkers by day and would play at 'juke joints' by night. Juke joints were unofficial businesses where black people could gather to socialize. They would drink, dance and play music at night.
lines.zh: 许多布鲁斯乐手从未成名。他们常常白天是农场工人，晚上在“自动点唱机酒馆”演奏。这种酒馆是非正式的店，黑人可以聚在那里交际，晚上喝酒、跳舞、演奏音乐。

lines.en: Leo Bud Welch was one of these musicians. He has played the blues since he was 13, about 65 years ago. He only performed music for families and friends. It was not until 2013, when Welch was 81, that he recorded his first album.
lines.zh: 利奥·巴德·韦尔奇就是这样的乐手。他从 13 岁就开始弹布鲁斯，大约有 65 年了。他只为家人和朋友演奏。直到 2013 年，81 岁的韦尔奇才录了他的第一张专辑。

lines.en: For most his life, he earned a living as a farm worker and tree cutter.
lines.zh: 他大半辈子都靠在农场干活和砍树谋生。

lines.en: "My daddy used to always say, it takes the money to make the mouth right. You ain't got no money you couldn't get nothin' done."
lines.zh: “我爸总说，有了钱嘴才好说话。你没钱，什么事也办不成。”

lines.en: "Most guys who started doing what I'm doing, got killed for they was doing."
lines.zh: “很多一开始做我这件事的人，都因为做这件事被杀了。”

lines.en: With a voice both playful and serious, Bobby Rush speaks as a blues musician as well as a historian. He grew up playing with famous blues musicians like Muddy Waters, Buddy Guy, and Howlin' Wolf. At 83, he is still performing. He just won his first Grammy award in February for his newest album, Porcupine Meat.
lines.zh: 鲍比·拉什的声音既俏皮又严肃，他既以布鲁斯乐手的身份说话，也以历史见证者的身份说话。他从小和泥水、巴迪·盖伊、嚎狼等著名布鲁斯乐手一起演奏。83 岁的他仍在演出，今年二月刚凭新专辑《豪猪肉》赢得了他的第一座格莱美奖。

lines.en: Rush's story, like the story of blues music, parallels the story of civil rights in the U.S.
lines.zh: 拉什的故事和布鲁斯音乐的故事一样，与美国民权运动的故事相互呼应。

lines.en: Rush, whose great-grandmother was a slave, often experienced racism early in his career.
lines.zh: 拉什的曾祖母是奴隶。他在职业生涯早期常常遭遇种族歧视。

lines.en: "In the past, blues had been something that, it wasn't good until the white guys did it. When I came along, this was the devil's music."
lines.zh: “过去，布鲁斯这东西，要等白人来做了才算好。我出道那会儿，这是‘魔鬼的音乐’。”

lines.en: When Rush started performing professionally, he was sometimes forced to play behind curtains because he is black and the audience was mostly white.
lines.zh: 拉什开始职业演出时，有时被迫在幕布后面演奏，因为他是黑人，而观众大多是白人。

lines.en: Over time, that changed. Martin Luther King, Jr. and other civil rights leaders organized to bring about change through nonviolent resistance. Blacks and whites began protesting racist laws together in the south. In 1964, the Civil Rights Act passed, barring discrimination based on race.
lines.zh: 后来情况变了。马丁·路德·金和其他民权领袖组织起来，通过非暴力抵抗推动变革。黑人和白人开始在南方一起抗议种族主义法律。1964 年，《民权法案》通过，禁止基于种族的歧视。

lines.en: Over time these actions affected the blues world.
lines.zh: 随着时间推移，这些行动影响了布鲁斯界。

lines.en: Now, Rush says he feels blessed for his popularity with a racially mixed audience. But he adds that he will always be proud of his roots and the struggles he went through on his road to success.
lines.zh: 如今，拉什说他很庆幸能受到不同种族观众的欢迎。但他补充说，他会永远为自己的根以及成功路上经历的奋斗而自豪。

lines.en: "I'm a blues singer, I'm a black blues singer, and I love what I do, I love who I am… love all people because they are all part of me."
lines.zh: “我是布鲁斯歌手，我是黑人布鲁斯歌手，我爱我做的事，我爱我自己……我爱所有人，因为他们都是我的一部分。”

lines.en: Blues music had a critical influence in the expansion of the American musical tradition.
lines.zh: 布鲁斯音乐对美国音乐传统的发展有着至关重要的影响。

lines.en: Over time, as blues musicians left Mississippi, the sound changed. In the north, Chicago and other cities became famous for the electric guitar style of blues, which helped create rock and roll. In the south, blues music was a building block for jazz, country, and bluegrass. Rhythm and blues and rap music also developed from the Mississippi blues.
lines.zh: 随着布鲁斯乐手离开密西西比，声音也变了。在北方，芝加哥等城市以电吉他风格的布鲁斯出名，它帮助催生了摇滚乐。在南方，布鲁斯是爵士、乡村和蓝草音乐的基石。节奏布鲁斯和说唱音乐也是从密西西比布鲁斯发展而来的。

lines.en: Historian Roger Stolle says, today, young people are more interested in learning musical styles like rap than traditional blues. However, there are efforts to document the life of the genre and keep it healthy for the future.
lines.zh: 历史学家罗杰·斯托尔说，如今年轻人对学说唱之类的音乐风格比对传统布鲁斯更感兴趣。不过，人们正在努力记录这种音乐类型的历史，让它在未来保持活力。

lines.en: The Mississippi Blue Commission has created The Blues Music Trail, a path of historic places throughout Mississippi that informs and entertains visitors about blues music.
lines.zh: 密西西比布鲁斯委员会开辟了“布鲁斯音乐之路”，这是一条贯穿密西西比州的历史地点路线，向游客介绍布鲁斯音乐，也让他们获得乐趣。

lines.en: The history of the music is also on display at the Delta Blues Museum. And it has programs that connect young musicians with established blues artists.
lines.zh: 三角洲布鲁斯博物馆也展示着这种音乐的历史，还有让年轻乐手和知名布鲁斯艺术家结对的项目。

lines.en: Also, record labels are trying to preserve the traditional style of Delta blues by recording older musicians like Welch and Holmes.
lines.zh: 此外，唱片公司也在通过为韦尔奇、霍姆斯这样的老乐手录音，努力保存传统的三角洲布鲁斯风格。

lines.en: But no matter what happens to the genre, almost every form of popular American music today has been touched by the blues.
lines.zh: 但无论这种音乐类型将来怎样，今天几乎每一种美国流行音乐都受过布鲁斯的影响。

lines.en: And it is almost impossible not to like it, says Bobby Rush.
lines.zh: 鲍比·拉什说，你几乎不可能不喜欢它。

lines.en: "The blues itself is the mother of all music …because if you don't like the blues, you don't like your mama. Because that's the root of music, man!"
lines.zh: “布鲁斯本身就是所有音乐之母……因为你要是不喜欢布鲁斯，你就是不喜欢你妈妈。因为那是音乐的根啊，伙计！”

lines.en: I'm Phil Dierking.
lines.zh: 我是菲尔·迪尔金。

lines.en: And I'm Dorothy Gundy
lines.zh: 我是多萝西·冈迪。

qs.q: Where was the blues born?
qs.why: "The blues was born in the Mississippi Delta area sometime in the late 1800s."

qs.q: What is the "A, A, B" style?
opts: sing a verse, repeat it, then an answer line
qs.a: sing a verse, repeat it, then an answer line
qs.why: "singing a verse, repeating the verse, and then there's an answer line."

qs.q: When did Leo "Bud" Welch record his first album?
qs.why: "It was not until 2013, when Welch was 81, that he recorded his first album."

lessons.title: Blue Crabs: A Messy Meal from the Chesapeake Bay
lessons.zh: 蓝蟹：切萨皮克湾的“狼狈”美餐
lessons.sum: 切萨皮克湾的蓝蟹是马里兰州的骄傲。传统做法是用水或啤酒加醋、撒上 Old Bay 调料活蒸，吃的时候用小锤敲开硬壳，弄得满手都是。蓝蟹曾在 2008 年几乎绝迹，经过保护，数量已恢复到 1990 年以来最多。

lines.en: What have ten legs, two of them large claws, a hard shell cover, and live in oceans, fresh water, and on land? Crabs, of course!
lines.zh: 什么东西有十条腿，其中两条是大螯，背着坚硬的壳，生活在海洋、淡水和陆地上？当然是螃蟹！

lines.en: There are thousands of different kinds of crabs all over the world. They can be as small as a few millimeters across or grow as big as 4 meters. And all play an important part in the environments in which they live.
lines.zh: 世界各地有几千种不同的螃蟹。它们可以小到只有几毫米宽，也可以长到 4 米大。它们在各自生活的环境中都扮演着重要角色。

lines.en: Crabs may look strange. But many people also find them delicious. The blue crab is an especially popular crab for eating in the United States. These crabs can grow up to about 23 centimeters and they get their name from the blue coloring on the legs and claws.
lines.zh: 螃蟹看起来也许很奇怪，但很多人也觉得它们很好吃。蓝蟹是美国特别受欢迎的食用蟹。这种螃蟹可以长到约 23 厘米，因腿和螯上的蓝色而得名。

lines.en: Blue crabs live in the waters of the western Atlantic Ocean, and in the Gulf of Mexico. However, one place in America is especially famous for its blue crabs: the Chesapeake Bay. This largest U.S. estuary borders Maryland and Virginia.
lines.zh: 蓝蟹生活在西大西洋和墨西哥湾的水域。不过，美国有一个地方的蓝蟹特别有名：切萨皮克湾。这个美国最大的河口与马里兰州和弗吉尼亚州接壤。

lines.en: Both states have long made use of the Chesapeake for food, transportation, and fun. All around the area you can see images of the blue crab on clothing, advertisements, cars, and in restaurant windows.
lines.zh: 长期以来，两州都利用切萨皮克湾获取食物、交通运输和娱乐。在这一带，到处都能在衣服、广告、汽车和餐馆橱窗上看到蓝蟹的图案。

lines.en: Scientists in Maryland and Virginia say the bay holds hundreds of millions of blue crabs. From early spring through much of fall thousands of people hit the water to capture some of these creatures.
lines.zh: 马里兰州和弗吉尼亚州的科学家说，海湾里有几亿只蓝蟹。从早春到大半个秋天，成千上万的人下水去捕捉它们。

lines.en: Pete White works with Captain White's Seafood City in Washington, D.C. The family-owned business gathers crabs and other seafood from the bay and sells it at its store right along the Potomac River. White told VOA that his family has been in the business for about 100 years. He is a big fan of Chesapeake blue crabs.
lines.zh: 皮特·怀特在华盛顿的“怀特船长海鲜城”工作。这家家族企业从海湾收购螃蟹和其他海鲜，在波托马克河边的店里出售。怀特告诉 VOA，他家做这一行已经约 100 年了。他是切萨皮克蓝蟹的忠实粉丝。

lines.en: "[These] are the best crabs, in my opinion, out of all the country," White said. "I get a lot of people coming from Pennsylvania … a lot of people out of Jersey, New York, North Carolina. … They come from Georgia and they take them home on their car ride."
lines.zh: “在我看来，（这些）是全国最好的螃蟹，”怀特说，“很多人从宾夕法尼亚来……很多人从新泽西、纽约、北卡罗来纳来……他们从佐治亚来，开车把螃蟹带回家。”

lines.en: White said blue crabs are special because of their sweet meat.
lines.zh: 怀特说，蓝蟹之所以特别，是因为它的肉很甜。

lines.en: There are many ways to cook blue crabs. Some people like to grill them, while others make crab soup. But the cooking style most traditional to the area is steaming.
lines.zh: 蓝蟹有很多种做法。有人喜欢烤，有人做蟹汤。但这一带最传统的做法是蒸。

lines.en: The first step, White explained, is to combine water or beer with vinegar in a large, metal container. Then, White adds "Old Bay."
lines.zh: 怀特解释说，第一步是在一个大金属容器里把水或啤酒和醋混在一起。然后，怀特加入“Old Bay”。

lines.en: Old Bay is a seasoning product of hot and salty spices. It was created in Baltimore, Maryland in 1939.
lines.zh: Old Bay 是一种又辣又咸的调味料，1939 年在马里兰州巴尔的摩发明。

lines.en: Then you turn on the heat and wait for the liquid to boil.
lines.zh: 接着开火，等液体烧开。

lines.en: The crabs are always cooked alive. But, White suggested, they should not touch the water directly. They normally are placed flat on a rack just above the water. Old Bay can be added to each layer of crabs.
lines.zh: 螃蟹总是活着下锅。不过怀特建议，它们不应该直接碰到水，通常平放在水面上方的架子上。每一层螃蟹上都可以撒 Old Bay。

lines.en: It takes 20 to 30 minutes for the steam from the boiling liquid to cook the crabs. Then, they are removed from the container. And White said, they can be mixed with more Old Bay.
lines.zh: 沸腾液体的蒸汽要 20 到 30 分钟才能把螃蟹蒸熟。然后把螃蟹从容器里取出来。怀特说，还可以再拌上更多 Old Bay。

lines.en: Cooking crabs is fairly easy. But eating them can be a challenge. The shells are still very hard. Some people use special tools called crackers and mallets to crack the shells and reach the meat. Other use their hands, breaking at weak points of the shell. Either way, it is a messy meal that usually leaves the eaters covered in shell, bits of meat and lots of red seasoning.
lines.zh: 蒸螃蟹相当容易，但吃螃蟹可能是个挑战。蟹壳还是很硬。有人用叫“蟹钳”和“木槌”的专门工具敲开蟹壳取肉，有人用手从壳的薄弱处掰开。不管哪种方式，这都是一顿弄得一团糟的饭，吃完通常满身都是蟹壳、碎肉和大量红色调料。

lines.en: Each blue crab only has between about 60 and 100 grams of meat in them. So sellers most often sell them by the bushel, meaning in groups of about 60 to 100. People usually buy them when they are feeding a lot of people. The so-called crab feast has become a summer tradition in the Chesapeake region.
lines.zh: 每只蓝蟹只有大约 60 到 100 克肉，所以卖家通常按“蒲式耳”卖，也就是一批大约 60 到 100 只。人们通常在要招待很多人时买。所谓的“螃蟹宴”已经成了切萨皮克地区的夏季传统。

lines.en: Kate Livie knows a lot about crab feasts. She is the director of education at the Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum in St. Michaels, Maryland.
lines.zh: 凯特·利维非常了解螃蟹宴。她是马里兰州圣迈克尔斯的切萨皮克湾海事博物馆的教育主任。

lines.en: Livie says that close access to the Bay and its resources have always been important to people. Native Americans such as the Powhatan, the Piscataway and the Nanticoke lived in the area long before Europeans arrived in the 1500s. Scientists have found evidence that these Native Americans enjoyed crabs as well as other seafood, such as oysters.
lines.zh: 利维说，靠近海湾、能利用海湾的资源，一直对人们很重要。早在欧洲人 16 世纪到来之前，波瓦坦、皮斯卡塔韦和南蒂科克等美洲原住民就生活在这一带。科学家发现证据表明，这些原住民也喜欢吃螃蟹和牡蛎等其他海鲜。

lines.en: In fact, oysters were the main seafood of choice from the Chesapeake for many early years, Livie says. But improvements in food preservation, especially in keeping it cold, changed everything for the crab market in the warm summer months.
lines.zh: 利维说，事实上，早年间切萨皮克湾的主要海鲜是牡蛎。但食物保存技术的进步，尤其是冷藏技术，彻底改变了温暖夏季的螃蟹市场。

lines.en: "Although [blue crabs] were [eaten] through the 17th and 18th century, you couldn't sell more than you could eat in a day," she told VOA via Skype. "So food preservation [technology] and transportation turned crabs from, kind of, free but priceless, into an incredibly successful and economically [important] harvest."
lines.zh: “虽然 17、18 世纪人们也吃（蓝蟹），但你卖的不能比一天吃得掉的多，”她通过 Skype 告诉 VOA，“所以食物保存（技术）和运输，让螃蟹从一种可以说免费却又无价的东西，变成了一项非常成功、经济上（重要）的收获。”

lines.en: There was also improvement in the crabbing industry. A local fisherman invented a trap for crabs in the 1920s. The trap, called a crab pot, made it easier to catch the animals.
lines.zh: 捕蟹业也有了进步。20 世纪 20 年代，一位当地渔民发明了一种捕蟹笼，叫“蟹笼”，让捕蟹变得更容易了。

lines.en: Plus, Livie says, Old Bay and some advertising campaigns helped grow the crab market. And she she says the blue crab became a major part of the Maryland identity.
lines.zh: 利维说，另外，Old Bay 和一些广告宣传也帮助扩大了螃蟹市场。她说，蓝蟹成了马里兰州身份认同的重要组成部分。

lines.en: However, the blue crab has weathered some stormy seas. Bruce Vogt is a manager of the Chesapeake Bay office of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, or NOAA.
lines.zh: 然而，蓝蟹也经历过一些风浪。布鲁斯·沃格特是美国国家海洋和大气管理局（NOAA）切萨皮克湾办公室的一位主管。

lines.en: He says that pollution and other problems have had a serious effect on the health of the bay and its crabs. In fact, in 2008 scientists reported that the blue crab came very close to disappearing from the Chesapeake completely.
lines.zh: 他说，污染和其他问题严重影响了海湾和螃蟹的健康。事实上，2008 年科学家报告说，蓝蟹几乎从切萨皮克湾完全消失。

lines.en: But efforts that began in the 1970s to improve the Chesapeake's conditions continue, Vogt says. And this year, researchers estimated there were 254 million female blue crabs in the bay, the largest population since 1990.
lines.zh: 沃格特说，从 20 世纪 70 年代开始的改善切萨皮克湾环境的努力仍在继续。今年，研究人员估计海湾里有 2.54 亿只雌性蓝蟹，是 1990 年以来最多的。

lines.en: Vogt argues that people who love crabs cannot simply hope they will always be there. He says people must work to guarantee their survival. That is why experts push for conservation action, including limiting the harvest of females to about 25 percent.
lines.zh: 沃格特认为，爱吃螃蟹的人不能只是指望它们永远都在。他说，人们必须努力保证它们存活下去。所以专家们推动保护行动，包括把雌蟹的捕捞量限制在约 25%。

lines.en: "There's obviously a lot of work to do," Vogt told VOA via Skype. "We can't just sit back and expect that everything is going well now and we'll have crabs in the future."
lines.zh: “显然还有很多工作要做，”沃格特通过 Skype 告诉 VOA，“我们不能坐等，指望现在一切都好，将来也会有螃蟹。”

lines.en: I'm Pete Musto. And I'm Lucija Millonig.
lines.zh: 我是皮特·穆斯托。我是露西亚·米洛尼格。

qs.q: How do blue crabs get their name?
opts: the blue color on their legs and claws
qs.a: the blue color on their legs and claws
qs.why: "they get their name from the blue coloring on the legs and claws."

qs.q: What is the most traditional way to cook blue crabs in the area?
qs.why: "the cooking style most traditional to the area is steaming."

qs.q: What is "Old Bay"?
qs.why: "Old Bay is a seasoning product of hot and salty spices."

lessons.title: National Food Days: An American Tradition
lessons.zh: 全国美食日：一个美国传统
lessons.sum: 在美国，几乎一年中每天都是某种食物的“节日”，比如全国洋葱圈日、奥利奥饼干日。很多是一位美食博主编出来的，但也有些有历史渊源：4 月 7 日啤酒日纪念禁酒令结束，甜甜圈日纪念一战时给士兵送甜甜圈的女性。

lines.en: If you look on the Internet, you will see that almost every day of the year celebrates some kind of food.
lines.zh: 如果你上网看看，会发现一年中几乎每一天都在庆祝某种食物。

lines.en: These "holidays" have become very popular across the United States. They often are trending stories on Twitter, and described in the U.S. media. They give people a chance to enjoy something they might not eat normally, like National Onion Ring Day, for example.
lines.zh: 这些“节日”在美国各地变得非常流行，常常成为推特上的热门话题，被美国媒体报道。它们让人们有机会享用一些平时可能不吃的东西，比如“全国洋葱圈日”。

lines.en: Food holidays also give restaurants and other businesses a chance to promote their products.
lines.zh: 美食节日也给餐馆和其他商家提供了推销产品的机会。

lines.en: But where did these distinctly American "holidays" come from?
lines.zh: 可这些独具美国特色的“节日”是从哪里来的呢？

lines.en: Many are the invention of an Alabama man, John-Bryan Hopkins. He writes about food for his Foodimentary.com website.
lines.zh: 很多是阿拉巴马州一个叫约翰-布赖恩·霍普金斯的人发明的。他在自己的网站 Foodimentary.com 上写美食。

lines.en: Hopkins told Time magazine that when he began his site in 2006, there were only 175 "holidays." "I filled in the rest," he said.
lines.zh: 霍普金斯告诉《时代》杂志，他 2006 年开办网站时，只有 175 个这样的“节日”。“剩下的都是我填上的。”他说。

lines.en: Some of his favorites are National Oreo Cookie Day on March 6 and National Tater Tot Day on February 2.
lines.zh: 他最喜欢的几个是 3 月 6 日的全国奥利奥饼干日和 2 月 2 日的全国炸土豆球日。

lines.en: The National Day Calendar has a list of all the different food and non-food related "holidays." In the past, the website used to let anyone create their own day -- for a price. But now, the site only accepts requests from businesses and other organizations.
lines.zh: “全国节日日历”网站列出了所有与食物有关和无关的“节日”。过去，这个网站允许任何人花钱创建自己的节日，但现在只接受企业和其他机构的申请。

lines.en: While some food "holidays" are indeed made-up, many have historical roots.
lines.zh: 虽然有些美食“节日”确实是编出来的，但很多都有历史渊源。

lines.en: For example, National Beer Day on April 7 marks the end of a U.S. ban on the production, transport, import and sale of alcoholic drinks. The ban lasted from 1920 until 1933.
lines.zh: 比如，4 月 7 日的全国啤酒日，标志着美国禁止生产、运输、进口和销售酒精饮料的禁令结束。这项禁令从 1920 年持续到 1933 年。

lines.en: The Salvation Army, a Christian group, launched U.S. National Doughnut Day on June 1, 1938. It was meant to honor women who served soldiers doughnuts during World War I.
lines.zh: 基督教团体救世军在 1938 年 6 月 1 日发起了美国全国甜甜圈日，目的是纪念第一次世界大战期间给士兵送甜甜圈的女性。

lines.en: But not everyone likes food holidays.
lines.zh: 不过，并不是每个人都喜欢美食节日。

lines.en: Bethany Jean Clement is a food writer for the Seattle Times newspaper. She wrote, "I get that some people might be excited by, say, National Doughnut Day. But you really can have a doughnut any day you want!"
lines.zh: 贝瑟尼·琼·克莱门特是《西雅图时报》的美食作家。她写道：“我明白有些人可能会为全国甜甜圈日之类的节日兴奋。可你真的想哪天吃甜甜圈都可以啊！”

lines.en: Tavi Juarez, also of Foodimentary.com, thinks national food holidays are here to stay. She told the Seattle Times, "In my humble opinion, I believe that food holidays will continue to grow in popularity online because there's a lot of negativity out there. Why not choose to celebrate food instead?"
lines.zh: 同样来自 Foodimentary.com 的塔维·华雷斯认为，全国美食节日会一直存在下去。她对《西雅图时报》说：“依我浅见，我相信美食节日在网上会越来越受欢迎，因为外面有太多负面的东西了。为什么不选择庆祝美食呢？”

lines.en: I'm Jonathan Evans.
lines.zh: 我是乔纳森·埃文斯。

qs.q: Who invented many of the food holidays?
qs.why: "Many are the invention of an Alabama man, John-Bryan Hopkins."

qs.q: What does National Beer Day on April 7 mark?
opts: the end of the ban on alcohol
qs.a: the end of the ban on alcohol
qs.why: "marks the end of a U.S. ban on the production, transport, import and sale of alcoholic drinks."

qs.q: Why was National Doughnut Day started?
opts: to honor women who served soldiers doughnuts in World War I
qs.a: to honor women who served soldiers doughnuts in World War I
qs.why: "to honor women who served soldiers doughnuts during World War I."

lessons.title: Ketchup: An American Condiment with an Asian Connection
lessons.zh: 番茄酱：一种与亚洲有渊源的美国调味品
lessons.sum: 97% 的美国厨房里都有番茄酱，可它的故事始于 500 年前的东南亚：ketchup 一词很可能来自厦门话“鲑汁”（腌鱼的卤汁）。英国人从印度尼西亚带回这种酱，用核桃、蘑菇做，却从不用番茄。番茄后来大量过剩，亨氏公司靠广告让番茄酱成了美国的国民调味品。

lines.en: At any given time, about 97 percent of American kitchens have a bottle of ketchup.
lines.zh: 任何时候，美国大约 97% 的厨房里都有一瓶番茄酱。

lines.en: American ketchup is made from red tomatoes, vinegar, salt, sugar and other ingredients. It has both a sweet and salty taste.
lines.zh: 美国的番茄酱是用红番茄、醋、盐、糖和其他配料做的，味道又甜又咸。

lines.en: It is, without question, America's condiment.
lines.zh: 毫无疑问，它是美国的调味品。

lines.en: But it was not always that way.
lines.zh: 但它并不是一直如此。

lines.en: In fact, the story of ketchup begins over 500 years ago -- in Southeast Asia.
lines.zh: 事实上，番茄酱的故事始于 500 多年前——在东南亚。

lines.en: Andy F. Smith is a professor of food history in New York City. He has published many books about American food, including Pure Ketchup: A History of America's National Condiment.
lines.zh: 安迪·F·史密斯是纽约市的一位饮食史教授。他出版过很多关于美国食物的书，包括《纯粹番茄酱：美国国民调味品的历史》。

lines.en: The word "ketchup," Smith says, most likely comes from a Chinese dialect called Amoy. Ke-tsiap meant "the brine of pickled fish." It probably originated in a Chinese community in northern Vietnam, Smith adds.
lines.zh: 史密斯说，“ketchup”这个词很可能来自一种叫“厦门话”（Amoy）的汉语方言。“鲑汁”（ke-tsiap）的意思是“腌鱼的卤汁”。史密斯补充说，它很可能起源于越南北部的一个华人社区。

lines.en: Yes, America's condiment developed from fish sauce.
lines.zh: 没错，美国的调味品是从鱼露发展而来的。

lines.en: The sauce and the word reached Indonesia, Smith explains. That is where, in his words, "the English ran into it."
lines.zh: 史密斯解释说，这种酱汁和这个词传到了印度尼西亚。用他的话说，就是在那里“英国人碰上了它”。

lines.en: "They had a colony in Indonesia, in the late 17th century. And it is from there that the word -- now kecap [in Indonesian] -- goes into the English language."
lines.zh: “17 世纪后期，他们在印度尼西亚有一个殖民地。这个词——在印尼语里现在叫 kecap——就是从那里进入英语的。”

lines.en: From Indonesia, ketchup made its way into British kitchens and cookbooks.
lines.zh: 番茄酱从印度尼西亚进入了英国的厨房和食谱。

lines.en: "Everything that you can think of they made a ketchup out of it. And that is one way to preserve those foods for longer periods of time. And then it was used on spicing foods."
lines.zh: “你能想到的东西，他们都拿来做酱。这是让食物保存更久的一种方法。然后它被用来给食物调味。”

lines.en: Early British ketchup was made from many different foods, such as walnuts, mushrooms and anchovies, Smith explains.
lines.zh: 史密斯解释说，早期的英国 ketchup 用很多不同的食物做，比如核桃、蘑菇和凤尾鱼。

lines.en: But never, ever tomatoes.
lines.zh: 但从来、从来不用番茄。

lines.en: "All of the early recipes for ketchup have nothing to do with tomatoes."
lines.zh: “所有早期的 ketchup 食谱都和番茄毫无关系。”

lines.en: Tomatoes are native to the Andes Mountains in South America. Tomato plants were first grown for food around 500 BC in what is now southern Mexico and Central America.
lines.zh: 番茄原产于南美洲的安第斯山脉。大约公元前 500 年，在今天的墨西哥南部和中美洲，人们最先种植番茄作为食物。

lines.en: Spanish explorers took the plant's seeds northward into the Caribbean and, then, back to Europe. Tomatoes arrived in U.S. colonies sometime in the late 17th century, Smith says.
lines.zh: 西班牙探险家把番茄的种子往北带到加勒比地区，然后又带回欧洲。史密斯说，番茄在 17 世纪后期的某个时候来到了美洲殖民地。

lines.en: For many years, however, some countries did not believe tomatoes were healthy to eat. Medical theories at the time considered the tomato to be a "cold" food. People living in cold-weather countries thought they would get sick if they ate tomatoes.
lines.zh: 不过，很多年里，有些国家并不相信番茄吃了对健康有益。当时的医学理论认为番茄是一种“寒性”食物，住在寒冷国家的人认为吃番茄会生病。

lines.en: But, medical theories about tomatoes changed. By the 1830s, they were thought to be good for health in many ways. Tomato pills even became popular medicine, Smith says.
lines.zh: 但关于番茄的医学理论变了。到 19 世纪 30 年代，人们认为番茄在很多方面都有益健康。史密斯说，番茄药片甚至成了流行的药。

lines.en: It was around then that tomato production in America took off. They were easy and low-cost to grow, Smith says. But there was one problem.
lines.zh: 大约就在那时，美国的番茄种植迅速发展起来。史密斯说，番茄好种又便宜，但有一个问题。

lines.en: "The problem is - is that they all mature about the same time -- from late July through early October, depending on where you are. And when the tomato comes up, massive amounts are produced. And you can only eat so many fresh tomatoes."
lines.zh: “问题是——它们差不多同时成熟——从七月底到十月初，看你在哪儿。番茄一上市，产量巨大。而新鲜番茄你只能吃那么多。”

lines.en: By the end of the growing season, American farmers had more tomatoes than they knew what to do with.
lines.zh: 到了生长季末，美国农民手里的番茄多得不知道怎么办。

lines.en: So, people began preserving tomatoes in different ways. Making ketchup from tomatoes was one solution.
lines.zh: 于是人们开始用不同方法保存番茄，用番茄做酱就是一个办法。

lines.en: Smith says two major things led to tomato ketchup's rise in American cuisine -- advertising and low cost.
lines.zh: 史密斯说，有两大因素让番茄酱在美国饮食中崛起——广告和低成本。

lines.en: The American food company Heinz led the way.
lines.zh: 美国食品公司亨氏走在了前面。

lines.en: "Heinz advertised it, promoted it. They were in the right position at the right time, in the early 20th century, when the health and food safety movements were taking off in the United States, and they claimed the tomato had no ingredients that were dangerous -- with the type of ketchup that they were making. So they promoted it as a health food. So they just dominated the market through advertising and promotion. And they've got a good product."
lines.zh: “亨氏大做广告、大力推广。他们在正确的时间站在了正确的位置：20 世纪初，美国的健康和食品安全运动正在兴起，他们宣称自己做的那种番茄酱里没有任何危险成分，所以把它当作健康食品来推广。他们靠广告和推广主导了市场。而且他们的产品确实不错。”

lines.en: In its early days, tomato ketchup was mostly used in cooking. It was not considered the condiment that it is today.
lines.zh: 早期，番茄酱主要用在烹饪里，还不是今天这样的调味品。

lines.en: Enter the hot dog and the hamburger, Smith explains. Both became part of American cuisine in the late 1800s and early 1900s.
lines.zh: 史密斯解释说，后来热狗和汉堡登场了。这两样都在 19 世纪末 20 世纪初成为美国饮食的一部分。

lines.en: "As soon as those became among the more important American foods, then ketchup became the condiment of choice."
lines.zh: “一旦它们成了比较重要的美国食物，番茄酱就成了首选的调味品。”

lines.en: Heinz continues to dominate the ketchup market in the United States and in many countries worldwide.
lines.zh: 亨氏至今仍主导着美国和世界许多国家的番茄酱市场。

lines.en: Today, most of the world's ketchup is produced where it all began: Asia.
lines.zh: 如今，世界上大部分番茄酱的产地，正是一切开始的地方：亚洲。

lines.en: In fact, the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region of China produces almost 20 percent of the world's ketchup trade, The Economist magazine reports. The far western region grows some 70 percent of all of China's tomatoes.
lines.zh: 事实上，据《经济学人》杂志报道，中国新疆维吾尔自治区生产了全球番茄酱贸易量的近 20%。这个最西部的地区种植了全中国约 70% 的番茄。

lines.en: And as a whole, China grows 25 percent of the world's tomatoes.
lines.zh: 而整个中国种植的番茄占全世界的 25%。

lines.en: Smith says he is impressed by the tomato's quick rise in China.
lines.zh: 史密斯说，番茄在中国的迅速崛起让他印象深刻。

lines.en: "Tomatoes were not an important part of Asian cuisine until the 20th century. What's surprising was, how quickly the tomato has become an important product in China."
lines.zh: “直到 20 世纪，番茄都不是亚洲饮食的重要组成部分。令人惊讶的是，番茄这么快就成了中国的一种重要产品。”

lines.en: Some may think of ketchup as all-American. But history shows its roots are much older than the United States itself. And its connection to several Asian countries -- both in the past and in the present -- is strong.
lines.zh: 有人也许认为番茄酱是地地道道的美国货。但历史表明，它的根比美国本身古老得多。它和几个亚洲国家的联系——无论过去还是现在——都很紧密。

lines.en: I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。

lines.en: And I'm Ashley Thompson.
lines.zh: 我是阿什莉·汤普森。

qs.q: Where does the word "ketchup" most likely come from?
qs.why: "most likely comes from a Chinese dialect called Amoy."

qs.q: What was early British ketchup made from?
qs.why: "made from many different foods, such as walnuts, mushrooms and anchovies."

qs.q: Which foods made ketchup the condiment of choice?
qs.why: "Enter the hot dog and the hamburger."

lessons.title: Preserving Street Art in Washington, DC
lessons.zh: 在华盛顿保护街头艺术
lessons.sum: 华盛顿一边打击非法涂鸦，一边鼓励公共艺术。Art Bloc D.C. 帮街头艺术家拿到楼主许可，合法创作大型壁画；市政府的 MuralsDC 项目雇艺术家画壁画美化城市。艺术家乌多菲亚在老字号“本的辣椒碗”外墙画了 16 位著名非裔美国人。

lines.en: Washington, D.C. has a complex relationship with graffiti and street art.
lines.zh: 华盛顿和涂鸦、街头艺术之间的关系很复杂。

lines.en: Local street artist Gobi knows this well. Not long ago, a police officer caught him spraying colorful paint on the side of a building. Gobi did not get permission to put his design on the building. What he was doing, then, was illegal.
lines.zh: 本地街头艺术家戈比对此深有体会。不久前，一名警察抓到他在一栋楼的侧墙上喷彩色油漆。戈比没有得到许可就把图案画在楼上，所以他的行为是违法的。

lines.en: The police officer arrested Gobi.
lines.zh: 警察逮捕了戈比。

lines.en: Then, he asked Gobi for his business card. The officer said he was interested in hiring him for a street art project in the future.
lines.zh: 然后，警察向戈比要了名片。他说他有兴趣以后雇戈比做一个街头艺术项目。

lines.en: America's capital city is trying hard to control its illegal graffiti problem. At the same time, city officials recognize the value and importance of street art.
lines.zh: 美国首都正在努力控制非法涂鸦问题。同时，市政官员也认识到街头艺术的价值和重要性。

lines.en: There is a high demand for more artists to make street art legally. But the city offers few chances for young D.C. street artists to develop their skills without breaking the law.
lines.zh: 社会上很需要更多艺术家合法地创作街头艺术，但这座城市很少给年轻的华盛顿街头艺术家提供在不违法的情况下提升技能的机会。

lines.en: Some local programs, however, are trying to change that.
lines.zh: 不过，一些本地项目正在努力改变这一点。
