lines.zh: 皮尤研究人员在瑞典也发现了类似的情况。99% 的瑞典受访者说至少去过一个其他国家，但只有少得多的 47% 表示与世界各地的人亲近。

lines.en: In fact, a higher number of Indian respondents – 68 percent – report feeling at least somewhat close to people all over the world. Yet just 3 percent of respondents from India said they had traveled to another country. Such findings show that international connectedness can be formed in ways other than traveling overseas.
lines.zh: 事实上，表示与世界各地的人至少有些亲近的印度受访者比例更高，达 68%。可只有 3% 的印度受访者说去过其他国家。这些发现表明，与世界的联系可以通过出国旅行以外的方式建立。

lines.en: Sadikova, the Uzbek English teacher, told VOA Learning English she feels connected to people all over the world even though she has never traveled outside Uzbekistan. She said, "Some years ago it was difficult for us to get information about people in the world, but currently, because of media, it is quite easy to get acquainted with events and news."
lines.zh: 乌兹别克英语老师萨迪科娃告诉 VOA 慢速英语，尽管她从没离开过乌兹别克斯坦，但她感到和世界各地的人有联系。她说：“几年前，我们很难获得世界上其他人的信息，但现在因为有了媒体，了解各种事件和新闻很容易。”

lines.en: I'm Gena Bennett.
lines.zh: 我是吉娜·贝内特。

qs.q: What percent of Americans feel at least somewhat close to people around the world?
qs.why: "only 35 percent of the respondents said they feel at least somewhat connected."

qs.q: What is surprising about India?
opts: Few people traveled abroad, but many feel close to the world.
Nobody feels close to the world.
qs.a: Few people traveled abroad, but many feel close to the world.
qs.why: "68 percent... Yet just 3 percent... had traveled to another country."

qs.q: How does Saodat Sadikova feel connected to the world?
opts: through her job as a flight attendant
qs.why: "because of media, it is quite easy to get acquainted with events and news."

lessons.title: Nickel Mine, Environmental Activists Exist Together in Michigan
lessons.zh: 密歇根：镍矿与环保人士和平共处
lessons.sum: 力拓公司在密歇根州北部开镍矿时，环保人士强烈反对。后来公司请环保团体当“监督者”，用比政府更严的标准检测污染，费用由公司承担。十多年来，鹰矿没出过事故，这种合作也许能成为全球新矿的“路线图”。

lines.en: About 20 years ago, the international mining company Rio Tinto said it would open a nickel mine in the far northern part of the American state of Michigan.
lines.zh: 大约 20 年前，国际矿业公司力拓说要在美国密歇根州的最北部开一座镍矿。

lines.en: Rio Tinto promised good jobs for people in the area close to Canada.
lines.zh: 力拓承诺为这个靠近加拿大的地区提供好工作。

lines.en: But environmental activists had concerns. They were worried about industrial pollution from the metal, the mining byproducts and contaminated water runoff into rivers and lakes.
lines.zh: 但环保人士很担心。他们担心金属带来的工业污染、采矿副产品，以及被污染的水流进河流湖泊。

lines.en: Many observers expected a long legal fight between the two sides. Some did not believe the mine would ever open.
lines.zh: 许多观察人士预计双方会有一场漫长的法律战，有些人根本不相信这座矿会开起来。

lines.en: But the Eagle mine has been open for more than 10 years. There have been no accidents or pollution problems.
lines.zh: 可是“鹰矿”已经开了 10 多年，没出过任何事故或污染问题。

lines.en: People in the area who once protested the mine have found a way to exist with the mine.
lines.zh: 当地曾经抗议这座矿的人，找到了与它共存的办法。

lines.en: Maura Davenport is one of those people. She is one of the top leaders of the Superior Watershed Partnership (SWP), an environmental interest group.
lines.zh: 莫拉·达文波特就是其中之一。她是环保团体“苏必利尔流域伙伴关系”（SWP）的高层领导之一。

lines.en: "I was fiercely opposed to the mine, and I changed," she said.
lines.zh: “我曾经激烈反对这座矿，后来我改变了。”她说。

lines.en: Davenport's group was invited to act as a "watchdog" for the mine. Rio Tinto asked the group to oversee pollution testing that has higher standards than regulators require.
lines.zh: 达文波特的团体受邀担任矿山的“监督者”。力拓请这个团体监督污染检测，检测标准比监管机构要求的更高。

lines.en: The cooperation between the environmental group and the mining company may be an example for other mines around the world.
lines.zh: 这个环保团体和矿业公司之间的合作，也许能成为世界上其他矿山的榜样。

lines.en: Many new mines are opening in order to provide minerals needed to make items used by the green energy economy. These items include batteries, electrical wire and magnets.
lines.zh: 为了提供绿色能源经济所需的矿物，许多新矿正在开张。这些物品包括电池、电线和磁铁。

lines.en: If countries around the world are to meet the climate goals set in Paris in 2015, there needs to be a 400-percent increase in the production of these minerals. The International Energy Agency said there needs to be an increase of 19 times in nickel production alone.
lines.zh: 如果世界各国要实现 2015 年在巴黎确定的气候目标，这些矿物的产量需要增加 400%。国际能源署说，仅镍的产量就需要增加到 19 倍。

lines.en: Davenport said the Eagle mine proposal "divided our community." Other mines in northern Michigan had opened in the 1800s and closed in the 1930s. The mining companies left behind large open holes and environmental damage. Water that ran from the mine polluted Lake Superior, one of the Great Lakes in the northern Midwest.
lines.zh: 达文波特说，鹰矿的提议“让我们的社区分裂了”。密歇根北部的其他矿山在 19 世纪开张、20 世纪 30 年代关闭，矿业公司留下了巨大的露天矿坑和环境破坏。从矿山流出的水污染了中西部北部五大湖之一的苏必利尔湖。

lines.en: Simon Nish worked for Rio Tinto when the Eagle mine was proposed. He said he understands the "dilemma" that communities face. They need jobs and an economic benefit, he said, but "don't want long-term environmental consequences."
lines.zh: 西蒙·尼什在鹰矿提出时在力拓工作。他说，他理解社区面临的“两难”：他们需要工作和经济利益，但“不想要长期的环境后果”。

lines.en: Residents do not trust the big mining companies he said, so it makes it easier to say no to proposals.
lines.zh: 他说，居民不信任大矿业公司，所以很容易对提议说不。

lines.en: He worked in Australia in the 1990s when mining companies wanted to use land where native Aboriginal people lived. He said he learned that businesses need to "understand the interests of both sides" if they want long-term success.
lines.zh: 20 世纪 90 年代，他在澳大利亚工作，当时矿业公司想使用原住民居住的土地。他说他从中学到，企业要想长期成功，就需要“了解双方的利益”。

lines.en: When Nish arrived in Michigan in 2011, the mine was under construction. But it faced several legal disputes. In order to find a way for the mine to open, Nish considered looking for a partner.
lines.zh: 2011 年尼什来到密歇根时，矿山正在建设中，但面临好几起法律纠纷。为了找到让矿山开张的办法，尼什考虑找一个合作伙伴。

lines.en: Nish said the Superior Watershed Partnership was already testing water around the area. He asked if they would consider running an environmental testing program for the mine.
lines.zh: 尼什说，苏必利尔流域伙伴关系当时已经在检测这一带的水质。他问他们是否愿意考虑为矿山运营一个环境检测项目。

lines.en: Over a few months, Rio Tinto and the SWP made a plan for testing. The group required open access to the mine. It would also test groundwater in the surrounding area. And it required permission to test a processing center 30 kilometers away. Rio Tinto was required to pay for the work.
lines.zh: 几个月里，力拓和 SWP 制定了检测计划。该团体要求可以自由进入矿山，还要检测周边地区的地下水，并要求获准检测 30 公里外的一个加工中心。力拓必须为这些工作付费。

lines.en: The agreement launching the Community Environmental Monitoring Program was signed in 2012. More than 10 years later, no major pollution problems have turned up.
lines.zh: 启动“社区环境监测项目”的协议于 2012 年签署。10 多年后，没有发现任何重大污染问题。

lines.en: But some environmental groups are still concerned. Rochelle Dale is head of the Yellow Dog Watershed Preserve. She said Eagle mine and the testing program are doing good work.
lines.zh: 但一些环保团体仍然担心。罗谢尔·戴尔是“黄狗流域保护区”的负责人。她说鹰矿和检测项目做得不错。

lines.en: But, she said, "a lot of the sulfide mines in the past haven't really had a problem until after closure. It's something that our grandchildren are going to inherit."
lines.zh: 可是她说：“过去很多硫化物矿山直到关闭以后才真正出问题。这是我们的孙辈将要继承的东西。”

lines.en: As more mines open up to help meet the world's demand for new minerals, mining companies are starting to understand how important local support is to their success.
lines.zh: 随着越来越多的矿山开张以满足世界对新矿物的需求，矿业公司开始明白当地的支持对它们的成功有多重要。

lines.en: The partnership in Northern Michigan gives large mining companies a "road map." But, although it has been successful so far, there is no guarantee that an accident will not happen that pollutes the area in the future.
lines.zh: 密歇根北部的这种合作关系，给大型矿业公司提供了一张“路线图”。不过，尽管到目前为止很成功，也不能保证将来不会发生污染这一地区的事故。

lines.en: I'm Dan Friedell.
lines.zh: 我是丹·弗里德尔。

qs.q: Why were environmental activists worried about the mine?
qs.why: "They were worried about industrial pollution... and contaminated water runoff into rivers and lakes."

qs.q: What did Rio Tinto ask the environmental group to do?
qs.why: "Rio Tinto asked the group to oversee pollution testing."

qs.q: Why are many new mines opening?
opts: to provide minerals for the green energy economy
qs.a: to provide minerals for the green energy economy
qs.why: "to provide minerals needed to make items used by the green energy economy."

lessons.title: What Will Office of the Future Be Like?
lessons.zh: 未来的办公室会是什么样？
lessons.sum: 疫情前只有 5.7% 的美国人在家工作，2022 年已有 58% 的人每周至少在家工作一天。专家说，办公室成了一种“选择”，必须比在家工作更有吸引力：更注重团队交流，甚至提供托儿和宠物照料。美国联邦总务管理局正在试验未来办公室。

lines.en: The COVID-19 pandemic has changed how people in the U.S. work.
lines.zh: 新冠疫情改变了美国人的工作方式。

lines.en: Before the pandemic, only 5.7 percent of people worked from their homes. But a recent report from the business advisor McKinsey & Company found that 58 percent of people worked from home at least one day a week in 2022.
lines.zh: 疫情前，只有 5.7% 的人在家工作。但商业咨询公司麦肯锡最近的一份报告发现，2022 年有 58% 的人每周至少在家工作一天。

lines.en: Ryan Luby helped write the report. He said the office needs to change because the role of the workplace has changed.
lines.zh: 瑞安·卢比参与撰写了这份报告。他说，办公室需要改变，因为工作场所的作用已经变了。

lines.en: Aditya Sanghvi is with the property business of McKinsey & Company. He said: "The office has suddenly become a choice. It's an option. And the office has to be better for someone than working from home and enduring the commute to come into the office."
lines.zh: 阿迪蒂亚·桑维在麦肯锡的房地产业务部门工作。他说：“办公室突然变成了一种选择，一个选项。办公室必须比在家工作、还要忍受通勤来上班更好才行。”

lines.en: One change office spaces need is more focus on community in the workplace. "When you get to the office, if you're not engaging with anyone else, you might as well not be there," Luby said.
lines.zh: 办公空间需要的一个改变，是更注重工作场所里的群体交流。“到了办公室，如果你不和任何人交流，那还不如不来。”卢比说。

lines.en: He added, "The office should be a place where you're doing group work."
lines.zh: 他还说：“办公室应该是你做团队工作的地方。”

lines.en: Sanghvi added that, in the new workspace, people should feel like "there's no difference between whether or not someone's sitting with you in the office or somebody's [on] video."
lines.zh: 桑维补充说，在新的工作空间里，人们应该觉得“和你一起坐在办公室里的人，跟在视频里的人没有区别”。

lines.en: The office of the future might even help workers with their personal responsibilities.
lines.zh: 未来的办公室甚至可能帮员工处理个人事务。

lines.en: "One of the reasons that a lot of people work from home is that they have to pick up the kids or take care of the dog," Sanghvi said. "And so, what if there were [animal] care in the building? What if there was child care in the building?"
lines.zh: “很多人在家工作的原因之一，是他们得接孩子或照顾狗，”桑维说，“那么，如果大楼里有（宠物）照料呢？如果大楼里有托儿服务呢？”

lines.en: Sanghvi believes companies that own the office space should be more active in changing workspaces for the new way of life.
lines.zh: 桑维认为，拥有办公空间的公司应该更积极地改造工作空间，适应新的生活方式。

lines.en: The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) is the government agency that supervises federal buildings. The GSA has been a leading force in establishing what the office of the future will look like.
lines.zh: 美国联邦总务管理局（GSA）是管理联邦建筑的政府机构，它一直在引领塑造未来办公室的样子。

lines.en: Chuck Hardy is GSA's chief architect. He supervises GSA's Workplace Innovation Lab, a 25,000-square-foot space inside the organization's headquarters in Washington, D.C.
lines.zh: 查克·哈迪是 GSA 的首席建筑师。他负责 GSA 的“工作场所创新实验室”，这是该机构华盛顿总部内一个 25000 平方英尺的空间。

lines.en: "What we're trying to do is create a workplace and an environment that allows you to be as productive as you can be without getting in the way. And that means a variety of spaces for a variety of the people that work for us," Hardy said.
lines.zh: “我们努力创造这样一个工作场所和环境：让你尽可能高效，又不碍事。这意味着为我们这里各种各样的员工提供各种各样的空间。”哈迪说。

lines.en: The Workplace Innovation Lab will be open for one year. Federal workers can try out the latest in workplace furnishings and technology and then provide comments on their experience.
lines.zh: 工作场所创新实验室将开放一年。联邦员工可以试用最新的办公家具和技术，然后反馈自己的体验。

lines.en: Some spaces in the lab look like traditional workspaces. Some spaces feel pleasant. Almost everything can be moved around. The air quality is controlled, and technology that is believed to be good for the environment is being tested.
lines.zh: 实验室里有些空间看起来像传统的办公区，有些空间让人感觉很舒适。几乎所有东西都可以挪动。空气质量是可控的，还在测试一些被认为环保的技术。

lines.en: Hardy said the office of the future needs three qualities. It should be well-designed, serve a purpose and feel pleasant.
lines.zh: 哈迪说，未来的办公室需要三个特点：设计精良、实用、让人感觉舒适。

lines.en: All of this might mean that the office of the future could feel a little bit more like home.
lines.zh: 这一切也许意味着，未来的办公室会感觉更像家一点。

lines.en: I'm Andrew Smith.
lines.zh: 我是安德鲁·史密斯。

qs.q: What percent of people worked from home at least one day a week in 2022?
qs.why: "58 percent of people worked from home at least one day a week in 2022."

qs.q: What should the office be a place for, says Ryan Luby?
qs.why: "The office should be a place where you're doing group work."

qs.q: What three qualities does the office of the future need?
qs.why: "It should be well-designed, serve a purpose and feel pleasant."

lessons.title: AM Radio Stations Oppose Removing AM Radios from Cars
lessons.zh: AM 电台反对车企取消车载 AM 收音机
lessons.sum: 一些车企说电动车的系统会干扰 AM 信号，开始在新车上取消 AM 收音机。美国约 4000 家 AM 电台为此担忧：AM 信号覆盖远，是农村居民、农民和韩语、印地语等少数语言社区获取本地新闻和紧急警报的重要渠道。国会议员提出法案要求保留。

lines.en: The move by automobile manufacturers to include radios in cars nearly 100 years ago helped spread AM radio across the United States.
lines.zh: 近 100 年前，汽车制造商在车里装上收音机，帮助 AM 广播传遍了全美国。

lines.en: But now, some carmakers want to stop providing AM radio in their new vehicles.
lines.zh: 可现在，一些车企想在新车上不再提供 AM 收音机。

lines.en: The first cars to be sold with radios were introduced in the 1930s. They only received one kind of radio transmission, those that broadcast using AM, or amplitude modulation.
lines.zh: 最早配收音机出售的汽车出现在 20 世纪 30 年代。它们只能接收一种广播信号，就是用 AM——调幅——广播的信号。

lines.en: After some time, radios could receive transmissions in AM and FM. FM stands for frequency modulation.
lines.zh: 过了一段时间，收音机可以接收 AM 和 FM 信号了。FM 是调频的意思。

lines.en: For many years, those were the only choices. But after a while, car makers added 8-track players, audio cassette players, compact disc players and eventually Bluetooth connections so people could play music from mobile devices such as an iPhone.
lines.zh: 很多年里，只有这两种选择。后来，车企又加了八轨磁带机、卡带机、CD 机，最后还有蓝牙连接，让人们可以播放 iPhone 等移动设备上的音乐。

lines.en: However, cars are no longer sold with 8-track players or compact disc players. And now, some new electric cars are being sold with radios that only receive FM signals. Car makers say the driving systems in electric vehicles interfere with the AM signal.
lines.zh: 然而，汽车已经不再配八轨磁带机或 CD 机了。现在，一些新电动车卖的时候只配能接收 FM 信号的收音机。车企说，电动车的驱动系统会干扰 AM 信号。

lines.en: That concerns the people who own and work at about 4,000 radio stations in the U.S. that broadcast in AM. One of them is in the small town of Dimmitt, Texas. Nancy and Todd Whalen own the radio station KDHN-1470, which has been broadcasting since 1963. They are the only employees, and they talk on the radio every morning. The Whalens have run the station for eight years.
lines.zh: 这让美国约 4000 家 AM 电台的老板和员工很担心。其中一家在德克萨斯州的小镇迪米特。南希和托德·惠伦经营着 KDHN-1470 电台，这家电台从 1963 年开始播音。他们俩是电台仅有的员工，每天早上在电台里说话。惠伦夫妇经营这家电台已经八年了。

lines.en: They say they do it, so Dimmitt has something to feel good about. "We feel like what we've done and continue to do is provide that, not just for Dimmitt, but for all the small towns in the area that no longer have local radio stations."
lines.zh: 他们说，这样做是为了让迪米特有一样让人感觉美好的东西。“我们觉得，我们做过的和一直在做的，就是提供这样东西，不只为迪米特，也为这一带所有不再有本地电台的小镇。”

lines.en: KDHN also runs a translator, or a system that changes the signal so their programs can also be heard on FM. But the AM signal is much stronger. The FM signal covers about a 30-kilometer radius from the transmitter while the AM signal covers 160 kilometers.
lines.zh: KDHN 还运营一个转播器，也就是一个把信号转换、让节目也能在 FM 上收听的系统。但 AM 信号强得多。FM 信号从发射机覆盖半径约 30 公里，而 AM 信号覆盖 160 公里。

lines.en: Nancy Whalen called the AM signal "our bread and butter since the beginning."
lines.zh: 南希·惠伦称 AM 信号“从一开始就是我们的饭碗”。

lines.en: The reduction in the number of AM stations has many people worried. That includes broadcasters, business owners, farmers and lawmakers. Some broadcasting companies that own AM radio stations are selling their land because it is more profitable than running a radio station.
lines.zh: AM 电台数量的减少让很多人担忧，包括广播人、企业主、农民和议员。一些拥有 AM 电台的广播公司正在卖地，因为卖地比经营电台更赚钱。

lines.en: Amy Klobuchar is a senator from Minnesota. She is concerned about losing AM radio stations. They keep people in her large state informed.
lines.zh: 艾米·克洛布彻是明尼苏达州的参议员。她担心失去 AM 电台，因为这些电台让她那个大州的人们了解消息。

lines.en: In an online video, Klobuchar said AM radio "gives people the information they need in many of our rural areas…" She noted that "a lot of people drive long distances" in rural areas and listen to the radio in the car. She also said of AM radio: "This is where people find their local news."
lines.zh: 克洛布彻在一段网络视频中说，AM 广播“在我们许多农村地区给人们提供所需的信息……”她指出，在农村地区，“很多人要开很远的车”，在车里听广播。她还说 AM 广播是“人们获取本地新闻的地方”。

lines.en: Klobuchar and others are working on the "AM For Every Vehicle Act."
lines.zh: 克洛布彻和其他人正在推动《每辆车都要有 AM 法案》。

lines.en: They want to keep AM radio in cars. The lawmakers say the car makers should find a way to keep AM radio.
lines.zh: 他们希望车里保留 AM 收音机。议员们说，车企应该想办法保留 AM 广播。

lines.en: When Klobuchar talks about people in rural areas, she is talking about people like Rodney Hunter. He supervises two grain storage structures, called silos, in Texas. He said farmers will listen to the radio on their way to sell grain. Without the news on AM radio, they would not know if grain prices were up or down.
lines.zh: 克洛布彻说到农村居民时，她说的就是像罗德尼·亨特这样的人。他在德克萨斯州管理两座叫“筒仓”的粮食储存建筑。他说，农民们去卖粮的路上会听广播。没有 AM 广播里的新闻，他们就不知道粮价是涨了还是跌了。

lines.en: "Farmers are in their (trucks or tractors) going up and down the road," Hunter said. He added it is easier for them to listen to the agriculture news on AM radio than to try to find the information online.
lines.zh: “农民们开着（卡车或拖拉机）在路上来来回回。”亨特说。他还说，对他们来说，在 AM 广播上听农业新闻比上网找信息更容易。

lines.en: But the people who run AM radio stations are not just farmers and small-town business people with a sense of civic pride.
lines.zh: 不过，经营 AM 电台的人不只有农民和有公民自豪感的小镇商人。

lines.en: About five hours southeast of the grain-storage building, Joann Whang is a pharmacist who listens to KKDA-730 in Dallas, Texas. It is a Korean-language station. At first, Whang said she thought listening to a Korean station was only for old people.
lines.zh: 在粮仓东南方向大约五小时车程的地方，药剂师乔安·黄收听德克萨斯州达拉斯的 KKDA-730 电台。这是一家韩语电台。黄说，起初她以为听韩语电台是老年人的事。

lines.en: "But it actually was pretty interesting," she said. She said she got a lot of information and even heard Korean pop songs, known as K-pop.
lines.zh: “但其实还挺有意思的。”她说。她说她获得了很多信息，甚至还听到了韩国流行歌曲，也就是 K-pop。

lines.en: The station is owned by DK Media Group. The company also runs two Korean-language newspapers. Stephanie Min Kim is the president. She said removing AM from cars would hurt small companies like hers that broadcast in languages other than English. It is too costly to buy a license, or government permission, to broadcast in FM, she said.
lines.zh: 这家电台属于 DK 传媒集团，该公司还办着两份韩文报纸。总裁斯蒂芬妮·闵·金说，从车上取消 AM 会伤害像她这样用英语以外的语言广播的小公司。她说，购买 FM 广播的执照——也就是政府许可——太贵了。

lines.en: Kim once worked for the Korean broadcaster KBS. She said, "We feel that it is our duty to help and support our Korean immigrants integrate into American society." She said her radio station hosts discussions with experts in law, healthcare and education that help people from Korea learn about life in the U.S.
lines.zh: 金曾在韩国广播公司 KBS 工作。她说：“我们觉得帮助和支持韩国移民融入美国社会是我们的责任。”她说，她的电台邀请法律、医疗和教育方面的专家做节目讨论，帮助来自韩国的人了解美国生活。

lines.en: She said, if AM is removed from cars, the transmissions face an "existential threat." That means the existence of the stations is threatened.
lines.zh: 她说，如果车上取消 AM，这些广播就面临“生存威胁”，意思是电台的存在受到了威胁。

lines.en: Radio Caravan is another small broadcaster in Dallas. It broadcasts in Hindi, Tamil and English on AM 700. Aparna Ragnan is a radio host. She said carmakers should find a way to keep AM.
lines.zh: “大篷车电台”是达拉斯的另一家小广播公司，在 AM 700 上用印地语、泰米尔语和英语播音。阿帕娜·兰甘是一名电台主持人。她说车企应该想办法保留 AM。

lines.en: Vaibhav Sheth is the station manager. He said the sound quality of the AM stations is not a problem. He said the information that the stations provide is more important than sound quality. In addition, he notes that AM stations are important in emergencies. The emergency signals go off to alert listeners about bad weather, like a tornado, or a child who is in danger.
lines.zh: 瓦伊巴夫·谢斯是电台经理。他说 AM 电台的音质不是问题，电台提供的信息比音质更重要。此外，他指出 AM 电台在紧急情况下很重要。紧急信号会响起，提醒听众注意龙卷风之类的恶劣天气，或者有儿童遇到危险。

lines.en: "Whatever it is that's happening," he said, "it goes to the AM frequency."
lines.zh: “不管发生什么，”他说，“都会发到 AM 频率上。”

lines.en: I'm Steve Herman. And I'm Dan Friedell.
lines.zh: 我是史蒂夫·赫尔曼。我是丹·弗里德尔。

qs.q: Why are some carmakers removing AM radio from electric cars?
opts: The driving systems interfere with the AM signal.
qs.a: The driving systems interfere with the AM signal.
qs.why: "Car makers say the driving systems in electric vehicles interfere with the AM signal."

qs.q: How far does the KDHN AM signal reach?
qs.why: "the AM signal covers 160 kilometers."

qs.q: Why is AM important in emergencies?
opts: Emergency alerts go to the AM frequency.
qs.a: Emergency alerts go to the AM frequency.
qs.why: "it goes to the AM frequency."

lessons.title: Oldest US City Remains a Mystery to Many
lessons.zh: 美国最古老的城市，很多人却不知道
lessons.sum: 美国学生常学到普利茅斯和詹姆斯敦是北美最早的定居点，可早在 50 多年前，西班牙人就在佛罗里达东北角建立了圣奥古斯丁。它是美国历史最悠久、有人连续居住的非原住民城市，有 1695 年的圣马科斯城堡，以及富豪弗拉格勒建的豪华旅馆。

lines.en: Students of United States history often learn that Plymouth Rock in Massachusetts and Jamestown in Virginia were the earliest settlements in North America.
lines.zh: 学美国历史的学生常常学到，马萨诸塞州的普利茅斯岩和弗吉尼亚州的詹姆斯敦是北美最早的定居点。

lines.en: But more than 50 years earlier, the Spanish had settled in the far northeastern corner of Florida in what is now the city of St. Augustine.
lines.zh: 但早在 50 多年前，西班牙人就已经在佛罗里达州最东北角定居了，就是今天的圣奥古斯丁市。

lines.en: Despite being the oldest continuously occupied settlement founded by non-Native Americans in the U.S., St. Augustine is rarely talked about in American history classes.
lines.zh: 尽管圣奥古斯丁是美国由非原住民建立、有人连续居住时间最长的定居点，美国历史课上却很少提到它。

lines.en: "I think it's because it's Spanish colonial history that we're talking about," says Nancy Sikes-Klein, mayor of St. Augustine. "Some people might say it's Anglo biased."
lines.zh: “我想这是因为我们说的是西班牙殖民史，”圣奥古斯丁市长南希·赛克斯-克莱因说，“有些人可能会说这是英裔偏见。”

lines.en: Thomas Graham, a retired history professor at Flagler College in St. Augustine, agrees. He said his ancestors are from the Spanish period and "for the longest time, St. Augustine and Florida were part of the Spanish Empire." He added that the two have been forgotten about for a long time in history, but that it is changing.
lines.zh: 圣奥古斯丁弗拉格勒学院的退休历史学教授托马斯·格雷厄姆同意这种说法。他说他的祖先来自西班牙统治时期，“很长时间里，圣奥古斯丁和佛罗里达都是西班牙帝国的一部分”。他还说，这两者长期以来在历史上被遗忘了，但这种情况正在改变。

lines.en: The Spanish controlled St. Augustine from 1565 until 1821, except for a brief period of English rule between 1763 and 1783. St. Augustine became part of the United States in 1821 when Spain turned its Florida territories, which were too costly for Spain to keep, over to the United States.
lines.zh: 从 1565 年到 1821 年，西班牙一直控制着圣奥古斯丁，只有 1763 年到 1783 年间短暂由英国统治。1821 年，西班牙把维持成本太高的佛罗里达领地交给了美国，圣奥古斯丁从此成为美国的一部分。

lines.en: Today, St. Augustine is a small town. It covers 27.7 square kilometers and has a population of about 15,000.
lines.zh: 如今的圣奥古斯丁是一座小城，面积 27.7 平方公里，人口约 1.5 万。

lines.en: And even with centuries of Spanish rule, it is difficult to see Spain's influence on St. Augustine because most of the buildings from that time are long gone.
lines.zh: 虽然经历了几百年的西班牙统治，但在圣奥古斯丁很难看到西班牙的影响，因为那个时期的大部分建筑早已不在了。

lines.en: Graham said, "The streets are still here, the narrow streets, the small city blocks, and they survive as a part of the oldest part of St. Augustine."
lines.zh: 格雷厄姆说：“街道还在，那些狭窄的街道、小小的街区，它们作为圣奥古斯丁最古老部分的一部分保留了下来。”

lines.en: The oldest structure in St. Augustine is Castillo de San Marcos. It is a fort built by the Spanish in 1695 to protect against English attacks. The fort is now a national monument.
lines.zh: 圣奥古斯丁最古老的建筑是圣马科斯城堡。这是西班牙人在 1695 年为抵御英国人的进攻而建的堡垒，现在是国家纪念地。

lines.en: "It was designed to protect an entire town. Whoever controls the city of St. Augustine and that fortress, at the time, controlled the territory of Florida," says Chris Leverett of the National Park Service.
lines.zh: “它是为保护整座城镇而设计的。那时候，谁控制了圣奥古斯丁城和那座堡垒，谁就控制了佛罗里达的领土。”国家公园管理局的克里斯·莱弗里特说。

lines.en: The city was once a popular place for wealthy Americans to escape the difficult winters in northern U.S. states. In the 1870s, businessman Henry Flagler, a founder of Standard Oil, decided to build three world-class hotels for rich visitors. They were Hotel Ponce de Leon, Hotel Alcazar, and Hotel Cordova.
lines.zh: 这座城市曾经是富有的美国人躲避北方各州严冬的热门去处。19 世纪 70 年代，标准石油公司创始人之一、商人亨利·弗拉格勒决定为富有的游客建三座世界一流的旅馆：庞塞·德莱昂酒店、阿尔卡萨酒店和科尔多瓦酒店。

lines.en: But the rich did not stay long. Within 20 years, the rich discovered that Palm Beach had even better weather.
lines.zh: 可富人们没待多久。不到 20 年，他们发现棕榈滩的天气更好。

lines.en: Today, Hotel Ponce de Leon is Flagler College and Hotel Alcazar houses city offices and a museum. Only Hotel Cordova, the smallest of the three, is still a hotel but is now called Hotel Casa Monica.
lines.zh: 如今，庞塞·德莱昂酒店成了弗拉格勒学院，阿尔卡萨酒店里是市政办公室和一座博物馆。只有三座中最小的科尔多瓦酒店仍是旅馆，现在叫莫妮卡之家酒店。

lines.en: Still, visitors remain a main source of income for the city. More than three million people visited the St. Augustine area between July 2021 and June 2022. Many stay for just the day, but the city is looking for ways to make visitors stay longer.
lines.zh: 尽管如此，游客仍然是这座城市的主要收入来源。2021 年 7 月到 2022 年 6 月间，有 300 多万人到访圣奥古斯丁地区。很多人只待一天，市政府正在想办法让游客多待些时候。

lines.en: Mayor Sikes-Klein said, "We have so many layers of history here that we want them to stay longer so that they can explore." The city hopes to bring in even more visitors as St. Augustine becomes more widely known as the oldest continuously occupied U.S. city.
lines.zh: 赛克斯-克莱因市长说：“我们这里有这么多层次的历史，希望他们多待些时候，好好探索。”随着圣奥古斯丁作为美国有人连续居住时间最长的城市越来越广为人知，这座城市希望吸引更多游客。

lines.en: I'm Gregory Stachel.
lines.zh: 我是格雷戈里·斯塔切尔。

qs.q: Who founded St. Augustine?
qs.why: "the Spanish had settled in the far northeastern corner of Florida."

qs.q: What is the oldest structure in St. Augustine?
qs.why: "The oldest structure in St. Augustine is Castillo de San Marcos."

qs.q: What is Hotel Ponce de Leon today?
qs.why: "Today, Hotel Ponce de Leon is Flagler College."

lessons.title: Shoeshine Businesses Disappearing in the US
lessons.zh: 美国的擦鞋摊正在消失
lessons.sum: 擦鞋在美国有几百年的历史，但疫情后居家办公流行、着装更随意，纽约车站里的擦鞋摊生意大减：有的从每天擦 100 双降到 30 双。不过随着通勤族慢慢回来，店主们相信这门手艺不会彻底消失。

lines.en: Penn Station Shoe Repair and Shoe Shine is a small shoeshining business in New York City. On a recent weekday, customers sat down at the shoeshine business and pulled out newspapers and phones to read while their shoes got shined. The shoeshiners cleaned the footwear and added an oily substance to protect the shoes' leather material. When finished, the customers paid eight dollars for the work.
lines.zh: “宾州车站修鞋擦鞋店”是纽约市一家小小的擦鞋店。最近一个工作日，顾客们坐下来，掏出报纸和手机看着，等擦鞋匠给他们擦鞋。擦鞋匠把鞋擦干净，再抹上一层油性物质保护皮面。擦完后，顾客付 8 美元。

lines.en: A sign hanging at the little business reads, "We're not God, but we do save soles."
lines.zh: 小店里挂着一块牌子，上面写着：“我们不是上帝，但我们确实拯救 soles（鞋底，谐音“灵魂”）。”

lines.en: Shoeshining has a long history in the United States, dating back hundreds of years. But today, the tradition of getting a quick shine is weakening. Shoeshine stands are disappearing in cities and towns across the country.
lines.zh: 擦鞋在美国有着悠久的历史，可以追溯到几百年前。但如今，快速擦个鞋的传统正在衰落。全国各城镇的擦鞋摊正在消失。

lines.en: The COVID-19 pandemic intensified the business decline. More people work from home than in the past. And it has become popular to wear more casual work clothes. All this means fewer customers for shoeshining businesses.
lines.zh: 新冠疫情加剧了这一行业的衰落。在家工作的人比过去多了，穿更休闲的上班服也流行起来。这一切都意味着擦鞋店的顾客变少了。

lines.en: Nisan Khaimov owns the Penn Station stand. He said his stand would shine 80 to 100 shoes each workday before the pandemic. Now it is between 30 to 50 from Tuesday to Thursday and even fewer on Mondays and Fridays. The work-from-home model that is common across America is hurting his business.
lines.zh: 尼桑·海莫夫是宾州车站擦鞋摊的老板。他说疫情前，他的摊位每个工作日要擦 80 到 100 双鞋。现在周二到周四每天只有 30 到 50 双，周一和周五更少。全美国普遍的居家办公模式正在损害他的生意。

lines.en: "Until people come back to work, the problems will not be solved," said Khaimov.
lines.zh: “除非人们回来上班，否则问题解决不了。”海莫夫说。

lines.en: Rory Heenan is a 38-year-old accountant from Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. He said as a young boy he would take the train with his father on his way to work one Friday each month and watch him get a shoeshine.
lines.zh: 罗里·希南是来自宾夕法尼亚州费城的 38 岁会计师。他说小时候，每个月有一个星期五，他会跟着父亲坐火车去上班，看父亲擦鞋。

lines.en: "I would just sit here as a little guy, you know, observing," he said. "And here I am, you know, 30 years later, doing the same thing. So, it's certainly something that's passed down over time."
lines.zh: “我那时还是个小家伙，就坐在这儿看着，”他说，“你看，30 年后我在这儿做着同样的事。所以这绝对是一代代传下来的东西。”

lines.en: Across town, Jairo Cardenas is also feeling the losses. Business at Alpha Shoes Repair Corporation is down 75 percent from before the pandemic. His business used to shine 60 or 70 shoes a day. Now, on a good day, he shines shoes for 10 to 15 customers.
lines.zh: 在城市另一头，海罗·卡德纳斯也感受到了损失。阿尔法修鞋公司的生意比疫情前下降了 75%。他的店过去每天擦 60 到 70 双鞋，现在生意好的时候也只有 10 到 15 个顾客。

lines.en: Shoe repairs generally bring in more money than shines. At David Mesquita's Leather Spa, which operates five shoe repair and shine businesses in the area, the repairs are the major part of its sales. But shoeshines are still an important offering to bring people in as most shoe repair businesses do not have the service.
lines.zh: 修鞋一般比擦鞋赚得多。戴维·梅斯基塔的“皮具水疗”在这一带经营着五家修鞋擦鞋店，修鞋是主要收入。但擦鞋仍是吸引顾客的重要服务，因为大多数修鞋店不提供这项服务。

lines.en: Before the pandemic, Leather Spa had four shoeshine chairs at its business inside New York's Grand Central Terminal. It employed six shoeshiners. Together, they would complete about 120 shines a day. Now, there are three shoeshiners who do 40 or 50 shines a day at most.
lines.zh: 疫情前，“皮具水疗”在纽约中央车站里的店有四把擦鞋椅，雇了六名擦鞋匠，他们每天一共擦大约 120 双鞋。现在只有三名擦鞋匠，每天最多擦 40 到 50 双。

lines.en: But Mesquita is seeing people slowly coming back. His December 2022 shoeshine numbers were up 52 percent compared with December 2021.
lines.zh: 不过梅斯基塔看到人们在慢慢回来。他 2022 年 12 月的擦鞋数量比 2021 年 12 月增加了 52%。

lines.en: "Traffic is slowly coming back in, we're seeing the commuters come in and everything, but we're still not back 100 percent of what we were," Mesquita said.
lines.zh: “客流在慢慢回来，我们看到通勤的人回来了，但还没有百分之百恢复到以前的样子。”梅斯基塔说。

lines.en: He added that shoeshining is not something that will ever fully go away.
lines.zh: 他补充说，擦鞋这件事永远不会彻底消失。

lines.en: "People like to treat themselves," he said, "whether it's once a week or twice a week or, you know, once every two weeks. It's just nice."
lines.zh: “人们喜欢犒劳一下自己，”他说，“不管是一周一次、一周两次，还是两周一次，就是觉得舒服。”

lines.en: I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。

qs.q: Why are shoeshine businesses losing customers?
opts: More people work from home and wear casual clothes.
qs.a: More people work from home and wear casual clothes.
qs.why: "More people work from home... it has become popular to wear more casual work clothes."

qs.q: What does the sign "We're not God, but we do save soles" play with?
qs.why: sole（鞋底）和 soul（灵魂）同音。

qs.q: Why do repair shops still offer shoeshines?
qs.why: "shoeshines are still an important offering to bring people in."

lessons.title: New Zealand Proposes Taxing Cow Burps, Angering Farmers
lessons.zh: 新西兰拟对牛打嗝征税，农民愤怒
lessons.sum: 新西兰约一半的温室气体来自农场——牛羊打嗝和排尿产生甲烷和一氧化二氮。政府提出从 2025 年起对农场排放征税，称这是世界首创，收入将全部返还农业。农民团体批评这会毁掉小城镇，2003 年类似方案也曾被放弃。

lines.en: New Zealand's government recently proposed taxing the greenhouse gases from farm animals as part of a plan to fight climate change. Farm animals produce gases through natural processes like burping and urinating.
lines.zh: 新西兰政府最近提议，对农场牲畜产生的温室气体征税，作为应对气候变化计划的一部分。牲畜通过打嗝、排尿等自然过程产生气体。

lines.en: The government said the taxes would be a world's first. They said that farmers should be able to get the money back by charging more for climate-friendly products.
lines.zh: 政府说这种税将是世界首创。他们说，农民应该可以通过提高气候友好型产品的售价把钱赚回来。

lines.en: But farmers quickly criticized the plan.
lines.zh: 但农民们很快就批评了这个计划。

lines.en: Federated Farmers is the industry's main political support group. It said the plan would "rip the guts out of small-town New Zealand" and see farms replaced with trees.
lines.zh: “联合农民会”是该行业主要的政治支持团体。它说这个计划会“掏空新西兰的小城镇”，让农场被树林取代。

lines.en: Andrew Hoggard, the group's president, said farmers had been trying to work with the government for more than two years. They were working on a plan to reduce greenhouse gas production that would not decrease food production. Hoggard said, "Our plan was to keep farmers farming." But, with the taxes, he said, farmers would be quickly selling their farms.
lines.zh: 该团体主席安德鲁·霍加德说，两年多来，农民一直在努力和政府合作，制定一个减少温室气体排放又不减少粮食生产的计划。霍加德说：“我们的计划是让农民继续种地。”但他说，有了这些税，农民们会很快卖掉自己的农场。

lines.en: The conservative ACT Party is the main opposition group. Members of the party said the plan would increase worldwide greenhouse gas production by moving farming to other countries that were less efficient at making food.
lines.zh: 保守派的 ACT 党是主要的反对党。该党成员说，这个计划会把农业转移到食物生产效率较低的其他国家，从而增加全球的温室气体排放。

lines.en: New Zealand's farming industry is very important for its economy. Milk products, including those used to make milk for baby food in China, are the nation's largest export earner.
lines.zh: 农业对新西兰经济非常重要。奶制品——包括用于在中国制作婴儿奶粉的产品——是这个国家最大的出口创汇产品。

lines.en: There are just 5 million people in New Zealand. But the country has some 26 million sheep and 10 million farm animals producing milk and meat.
lines.zh: 新西兰只有 500 万人口，却有约 2600 万只羊和 1000 万头产奶产肉的牲畜。

lines.en: About half of New Zealand's greenhouse gas comes from farms. Farm animals produce gasses that warm the planet like methane and nitrous oxide from burping and urinating.
lines.zh: 新西兰约一半的温室气体来自农场。牲畜通过打嗝和排尿产生让地球变暖的气体，比如甲烷和一氧化二氮。

lines.en: The New Zealand government wants to reduce greenhouse gas production and make the country carbon neutral by 2050. Under the government's proposal, farmers would start to pay for greenhouse gas production in 2025. The price has yet to be finalized.
lines.zh: 新西兰政府希望减少温室气体排放，到 2050 年实现碳中和。按照政府的提议，农民将从 2025 年开始为温室气体排放付费，价格尚未最终确定。

lines.en: Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern said all the money collected from the proposed tax would be put back into the industry. It would support new technology, research, and payments for farmers.
lines.zh: 总理杰辛达·阿德恩说，拟议税收所得的所有资金都会重新投入这个行业，用于支持新技术、研究和对农民的补贴。

lines.en: Agriculture Minister Damien O'Connor said New Zealand farmers were already experiencing the impact of climate change with periods of dry weather and flooding. "Taking the lead on agricultural emissions is both good for the environment and our economy," he said.
lines.zh: 农业部长达米恩·奥康纳说，新西兰农民已经在经历气候变化的影响，出现了干旱和洪水。“在农业排放问题上带头，对环境和我们的经济都有好处。”他说。

lines.en: The proposal is similar to another unsuccessful proposal made in 2003 to tax farm animals for their methane production. Back then, farmers greatly opposed the idea and political opponents criticized it. And the government dropped the plan.
lines.zh: 这个提议和 2003 年另一个对牲畜甲烷排放征税、最终失败的提议类似。当时农民强烈反对，政治对手也提出批评，政府就放弃了这个计划。

lines.en: The debate in New Zealand is part of a larger international discussion on the effects of farming on the environment and the steps some say are needed to reduce its impact.
lines.zh: 新西兰的这场争论，是一场更大的国际讨论的一部分：农业对环境有什么影响，以及一些人认为需要采取哪些措施来减少这种影响。

lines.en: In the European nation of the Netherlands, farmers have blocked large, busy roads with farming products and vehicles. They did so to protest government proposals to decrease the production of greenhouse gases.
lines.zh: 在欧洲国家荷兰，农民们用农产品和农用车辆堵住了繁忙的大路，抗议政府减少温室气体排放的提议。

lines.en: I'm Jill Robbins.
lines.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

qs.q: Where does about half of New Zealand's greenhouse gas come from?
qs.why: "About half of New Zealand's greenhouse gas comes from farms."

qs.q: How many sheep does New Zealand have?
qs.why: "the country has some 26 million sheep."

qs.q: What would the government do with the tax money?
opts: put it back into the farming industry
qs.a: put it back into the farming industry
qs.why: "all the money collected... would be put back into the industry."

lessons.title: US Workers Secretly Take 'Workations'
lessons.zh: 美国员工偷偷“工作度假”
lessons.sum: “workation”由 work 和 vacation 组成，指员工不告诉老板，在度假地远程工作。调查显示约 29% 的美国员工这样做过，Z 世代比例更高。一些旅馆推出工作度假套餐吸引远程办公者；培训师认为，快乐的员工效率更高。

lines.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle report.
lines.zh: 这里是 VOA 慢速英语《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: In the United States, a quiet change is happening at work. Many workers are taking "workations." This is when employees work remotely from a vacation place without telling their boss.
lines.zh: 在美国，职场上正在悄悄发生一个变化：很多员工在“工作度假”（workation），也就是员工不告诉老板，在度假的地方远程工作。

lines.en: Workation combines the words "work" and "vacation." Another example is "staycation." This word describes when a person decides to stay home during vacation rather than traveling.
lines.zh: Workation 由 work（工作）和 vacation（度假）两个词合成。另一个例子是 staycation，指一个人假期决定待在家里而不是出去旅行。

lines.en: During the COVID-19 pandemic, teleworking and remote work led people to re-think parts of their professional and personal lives. This increased the popularity of workations.
lines.zh: 新冠疫情期间，居家办公和远程工作让人们重新思考自己职业生活和个人生活的某些方面，这让工作度假变得更流行了。

lines.en: Corporate trainer Rudi Riekstins works with businesses and employees. He told VOA the pandemic made people question what they really wanted in their work and personal lives.
lines.zh: 企业培训师鲁迪·里克斯廷斯与企业和员工打交道。他告诉 VOA，疫情让人们开始思考，自己在工作和个人生活中真正想要的是什么。

lines.en: Riekstins said that as a result, some people started to feel like they wanted to avoid the busy, work-driven life sometimes described as a "rat race." And as people went back to work, they sought to have more control.
lines.zh: 里克斯廷斯说，结果有些人开始想远离那种忙碌、被工作驱使、有时被称为“老鼠赛跑”的生活。人们回去上班时，也希望能有更多自主权。

lines.en: One study by hospitality management company Mews found that about 29 percent of employees said they had worked remotely from a vacation place without telling employers. The study, carried out by market research company OnePoll, involved 1,000 American travelers and 1,000 American hotel workers.
lines.zh: 酒店管理公司 Mews 的一项研究发现，约 29% 的员工说他们曾在度假地远程工作而没有告诉雇主。这项研究由市场研究公司 OnePoll 进行，调查了 1000 名美国旅行者和 1000 名美国酒店员工。

lines.en: The research suggested that 52 percent of employed Americans would use vacation travels as a chance to work remotely.
lines.zh: 研究表明，52% 有工作的美国人会把度假旅行当作远程工作的机会。

lines.en: Riekstins said workations can be good for both workers and employers. For example, a workation can improve worker happiness by making life more interesting.
lines.zh: 里克斯廷斯说，工作度假对员工和雇主都有好处。比如，工作度假能让生活更有趣，从而提高员工的幸福感。

lines.en: "Productivity goes up by 70 percent on average when people are happier when they are working. And we see happy people when they're traveling because they feel stimulated," said Riekstins. "You start to be stimulated emotionally, mentally, and physically, and then when you show up to work, you are more creative."
lines.zh: “人们工作时更快乐，生产率平均会提高 70%。而人们旅行时很快乐，因为受到了刺激，”里克斯廷斯说，“你在情感上、精神上、身体上都受到激发，然后去工作时，你就更有创造力。”

lines.en: Some hotel companies offer workation specials to boost business, especially during slower times.
lines.zh: 一些酒店公司推出工作度假优惠来提振生意，尤其是在淡季。

lines.en: Sandy Wieber owns the 17-room Bayfront Marin House in St. Augustine, Florida. She also rents out eight beach cottages. Wieber herself worked remotely for eight years and now offers workation services that she would have liked using.
lines.zh: 桑迪·威伯在佛罗里达州圣奥古斯丁经营着有 17 间客房的“海湾马林之家”，还出租八间海滨小屋。威伯自己远程工作过八年，现在提供她当年也想用的工作度假服务。

lines.en: In Georgetown, Maine, the 13-room Gray Havens Inn, which sits near the water, created a special program that aims to appeal to younger, remote workers.
lines.zh: 在缅因州乔治敦，紧邻海边、有 13 间客房的灰港旅馆推出了一个特别项目，想吸引年轻的远程工作者。

lines.en: "We have a lot of younger travelers, but not as many as we would like. This is part of the reason we started this program," said innkeeper Ali Barrionuevo. "I read about other hotels doing it, so we put it out there to see if we could attract people who were teleworking."
lines.zh: “我们有很多年轻旅客，但没有我们希望的那么多。这是我们推出这个项目的部分原因，”旅馆老板阿里·巴里奥努埃沃说，“我读到别的酒店在这么做，于是我们也推出来，看看能不能吸引远程办公的人。”

lines.en: The special includes 25 percent off the room rate for a seven-day stay. The room comes with daily breakfast, a welcome gift, and some food and drinks. Barrionuevo also provides advice and support for seeing the area and taking part in activities.
lines.zh: 这个优惠包括住满七天房价打七五折，房间含每日早餐、一份欢迎礼物和一些食品饮料。巴里奥努埃沃还为客人游览当地和参加活动提供建议和帮助。

lines.en: "When they are done working, we help them find out what they like and create itineraries to help them see the things they want or should see with limited time," she added.
lines.zh: “他们工作结束后，我们帮他们了解自己喜欢什么，制定行程，帮助他们在有限的时间里看到想看或者值得看的东西。”她补充说。

lines.en: A public opinion study carried out by ResumeBuilder.com found that one in six Gen Z workers used a false online background of a home office to fool their employer.
lines.zh: ResumeBuilder.com 的一项民意调查发现，每六个 Z 世代员工中就有一个用过虚假的线上家庭办公室背景来骗雇主。

lines.en: Gen Z is a name for the generation of people born in the late 1990s through the early 2000s.
lines.zh: Z 世代指出生于 20 世纪 90 年代末到 21 世纪初的那一代人。

lines.en: Another study from 2023, found that 51 percent of Gen Z workers said they had worked remotely from a vacation place, but did not tell their employers.
lines.zh: 2023 年的另一项研究发现，51% 的 Z 世代员工说他们曾在度假地远程工作，但没有告诉雇主。

lines.en: Riekstins noted that not all workations have to be secret. Some employers permit workations as long as employees get their work done. "A number of the organizations that I do currently work with don't care where their employees work, as long as they produce the results and it's done within the office hours."
lines.zh: 里克斯廷斯指出，并不是所有的工作度假都必须偷偷摸摸。有些雇主只要员工完成工作就允许工作度假。“我目前合作的一些机构并不在乎员工在哪里工作，只要他们出成果，并且在办公时间内完成就行。”

lines.en: Riekstins said he thinks more companies should accept remote work situations as a way to improve worker satisfaction and business productivity.
lines.zh: 里克斯廷斯说，他认为更多公司应该接受远程工作，把它当作提高员工满意度和企业生产率的一种方式。

lines.en: He said employers should be asking: Are workers happy? Are they able to work anywhere and still get the job done? Can companies get better products and better results with happier workers? And will this make them stay at the company?
lines.zh: 他说，雇主应该问：员工开心吗？他们能不能在任何地方工作还把活干完？员工更开心，公司能不能得到更好的产品和更好的结果？这会不会让他们留在公司？

lines.en: And that's the Health & Lifestyle Report. I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 以上就是《健康与生活》节目。我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: What is a "workation"?
opts: working remotely from a vacation place
a long holiday with no work
qs.a: working remotely from a vacation place
qs.why: "This is when employees work remotely from a vacation place."

qs.q: What is a "staycation"?
qs.why: "when a person decides to stay home during vacation rather than traveling."

opts: used a false home office background online
qs.a: used a false home office background online

lessons.title: Little-known Garden Supports US Nursery Industry
lessons.zh: 鲜为人知的花园支撑着美国苗圃业
lessons.sum: 位于华盛顿的美国国家树木园占地 183 公顷，很多美国人从没听说过。这里的政府科学家培育了 650 多种植物，保存了约 70 万份种子样本，支持每年销售额 138 亿美元的观赏植物产业，也为应对气候变化保护植物基因。

lines.en: Placed among the busy streets of Washington, D.C. is a large public garden that many Americans have never heard of.
lines.zh: 在华盛顿繁忙的街道之间，有一座很多美国人从没听说过的大型公共花园。

lines.en: The U.S. National Arboretum includes a collection of flowering plants called azaleas, a field of native plants called ferns, and flowering trees in the dogwood tree area.
lines.zh: 美国国家树木园里有一片叫杜鹃花的开花植物，一片原生蕨类植物，还有一个种着开花树木的山茱萸园。

lines.en: Government scientists are in charge of the 183-hectare area. Their main goal is to strengthen the U.S. economy by making sure an important kind of agriculture, called the nursery industry, continues to perform well.
lines.zh: 政府科学家负责管理这片 183 公顷的园地。他们的主要目标是确保一种重要的农业——苗圃业——持续良好发展，从而增强美国经济。

lines.en: "What we do is support the American nursery industry … which is really one of the largest forms of agriculture," said Richard Olsen, director of the National Arboretum.
lines.zh: “我们做的是支持美国苗圃业……它确实是规模最大的农业形式之一。”国家树木园主任理查德·奥尔森说。

lines.en: He said that different kinds of agriculture industry like ornamental landscapes, horticulture, and turf, "… all of that occurs in every county, in every state of the union. So, it forms a large portion of American agriculture and therefore, an important part of the economy."
lines.zh: 他说，观赏景观、园艺和草坪等不同的农业产业“……在联邦每个州的每个县都有。所以它在美国农业中占很大一部分，因此也是经济的重要组成部分”。

lines.en: The most recent numbers from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, or USDA, show that the ornamental and landscape plant industry creates $13.8 billion in sales each year.
lines.zh: 美国农业部的最新数据显示，观赏和景观植物产业每年创造 138 亿美元的销售额。

lines.en: The garden was established by Congress in 1927. It plays a leading part in researching and developing plants like trees, shrubs, flowers, and grasses.
lines.zh: 这座花园于 1927 年由国会设立，在研究和开发树木、灌木、花卉和草类等植物方面起着领先作用。

lines.en: Olsen called the arboretum a "science-based research facility and public garden." He said the place has bred or released around 650-plus plants. They include more than 450 azaleas for landscaping, but also trees like maples, American elms, and hemlocks.
lines.zh: 奥尔森称树木园是一个“以科学为基础的研究机构和公共花园”。他说这里已经培育或发布了 650 多种植物，其中包括 450 多种用于园林的杜鹃花，还有枫树、美国榆和铁杉等树木。

lines.en: The arboretum is home to one of the largest collections of preserved seeds in the world. The National Arboretum Herbarium houses around 700,000 example seeds. They include seeds from plants that the USDA considers as economically important.
lines.zh: 树木园拥有世界上最大的种子保存库之一。国家树木园标本馆收藏着约 70 万份种子样本，包括美国农业部认为有重要经济价值的植物的种子。

lines.en: Scientists collect many genetically different seeds within a kind of plant from both native and non-native plants. The reason for collecting that data is to protect plants from harmful situations like climate change, changed environments, or other new and possible risks.
lines.zh: 科学家们从原生和非原生植物中，收集同一种植物里基因各不相同的种子。收集这些资料的原因，是保护植物免受气候变化、环境改变或其他新出现的潜在风险的伤害。

lines.en: Kevin Conrad is a lead plant scientist at the arboretum. He said there are examples in USDA history where a gene from a plant like wheat or grapes has been able to solve a disaster or a collapse of an important agricultural crop.
lines.zh: 凯文·康拉德是树木园的首席植物科学家。他说，美国农业部历史上有过这样的例子：小麦或葡萄等植物的一个基因，帮助化解了一场灾难，或挽救了一种重要农作物的崩溃。

lines.en: While the scientists do their work, the public is free to explore the arboretum grounds. About 600,000 people visit the gardens each year. That is a small amount compared to the 25 million who visit the monuments and places in the National Mall.
lines.zh: 科学家们工作的同时，公众可以免费游览树木园。每年约有 60 万人参观这里的花园。和参观国家广场纪念碑和景点的 2500 万人相比，这个数字很小。

lines.en: Although many people may not know it, the arboretum has had a hand in developing many of the plants that are part of American landscaping.
lines.zh: 虽然很多人可能不知道，但美国园林中的许多植物，都有树木园参与培育。

lines.en: Conrad says the goal is to green the landscape. And he added, "It's to create a welcoming, secure, safe, beautiful, calming landscape for the public."
lines.zh: 康拉德说，目标是让景观绿起来。他还说：“是为公众创造一个温馨、安全、美丽、让人平静的环境。”

lines.en: I'm Gregory Stachel.
lines.zh: 我是格雷戈里·斯塔切尔。

qs.q: What is the main goal of the National Arboretum scientists?
opts: to support the nursery industry and the economy
qs.a: to support the nursery industry and the economy
qs.why: "Their main goal is to strengthen the U.S. economy by making sure... the nursery industry, continues to perform well."

qs.q: How many seed examples does the Herbarium hold?
qs.why: "houses around 700,000 example seeds."

qs.q: Why do scientists collect many different seeds?
opts: to protect plants from risks like climate change
qs.a: to protect plants from risks like climate change
qs.why: "to protect plants from harmful situations like climate change."

lessons.title: Some Americans Want Fewer Grass Lawns
lessons.zh: 一些美国人想少种草坪
lessons.sum: 越来越多美国人用原生植物取代草坪，这叫“再野化”。草坪被称为“生态死区”：不给野生动物提供食物和庇护，还耗费大量水和化学品。马里兰州的克劳奇夫妇因此和业主协会打了三年官司，最终促成州里立法，允许居民种原生植物。

lines.en: The area in front of Janet and Jeffrey Crouch's house in Columbia, Maryland, does not look usual for their neighborhood.
lines.zh: 珍妮特和杰弗里·克劳奇夫妇在马里兰州哥伦比亚的房前，看起来和他们的街区不太一样。

lines.en: That is because the Crouches do not have a grass lawn. Instead, they have some small trees and many native plants.
lines.zh: 这是因为克劳奇夫妇没有草坪，取而代之的是一些小树和许多原生植物。

lines.en: Lawns are areas around a house or in a park that are covered with short grass. In recent years, support for replacing lawns with native plants has been increasing in the United States. The process is called rewilding.
lines.zh: 草坪是房子周围或公园里覆盖着矮草的区域。近年来，在美国，支持用原生植物替代草坪的人越来越多。这个过程叫“再野化”。

lines.en: In fact, the number of Americans planning to turn part of their lawn to native wildflowers doubled between 2019 and 2021. That information comes from the National Gardening Survey of 2,061 U.S. adults. In 2019, the percentage was nine percent. By 2021, it rose to 19 percent.
lines.zh: 事实上，计划把部分草坪改种原生野花的美国人数量在 2019 年到 2021 年间翻了一番。这个信息来自对 2061 名美国成年人进行的全国园艺调查：2019 年比例为 9%，到 2021 年升至 19%。

lines.en: Paul Robbins is the writer of Lawn People: How Grasses, Weeds, and Chemicals Make Us Who We Are.
lines.zh: 保罗·罗宾斯是《草坪之人：草、杂草和化学品如何塑造了我们》一书的作者。

lines.en: He said that most people would prefer not to have lawns. "But they feel that they need to have them, or that they can't do anything about it." He added that many homeowners feel they should have lawns to please their neighbors.
lines.zh: 他说，大多数人宁愿不要草坪。“但他们觉得必须有，或者觉得对此无能为力。”他还说，许多房主觉得应该有草坪来让邻居满意。

lines.en: It can be costly to keep a lawn looking good and green. But the Crouches had to spend much more money for the right not to have one.
lines.zh: 要让草坪保持好看、翠绿，可能花费不菲。但克劳奇夫妇为了不要草坪的权利，花的钱要多得多。

lines.en: People living in a house next to them complained to their homeowner's association, or HOA. The neighbors did not like that the Crouches did not have a grass lawn. HOAs can make rules about the plants that homeowners in a neighborhood are permitted to grow. Many HOAs require grass lawns.
lines.zh: 住在他们隔壁的人向业主协会（HOA）投诉，邻居不满克劳奇家没有草坪。业主协会可以规定社区房主可以种哪些植物，很多业主协会要求必须有草坪。

lines.en: The HOA ordered the Crouches to pull out their native plants and put in grass. However, they refused.
lines.zh: 业主协会命令克劳奇夫妇拔掉原生植物、种上草。但他们拒绝了。

lines.en: "We knew we were doing things that were beneficial for the environment," said Janet Crouch. She told VOA that it seemed wrong to put in only grass, which she called an environmental dead zone.
lines.zh: “我们知道自己做的事对环境有益。”珍妮特·克劳奇说。她告诉 VOA，只种草似乎是错的，她称草坪为“生态死区”。

lines.en: Lawns are called environmental dead zones in part because they provide no food or shelter for wildlife. They also do not support pollinators like birds, bees, and butterflies. Bee populations have been getting smaller in North America and may be getting smaller around the world.
lines.zh: 草坪被称为生态死区，部分原因是它们不给野生动物提供食物和庇护，也不支持鸟、蜜蜂、蝴蝶等传粉者。北美的蜜蜂数量一直在减少，全世界可能也是如此。

lines.en: Ted Steinberg is the writer of American Green: The Obsessive Quest for the Perfect Lawn. He said there are other reasons that lawns are bad for the environment.
lines.zh: 特德·斯坦伯格是《美国绿：对完美草坪的执念》一书的作者。他说草坪对环境不利还有其他原因。

lines.en: He said they require a lot of water and chemicals. Large amounts of water can remove nutrients from the soil.
lines.zh: 他说草坪需要大量的水和化学品，大量的水会把土壤里的养分冲走。

lines.en: Steinberg said that after the water removes the nutrients, people buy even more chemicals to put on their lawns. Scientists say some of these chemicals might cause cancer and other health problems.
lines.zh: 斯坦伯格说，水把养分冲走后，人们又会买更多化学品撒在草坪上。科学家说，其中一些化学品可能致癌并引起其他健康问题。

lines.en: Nancy Lawson is the writer of The Humane Gardener and Wildscapes. She is also Janet Crouch's sister and the person who urged the Crouches to put in native plants.
lines.zh: 南希·劳森是《人道园丁》和《野景》的作者。她也是珍妮特·克劳奇的姐妹，正是她劝克劳奇夫妇种原生植物的。

lines.en: Lawson said there are over 16 million hectares of grass lawns in the U.S. That means lawns use more water than any other irrigated crop in the country.
lines.zh: 劳森说，美国有超过 1600 万公顷的草坪。这意味着草坪的用水量超过了全国任何其他灌溉作物。

lines.en: The Crouches' battle against their HOA took three years. They say they spent $60,000 fighting to keep their natural garden. They won. Because of their efforts, the state of Maryland passed a law that lets people grow native plants instead of grass, no matter what their HOA wants.
lines.zh: 克劳奇夫妇和业主协会的斗争持续了三年。他们说，为了保住自己的自然花园，他们花了 6 万美元。他们赢了。由于他们的努力，马里兰州通过了一项法律，允许人们种原生植物代替草坪，不管业主协会怎么想。

lines.en: I'm Andrew Smith.
lines.zh: 我是安德鲁·史密斯。

qs.q: What is "rewilding"?
qs.why: "support for replacing lawns with native plants... The process is called rewilding."

qs.q: Why are lawns called "environmental dead zones"?
opts: They give no food or shelter to wildlife.
qs.a: They give no food or shelter to wildlife.
qs.why: "they provide no food or shelter for wildlife."

qs.q: What happened after the Crouches won?
opts: Maryland passed a law allowing native plants.
qs.a: Maryland passed a law allowing native plants.
qs.why: "the state of Maryland passed a law that lets people grow native plants instead of grass."

lessons.title: How to Keep a Betta Fish
lessons.zh: 怎样养斗鱼
lessons.sum: 斗鱼色彩鲜艳，是美国人喜爱的宠物，能活三到五年。养斗鱼需要至少 11 升（最好 19 升）的鱼缸、底沙、过滤器、加热器（水温 24～28℃），自来水要先除氯；每天喂一两次含肉或昆虫的饲料，每一两周换四分之一的水。雄鱼好斗，要单独养。

lines.en: Betta fish are known for their bright colors. They are popular with Americans as pets.
lines.zh: 斗鱼以色彩鲜艳出名，是美国人喜爱的宠物。

lines.en: They are often kept alone in a small tank. Male fish are prized for their stronger colors and beautiful fins.
lines.zh: 它们常常被单独养在小鱼缸里。雄鱼因为颜色更鲜艳、鳍更漂亮而备受珍视。

lines.en: With good care, bettas live three to five years, but some are known to live 10 years.
lines.zh: 照料得好的话，斗鱼能活三到五年，有些甚至能活 10 年。

lines.en: In the northern parts of the world, winter has arrived, and some people might be wondering what to do with their time now that they are indoors. Keeping a betta fish can be a fun hobby that does not involve going outside. It also does not require too much skill, but you do have to be willing to learn.
lines.zh: 在世界北部地区，冬天已经到了，有些人可能在想，待在室内时该做点什么。养斗鱼可以是一个不用出门的有趣爱好。它也不需要太多技巧，但你得愿意学习。

lines.en: But how do you take care of a betta fish?
lines.zh: 那么，怎样照顾斗鱼呢？

lines.en: First, betta fish need a home. A tank that holds at least 11 liters of water is suggested although 19 liters is better. Larger tanks are better because the water needs to be changed less often and provides a healthier environment for the fish.
lines.zh: 第一，斗鱼需要一个家。建议用至少能装 11 升水的鱼缸，19 升更好。鱼缸越大越好，因为换水的次数更少，还能为鱼提供更健康的环境。

lines.en: Second, the tank needs small rocks or sand at the bottom. In the pet fish industry, this is called substrate. A few centimeters at the bottom are all that is needed. Clean the rocks or sand with running water without soap until it runs clear before adding them to the tank.
lines.zh: 第二，鱼缸底部需要铺小石子或沙子，宠物鱼行业称之为“底砂”，铺几厘米就够了。放进鱼缸前，用流水（不加肥皂）把石子或沙子冲洗到水变清为止。

lines.en: Third, a filter is needed to purify the water. Many people keep bettas without filters. But the fish should be raised with a filter to stay healthy. Follow the filter's guidelines and choose a filter that is the right size for the tank.
lines.zh: 第三，需要一个过滤器来净化水。很多人养斗鱼不用过滤器，但要让鱼保持健康，应该用过滤器。按照过滤器的说明，选一个和鱼缸大小相配的。

lines.en: Fourth, a heater is suggested to keep your fish in good condition. These fish prefer warmer water, usually between 24 and 28 degrees Celsius. Pet stores sell heaters for fish. Choose the right size for your aquarium and follow its guidelines, or instructions, to set it up.
lines.zh: 第四，建议用加热器让鱼保持良好状态。这种鱼喜欢较暖的水，通常在 24 到 28 摄氏度之间。宠物店有卖鱼用加热器。选一个适合你鱼缸大小的，按照说明安装。

lines.en: A light and decorations are the final details to set up your tank. A light may not be necessary if the room receives enough natural light. But an electric light might be helpful if you wish to grow plants in the tank. If real plants seem like too much work, plastic plants work as well. You can also find other decorations like rocks, or wood pieces. Just make sure they are safe for fish.
lines.zh: 灯和装饰是布置鱼缸的最后细节。如果房间自然光足够，灯可能不是必需的。但如果你想在鱼缸里种植物，电灯可能会有帮助。如果觉得真植物太麻烦，塑料植物也可以。你还可以找到石头、木块之类的其他装饰，只要确保它们对鱼安全就行。

lines.en: The quality of the water is important to keeping a fish alive and healthy. The filter and heater will do a lot to keep the water safe for the fish, but there are additional steps you should take.
lines.zh: 水质对鱼的存活和健康很重要。过滤器和加热器能在很大程度上保证水对鱼是安全的，但你还应该再做一些事。

lines.en: Make sure the water you add to the tank is safe for fish. Tap water can be used. But it usually contains a chlorine-based chemical harmful to fish, so additional steps need to be taken.
lines.zh: 确保你加进鱼缸的水对鱼是安全的。可以用自来水，但自来水通常含有一种对鱼有害的含氯化学物质，所以需要额外处理。

lines.en: Krista Keller is a professor at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign College of Veterinary Medicine. Writing online in 2019, she said, "If tap water is used in the tank, it is recommended to use a dechlorinating product and test for heavy metals."
lines.zh: 克丽斯塔·凯勒是伊利诺伊大学厄巴纳-香槟分校兽医学院的教授。她在 2019 年的一篇网文中写道：“如果鱼缸用的是自来水，建议使用除氯产品，并检测重金属。”

lines.en: Pet stores sell dechlorinating chemicals and they are easy to use. Just follow the instructions on the container. Stores also sell home water testing products. But many fish stores are happy to test your water if you bring in a small amount. They can also provide advice on keeping fish in your area's water.
lines.zh: 宠物店有卖除氯剂，用起来很简单，按照瓶上的说明做就行。商店也卖家用水质检测产品。不过很多鱼店很乐意帮你检测水，只要你带一点水过去。他们还能就用你所在地区的水养鱼给你提些建议。

lines.en: After setting up your tank, there are a few more things to consider. You will need to feed your fish and change its water.
lines.zh: 布置好鱼缸后，还有几件事要考虑：你得喂鱼、给它换水。

lines.en: There are many choices for food. There are pellets, frozen whole foods, freeze-dried foods, and live food. Pet stores will carry many of these. Feed your fish once to twice a day. Whatever food you choose, make sure it contains meat or insects because that is what bettas eat in the wild.
lines.zh: 饲料有很多选择：颗粒饲料、冷冻整只食物、冻干食物和活饵。宠物店都有很多。每天喂一到两次。不管选哪种，确保里面有肉或昆虫，因为斗鱼在野外就吃这些。

lines.en: It is suggested to change one fourth of your tank's water once every week or two. Remove the old water and add fresh water. Your filter also may require some additional cleaning every month or so.
lines.zh: 建议每一到两周换鱼缸四分之一的水：把旧水抽掉，加入新水。过滤器大概每个月也需要额外清洗一次。

lines.en: Male betta fish are kept alone because they are aggressive fish. Another name for bettas is Siamese fighting fish. Males should never be kept with other betta males. If you have a larger tank with other fish, they might live together peacefully. But know that male betta fish often attack other fish and may have to live separately.
lines.zh: 雄斗鱼要单独养，因为它们很凶。斗鱼的另一个名字是“暹罗斗鱼”。雄鱼绝不能和其他雄斗鱼养在一起。如果你有个大鱼缸，里面有别的鱼，它们也许能和平相处。但要知道，雄斗鱼常常攻击其他鱼，可能得分开养。

lines.en: Female betta fish can live with other fish peacefully. A group of females can be kept too. Make sure they have a tank that is large enough and a filter designed for the tank's size.
lines.zh: 雌斗鱼可以和其他鱼和平相处，一群雌鱼也可以养在一起。只要确保鱼缸足够大，过滤器适合鱼缸大小就行。

lines.en: I'm Jill Robbins.
lines.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

qs.q: What water temperature do bettas prefer?
qs.why: "usually between 24 and 28 degrees Celsius."

qs.q: Why must you treat tap water?
opts: It contains chlorine that harms fish.
qs.a: It contains chlorine that harms fish.
qs.why: "it usually contains a chlorine-based chemical harmful to fish."

qs.q: Why are male bettas kept alone?
qs.why: "Male betta fish are kept alone because they are aggressive fish."

lessons.title: Sharing Our Loneliness May Help Us Feel Less Lonely
lessons.zh: 分享孤独，也许会让我们不那么孤独
lessons.sum: 娜塔莉·加勒特编了一本书《孤独故事》，请 22 位作家讲述独处的喜悦与挣扎：失去亲人、移民失去文化、疫情中与家人朝夕相处反而没有“独处时间”。孤独会危害身心健康，研究显示疫情后 36% 的美国人感到严重孤独。

lines.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle report.
lines.zh: 这里是 VOA 慢速英语《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: In English, there is an expression that goes like this: Laugh and the world laughs with you, cry and you cry alone. It suggests that people do not want to share in the sadness of others.
lines.zh: 英语里有句俗话：你笑，全世界和你一起笑；你哭，只有你独自哭泣。它暗示人们不愿分担别人的悲伤。

lines.en: But what if sharing our sadness actually helps us feel better? That was the goal of Natalie Eve Garrett when she thought of collecting stories about loneliness.
lines.zh: 可如果分享悲伤其实能让我们感觉好些呢？娜塔莉·伊芙·加勒特想到收集关于孤独的故事时，目的就在于此。

lines.en: In the book, The Lonely Stories: 22 Celebrated Writers on the Joys & Struggles of Being Alone, Garrett wanted to share personal stories of loneliness. Garrett said she hopes the stories give people suffering from loneliness comfort and perhaps even joy.
lines.zh: 在《孤独故事：22 位著名作家谈独处的喜悦与挣扎》一书中，加勒特想分享关于孤独的个人故事。加勒特说，她希望这些故事能给饱受孤独之苦的人带来安慰，甚至也许带来喜悦。

lines.en: "I think we all have felt alone. We all feel lonely. And we all will continue to feel lonely sometimes. I think when we read about varied experiences it can be a way of using loneliness and aloneness to connect with each other. And that was really my hope with the book."
lines.zh: “我想我们都感到过孤单，都感到过寂寞，以后有时也还会感到寂寞。我认为，当我们读到各种不同的经历时，它可以成为一种利用寂寞和孤单来彼此连接的方式。这正是我对这本书的希望。”

lines.en: The writers and stories in this collection are all very different. Some are tragic, such as the death of a loved one. While others are lighter, such as feeling alone at a Star Trek event. This variety is something Garrett wanted readers to also experience.
lines.zh: 这本集子里的作家和故事都很不一样。有些很悲伤，比如失去亲人；有些则比较轻松，比如在一场《星际迷航》活动上感到孤单。加勒特也希望读者体验到这种多样性。

lines.en: The book project was sold in 2019. And then COVID-19 spread around the world. Suddenly isolation became a part of nearly everyone's lives. People were separated from friends, family members, co-workers, and neighbors.
lines.zh: 这本书的出版项目在 2019 年谈成。接着新冠病毒传遍世界。突然之间，隔离成了几乎每个人生活的一部分。人们和朋友、家人、同事、邻居分开了。

lines.en: At the same time, many people were forced to be around their immediate families all the time. For some, this led to a different kind of loneliness – a loneliness for oneself. The book The Lonely Stories also deals with the challenges of a lack of solitude, or as we often call it, alone time.
lines.zh: 同时，很多人被迫一直和直系亲属待在一起。对一些人来说，这带来了另一种孤独——渴望拥有自己的孤独。《孤独故事》这本书也谈到了缺少独处——也就是我们常说的“一个人的时间”——带来的挑战。

lines.en: Garrett talked about the difference between loneliness and solitude.
lines.zh: 加勒特谈到了寂寞和独处的区别。

lines.en: "They're not the same. I, you know, I think of loneliness as feeling of lack. Solitude, I think, is chosen whereas loneliness happens to us."
lines.zh: “它们不一样。我认为寂寞是一种缺失的感觉。而独处是选择的，寂寞则是发生在我们身上的。”

lines.en: A writer and a painter, Garrett found being in quarantine with her two young children to be both good and bad. She was able to spend much time with her family. But this also meant she did not have time to paint. When talking about the lack of time to herself, Garrett used the words "longing" and "crave" – both mean to deeply want something.
lines.zh: 加勒特是一位作家和画家。她觉得和两个年幼的孩子一起隔离在家有好有坏：她能和家人共度很多时光，但这也意味着她没时间画画。谈到缺少自己的时间时，加勒特用了 longing 和 crave 两个词，都表示非常想要某样东西。

lines.en: "During the pandemic, I really found myself longing for alone time. I have two small children. They're 9 and eleven, and we were all quarantining at home together. Which while joyful … I felt so often disconnected from myself and really craved more time to be with myself to have time to paint and … sort of reconnect."
lines.zh: “疫情期间，我真的发现自己渴望独处的时间。我有两个小孩，一个 9 岁、一个 11 岁，我们一起在家隔离。虽然很快乐……但我常常觉得和自己失去了联系，真的渴望有更多时间和自己待在一起，有时间画画……重新找回自己。”

lines.en: While most of the stories were written during the pandemic, only a few writers deal with the pandemic directly.
lines.zh: 虽然大部分故事是在疫情期间写的，但只有少数几位作家直接写到了疫情。

lines.en: In the story "On Witness and Respair," Jesmyn Ward writes about her husband dying at the beginning of the pandemic. Her whole family caught what they thought was just a severe flu. Her husband did not survive.
lines.zh: 在《见证与重燃希望》中，杰斯敏·沃德写了她丈夫在疫情初期去世的事。她全家都染上了他们以为只是重感冒的病，她丈夫没能挺过来。

lines.en: In "Exodus, 2020," Emily Raboteau describes the emptying of a large apartment building where she lives in New York City. One by one, neighbors and friends left the city for safer places to live during the pandemic.
lines.zh: 在《出走，2020》中，埃米莉·拉博托描述了她在纽约市居住的一栋大公寓楼渐渐空了。疫情期间，邻居和朋友们一个接一个离开城市，去更安全的地方生活。

lines.en: Several writers describe the loneliness of leaving their culture.
lines.zh: 有几位作家描写了离开自己文化的孤独。

lines.en: Jhumpa Lahiri's "Trading Stories" is about her parents' struggle to fit in to a different culture and how that affected her life and work.
lines.zh: 裘帕·拉希莉的《交换故事》讲她父母努力融入另一种文化，以及这如何影响了她的生活和创作。

lines.en: Writer Jean Kwok shares the experience of her family moving from Hong Kong to New York City. They lost everything: money, jobs, and more. In "Perpetual Foreigner," she wrote:
lines.zh: 作家郭珍芳讲述了她一家从香港搬到纽约市的经历。他们失去了一切：钱、工作，还有更多。她在《永远的外国人》中写道：

lines.en: "But the heavier price was losing our language, our friends, our culture, and in some ways, one another."
lines.zh: “但更沉重的代价是失去了我们的语言、我们的朋友、我们的文化，在某种程度上，也失去了彼此。”

lines.en: Some of the writers wrote about choosing to be alone for personal or creative reasons and the challenges they faced.
lines.zh: 有些作家写了自己出于个人或创作原因选择独处，以及他们面临的挑战。

lines.en: -- In "Maine Man," Lev Grossman wrote about nearly losing his mind. While in his twenties, he chose to work on a book in a small town, isolated from other people.
lines.zh: ——在《缅因人》中，列夫·格罗斯曼写了自己差点疯掉的经历。二十多岁时，他选择在一个小镇上与世隔绝地写书。

lines.en: -- In the story "Javelinas," Claire Dederer wrote about facing her alcohol addiction during a period of solitude.
lines.zh: ——在《西猯》中，克莱尔·德德勒写了她在一段独处时期面对自己的酒瘾。

lines.en: -- And in "Am I Still Here?" Anthony Doerr, a man addicted to the internet, wrote of his struggle to turn off social media and reconnect with nature and himself.
lines.zh: ——在《我还在吗？》中，网络成瘾的安东尼·多尔写了他如何努力关掉社交媒体，重新与大自然和自己建立联系。

lines.en: Loneliness is not just a mental state. It can also lead to serious physical health problems.
lines.zh: 孤独不只是一种心理状态，它还可能导致严重的身体健康问题。

lines.en: The U.S. Department of Health & Human Services National Institute on Aging says that loneliness and isolation can be harmful for older people. Loneliness can lead to high blood pressure, heart disease, depression, a decrease in mental abilities, and even death.
lines.zh: 美国卫生与公众服务部国家老龄化研究所说，孤独和隔离对老年人可能有害。孤独可能导致高血压、心脏病、抑郁、心智能力下降，甚至死亡。

lines.en: Younger people are not protected against the harm of loneliness either. Researchers at Harvard University have found that in the United States loneliness has increased in young adults and others since the beginning of the pandemic.
lines.zh: 年轻人也不能免受孤独之害。哈佛大学的研究人员发现，自疫情开始以来，美国年轻人和其他人群的孤独感都增加了。

lines.en: The Harvard study was released in February of 2021. It suggests that "36% of all Americans feel 'serious loneliness.'" This includes "61% of young adults and 51% of mothers with young children."
lines.zh: 这项哈佛研究于 2021 年 2 月发布。它表明“36% 的美国人感到‘严重孤独’”，其中包括“61% 的年轻人和 51% 有年幼孩子的母亲”。

lines.en: Garrett told VOA that sharing stories of loneliness is a way to bring attention to the problem and to feel connected to others.
lines.zh: 加勒特告诉 VOA，分享孤独的故事是一种引起人们关注这个问题、感受到与他人联系的方式。

lines.en: "So, I'm really grateful that so many extraordinary writers joined me on this lonely journey and made it really un-lonely! And my hope is that the book will remind us that we're not as alone as we think we are and we're not alone in feeling ... lonely."
lines.zh: “所以我真的很感激这么多杰出的作家陪我走过这段孤独的旅程，让它一点也不孤独！我希望这本书能提醒我们：我们并不像自己以为的那样孤单，在感到孤独这件事上，我们也并不孤单。”

lines.en: And that's the Health & Lifestyle report. I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 以上就是《健康与生活》节目。我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: What is the difference between loneliness and solitude, says Garrett?
opts: Solitude is chosen; loneliness happens to us.
qs.a: Solitude is chosen; loneliness happens to us.
qs.why: "Solitude, I think, is chosen whereas loneliness happens to us."

qs.q: What did Garrett long for during the pandemic?
qs.why: "I really found myself longing for alone time."

qs.q: What percent of all Americans feel "serious loneliness"?
qs.why: "36% of all Americans feel 'serious loneliness.'"

lessons.title: Plant Native Plants to Support Local Environment, Wildlife
lessons.zh: 种本地植物，支持当地环境和野生动物
lessons.sum: 4 月 22 日是世界地球日。种植本地原生植物能帮助与它们共同进化的鸟和昆虫——很多传粉动物认不出外来植物是食物。昆虫支撑着整个生态系统；而原生植物好养活，少浇水少施肥，对园丁和传粉者是双赢。

lines.en: Earth Day is April 22. Every year, people around the world observe the day by helping to care for the environment. They carry out all kinds of activities in an effort to better the planet's health.
lines.zh: 4 月 22 日是地球日。每年，世界各地的人们都会通过帮助保护环境来纪念这一天，开展各种活动，努力改善地球的健康。

lines.en: One way to support this goal is to grow plants native to your area. This helps wildlife like birds and insects that evolved alongside native plants. For many of these animals, plant pollen is their food.
lines.zh: 支持这一目标的方法之一，是种植你所在地区的本地植物。这能帮助那些与本地植物共同进化的鸟类和昆虫等野生动物。对其中很多动物来说，花粉就是它们的食物。

lines.en: Native pollinators often cannot recognize non-native plants as food. This means they do not collect the pollen or spread plants' seeds.
lines.zh: 本地传粉者往往认不出外来植物是食物，也就是说它们不会采集这些植物的花粉，也不会传播它们的种子。

lines.en: Planting non-native species creates so-called "food deserts" for pollinators including bees, birds, bats, butterflies and more.
lines.zh: 种植外来物种会给蜜蜂、鸟类、蝙蝠、蝴蝶等传粉者制造所谓的“食物沙漠”。

lines.en: Doug Tallamy is a professor of entomology at the University of Delaware. Entomology is the study of insects. He found that non-native plant species can harm the natural food chain, which can lead to a collapse of the environment.
lines.zh: 道格·塔拉米是特拉华大学的昆虫学教授。昆虫学是研究昆虫的学科。他发现外来植物物种会破坏自然食物链，可能导致环境崩溃。

lines.en: "Plant choice matters," he said. "The plants we choose to landscape our properties (with) should be determined by how much life can live there."
lines.zh: “选择种什么植物很重要，”他说，“我们用来绿化自己土地的植物，应该由有多少生命能在那里生活来决定。”

lines.en: Humans depend strongly on insects. Without them, we would have no flowering plants, which would harm the food web that supports important animals. Birds, for example, depend on plants for food and spread their seeds while keeping the populations of harmful insects down.
lines.zh: 人类非常依赖昆虫。没有昆虫，就没有开花植物，这会破坏养活重要动物的食物网。比如，鸟类依靠植物获取食物，也帮植物传播种子，同时控制有害昆虫的数量。

lines.en: Insects support plants that provide oxygen, clean our water, capture carbon and add nutrients to the soil. That builds topsoil and prevents flooding. Without insects, the biosphere – the living parts of the Earth – would rot because of the loss of insect decomposers. Humans simply could not survive that, Tallamy said.
lines.zh: 昆虫支撑着那些提供氧气、净化水、吸收碳并为土壤增加养分的植物。这能形成表土，防止洪水。塔拉米说，没有昆虫，生物圈——地球上有生命的部分——就会因为失去昆虫分解者而腐烂。人类根本无法在那种情况下生存。

lines.en: In addition to providing food and habitat for insects and other wildlife, native plants are able to grow easily and do not require much care. That means less watering and less fertilizing. The situation is a win-win for gardeners and pollinators.
lines.zh: 除了为昆虫和其他野生动物提供食物和栖息地，本地植物还很容易生长，不需要太多照料。这意味着少浇水、少施肥。对园丁和传粉者来说，这是双赢的局面。

lines.en: I'm Ashley Thompson.
lines.zh: 我是阿什莉·汤普森。

qs.q: Why do native plants help wildlife?
opts: Wildlife evolved alongside them and use them for food.
qs.a: Wildlife evolved alongside them and use them for food.
qs.why: "wildlife like birds and insects that evolved alongside native plants."

qs.q: What are "food deserts" for pollinators?
opts: areas with non-native plants they cannot use for food
qs.a: areas with non-native plants they cannot use for food
qs.why: "Planting non-native species creates so-called 'food deserts' for pollinators."

qs.q: Why is planting native plants a "win-win"?
opts: They need less care and help pollinators.
qs.a: They need less care and help pollinators.
qs.why: "less watering and less fertilizing."

lessons.title: Hugelkultur: A Different Way of Container Gardening
lessons.zh: “山丘栽培法”：一种不一样的种菜方式
lessons.sum: Hugelkultur 在德语里是“山丘栽培”的意思：把旧木头、树枝、落叶和厨余一层层埋进种植箱或土堆，让它们像森林地面一样慢慢分解成肥沃的土壤。这样能少买土、少浇水，土堆可以让植物长得更好长达 20 年。

lines.en: People without a lot of outdoor space sometimes grow a garden in containers such as raised beds. They refill the containers each year with several bags of nutrient-rich soil and compost that they purchase.
lines.zh: 户外空间不多的人有时会用高架苗床之类的容器种菜。他们每年都要买好几袋富含养分的土和堆肥，把容器重新填满。

lines.en: But there is another way to provide soil for small gardens. The method is called "Hugelkultur." The idea is that nature should be left to do its own thing with as little human interference as possible.
lines.zh: 但给小菜园提供土壤还有另一种方法，叫“Hugelkultur”（山丘栽培法）。它的理念是让大自然自己去做，人为干预越少越好。

lines.en: Hugelkultur means "hill culture" in German.
lines.zh: Hugelkultur 在德语里的意思是“山丘栽培”。

lines.en: The process involves letting large pieces of trees and plants decompose and turn into nutrient-rich soil, just as they would on a forest floor. The resulting soil is arguably better than anything that you can buy at a garden store.
lines.zh: 这个方法是让大块的树木和植物分解，变成富含养分的土壤，就像它们在森林地面上那样。这样得到的土壤，可以说比你在园艺店买到的任何东西都好。

lines.en: Hugelkultur can be used in raised beds or in mounds directly on the ground.
lines.zh: 山丘栽培法可以用在高架苗床里，也可以直接在地面上堆成土堆。

lines.en: Here is how it works:
lines.zh: 具体做法如下：

lines.en: Instead of filling deep raised beds with purchased soil and compost, fill them with yard waste. This reduces the amount of soil needed and increases nutrients and plant growth.
lines.zh: 不要用买来的土和堆肥填满深深的高架苗床，而是用院子里的废弃物来填。这能减少所需的土量，增加养分，促进植物生长。

lines.en: Start by building up about 40 percent of the depth of your container with a layer of old logs. The logs should come from hardwood trees like maple, oak, poplar or birch. Softwoods from evergreens are also acceptable but they decompose more quickly. Do not use wood from redwood trees or black locusts because they are decay-resistant. Wood from trees like the black walnut release matter that prevents growth and should be avoided, too.
lines.zh: 先用一层旧木头铺满容器深度的大约 40%。木头应该来自枫树、橡树、杨树或桦树等硬木树。常绿树的软木也可以，但分解得更快。不要用红杉或刺槐的木头，因为它们不易腐烂。黑胡桃这类树的木头会释放抑制生长的物质，也应该避免。

lines.en: Cover the logs with smaller pieces of wood, like fallen branches, twigs and sticks. These make up the next 10 percent of depth.
lines.zh: 在木头上盖一层较小的木料，比如掉落的树枝、细枝和小棍，它们占接下来 10% 的深度。

lines.en: Next, add a layer of leaves and other soft plant remains, plus pieces of fruit, vegetables and eggshells that are left over from your own food. Make sure these fresh foods fill spaces in the woody layer under them. Then, water the layer well.
lines.zh: 接着，加一层落叶和其他柔软的植物残余，再加上你自己吃剩的水果、蔬菜和蛋壳。确保这些新鲜食物填满下面木头层的空隙。然后把这一层浇透水。

lines.en: Finally, add a layer of compost and a layer of topsoil in equal amounts. Water each layer as you add it.
lines.zh: 最后，加一层堆肥和一层表土，两者分量相同。每加一层就浇一次水。

lines.en: If you are making a free-standing mound, decide how big you would like it to be. Dig a trench in the ground that is about 30 centimeters deep. Fill the trench with logs and cover it with a layer of twigs, sticks and branches.
lines.zh: 如果你要堆一个独立的土堆，先决定想要多大。在地上挖一条约 30 厘米深的沟，用木头填满沟，再盖一层细枝、小棍和树枝。

lines.en: Cover the woody layers with upside-down sections of the removed ground. Cover that with kitchen leftovers, compost and topsoil. Aim for a mound that is wider at its base than its top.
lines.zh: 把挖出来的草皮土块翻过来盖在木头层上，再盖上厨余、堆肥和表土。目标是堆成一个底部比顶部宽的土堆。

lines.en: As the organic matter in Hugelkultur beds breaks down, the height of the mound will sink. Simply add compost as needed. The breakdown will warm the soil and create air flow. It also will greatly reduce the need for irrigation, and provide plants with a long-term supply of nutrients.
lines.zh: 随着山丘栽培床里的有机物分解，土堆的高度会下降，需要时补些堆肥就行。分解过程会让土壤变暖，并形成空气流通。它还会大大减少浇水的需要，为植物提供长期的养分。

lines.en: Soil in Hugelkultur beds, or mounds, can increase harvests and create larger plants for up to 20 years.
lines.zh: 山丘栽培床或土堆里的土壤，可以在长达 20 年的时间里提高收成、让植物长得更大。

lines.en: I'm Ashley Thompson.
lines.zh: 我是阿什莉·汤普森。

qs.q: What does "Hugelkultur" mean?
qs.why: "Hugelkultur means 'hill culture' in German."

qs.q: What goes in the first layer?
qs.why: "a layer of old logs. The logs should come from hardwood trees."

qs.q: How long can a Hugelkultur bed help plants?
qs.why: "for up to 20 years."

lessons.title: Staying Safe in Hot Temperatures
lessons.zh: 高温天气如何保持安全
lessons.sum: 极端高温每年夺走数百人的生命，但热相关疾病是可以预防的。湿度高、夜间降温少都会让身体难以散热；酒精、咖啡因和糖也有影响。65 岁以上和 2 岁以下的人风险最高。文章列出了中暑衰竭和中暑的症状，以及美国疾控中心建议的预防措施。

lines.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle report.
lines.zh: 这里是 VOA 慢速英语《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: Hot weather kills hundreds of people every year. The World Health Organization estimates that from 1998 to 2017 more than 166,000 people died as a result of extreme heatwaves. That includes the more than 70,000 people who died during the 2003 heatwave in Europe.
lines.zh: 炎热天气每年导致数百人死亡。世界卫生组织估计，1998 年到 2017 年间，有 16.6 万多人死于极端热浪，其中包括 2003 年欧洲热浪中死亡的 7 万多人。

lines.en: Yet, heat-related deaths and sickness are preventable. There are steps you can take to stay safe during periods of very high temperatures.
lines.zh: 然而，与高温有关的死亡和疾病是可以预防的。在气温非常高的时期，你可以采取一些措施保持安全。

lines.en: Many things can affect your body's ability to cool itself during extremely hot weather.
lines.zh: 在极端炎热的天气里，很多因素会影响身体自我降温的能力。

lines.en: For example, when the humidity is high, body sweat will not dry as quickly. This restricts the body's ability to release heat. So, pay attention to not only the temperature in your area but also the level of humidity.
lines.zh: 比如，湿度高时，身上的汗不会那么快干，这会限制身体散热的能力。所以，不仅要注意你所在地区的气温，还要注意湿度。

lines.en: Also, take note of nighttime temperatures. Experts say heat waves often become dangerous when the nighttime temperature does not drop much past the highest daytime temperature. Our bodies repair themselves at night when we sleep. So, hot nighttime temperatures put great pressure on the human body.
lines.zh: 还要留意夜间气温。专家说，当夜间气温比白天最高气温低不了多少时，热浪往往会变得危险。我们的身体在夜里睡觉时自我修复，所以夜间高温会给人体带来很大压力。

lines.en: Some foods and drugs can also affect the body's temperature. Alcohol, caffeine, and sugar, for example, can weaken the body's system for cooling itself.
lines.zh: 一些食物和药物也会影响体温。比如酒精、咖啡因和糖，会削弱身体的自我降温系统。

lines.en: On its website, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, or CDC, explains that some people are at high risk of suffering from heat-related illnesses.
lines.zh: 美国疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）在网站上解释说，有些人患热相关疾病的风险很高。

lines.en: A person's age and weight play a part in surviving high temperatures. People over 65 years of age and under the age of two are especially at risk of becoming sick from heat.
lines.zh: 一个人的年龄和体重对能否熬过高温有影响。65 岁以上和 2 岁以下的人尤其容易因高温生病。

lines.en: Your general health is also important to consider. The CDC states that long-term diseases and conditions such as diabetes, heart disease and mental illness can put a person at greater risk.
lines.zh: 你的总体健康状况也需要考虑。CDC 说，糖尿病、心脏病和精神疾病等长期疾病和状况会让人面临更大风险。

lines.en: On its website the CDC also explains different types of heat-related illness – what to look for and what to do.
lines.zh: CDC 还在网站上解释了不同类型的热相关疾病——要注意什么、该怎么做。

lines.en: They include heat rash, sunburn, heat cramps, heat exhaustion, and, the most serious, heat stroke.
lines.zh: 包括痱子、晒伤、热痉挛、热衰竭，以及最严重的中暑（热射病）。

lines.en: These are the symptoms of heat exhaustion:
lines.zh: 以下是热衰竭的症状：

lines.en: heavy sweating
lines.zh: 大量出汗

lines.en: cold, damp skin that looks lighter than usual
lines.zh: 皮肤湿冷，颜色比平时浅

lines.en: fast, weak heartbeat
lines.zh: 心跳快而弱

lines.en: feeling sick to your stomach, or nausea
lines.zh: 恶心想吐

lines.en: muscle pains, often called cramps
lines.zh: 肌肉疼痛，常叫作抽筋

lines.en: tired and weak feeling
lines.zh: 感到疲倦无力

lines.en: dizziness
lines.zh: 头晕

lines.en: headache
lines.zh: 头痛

lines.en: passing out
lines.zh: 昏倒

lines.en: If you have these symptoms, you must move to a cool place, loosen your clothing, put a cool wet cloth on your body or take a cool bath and drink water. Get medical attention if you begin vomiting, or if your sickness worsens or lasts for more than an hour.
lines.zh: 如果出现这些症状，必须转移到凉爽的地方，松开衣服，在身上放一块凉的湿布或洗个凉水澡，并喝水。如果开始呕吐，或者病情加重、持续超过一小时，就要去看医生。

lines.en: The CDC calls heat stroke a medical emergency. Get medical help right away. These are the symptoms of heat stroke:
lines.zh: CDC 把中暑称为医疗急症，要立即寻求医疗帮助。以下是中暑的症状：

lines.en: high body temperature of 39.4 degrees Celsius or higher
lines.zh: 体温达到或超过 39.4 摄氏度

lines.en: hot, red, dry, damp skin
lines.zh: 皮肤又热又红，干燥或潮湿

lines.en: fast, strong heartbeat
lines.zh: 心跳快而有力

lines.en: headache
lines.zh: 头痛

lines.en: dizziness
lines.zh: 头晕

lines.en: nausea
lines.zh: 恶心

lines.en: confusion
lines.zh: 意识混乱
