lines.en: and passing out
lines.zh: 以及昏倒

lines.en: Experts at the CDC say that "everyone should take these steps to prevent heat-related illnesses, injuries, and death" when the weather is very hot:
lines.zh: CDC 的专家说，天气非常炎热时，“每个人都应该采取这些措施，预防与高温有关的疾病、伤害和死亡”：

lines.en: Stay inside in air-conditioned spaces as much as possible. Contact your local health department or locate an air-conditioned shelter in your area, if possible.
lines.zh: 尽量待在有空调的室内。如果可能，联系当地卫生部门或找到你所在地区有空调的避暑场所。

lines.en: Drink a lot of water even if you do not feel thirsty.
lines.zh: 即使不觉得渴，也要多喝水。

lines.en: Wear loose, lightweight, light-colored clothing and use skin products that protect you from sunburn.
lines.zh: 穿宽松、轻薄、浅色的衣服，并使用防晒护肤品。

lines.en: Do not try to do too much outside. Plan your outdoor activities carefully.
lines.zh: 不要在户外做太多事，仔细安排户外活动。

lines.en: Get in cool water to lower your body temperature.
lines.zh: 泡凉水降低体温。

lines.en: Check on friends or neighbors, especially those at-risk. Have someone do the same for you.
lines.zh: 关心朋友或邻居，特别是高风险人群，也请别人同样关心你。

lines.en: Never leave children or pets in cars.
lines.zh: 绝不要把孩子或宠物留在车里。

lines.en: Check your local news for health and safety updates.
lines.zh: 留意当地新闻里的健康和安全最新消息。

lines.en: Do not use heating elements, like indoor stoves and ovens, to cook food. This will make you and your house hotter.
lines.zh: 不要用室内炉灶和烤箱之类的加热设备做饭，这会让你和房子更热。

lines.en: And that's the Health & Lifestyle report. I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 以上就是《健康与生活》节目。我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: Why does high humidity make heat more dangerous?
opts: Sweat does not dry as quickly.
qs.a: Sweat does not dry as quickly.
qs.why: "when the humidity is high, body sweat will not dry as quickly."

qs.q: Who is especially at risk in hot weather?
qs.why: "People over 65 years of age and under the age of two are especially at risk."

qs.q: What is one step to prevent heat illness?
opts: Drink a lot of water even if you are not thirsty.
qs.a: Drink a lot of water even if you are not thirsty.
qs.why: "Drink a lot of water even if you do not feel thirsty."

lessons.title: Trillions of Cicadas Coming after 17 Years Underground
lessons.zh: 地下蛰伏 17 年，亿万蝉虫即将破土
lessons.sum: 每隔 17 年，“X 群”周期蝉就会从美国东部 15 个州的地下钻出来，数量可能达到万亿只。它们爬上树梢鸣唱求偶，六周后幼虫落回地下，再等 17 年。同时大量出现、间隔这么久，是它们躲避天敌的生存之道。

lines.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle report.
lines.zh: 这里是 VOA 慢速英语《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: Every 17 years, billions of insects, known as the cicadas of Brood X, rise from the earth. This year, perhaps, there will be trillions!
lines.zh: 每隔 17 年，数十亿只被称为“X 群”的蝉就会从地下钻出来。今年，数量也许会达到万亿只！

lines.en: Different broods, or groups, of cicadas come out on different years. The last time Brood X appeared was in 2004. The brood is one of the largest and will appear sometime in May in 15 states, from Georgia in the south to New York in the northeast.
lines.zh: 不同的“群”蝉在不同的年份出现。X 群上一次出现是在 2004 年。它是规模最大的群之一，将在五月某个时候出现在从南部的佐治亚州到东北部的纽约州的 15 个州。

lines.en: Many scientists and insect lovers say they are looking forward to the red-eyed insects after a 17-year wait. One of them is Mike Raupp, an insect expert at the University of Maryland.
lines.zh: 许多科学家和昆虫爱好者说，等了 17 年，他们很期待这些红眼睛的昆虫。马里兰大学的昆虫专家迈克·劳普就是其中之一。

lines.en: "What they're waiting for is the soil temperatures to reach about 18 degrees Celsius, I believe that's about 64 degrees Fahrenheit. Then they're going to be up and out of the ground."
lines.zh: “它们在等土壤温度达到大约 18 摄氏度，我想大约是华氏 64 度。然后它们就会钻出地面。”

lines.en: Raupp called the event a "party on the treetops." When the insects come out of the ground, they will drop their skin, get their wings, and will try to go up on the treetops to escape from the predators.
lines.zh: 劳普称这一事件是一场“树梢上的派对”。昆虫从地下钻出来后，会蜕皮、长出翅膀，然后想爬到树梢上躲避天敌。

lines.en: Raupp told VOA every creature will want to eat a cicada, and they will!
lines.zh: 劳普告诉 VOA，每种动物都想吃蝉，而且它们真的会吃！

lines.en: "On that night of emergence when the cicadas come up from the earth, everything on the planet is going to want to eat a cicada."
lines.zh: “在蝉从地下钻出来的那个晚上，地球上的一切都想吃一只蝉。”

lines.en: Once on the treetops, the male cicadas will "sing" their mating songs to draw the females. And it is loud!
lines.zh: 一到树梢，雄蝉就会“唱”求偶的歌吸引雌蝉。声音很响！

lines.en: If she likes the singing, they will have sex and reproduce. About six weeks later, the nymphs will fall off the treetops and go into the ground. Underfoot, the insects will quietly feed off tree roots and wait for another 17 years to start the party on the treetops all over again.
lines.zh: 如果雌蝉喜欢这歌声，它们就会交配繁殖。大约六周后，若虫会从树梢上掉下来钻进地里。在人们脚下，这些昆虫会悄悄地吸食树根，再等 17 年，重新开始树梢上的派对。

lines.en: "I think the periodical cicadas give tens of millions of people an opportunity to simply go out in their backyard and witness and enjoy a natural event that happens nowhere else on the planet, only a handful of times in a lifetime."
lines.zh: “我认为周期蝉给了几千万人一个机会，只要走到自家后院，就能见证和欣赏一个地球上别处没有、一生只能遇到几次的自然奇观。”

lines.en: Raup explained that some cicadas appear every year. But they have a much shorter life cycle and stay alive in two ways. They are green and can hide in nature. Also, they can fly very fast. So, they avoid being captured by predators.
lines.zh: 劳普解释说，有些蝉每年都会出现，但它们的生命周期短得多，靠两种方式生存：它们是绿色的，能藏在大自然里；它们还飞得很快。所以能躲开天敌的捕捉。

lines.en: Periodical cicadas like Brood X do not have either of those lifesaving methods. To continue the species, he said billions of periodical cicadas will appear all at the same time. So, their predators cannot eat all of them. Also, by coming out every 17 years, they are not a dependable food source for predators and simply outlive them.
lines.zh: X 群这样的周期蝉这两种保命的办法都没有。他说，为了延续物种，几十亿只周期蝉会同时出现，这样天敌没法把它们全吃掉。而且每 17 年才出来一次，它们就不是天敌可靠的食物来源，干脆比天敌活得更久。

lines.en: Some people might be afraid of Brood X or concerned about the noise. Raupp advised it may help to think of the similarities between Brood X and people.
lines.zh: 有些人可能害怕 X 群蝉，或者担心噪音。劳普建议，想想 X 群蝉和人类的相似之处可能会有帮助。

lines.en: "You know, this past year for humans has been a year of many challenges, right? We've had COVID. We've had social unrest. But now with the vaccines, with restrictions being lifted, people are getting outside again. There's no longer social distancing. They're having fun with their friends. Now, think about the cicadas. They've been underground for 17 years social distancing. They're not hanging out together. And just like us, this spring in May, they're coming up and out of the ground. They're going to go to the treetops. They're going to have fun."
lines.zh: “你知道吗，过去这一年对人类来说充满挑战，对吧？我们经历了新冠，经历了社会动荡。可现在有了疫苗，限制解除了，人们又开始出门了，不再保持社交距离，和朋友们玩得很开心。再想想蝉。它们在地下保持了 17 年的社交距离，不聚在一起。和我们一样，今年春天五月，它们要钻出地面了，要去树梢上，要去玩个痛快了。”

lines.en: For those feeling even braver, a student at the University of Maryland, Jenna Jadin, wrote a book in 2004 to give cooking directions for eating cicadas.
lines.zh: 至于更大胆的人，马里兰大学的学生珍娜·贾丁在 2004 年写了一本书，教人们怎么烹饪、吃蝉。

lines.en: In Cicada-Licious: Cooking and Enjoying Periodical Cicadas, she suggests eating only newly-emerged cicadas whose outer bodies have not hardened. Boil them for about four to five minutes. Remove the hard parts -- the wings and the legs. They will not hurt you, she writes. But they are not that tasty. Then you can fry them in seasonings.
lines.zh: 在《美味蝉：烹饪和享用周期蝉》一书中，她建议只吃刚钻出来、外壳还没变硬的蝉。煮大约四五分钟，去掉翅膀和腿这些硬的部分。她写道，它们不会伤害你，但也没那么好吃。然后可以加调料炸一炸。

lines.en: Raupp and other experts warn that people should talk to their doctor before eating any insect. He also suggests that those people who are afraid of cicadas think of them this way.
lines.zh: 劳普和其他专家提醒，吃任何昆虫之前都应该先问问医生。他还建议害怕蝉的人这样看待它们：

lines.en: "Yes. I think everybody feels that it's a new day. It's a new day for us. It's certainly going to be a new and wonderful day for cicadas. So, I think we have a lot to look forward to."
lines.zh: “是的。我想每个人都觉得这是新的一天。对我们来说是新的一天，对蝉来说肯定也是美好的新一天。所以我想，我们有很多值得期待的。”

lines.en: And that's the Health & Lifestyle report. I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 以上就是《健康与生活》节目。我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: How often do Brood X cicadas come out?
qs.why: "Every 17 years, billions of insects, known as the cicadas of Brood X, rise from the earth."

qs.q: What are the cicadas waiting for?
opts: the soil temperature to reach about 18 degrees Celsius
qs.a: the soil temperature to reach about 18 degrees Celsius
qs.why: "for the soil temperatures to reach about 18 degrees Celsius."

qs.q: How do periodical cicadas survive predators?
opts: Billions come out at the same time.
qs.a: Billions come out at the same time.
qs.why: "billions of periodical cicadas will appear all at the same time."

lessons.title: Longleaf Pine Trees Give Us More than Just Wood
lessons.zh: 长叶松带给我们的不只是木材
lessons.sum: 长叶松林曾覆盖美国东南部三分之二的土地，过去百年失去了约 95%。它的木材坚固防虫，还能储存碳、为濒危的红顶啄木鸟提供栖息地。如今农民种长叶松不为砍伐，而是卖松针做地面覆盖物、卖狩猎权，原住民还用松针编篮子。

lines.en: The longleaf pine tree has deep connections with the history and life of the eastern part of America.
lines.zh: 长叶松与美国东部的历史和生活有着深厚的联系。

lines.en: Forests of these trees once covered two-thirds of the southeastern United States. About 95 percent of those forests were lost in the past 100 years. Many of the forests were cut for their wood, but now they are returning, with the help of government programs that build ties with private landowners.
lines.zh: 这种树组成的森林曾经覆盖美国东南部三分之二的土地，过去 100 年里约 95% 消失了。许多森林被砍伐取木材，但现在，在与私人土地所有者合作的政府项目帮助下，它们正在恢复。

lines.en: The wood of the tree is very strong. Most buildings built in the southern U.S. from the 1800s contained longleaf pine wood. Today, after a building made with longleaf pine is no longer wanted, people are re-using the wood because it is still good and resists water and insect damage.
lines.zh: 这种树的木材非常坚固。19 世纪美国南方建造的大多数建筑都用了长叶松木材。如今，长叶松建造的建筑不再需要时，人们会重新利用这些木材，因为它们仍然很好，能防水、防虫蛀。

lines.en: The longleaf pine also captures carbon dioxide in the air. It stores the substance in its wood. So, the tree is valuable to the environment as a way to store carbon.
lines.zh: 长叶松还能吸收空气中的二氧化碳，把它储存在木材里。所以作为储存碳的一种方式，这种树对环境很有价值。

lines.en: In addition, the pine forests are places for animals to live. The U.S. government has several programs to protect and expand longleaf pine forests. One is the Safe Harbor Program. It uses voluntary agreements with private landowners to help endangered animals. One such agreement protects the red-cockaded woodpecker and also lets landowners use their land, as long as the birds and other related animals can safely live on it.
lines.zh: 此外，松林是动物生活的地方。美国政府有好几个保护和扩大长叶松林的项目，其中之一是“安全港计划”。它通过与私人土地所有者签订自愿协议来帮助濒危动物。其中一项协议保护红顶啄木鸟，同时也允许土地所有者使用自己的土地，只要这种鸟和其他相关动物能在上面安全生活。

lines.en: Now, farmers and landowners in the Southeastern U.S. are growing new longleaf pine trees. Instead of cutting the trees to use as building materials, they are finding ways to make money from the forest of living trees. One way to get income is by selling the leaves, or needles, of the trees as a ground cover.
lines.zh: 如今，美国东南部的农民和土地所有者在种新的长叶松。他们不是把树砍下来当建材，而是想办法从活着的森林中赚钱。一种收入来源是把树叶——也就是松针——当作地面覆盖物出售。

lines.en: Farmers can gather the pine straw by hand or with use of a machine. Pine straw can be used instead of wood pieces or bark as a ground cover. It lasts a long time, is light weight and stays in place because the needles connect to each other. The straw is high in nitrogen, a nutrient that helps plants grow. And, it does not attract harmful insects!
lines.zh: 农民可以用手或机器收集松针。松针可以代替木片或树皮做地面覆盖物。它持久、轻便，而且因为针叶相互交织，不容易被吹散。松针富含氮——一种帮助植物生长的养分。而且它不招害虫！

lines.en: Native American tribes, such as the Choctaw and Cherokee nations in Louisiana, make coiled baskets from the long needles of the longleaf pine. A basket made of the pine needles by Native American artists can sell for as much as $750.
lines.zh: 路易斯安那州的乔克托和切罗基等美洲原住民部落，用长叶松的长松针编盘绕式篮子。原住民艺术家用松针编的篮子能卖到 750 美元。

lines.en: Another way forests can produce income is to sell hunting rights. Wild boars – a kind of pig – live in some forests. Their population has been growing out of control in recent years. The animals can damage the young longleaf pine trees, so landowners want to reduce their numbers. Hunting boar is a popular sport in the southern U.S. and the right to hunt on land can cost from $200 to $1,000 a day.
lines.zh: 森林创收的另一种方式是出售狩猎权。有些森林里生活着野猪。近年来它们的数量增长失控。这些动物会破坏长叶松幼树，所以土地所有者想减少它们的数量。猎野猪是美国南方很受欢迎的运动，在土地上打猎的权利每天要花 200 到 1000 美元。

lines.en: The Kisatchie National Forest in west central Louisiana contains most of the remaining longleaf pines in that state. In the past, Native Americans burned the forest every two to four years, if lightning did not cause fires naturally. Fire helps the young pine trees to grow by clearing away the other plants on the floor of the forest. Recent debate has centered on the value of letting some parts of the forests burn for this purpose.
lines.zh: 路易斯安那州中西部的基萨奇国家森林保存着该州大部分仅存的长叶松。过去，如果闪电没有自然引起火灾，美洲原住民每两到四年就会烧一次森林。火能清除林地上的其他植物，帮助松树幼苗生长。最近的争论集中在是否值得为此让部分森林燃烧。

lines.en: I'm Jill Robbins.
lines.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

qs.q: How much of the longleaf pine forests were lost in the past 100 years?
qs.why: "About 95 percent of those forests were lost in the past 100 years."

qs.q: What can pine straw be used for?
qs.why: "Pine straw can be used instead of wood pieces or bark as a ground cover."

qs.q: How does fire help young longleaf pines?
opts: It clears away other plants on the forest floor.
qs.a: It clears away other plants on the forest floor.
qs.why: "Fire helps the young pine trees to grow by clearing away the other plants."

lessons.title: Can Birdsong Make You Happier?
lessons.zh: 鸟鸣能让你更快乐吗？
lessons.sum: 两项研究发现，听到多样的鸟鸣能提升幸福感。在科罗拉多的徒步小道上播放本地鸟叫，听到的徒步者幸福感更强；对欧洲 26 国 2.6 万人的研究也发现，身边鸟类种类越多的人生活满意度越高。研究者建议多种本地树木和花卉。

lines.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle report.
lines.zh: 这里是 VOA 慢速英语《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: If you are able to step outside and hear many types of birds, you might also have a greater feeling of well-being.
lines.zh: 如果你走出门能听到许多种鸟叫，你可能也会有更强的幸福感。

lines.en: Two studies show that hearing diverse birdsongs may help increase our happiness.
lines.zh: 两项研究表明，听到多样的鸟鸣可能有助于提升我们的幸福感。

lines.en: One study was done by researchers at California Polytechnic State University (Cal Poly, for short). A research team studied the effects of birdsong on people walking through a park in the U.S. state of Colorado.
lines.zh: 其中一项研究由加州理工州立大学（简称 Cal Poly）的研究人员完成。研究团队研究了鸟鸣对在美国科罗拉多州一座公园里散步的人有什么影响。

lines.en: A biology graduate student, Danielle Ferraro, led the Cal Poly study. Ferraro says that there could be an evolutionary reason why we like birdsong.
lines.zh: 生物学研究生丹妮尔·费拉罗领导了这项研究。费拉罗说，我们喜欢鸟鸣可能有进化上的原因。

lines.en: "There could be, sort of, an evolutionary reason why we like birdsong so much. And the idea is that when we hear birdsong it could … signal safety to us."
lines.zh: “我们这么喜欢鸟鸣，可能有某种进化上的原因。这个想法是，我们听到鸟鸣时，它可能……向我们发出安全的信号。”

lines.en: There could be many other reasons too. Ferraro states that in some areas around the world birdsong can also signal the arrival of spring and nice weather. Bird diversity, she adds, can also mean a healthy environment.
lines.zh: 也可能有很多别的原因。费拉罗说，在世界一些地方，鸟鸣也预示着春天和好天气的到来。她还说，鸟类多样也意味着环境健康。

lines.en: She explained her study to VOA. Ferraro and her team played recorded songs from a diverse group of birds native to the area. They did this on hiking trails in a park in Boulder, Colorado.
lines.zh: 她向 VOA 介绍了她的研究。费拉罗和团队在科罗拉多州博尔德一座公园的徒步小道上，播放了录制的多种本地鸟的叫声。

lines.en: Over several weeks, the researchers played recorded birdsong at certain times of the day and other times they did not. Then they talked with hikers after they passed by.
lines.zh: 几个星期里，研究人员在一天中某些时间播放鸟叫录音，其他时间不播。然后在徒步者经过后和他们交谈。

lines.en: Hikers who heard the recorded diverse birdsongs reported a greater sense of well-being than those who heard simply the natural birds. The researchers suggest that both the bird sounds and biodiversity can increase feelings of well-being.
lines.zh: 听到多样鸟鸣录音的徒步者，报告的幸福感比只听到自然鸟叫的人更强。研究人员认为，鸟的声音和生物多样性都能增加幸福感。

lines.en: Ferraro explained that she used native birdsong for the study. This way it would sound as natural as possible. They also did the study during the summer. She explains why this is important.
lines.zh: 费拉罗解释说，她在研究中用的是本地鸟的叫声，这样听起来尽可能自然。他们还选在夏天做研究。她解释了这为什么重要。

lines.en: "So the study took place in the summer and that's kind of important because the spring...is most birds' breeding season. And if we would've played the (bird)song during breeding season, you know, that might've disturbed them. We didn't want to disturb the birds too much."
lines.zh: “研究是在夏天进行的，这有点重要，因为春天……是大多数鸟的繁殖季节。如果我们在繁殖季节播放（鸟）叫声，你知道，可能会打扰它们。我们不想过多打扰鸟儿。”

lines.en: The study was published in the Proceedings of the Royal Society B in December 2020.
lines.zh: 这项研究于 2020 年 12 月发表在《英国皇家学会学报 B 辑》上。

lines.en: The Science Daily recently reported that scientists in Germany examined for the first time whether a diverse nature also increases human well-being across Europe.
lines.zh: 《科学日报》最近报道，德国科学家首次研究了多样的大自然是否也会提升全欧洲人的幸福感。

lines.en: The researchers looked at the "2012 European quality of Life Survey" to study the connection between the different kinds of birds in their surroundings and life satisfaction. They looked at more than 26,000 adults from 26 European countries.
lines.zh: 研究人员利用“2012 年欧洲生活质量调查”，研究周围环境中鸟的种类与生活满意度之间的联系。他们研究了来自 26 个欧洲国家的 2.6 万多名成年人。

lines.en: "Europeans are particularly satisfied with their lives" if their surroundings have a "high species diversity," explains the study's lead author, Joel Methorst. He is a researcher at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre, the German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research (also known as iDiv), and the Goethe University in Frankfurt.
lines.zh: “如果周围环境‘物种多样性高’，欧洲人对生活就特别满意。”研究的第一作者乔尔·梅索斯特解释说。他是森肯伯格生物多样性与气候研究中心、德国综合生物多样性研究中心（iDiv）以及法兰克福歌德大学的研究员。

lines.en: He and his team found that the "happiest Europeans are those who can experience" many different kinds of birds "in their daily life, or who live in near-natural surroundings that are home to many species."
lines.zh: 他和团队发现，“最快乐的欧洲人，是那些在日常生活中能接触到”许多种鸟“的人，或者住在有许多物种栖息的接近自然环境中的人”。

lines.en: They reported their findings in the December 2020 issue of Ecological Economics.
lines.zh: 他们在 2020 年 12 月的《生态经济学》杂志上报告了研究结果。

lines.en: So, if birdsong is good for our mental health, how can we increase the different types of birdsong we hear?
lines.zh: 那么，既然鸟鸣对我们的心理健康有好处，怎样才能听到更多种类的鸟鸣呢？

lines.en: "I would recommend planting native trees and flowers because we have a lot of, you know, pretty ornamental plants in our cities. And they might look nice to us, but birds can't necessarily use them. So, I think it's important to have species that are native to the area to increase bird diversity."
lines.zh: “我建议种植本地的树木和花卉，因为我们的城市里有很多漂亮的观赏植物，它们在我们看来也许很好看，但鸟不一定能利用它们。所以我认为种本地物种来增加鸟类多样性很重要。”

lines.en: And that's the Health & Lifestyle report. I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 以上就是《健康与生活》节目。我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: What did hikers who heard diverse birdsong report?
qs.why: "Hikers who heard the recorded diverse birdsongs reported a greater sense of well-being."

qs.q: Why was the study done in summer?
opts: to avoid disturbing birds in breeding season
because there are no birds in spring
qs.a: to avoid disturbing birds in breeding season
qs.why: "spring...is most birds' breeding season... We didn't want to disturb the birds."

qs.q: What does Ferraro recommend?
qs.why: "I would recommend planting native trees and flowers."

lessons.title: What Is Composting? And How to Start
lessons.zh: 什么是堆肥？怎样开始？
lessons.sum: 食物残渣、剪下的草和植物残余占美国人扔掉的垃圾的 28% 以上。把它们堆成堆肥，能让土壤健康、减少化肥，还能减少垃圾填埋场排放的甲烷。韩国回收了 95% 的食物垃圾。堆肥只需要三样东西：“棕色”材料、“绿色”材料和水。

lines.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle report.
lines.zh: 这里是 VOA 慢速英语《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: Improvements to the world around us can sometimes result from actions taken by individuals. For example, take composting.
lines.zh: 我们周围世界的改善，有时来自个人采取的行动。比如堆肥。

lines.en: Compost is organic material that, when added to soil, can help plants grow. And there are many different kinds of organic material. Food waste, grass cuttings and other plant remains make up more than 28 percent of what Americans throw away. That information comes from the United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).
lines.zh: 堆肥是一种有机物质，加进土壤里能帮助植物生长。有机物质有很多种。据美国环境保护署（EPA）的信息，食物残渣、剪下的草和其他植物残余占美国人扔掉的东西的 28% 以上。

lines.en: The EPA website tells how composting helps the environment. It says:
lines.zh: EPA 网站介绍了堆肥如何帮助环境。网站上说：

lines.en: Composting helps to keep soil healthy.
lines.zh: 堆肥有助于保持土壤健康。

lines.en: It reduces the need for chemical fertilizers.
lines.zh: 它减少了对化肥的需要。

lines.en: Composting can help the production of good bacteria and fungi, which break down organic matter.
lines.zh: 堆肥有助于产生分解有机物的有益细菌和真菌。

lines.en: Composting also reduces methane gas emissions from landfills. Studies have linked methane to rising temperatures in Earth's atmosphere.
lines.zh: 堆肥还能减少垃圾填埋场的甲烷排放。研究把甲烷与地球大气层的升温联系在一起。

lines.en: Yet many Americans do not compost their food and plant waste.
lines.zh: 然而，很多美国人并不把食物和植物垃圾拿去堆肥。

lines.en: In 2014, a survey of 2,000 Americans found that 72 percent of those questioned did not compost. However, 67 percent said they would do so if it were easier. The National Waste & Recycling Association paid for that study.
lines.zh: 2014 年，一项对 2000 名美国人的调查发现，72% 的受访者不做堆肥。不过 67% 的人说，如果更方便的话他们会做。这项研究由全国废物与回收协会出资。

lines.en: There are only a few U.S. communities that have passed laws restricting some organic material from garbage collection. Two examples are New York City and San Francisco, California. And five months ago, the state of Vermont banned the collection of food waste.
lines.zh: 美国只有少数几个社区通过了限制把部分有机物混进垃圾收运的法律，纽约市和加州旧金山是两个例子。五个月前，佛蒙特州禁止收运食物垃圾。

lines.en: While the numbers of Americans composting remains low, some people are trying to increase the number of composters. They often talk about landfills releasing methane into the atmosphere.
lines.zh: 虽然做堆肥的美国人仍然很少，但有些人正在努力让更多人加入。他们常常谈到垃圾填埋场向大气释放甲烷。

lines.en: "Garbage piles contribute to global warming. And so there's a lot of methane that's released. And from everything that scientists know that that's contributing to the warming of the planet which is not a good thing."
lines.zh: “垃圾堆加剧了全球变暖，释放出大量甲烷。据科学家所知，这正在加剧地球变暖，这可不是好事。”

lines.en: That is Katie Ablard of Maryland. She has been composting for 15 years and enjoys teaching others.
lines.zh: 说这话的是马里兰州的凯蒂·阿布拉德。她做堆肥已经 15 年了，喜欢教别人。

lines.en: "Instead of putting our food waste into the garbage, we're putting our food waste into the compost pile. And in the compost pile in our backyard, within a couple of months that breaks down and it breaks down and turns into really, really fertile soil."
lines.zh: “我们不把食物垃圾扔进垃圾桶，而是放进堆肥堆。在我们后院的堆肥堆里，几个月之内它就会分解、再分解，变成非常非常肥沃的土壤。”

lines.en: Some countries are much better at making compost than the United States.
lines.zh: 有些国家做堆肥比美国好得多。

lines.en: In a 2019 report, the World Economic Forum found that South Korea recycled 95 percent of its food waste. But this did not happen overnight. In 1995, South Koreans only recycled two percent of their food waste.
lines.zh: 世界经济论坛在 2019 年的一份报告中发现，韩国回收了 95% 的食物垃圾。但这不是一夜之间做到的。1995 年，韩国人只回收了 2% 的食物垃圾。

lines.en: Back in 2013, the Yale School of the Environment published a paper on composting around the world. At that time, researchers found that Norway, Sweden, the Netherlands, Denmark, Switzerland, Belgium, Austria, and Germany sent less than three percent of their food waste to landfills.
lines.zh: 早在 2013 年，耶鲁大学环境学院发表了一篇关于世界各地堆肥情况的论文。当时研究人员发现，挪威、瑞典、荷兰、丹麦、瑞士、比利时、奥地利和德国送往填埋场的食物垃圾不到 3%。

lines.en: If you want to make compost, there are some things to know. The EPA website says all composting requires three basic ingredients:
lines.zh: 如果你想做堆肥，有些事情要知道。EPA 网站说，所有堆肥都需要三种基本原料：

lines.en: Brown material -- such as dead leaves and tress branches
lines.zh: 棕色材料——比如枯叶和树枝

lines.en: Green material -- such as grass cuttings and vegetable waste
lines.zh: 绿色材料——比如剪下的草和菜叶果皮

lines.en: Water
lines.zh: 水

lines.en: When composting outdoors the EPA offers these suggestions.
lines.zh: 在户外做堆肥时，EPA 给出了这些建议。

lines.en: Choose a dry area for your compost pile. The area should receive very little sunshine. Make sure there is no standing water on the ground.
lines.zh: 为堆肥堆选一块干燥的地方，那里应该很少晒到太阳，确保地上没有积水。

lines.en: Next, add green and brown materials, in equal amounts, as they are collected. Try to break down larger pieces. And add water if the brown materials are too dry.
lines.zh: 接着，把收集来的绿色和棕色材料等量加进去，尽量把大块的弄碎。如果棕色材料太干就加点水。

lines.en: If your area gets a lot of rain, cover up the compost pile. And make sure you can easily get to the area, but animals cannot. When the waste material at the bottom is dark and rich in color, your compost is ready to use.
lines.zh: 如果你那里雨水多，就把堆肥堆盖起来。确保你自己方便过去，而动物进不去。等底部的废料变成深色、颜色浓郁时，堆肥就可以用了。

lines.en: Here is another piece of advice. Mix or stir the compost often. This adds air to keep it light, or as Katie says, fluffy. What you do not want, she warns, is for the material to get hard or compacted.
lines.zh: 还有一条建议：经常翻动搅拌堆肥。这能让空气进去，保持松软，或者像凯蒂说的那样“蓬松”。她提醒说，你不希望材料变硬或被压实。

lines.en: "I think of it as stirring and turning the compost. And getting it so it's kind of fluffy so that the soil is kind of light and airy and not compacted. You don't want it hard and compacted. (So, you need air flow?) You do need air flow, yeah."
lines.zh: “我把它看作搅拌和翻动堆肥，让它变得有点蓬松，这样土壤就轻盈透气，不被压实。你不希望它又硬又实。（所以需要空气流通？）对，确实需要空气流通。”

lines.en: The EPA website says that if you do not have space for a compost pile outside your home, you can compost materials indoors. But you may need a special container for that.
lines.zh: EPA 网站说，如果你家外面没地方堆肥，也可以在室内堆肥，不过可能需要一个专门的容器。

lines.en: The site says to be careful of what you throw in. A properly managed compost bin will not attract animals and will not smell bad. And your indoor compost should be ready in two to five weeks.
lines.zh: 网站说，要注意往里扔什么。管理得当的堆肥桶不会招来动物，也不会发臭。室内堆肥应该在两到五周内就能用了。

lines.en: Katie Ablard says composting is great for the environment. But she says it gives her a smaller, but still very important prize.
lines.zh: 凯蒂·阿布拉德说，堆肥对环境很好。但她说，它也给了她一份小小的、却非常重要的奖赏。

lines.en: "Twice a year I'm able to pull out the soil that the worms and the other bugs and insects have created by breaking down the food waste. And that soil or compost then I use in our garden. And so, the soil in our community garden is very rich and very healthy and has consistently been good soil for growing vegetables. So, it's instead of using chemical fertilizers and it's instead of using other products that might help things grow, but we can just use the compost!"
lines.zh: “每年两次，我能取出蚯蚓和其他虫子分解食物垃圾后形成的土壤，然后把这些土或者说堆肥用在我们的菜园里。所以我们社区菜园的土壤非常肥沃、非常健康，一直是种菜的好土。我们不用化肥，也不用其他可能帮助植物生长的产品，只用堆肥就行！”

lines.en: And that's the Health & Lifestyle report. I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 以上就是《健康与生活》节目。我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: What are the three basic ingredients for composting?
opts: brown material, green material and water
qs.a: brown material, green material and water
qs.why: "all composting requires three basic ingredients."

qs.q: How much of its food waste did South Korea recycle in 2019?
qs.why: "South Korea recycled 95 percent of its food waste."

qs.q: Why should you stir the compost often?
opts: to add air and keep it light
qs.a: to add air and keep it light
qs.why: "This adds air to keep it light."

lessons.title: Deep Breathing Helps the Lungs
lessons.zh: 深呼吸有益肺部
lessons.sum: 我们每天呼吸约 2 万次，却很少注意它。深呼吸时空气充满肺部，腹部隆起，能减慢心跳、降低血压、缓解压力；很多人习惯浅短的“胸式呼吸”，让陈旧空气留在肺里。文章介绍了一个简单的腹式深呼吸练习。

lines.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle report.
lines.zh: 这里是 VOA 慢速英语《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: When was the last time you thought about breathing? Most people usually do not.
lines.zh: 你上一次想到呼吸是什么时候？大多数人通常不会想。

lines.en: When we are healthy, breathing happens naturally and easily. Without much effect on our part, the human respiratory system works hard. Experts say we take about 20,000 breaths every day.
lines.zh: 我们健康时，呼吸自然而轻松地进行。我们几乎不用费力，人体的呼吸系统就在努力工作。专家说，我们每天呼吸约 2 万次。

lines.en: One such expert is James Hoyt, a doctor at the University of Colorado's Health Pulmonology Clinic, also called UCHealth. Hoyt is a pulmonologist -- a specialist on respiratory disorders.
lines.zh: 詹姆斯·霍伊特就是这样一位专家，他是科罗拉多大学健康肺科诊所（也叫 UCHealth）的医生。霍伊特是肺科医生——呼吸系统疾病专家。

lines.en: On the UCHealth website, he notes that our "respiratory muscles are working every minute of the day, every day of our lives."
lines.zh: 他在 UCHealth 网站上指出，我们的“呼吸肌在我们一生中的每一天、每一分钟都在工作”。

lines.en: A muscle called the diaphragm separates the chest and abdominal cavities. As we breathe in, the diaphragm tightens. The chest cavity opens, and the lungs expand. When we breathe out, the diaphragm relaxes and moves upward, pushing air out.
lines.zh: 一块叫膈肌的肌肉把胸腔和腹腔分开。我们吸气时，膈肌收紧，胸腔张开，肺扩张。我们呼气时，膈肌放松并向上移动，把空气推出去。

lines.en: When you breathe deeply, the air coming in through your nose fully fills your lungs, and the lower belly rises. On its website, Harvard Medical School notes that deep breathing may slow the heartbeat, lower blood pressure and lower stress. Deep breaths help your body fully exchange incoming oxygen with outgoing carbon dioxide.
lines.zh: 深呼吸时，从鼻子进来的空气充满整个肺部，小腹随之隆起。哈佛医学院在网站上指出，深呼吸可以减慢心跳、降低血压、减轻压力。深呼吸能帮助身体充分地用吸进的氧气交换呼出的二氧化碳。

lines.en: However, many people do the opposite of deep breathing. They take short breaths and have shallow breathing. Experts call this "chest breathing."
lines.zh: 然而，很多人的做法恰恰相反。他们呼吸短促、浅薄，专家称之为“胸式呼吸”。

lines.en: Shallow breathing limits the expansion of the diaphragm and its movement. The lowest part of the lungs does not get a full share of oxygenated air. This can make you feel short of breath and worried, or anxious.
lines.zh: 浅呼吸限制了膈肌的扩展和运动，肺的最下部得不到足够的含氧空气。这会让你感到气短、担心或焦虑。

lines.en: The American Lung Association notes that shallow breathing, over time, leaves old, stale air in the lungs. This leaves less room for the diaphragm to bring in fresh oxygen. And that means lower oxygen levels and less oxygen for exercise and activity.
lines.zh: 美国肺脏协会指出，长期浅呼吸会让陈旧的空气留在肺里，膈肌吸入新鲜氧气的空间就小了。这意味着氧气水平降低，运动和活动时可用的氧气也更少。

lines.en: Several health websites explain an easy deep breathing exercise.
lines.zh: 好几个健康网站介绍了一个简单的深呼吸练习。

lines.en: Find a place to sit or lie down. Place one hand just below your ribs. Take a slow, deep breath -- or inhale -- through your nose. Feel your hand go up. Your stomach should rise and expand. Now breathe out slowly through your mouth. Make sure to breathe out -- or exhale -- all the way. Feel your hand and stomach go down.
lines.zh: 找个地方坐下或躺下。把一只手放在肋骨下方。用鼻子慢慢地深吸一口气，感觉手往上抬，你的肚子应该鼓起来、扩张开。现在用嘴慢慢呼气，一定要把气全部呼出去，感觉手和肚子往下落。

lines.en: The American Lung Association website states that if done repeatedly, breathing exercises can help remove stale air from the lungs. This will increase oxygen levels and get the diaphragm to return to its job of helping you breathe.
lines.zh: 美国肺脏协会网站说，反复做呼吸练习可以帮助排出肺里的陈旧空气。这会提高氧气水平，让膈肌恢复帮助你呼吸的工作。

lines.en: Pulmonologist James Hoyt adds that "deep breathing is a good way to reduce stress and relax."
lines.zh: 肺科医生詹姆斯·霍伊特补充说：“深呼吸是减轻压力、放松身心的好办法。”

lines.en: Hoyt tells patients to avoid smoking, to eat a good diet and to get a good night's rest. He also urges them to seek help for respiratory conditions as soon as they are observed.
lines.zh: 霍伊特告诉病人不要吸烟，要吃得健康，晚上睡个好觉。他还敦促他们一发现呼吸方面的问题就尽快求医。

lines.en: Shortness of breath happens when you are worried, frightened, or are in poor physical shape. But it can also be a sign of health problems.
lines.zh: 人在担心、害怕或身体状况不好时会气短，但气短也可能是健康问题的信号。

lines.en: And that's the Health & Lifestyle report. I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 以上就是《健康与生活》节目。我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: About how many breaths do we take every day?
qs.why: "we take about 20,000 breaths every day."

qs.q: What is "chest breathing"?
qs.why: "They take short breaths and have shallow breathing. Experts call this 'chest breathing.'"

qs.q: In the exercise, what should your stomach do when you breathe in?
qs.why: "Your stomach should rise and expand."

lessons.title: Why You Need to Start Strength Training Today
lessons.zh: 为什么今天就该开始力量训练
lessons.sum: 30 岁以后，人每十年会流失 3%～5% 的肌肉，不运动会让流失加快。力量训练能增加骨密度、控制体重、改善平衡、减轻多种慢性病的问题。可以用弹力带、哑铃、器械，或者用自己的体重做俯卧撑、平板支撑、深蹲；记得热身、休息、吃蛋白质。

lines.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle report.
lines.zh: 这里是 VOA 慢速英语《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: The aging process affects the human body in many ways. One thing that happens to all of us as we age is muscle loss.
lines.zh: 衰老会在很多方面影响人体。随着年龄增长，我们每个人都会遇到的一件事就是肌肉流失。

lines.en: Some experts say muscle loss begins around age 50. But others say it can start as early as age 30.
lines.zh: 有些专家说肌肉流失从 50 岁左右开始，也有人说最早 30 岁就开始了。

lines.en: The Harvard Health Publishing website notes that "after age 30, you begin to lose as much as three percent to five percent" of muscle every 10 years. They add that most "men will lose about 30% of their muscle mass during their lifetimes."
lines.zh: 哈佛健康出版社网站指出，“30 岁以后，你每十年会流失多达 3% 到 5%”的肌肉。他们还说，大多数“男性一生中会流失约 30% 的肌肉量”。

lines.en: Experts may not know exactly when muscles loss starts. But they do know this: being inactive can speed up the process.
lines.zh: 专家也许不确切知道肌肉流失从何时开始，但他们确实知道：不运动会加速这个过程。

lines.en: Now, the good news!
lines.zh: 现在，说说好消息！

lines.en: Lost muscles are not gone forever. Although muscle loss may be a natural part of aging, you can do some things to slow it down. It is better to start building muscles when you are younger and in good health. But it is never too late to start strength training.
lines.zh: 流失的肌肉并不是永远找不回来。虽然肌肉流失可能是衰老的自然过程，但你可以做一些事来减缓它。最好在年轻健康时就开始锻炼肌肉，但开始力量训练永远不嫌晚。

lines.en: But what exactly is "strength training"?
lines.zh: 那么，“力量训练”到底是什么？

lines.en: Simply put, strength training is any activity that makes one's muscles stronger. We will talk about those exercises a little later. But first, let us talk about some of the health benefits of strength training. This information comes from Harvard Medical School and the Mayo Clinic, a nonprofit health and research organization in the United States.
lines.zh: 简单地说，力量训练就是任何能让肌肉更强壮的活动。我们稍后再讲这些练习。先来谈谈力量训练对健康的一些好处。这些信息来自哈佛医学院和美国的非营利医疗研究机构梅奥诊所。

lines.en: Here are reasons to start your strength training today.
lines.zh: 下面是今天就开始力量训练的理由。

lines.en: Harvard University researchers say that strength training puts pressure on your bones. And that is a good thing. This pressure can increase the thickness or density of bones. This can reduce your risk of developing osteoporosis -- a disease that weakens bones, making them easy to break.
lines.zh: 哈佛大学的研究人员说，力量训练会给你的骨骼施加压力。这是好事。这种压力能增加骨骼的厚度或密度，从而降低患骨质疏松症的风险——这种病会让骨骼变弱、容易骨折。

lines.en: Osteoporosis affects men and women of all races. But the Mayo Clinic notes that "white and Asian women — especially older women who are past menopause — are at highest risk."
lines.zh: 骨质疏松症影响所有种族的男性和女性。但梅奥诊所指出，“白人和亚裔女性——尤其是绝经后的老年女性——风险最高”。

lines.en: Strength training can help you to take control of your weight and even lose weight. Muscle weighs more than fat. But muscle increases your metabolism, and a higher metabolism helps you burn more calories.
lines.zh: 力量训练能帮你控制体重，甚至减重。肌肉比脂肪重，但肌肉能提高新陈代谢，而更高的新陈代谢帮你燃烧更多卡路里。

lines.en: Strength training can improve your ability to do everyday activities. For example, having stronger muscles makes it easier to lift and move things.
lines.zh: 力量训练能提高你进行日常活动的能力。比如，肌肉更强壮，提东西、搬东西就更容易。

lines.en: Strong muscles can improve your balance. So, your risk of falling or getting injured may be lessened. As we age, this can greatly add to your quality of life.
lines.zh: 强壮的肌肉能改善平衡，所以你摔倒或受伤的风险可能会降低。随着年龄增长，这能大大提高你的生活质量。

lines.en: Experts say strength training can reduce the problems of many chronic -- or long-term -- disorders, such as arthritis, back pain, heart disease, diabetes and depression.
lines.zh: 专家说，力量训练能减轻许多慢性——也就是长期——疾病带来的问题，比如关节炎、背痛、心脏病、糖尿病和抑郁症。

lines.en: The Mayo Clinic says some research shows that regular strength training, when combined with other kinds of exercise, may help older adults think and learn better.
lines.zh: 梅奥诊所说，一些研究表明，定期力量训练与其他运动结合，可能帮助老年人更好地思考和学习。

lines.en: Resistance material is rubbery. When you pull on it, it gives your muscles resistance. There are many kinds of resistance material. They do not cost much and are often sold in sporting goods stores.
lines.zh: 弹力带是一种橡胶材料。拉它时，它会给你的肌肉提供阻力。弹力带有很多种，价格不贵，体育用品店里常有卖。

lines.en: Free weights, commonly used in strength training, are handheld weights. They are not connected to exercise equipment; so, we call them "free." We also call them barbells or dumbbells. If you do not have free weights, you can use any heavy object that is safe to lift.
lines.zh: 力量训练中常用的“自由重量”是手持的重物。它们不连在健身器械上，所以叫“自由”重量，我们也叫它杠铃或哑铃。如果你没有哑铃，可以用任何可以安全举起的重物。

lines.en: Many gyms and health clubs have weightlifting or resistance machines. Some people also buy these machines and set them up at home. But they can cost a lot of money.
lines.zh: 很多健身房和健身俱乐部有举重或阻力训练器械。有些人也会买这些器械放在家里，但可能很贵。

lines.en: Working with free weights or weightlifting machines can be riskier. If you are new to weight training, experts suggest working with a trainer or physical fitness specialist. This way you will learn the right way to move and avoid injury.
lines.zh: 用自由重量或举重器械训练风险更大一些。如果你刚开始练力量，专家建议跟着教练或健身专家一起练，这样你能学会正确的动作，避免受伤。

lines.en: The Mayo Clinic has this warning for those wanting to start weight training. Its experts say you should talk with your doctor before beginning if you:
lines.zh: 梅奥诊所给想开始负重训练的人提出了这样的警告。专家们说，如果你有以下情况，开始前应该先咨询医生：

lines.en: have a chronic health condition,
lines.zh: 有慢性疾病，

lines.en: are older than age 40, and
lines.zh: 年龄超过 40 岁，并且

lines.en: have not been active recently.
lines.zh: 最近一直不怎么运动。

lines.en: If you are using weights, how much should you use? The right amount should tire muscles after 12 to 15 repetitions. You can slowly increase the amount as you get stronger.
lines.zh: 如果你用重物，该用多重的？合适的重量应该在做 12 到 15 次后让肌肉感到疲劳。随着力量增强，你可以慢慢增加重量。

lines.en: Also listen to your body. If an exercise causes pain, stop the exercise. Experts say after the pain goes away you can try the exercise again, but with a lower weight.
lines.zh: 还要倾听身体的声音。如果某个动作引起疼痛，就停下来。专家说疼痛消失后可以再试，但要减轻重量。

lines.en: You do not have to use special exercise equipment or go to a gym to do strength training. You can use your own body weight as resistance.
lines.zh: 做力量训练不一定要用专门的器械或去健身房，你可以用自己的体重作为阻力。

lines.en: Exercises that use body weight as resistance are usually safer for beginners. They can also be easier on the body, and you can do them anywhere. Push-ups, plank poses, jumping jacks, side jumps and squats - or deep knee bends - are great exercises for making muscles stronger.
lines.zh: 用体重作阻力的练习通常对初学者更安全，对身体也更温和，而且随时随地都能做。俯卧撑、平板支撑、开合跳、侧跳和深蹲都是让肌肉更强壮的好练习。

lines.en: The experts also suggest warming up before strength training. Cold muscles injure more easily than warm muscles. Walking for five to 10 minutes is enough to warm up your muscles.
lines.zh: 专家们还建议力量训练前先热身。冷的肌肉比热的肌肉更容易受伤。走五到十分钟就足以让肌肉热起来。

lines.en: And give your muscles time to recover. They say to rest one full day between exercising each specific muscle group.
lines.zh: 还要给肌肉恢复的时间。他们说，锻炼同一组肌肉之间要休息一整天。

lines.en: And do not forget that some foods help you build muscle. The body breaks down protein into amino acids, which it uses to build muscle. So, experts say eat a little healthy protein with each meal -- foods such as chicken, salmon, beans and yogurt.
lines.zh: 别忘了，有些食物能帮你增长肌肉。身体会把蛋白质分解成氨基酸，用来构建肌肉。所以专家说，每顿饭都吃一点健康的蛋白质——比如鸡肉、三文鱼、豆类和酸奶。

lines.en: And that's the Health & Lifestyle report for this week.
lines.zh: 以上就是本周的《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: I'm Jonathan Evans.
lines.zh: 我是乔纳森·埃文斯。

lines.en: And I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: How much muscle can you lose every 10 years after age 30?
qs.why: "you begin to lose as much as three percent to five percent of muscle every 10 years."

qs.q: How does strength training help your bones?
qs.why: "This pressure can increase the thickness or density of bones."

qs.q: Which exercise uses your own body weight?
qs.why: "Push-ups, plank poses, jumping jacks, side jumps and squats."

lessons.title: Flowers You Can Eat
lessons.zh: 可以吃的花
lessons.sum: 一些花能给食物增添色彩和意想不到的味道。专家提醒三件事：认清哪些花能吃、知道花的来源、了解自己对什么过敏。蒲公英、旱金莲、琉璃苣（味道像黄瓜）、紫罗兰、洋甘菊和香草的花都可以吃；毛茛、香豌豆、杜鹃等有毒。四岁以下儿童不要吃。

lines.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle report.
lines.zh: 这里是 VOA 慢速英语《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: Flowers are an important part of our natural world. Their beauty and smell can make us happy. Flowers serve as food for insects, birds, and animals. And they can also feed us!
lines.zh: 花是大自然的重要组成部分。它们的美丽和香气能让我们快乐。花是昆虫、鸟类和动物的食物。它们也可以喂饱我们！

lines.en: Some flowers add color, unexpected taste, and beauty to food and drinks. And more people are adding them to their meals. To find out more, we talked with a few Americans who like to grow and eat their own flowers.
lines.zh: 有些花能给食物和饮料增添色彩、意想不到的味道和美感，越来越多的人把它们加进饭菜里。为了了解更多，我们采访了几位喜欢自己种花吃花的美国人。

lines.en: Kathy Jentz is the publisher of Washington Gardener magazine. She also gives talks to Washington, D.C. area gardeners. She tells them how to grow and use edible flowers.
lines.zh: 凯西·詹茨是《华盛顿园丁》杂志的出版人，她还给华盛顿地区的园丁们做讲座，告诉他们怎样种植和使用可食用的花。

lines.en: Jentz says the way to prepare most edible flowers for your next dish or meal is to wash them lightly under water. Then remove the white parts of the flower. She also says to cut off the pistil and stamen.
lines.zh: 詹茨说，把大多数可食用花用于下一道菜或下一顿饭的准备方法，是用水轻轻冲洗，然后去掉花的白色部分。她还说要剪掉雌蕊和雄蕊。

lines.en: When speaking about edible flowers, Jentz often begins with three talking points:
lines.zh: 谈到可食用花时，詹茨常常从三个要点讲起：

lines.en: Know your flowers. Which ones are safe to eat?
lines.zh: 认识你的花。哪些可以安全食用？

lines.en: Know the source. Where did the flowers come from?
lines.zh: 了解来源。花是从哪里来的？

lines.en: Know your allergies. Which plants are you allergic to?
lines.zh: 了解你的过敏。你对哪些植物过敏？

lines.en: Some flowers are poisonous and can make you sick. There are a few flowers that people think are edible, Jentz says, even though they are poisonous.
lines.zh: 有些花有毒，会让你生病。詹茨说，有几种花人们以为能吃，其实有毒。

lines.en: The most common are buttercup and sweet pea. She says the flower of the sweet pea should not be mixed up with the flower of the pea plant, which is a vegetable. Other poisonous flowers are azalea, wisteria, and fox glove.
lines.zh: 最常见的是毛茛和香豌豆。她说不要把香豌豆的花和豌豆——一种蔬菜——的花搞混。其他有毒的花还有杜鹃、紫藤和毛地黄。

lines.en: Now, here is a quick list of common edible flowers.
lines.zh: 下面简单列一列常见的可食用花。

lines.en: One of the best edible flowers to start with is the dandelion. Jentz says they are nutritious, and you can eat the entire plant, not just the flower. This is not true for many edible flowers.
lines.zh: 最适合入门的可食用花之一是蒲公英。詹茨说它很有营养，而且整株都可以吃，不只是花。很多可食用花并不是这样。

lines.en: Nasturtium is easy to grow and, Jentz says, has a peppery taste. It is perfect for container gardening and for people living in a hot, big city. This flower often grows well in very difficult conditions.
lines.zh: 旱金莲很好种。詹茨说，它有一股胡椒般的辛辣味，非常适合盆栽，也适合住在炎热大城市的人。这种花常常在非常艰苦的条件下长得很好。

lines.en: "A container-grown flower that works really is nasturtium. It actually prefers container growing to being in the ground. The worst conditions you can give nasturtium -- the better it grows."
lines.zh: “真正适合盆栽的花是旱金莲。比起种在地里，它其实更喜欢盆栽。你给它的条件越差，它长得越好。”

lines.en: Many people add nasturtium to fruit or green salads. One such person is Elizabeth Lyttleton, a mother and cycling activist in the D.C. area. In warm weather, Lyttleton says she grows nasturtium on her front doorstep. She likes to add its flowers to salads or serve with other foods.
lines.zh: 很多人把旱金莲加进水果沙拉或蔬菜沙拉里，伊丽莎白·利特尔顿就是其中之一，她是华盛顿地区的一位母亲和自行车运动倡导者。利特尔顿说，天气暖和时她在家门口种旱金莲，喜欢把花加进沙拉或配其他菜一起吃。

lines.en: Also, in the D.C. area, Roshani Kothari says she has been growing and eating edible flowers for many years. She says that herbs are great ways to get into the world of edible flowers. Flowers from mint, rosemary, dill, oregano, cilantro, and sage add a little flavor of the herb. But they are not as strong as the leaves of the plant.
lines.zh: 同样住在华盛顿地区的罗莎妮·科塔里说，她种花吃花已经很多年了。她说香草是进入可食用花世界的好途径。薄荷、迷迭香、莳萝、牛至、香菜和鼠尾草的花会带一点香草的味道，但没有叶子那么浓。

lines.en: Kothari says one of her favorite herbs is cilantro.
lines.zh: 科塔里说，她最喜欢的香草之一是香菜。

lines.en: "And cilantro is easy to grow in a pot. If you let it go to flower, it will come back year after year. And um, it's used in so many different cultures. For example, I'm from India originally from the state of Gujarat and we use cilantro as a garnish in all the dishes we make. Without cilantro it's not quite … quite done yet!"
lines.zh: “香菜很容易在花盆里种。如果你让它开花，它会年复一年地长回来。而且，嗯，很多不同的文化都用它。比如我来自印度，老家在古吉拉特邦，我们做的每道菜都用香菜点缀。没有香菜，这道菜就还……还没做完！”

lines.en: Experts say the safest way to eat edible flowers is to grow them yourself. If you buy from a farmer's market or a farmer, ask them directly if they used any chemicals. Be careful buying from a food or flower store. Their flowers may have been treated with dangerous chemicals.
lines.zh: 专家说，吃可食用花最安全的方法是自己种。如果你从农贸市场或农民那里买，要直接问他们有没有用化学药剂。从食品店或花店买要小心，那里的花可能用危险的化学品处理过。

lines.en: If you go outdoors to pick edible flowers, says Kathy Jentz, do so in a safe area. Do not collect flowers from an area where dog owners walk their dogs or where chemical treatments have been used.
lines.zh: 凯西·詹茨说，如果你去户外采可食用花，要在安全的地方采。不要在人们遛狗或用过化学药剂的地方采花。

lines.en: Jentz says her personal favorite edible flower is borage. She says the plant's blue star-shaped flowers taste like cucumbers. So, borage can go with many dishes.
lines.zh: 詹茨说她个人最喜欢的可食用花是琉璃苣。她说这种植物蓝色星形的花尝起来像黄瓜，所以琉璃苣可以配很多菜。

lines.en: "My personal favorite is borage. The flower petals smell and taste like cucumber. The fact that you can add it on fruit salads, throw it in your gazpacho or use it to garnish a drink is a nice bonus."
lines.zh: “我个人最喜欢的是琉璃苣。它的花瓣闻起来、吃起来都像黄瓜。可以加在水果沙拉上，丢进西班牙冷汤里，或者用来装饰饮料，这是一个不错的额外好处。”

lines.en: Violets are another popular edible flower. They have a sweet flavor. Use the violets in salads, sweet treats, and drinks.
lines.zh: 紫罗兰是另一种受欢迎的可食用花，味道甜，可以用在沙拉、甜点和饮料里。

lines.en: Also, Jentz says violets can last a long time when left in a sealed container in the refrigerator. But she adds it is important to cut the flowers at the right time -- just as they open.
lines.zh: 詹茨还说，紫罗兰放在冰箱的密封容器里可以保存很久。但她补充说，在对的时间剪花很重要——就在它刚开的时候。

lines.en: This is not true of all edible flowers. Some wilt quite fast. To avoid this, Jentz says you can use the method people have been using for centuries – dry them.
lines.zh: 并不是所有可食用花都这样，有些很快就枯萎了。詹茨说，要避免这种情况，可以用人们几百年来一直用的办法——把它们晒干。

lines.en: Kothari explains that it is important to know how plants grow. Vegetables send out edible flowers if you let them go to seed.
lines.zh: 科塔里解释说，了解植物怎样生长很重要。如果你让蔬菜结籽，它们就会开出可以吃的花。

lines.en: However, if you take all the flowers from your vegetable plants, our experts warn, you will not have any vegetables! If you want to harvest the flowers of vegetables, Jentz suggests growing a vegetable plant just for its flowers.
lines.zh: 可是我们的专家提醒，如果你把蔬菜上的花全摘了，就收不到蔬菜了！如果你想收获蔬菜的花，詹茨建议专门种一棵蔬菜来采花。

lines.en: Chamomile flowers are small and taste like apple. Chamomile is often used in tea. Jentz says chamomile flowers dry nicely and they keep their flavor.
lines.zh: 洋甘菊的花很小，吃起来像苹果，常用来泡茶。詹茨说洋甘菊晒干后很好，还能保留味道。

lines.en: However, the website WebMD warns avoid chamomile "if you are allergic to these plants: ragweed, daisies, marigolds, or chrysanthemums.
lines.zh: 不过 WebMD 网站警告说，“如果你对豚草、雏菊、万寿菊或菊花这些植物过敏”，就要避免洋甘菊。

lines.en: If you have allergies to ragweed and other types of pollen, Jentz advises to avoid any flower in the daisy family.
lines.zh: 詹茨建议，如果你对豚草和其他花粉过敏，就避开所有菊科的花。

lines.en: Also, if you suffer from allergies or have other food sensitivities, Jentz suggests trying new edible flowers one at a time. If you eat many different ones for the first time and then get sick, you will not know which one made you sick.
lines.zh: 另外，如果你有过敏或其他食物敏感，詹茨建议一次只尝试一种新的可食用花。如果你第一次就吃了很多种，然后生病了，就不知道是哪一种让你生病的。

lines.en: Jentz also gives this warning: Do not give edible flowers to any child under the age of four.
lines.zh: 詹茨还提出了这样的警告：不要给四岁以下的孩子吃可食用花。

lines.en: And that's the Health & Lifestyle report. Have fun trying different edible flowers.
lines.zh: 以上就是《健康与生活》节目。祝你尝试各种可食用花玩得开心。

lines.en: I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: What are Kathy Jentz's three talking points?
opts: know your flowers, the source, and your allergies
qs.a: know your flowers, the source, and your allergies
qs.why: "Know your flowers... Know the source... Know your allergies."

qs.q: What does borage taste like?
qs.why: "The flower petals smell and taste like cucumber."

qs.q: Which flower is poisonous?
qs.why: "The most common are buttercup and sweet pea."

lessons.title: Understanding Your Brain and Clutter
lessons.zh: 了解你的大脑与杂乱
lessons.sum: 春天很多美国人会大扫除、清理杂物。可普林斯顿大学研究大脑如何处理杂乱的卡斯特纳教授说，并非所有杂乱都不好：大脑天生就能应对杂乱。有人在整洁的地方效率高，有人反而需要满桌东西激发灵感——关键是找到适合自己的方式。

lines.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle Report.
lines.zh: 这里是 VOA 慢速英语《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: In springtime, many Americans take on a major project: cleaning their homes from top to bottom. We often call this kind of work "spring cleaning."
lines.zh: 春天，许多美国人会承担一项大工程：把家里从上到下打扫一遍。我们常把这种活叫“春季大扫除”。

lines.en: Part of spring cleaning often involves clearing out clutter. We do away with things we no longer need – like old magazines, toys from our childhood, collections of things we no longer collect ...
lines.zh: 春季大扫除常常包括清理杂物。我们扔掉不再需要的东西——比如旧杂志、小时候的玩具、不再收集的收藏品……

lines.en: If we are to believe the many stories on Marie Kondo, the Queen of Clean, clutter adds unnecessary stress to our lives. Clutter is holding us back from our dreams and goals.
lines.zh: 如果相信关于“整理女王”近藤麻理惠的种种报道，杂乱给我们的生活增加了不必要的压力，阻碍我们实现梦想和目标。

lines.en: But is it?
lines.zh: 可真的是这样吗？

lines.en: To answer this question, I spoke with an expert on the subject -- Sabine Kastner of Princeton University. She has been studying how the brain processes clutter for 20 years.
lines.zh: 为了回答这个问题，我采访了这方面的一位专家——普林斯顿大学的萨宾·卡斯特纳。她研究大脑如何处理杂乱已经 20 年了。

lines.en: From the start of our interview, Professor Kastner wants to make two things clear: Not all clutter is bad. And our brains can deal with it.
lines.zh: 采访一开始，卡斯特纳教授就想讲清楚两件事：不是所有杂乱都不好；而且我们的大脑能应对它。

lines.en: The media, Kastner says, often writes about clutter in a very simple, black-and-white way: Clutter affects the mind and we need to clear it out. But Kastner says it is much more complex than that. For starters, she says, our brains are designed to deal with clutter.
lines.zh: 卡斯特纳说，媒体常常用非常简单、非黑即白的方式写杂乱：杂乱影响心智，我们需要把它清理掉。但卡斯特纳说，实际情况要复杂得多。首先，她说，我们的大脑天生就是为应对杂乱而设计的。

lines.en: "Clutter is all around us -- all the time -- as soon as we open our eyes. And the fact that we do not perceive it as that...just speaks to this enormous capability that we have to deal with it."
lines.zh: “只要我们一睁开眼睛，杂乱就一直在我们周围。而我们并不觉得它杂乱……这恰恰说明我们有应对它的巨大能力。”

lines.en: Kastner uses a Christmas tree as an example. When we see a Christmas tree, we know what it is -- a sign of the winter holiday season. We do not need to see each separate item hanging on the tree to understand this.
lines.zh: 卡斯特纳以圣诞树为例。我们看到圣诞树时，就知道它是什么——冬季节日的象征。我们不需要看清树上挂的每一样东西才明白这一点。

lines.en: Kastner says very early in the development of our eyesight, we begin to group objects that we see. This helps us to structure our environment. She explains that it helps us sort out anything that is not necessary.
lines.zh: 卡斯特纳说，在视觉发育的很早阶段，我们就开始把看到的物体分组。这帮助我们把环境变得有条理。她解释说，这帮我们筛掉任何不必要的东西。

lines.en: "The attention system in our brains actually likes clutter because that is what it is used to. And it is using this cluttered environment to make meaningful selections from it."
lines.zh: “我们大脑里的注意力系统其实喜欢杂乱，因为它就是习惯杂乱的。它正是利用这种杂乱的环境，从中做出有意义的选择。”

lines.en: When we talk about clutter and how best our brains perform around it, Kastner says there is not a one-size-fits-all solution. The idea that an uncluttered workplace is better, she says, is not "universally true."
lines.zh: 卡斯特纳说，说到杂乱以及大脑在杂乱中怎样表现最好，没有一刀切的解决办法。她说，整洁的工作场所更好这种观念并非“普遍正确”。

lines.en: Kastner says some people need to see their work. If something is carefully put away, to them it does not exist anymore. Out of sight, out of mind. For other people, objects can stimulate their creativity and give them ideas.
lines.zh: 卡斯特纳说，有些人需要看到自己的工作。如果东西被仔细收起来了，对他们来说就不存在了，眼不见心不想。对另一些人来说，身边的东西能激发他们的创造力，给他们灵感。

lines.en: "Then there are other people who actually like that clutter. And they, you know, clutter their environment because it actually helps them. It almost like stimulating their brain to do something."
lines.zh: “还有一些人其实喜欢那种杂乱。你知道，他们把周围弄得乱糟糟的，因为这真的对他们有帮助，几乎像是在刺激他们的大脑去做事。”

lines.en: However, other people are unable to work in a cluttered environment. Kastner notes that some people may get distracted by having lots of things around them. These people may need more organization and less clutter to work well.
lines.zh: 然而，另一些人在杂乱的环境中无法工作。卡斯特纳指出，有些人身边东西一多就容易分心。这些人可能需要更整齐、更少杂物才能好好工作。

lines.en: Some people do not care either way. Whether the area is cluttered or clear -- they work the same.
lines.zh: 有些人两种都无所谓，不管地方乱还是整洁，他们工作起来都一样。

lines.en: And for others it may depend on the project. For administrative work, they might need a clear workspace. But for more creative projects, they may need many things around them.
lines.zh: 对还有些人来说，这取决于项目。做行政工作时，他们可能需要整洁的工作区；但做更有创意的项目时，他们可能需要身边有很多东西。

lines.en: Like Kastner said earlier, it is complex.
lines.zh: 就像卡斯特纳之前说的，这很复杂。

lines.en: However, on one thing, she is very clear: One way is not better than another. People need to be able to design their workspaces, she says, in a way that works best for them.
lines.zh: 不过，有一点她说得非常明确：没有哪种方式比另一种更好。她说，人们需要能够按最适合自己的方式布置工作空间。

lines.en: "But again I think it's important to take this all into consideration when you create workspaces because you need to give people, I think, the individual choices -- whatever serves them best."
lines.zh: “不过，我认为在设计工作空间时把这一切都考虑进去很重要，因为我认为你需要给人们个人的选择——怎样对他们最好就怎样。”

lines.en: To know how your brain reacts to clutter, Kastner says you need to take an honest look at your home and work environments. What is working and what is not? If your home or office is cluttered and you cannot find anything, you may need more organizing. However, if your house or office is cluttered but you can find everything you need – then perhaps your brain works fine around clutter.
lines.zh: 卡斯特纳说，要想知道你的大脑对杂乱有什么反应，你需要诚实地审视自己的家和工作环境：什么管用，什么不管用？如果你的家或办公室很乱，你什么都找不到，你可能需要多整理整理。但如果你的家或办公室很乱，你却能找到需要的一切——那也许你的大脑在杂乱中运转得很好。

lines.en: Kastner gives this warning: Do not continue doing something that is not working for you.
lines.zh: 卡斯特纳提出了这样的警告：不要继续做对你不管用的事。

lines.en: She has another warning: We should not blame clutter for all of our stress and lack of productivity. There could be many issues involved in both.
lines.zh: 她还有另一个警告：我们不应该把自己所有的压力和效率低下都归咎于杂乱，这两者可能涉及许多问题。

lines.en: Now, if you are wondering which way Kastner prefers…she likes clutter! Both at home and at work. In fact, she says she feels sad if her workspace is too clean.
lines.zh: 那么，如果你想知道卡斯特纳更喜欢哪种……她喜欢杂乱！家里和单位都是。事实上，她说如果工作区太干净，她会觉得难过。

lines.en: "But I know a lot of people who really need clear workspaces. Those would be spaces that would depress me. I would never excel in spaces like that. But I know that there are people who really excel in these spaces. So, they are just different from me. I think that's great and that's wonderful."
lines.zh: “但我知道很多人真的需要整洁的工作区。那样的空间会让我沮丧，我在那样的地方绝不会有出色的表现。但我知道有人在那样的空间里确实表现出色。他们只是和我不一样。我觉得这很好，很美妙。”

lines.en: Kastner says our brains are all so different and that is what makes us who we are.
lines.zh: 卡斯特纳说，我们每个人的大脑都如此不同，这正是我们之所以成为自己的原因。

lines.en: And that's the Health & Lifestyle report. I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 以上就是《健康与生活》节目。我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: What does Professor Kastner say about clutter?
opts: Not all clutter is bad, and our brains can deal with it.
qs.a: Not all clutter is bad, and our brains can deal with it.
qs.why: "Not all clutter is bad. And our brains can deal with it."

qs.q: Which workspace does Kastner prefer?
qs.why: "she likes clutter! Both at home and at work."

qs.q: What is Kastner's warning?
opts: Don't keep doing something that isn't working for you.
qs.a: Don't keep doing something that isn't working for you.
