lessons.title: Fight Tension, Boredom with a Container Garden
lessons.zh: 用盆栽菜园对抗紧张和无聊
lessons.sum: 种菜能让人更快乐、缓解压力。没有大院子也可以用桶、篮子、布袋做容器种菜：吃果实和根的蔬菜需要全日照，吃叶子的半日照就行；可以往上搭架子、往下挂篮子；注意哪些植物能种在一起。文章最后给出了自制无土基质和开始种植的七个步骤。

lines.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle Report.
lines.zh: 这里是 VOA 慢速英语《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: Research shows that growing fruits, vegetables and other plants can make us happier and relieve tension. Working with dirt and plants can be fun. Also, when we garden, we are outside, getting sunshine, fresh air and exercise.
lines.zh: 研究表明，种水果、蔬菜和其他植物能让我们更快乐，缓解紧张。摆弄泥土和植物很有趣。而且种菜时我们在户外，能晒太阳、呼吸新鲜空气、活动身体。

lines.en: Best of all – a garden gives us healthy fruits and vegetables to feed our families. This can increase our sense of independence. Every time we bite into a sweet tomato or a fresh green bean, we can say happily, "I grew this!"
lines.zh: 最棒的是——菜园能给我们提供健康的水果和蔬菜养活家人。这能增强我们的独立感。每次咬一口甜甜的番茄或新鲜的四季豆，我们都可以高兴地说：“这是我种的！”

lines.en: That's right. But not all of us have space, time or money for a large garden.
lines.zh: 没错。可不是每个人都有地方、时间或钱来弄一个大菜园。

lines.en: Well, you can garden in small spaces with containers. Container gardening is an easy way to grow vegetables when you lack the space. Even on a balcony or rooftop, you can still garden in containers.
lines.zh: 不过，你可以在小空间里用容器种菜。没有地方时，容器种植是种蔬菜的简单方法。即使在阳台或屋顶上，你也能用容器种菜。

lines.en: If you do not have money to buy containers, look around your home or neighborhood. You can start your garden in just about anything. Do you have buckets, baskets, cloth bags or boxes? You can use all of them!
lines.zh: 如果没钱买容器，就在家里或附近找找。你几乎可以用任何东西开始你的菜园。你有桶、篮子、布袋或箱子吗？都可以用！

lines.en: Before starting, decide on a place. How much sunlight will it get? Do you have safe access to a rooftop? Is it protected from the wind? Are you able to easily water the plants? All these things are important.
lines.zh: 开始之前，先决定放在哪里。那里能晒到多少阳光？你能安全地上屋顶吗？那里避风吗？方便浇水吗？这些都很重要。

lines.en: In your containers, you can control the soil and the amount of water, but not the sunlight. So, find out which plants can grow in the light conditions you have.
lines.zh: 在容器里，你可以控制土壤和水量，却控制不了阳光。所以要弄清楚，在你现有的光照条件下哪些植物能长。

lines.en: The website Gardeners.com says that most vegetables need at least six hours of sunlight every day or full sun. However, some plants can grow in partial shade. This means direct sunlight for about three to six hours.
lines.zh: Gardeners.com 网站说，大多数蔬菜每天至少需要六小时阳光，也就是全日照。不过有些植物可以在半阴处生长，也就是每天有三到六小时的直射阳光。

lines.en: Here is a rule of thumb: If you eat the fruit or root of the plant, it needs full sun. This includes tomatoes, eggplant, peppers, squash, potatoes or carrots.
lines.zh: 有一条经验法则：如果你吃的是植物的果实或根，它就需要全日照，包括番茄、茄子、辣椒、南瓜、土豆或胡萝卜。

lines.en: If you eat the leaves, it can grow in partial sun. This includes broccoli, cauliflower, beans, beets, kale and salad greens. Some herbs, such as mint, cilantro and thyme, grow well in partial sun.
lines.zh: 如果你吃的是叶子，它就能在半日照下生长，包括西兰花、花菜、豆子、甜菜、羽衣甘蓝和沙拉菜。一些香草，比如薄荷、香菜和百里香，在半日照下也长得很好。

lines.en: When growing in containers, the soil depth is important. For example, potatoes and carrots need a deeper container than other vegetables. Plants that do well in containers do not have very deep roots. However, you will have to research which plants grow well in your area of the world.
lines.zh: 用容器种植时，土的深度很重要。比如，土豆和胡萝卜需要比其他蔬菜更深的容器。适合容器种植的植物根都不太深。不过，你得研究一下哪些植物在你所在的地区长得好。

lines.en: In small spaces, do not forget about growing upward. You can buy or build a lightweight, ladder-like structure for your plants to grow up. Plants that grow up nicely are peas, beans, cucumbers and tomatoes.
lines.zh: 在小空间里，别忘了往上种。你可以买或自己搭一个轻便的梯子状架子，让植物往上爬。往上长得好的植物有豌豆、豆角、黄瓜和番茄。

lines.en: Another way to use a small space is to grow down in hanging baskets. If your baskets are not very deep, pick plants with shallow root systems. Strawberries and many kinds of herbs can grow very nicely in a small hanging container.
lines.zh: 利用小空间的另一种方法是用吊篮往下种。如果吊篮不太深，就选根系浅的植物。草莓和很多香草在小吊盆里都能长得很好。

lines.en: Just remember: With smaller containers or hanging baskets, you will need to water them more.
lines.zh: 只要记住：容器越小，或者用吊篮，就需要越常浇水。

lines.en: With container gardening, you can grow different plants in the same pot. This saves room. And some plants may grow better when paired with another plant.
lines.zh: 用容器种菜时，你可以把不同的植物种在同一个盆里，这样能节省空间。有些植物和别的植物搭配时可能长得更好。

lines.en: However, not all plants grow well together. Some compete for the same nutrients. Also, do not grow plants in the same pot if they have very different water and soil needs.
lines.zh: 不过，不是所有植物都能和睦相处。有些会争夺同样的养分。另外，对水和土要求差别很大的植物，也不要种在同一个盆里。

lines.en: These plants grow well together:
lines.zh: 这些植物种在一起长得好：

lines.en: Beans, carrots and squash
lines.zh: 豆子、胡萝卜和南瓜

lines.en: Eggplant and beans
lines.zh: 茄子和豆子

lines.en: Tomatoes, basil and onions
lines.zh: 番茄、罗勒和洋葱

lines.en: Lettuce and herbs or
lines.zh: 生菜和香草，或者

lines.en: Spinach, chard and onions
lines.zh: 菠菜、甜菜叶和洋葱

lines.en: These groupings may not work so well:
lines.zh: 这些组合可能不太好：

lines.en: Carrots with dill or fennel
lines.zh: 胡萝卜和莳萝或茴香

lines.en: Tomatoes or squash with potatoes
lines.zh: 番茄或南瓜和土豆

lines.en: Onions or garlic with beans and peas
lines.zh: 洋葱或大蒜和豆子、豌豆

lines.en: If wind is a problem where you live, remember to protect the plants. Wind can damage parts of the plants. It can also dry them out. Choose a location for your garden that has shelter from a building or make your own wind protection. Grouping plants together can help, too.
lines.zh: 如果你住的地方风大，记得保护植物。风会损伤植物的部分枝叶，还会让它们变干。给菜园选一个有建筑物挡风的地方，或者自己做挡风的东西。把植物放在一起也有帮助。

lines.en: Your garden will need a regular supply of water. So, try to water your plants at the same time each day unless there is rain. It is best to water early in the morning. Watering at night can cause problems.
lines.zh: 你的菜园需要定期浇水。所以除非下雨，尽量每天在同一时间浇水。最好在清晨浇，晚上浇水可能会带来问题。

lines.en: However, if you can't water in the morning, water in the late afternoon or early evening. And put the water directly on the dirt.
lines.zh: 不过，如果早上没法浇，就在傍晚或天刚黑时浇，并且把水直接浇在土上。

lines.en: Also, try not to water during the hottest part of the day. The water may evaporate too fast. Also, water droplets on leaves can burn them.
lines.zh: 另外，尽量不要在一天中最热的时候浇水。水可能蒸发得太快，叶子上的水珠还可能把叶子灼伤。

lines.en: Regular garden dirt will not work as well for container gardens. The perfect mix is made up of peat moss, vermiculite or perlite and compost. Styrofoam, rice hulls or sand can be used instead of vermiculite or perlite.
lines.zh: 普通的园土不太适合容器菜园。最理想的混合物由泥炭藓、蛭石或珍珠岩以及堆肥组成。也可以用泡沫塑料、稻壳或沙子代替蛭石或珍珠岩。

lines.en: This soil-free mix delivers water, fertilizer and air to plant roots more quickly. It also drains well. If water sits on the roots, you may get root rot.
lines.zh: 这种无土混合物能更快地把水、肥料和空气输送到植物根部，排水也好。如果水积在根上，可能会烂根。

lines.en: Also, when growing in containers, plant food, such as compost, is especially important. Some plants just won't grow without it.
lines.zh: 另外，用容器种植时，堆肥这样的植物养料尤其重要，有些植物没有它根本长不起来。

lines.en: Okay, so you have chosen your location and your plants. Now, you are now ready to start growing!
lines.zh: 好了，你已经选好了地方和植物，现在可以开始种了！

lines.en: Here's how to start your garden.
lines.zh: 下面是开始你的菜园的方法。

lines.en: Make a soil-free mix for container gardening:
lines.zh: 为容器种植制作无土混合物：

lines.en: Step 1. Wear a mask. The materials are dry. They may irritate your nose and eyes as you mix them.
lines.zh: 第 1 步：戴上口罩。这些材料很干，混合时可能刺激你的鼻子和眼睛。

lines.en: Step 2. Mix equal parts of peat moss, compost and perlite or vermiculite together with a small amount of wood ash if you have it. If you are using sand, do not use as much because sand is heavy.
lines.zh: 第 2 步：把等量的泥炭藓、堆肥和珍珠岩或蛭石混在一起，如果有的话加一点草木灰。如果用沙子，别放太多，因为沙子很重。

lines.en: Step 3. Choose a container. Anything that will hold the mix and let some water out can be a container garden.
lines.zh: 第 3 步：选一个容器。任何能装住混合物、又能让部分水流出去的东西，都可以做容器菜园。

lines.en: You can even use a cloth bag. Use cardboard around the sides and bottom to help it stand up.
lines.zh: 你甚至可以用布袋，在四周和底部垫上纸板帮它立起来。

lines.en: Step 4. Fill the container with your mix. Water it well.
lines.zh: 第 4 步：把混合物装进容器，浇透水。

lines.en: Step 5. Start seedlings or buy small plants. To grow from seeds, use any small container, such as egg cartons or milk boxes. You can even use a cardboard toilet paper roll. Simply close one end, put the mix inside, wait for it to grow, then plant it in the ground.
lines.zh: 第 5 步：育苗或买小苗。要用种子种，可以用任何小容器，比如鸡蛋盒或牛奶盒，甚至可以用卫生纸的纸筒。只要把一端封住，装进混合物，等它长出来，再种到土里。

lines.en: Step 6. Label the plants. You don't want to forget what you planted! You also can make signs for your garden, reminding you when to water and when to fertilize. You can use your phone to keep notes and reminders. If you like notebooks, like I do, you can keep a record of what you plant.
lines.zh: 第 6 步：给植物贴标签。你可不想忘了自己种的是什么！你还可以给菜园做些牌子，提醒自己什么时候浇水、什么时候施肥。可以用手机做笔记和提醒。如果你像我一样喜欢用笔记本，也可以记下你种了什么。

lines.en: Step 7. Plant the seedlings. When seedlings have a second set of leaves, you can put them into the larger container. Leave some space between the seedlings so they have room to grow. Water and put in a place that gets some sun.
lines.zh: 第 7 步：移栽幼苗。幼苗长出第二对叶子时，就可以移到大容器里。幼苗之间留些空隙，给它们生长的空间。浇水，放在能晒到一些太阳的地方。

lines.en: I hope you have lots of fun with container gardening. I do!
lines.zh: 希望你玩容器种菜玩得开心。我就很开心！

lines.en: Gardening is fun! And we hope you can grow some tasty and healthy food for your meals.
lines.zh: 种菜很有趣！希望你能为自己的饭桌种出一些美味健康的食物。

lines.en: And join us again next week for another Health & Lifestyle report from VOA Learning English.
lines.zh: 下周请继续收听 VOA 慢速英语的《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: I'm Jill Robbins.
lines.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

lines.en: And I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: Which plants need full sun?
opts: plants whose fruit or root you eat
qs.a: plants whose fruit or root you eat
qs.why: "If you eat the fruit or root of the plant, it needs full sun."

qs.q: When is the best time to water?
opts: the hottest part of the day
qs.why: "It is best to water early in the morning."

qs.q: Which plants do not grow well together?
qs.why: "Tomatoes or squash with potatoes"

lessons.title: Pets, Especially Dogs, Help During Quarantine
lessons.zh: 居家隔离时，宠物尤其是狗能帮上忙
lessons.sum: 疫情期间人们被困在家里，容易感到孤独。美国疾控中心说，宠物能缓解孤独和抑郁，狗尤其能让主人多运动、减轻压力和焦虑。约 38% 的美国家庭养狗。网上的段子里，狗高兴主人天天在家，猫却嫌主人“怎么还不去上班”。

lines.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle report.
lines.zh: 这里是 VOA 慢速英语《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: Throughout human history, we have used animals for food and for work. But thousands of years ago, we began using them for something else – companionship.
lines.zh: 纵观人类历史，我们一直把动物当作食物和劳力。但几千年前，我们开始把它们用于另一件事——陪伴。

lines.en: They became our pets.
lines.zh: 它们成了我们的宠物。

lines.en: Pets are a source of comfort and happiness. They give their owners good feelings and a sense of purpose, especially during stressful or difficult times.
lines.zh: 宠物是安慰和快乐的来源。它们给主人带来好心情和一种目标感，尤其在压力大或困难的时候。

lines.en: And we are, indeed, in stressful times.
lines.zh: 而我们现在确实处在压力很大的时期。

lines.en: In many parts of the world, people are under stay-at-home orders to slow the spread of the new coronavirus. Stuck indoors, many people may feel isolated and lonely.
lines.zh: 在世界许多地方，人们按居家令待在家里，以减缓新冠病毒的传播。困在室内，很多人可能会感到孤立和寂寞。

lines.en: Having a pet – especially a dog – can help.
lines.zh: 养一只宠物——尤其是一只狗——会有帮助。

lines.en: Experts at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in the United States say pets can help ease "loneliness and depression by giving us companionship."
lines.zh: 美国疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）的专家说，宠物能“通过陪伴我们”缓解“孤独和抑郁”。

lines.en: They make special note of the helpful effects of dogs. The CDC says that dogs can have many helpful and healthy effects on the lives of their owners.
lines.zh: 他们特别提到了狗的有益作用。CDC 说，狗能对主人的生活产生许多有益健康的影响。

lines.en: Dogs, the health organization says, can: influence social, emotional and mental development in children; help make their owners more physically active; provide companionship; and reduce people's stress and anxiety.
lines.zh: 这个卫生机构说，狗能够：影响孩子的社交、情感和心智发展；让主人多活动身体；提供陪伴；减轻人们的压力和焦虑。

lines.en: The CDC estimates that around 38 percent of American households have one or more dogs.
lines.zh: CDC 估计，约 38% 的美国家庭养着一只或几只狗。

lines.en: Cats are the other most common pet in the United States. Of course, cats can provide affection and companionship. But they also are known for sometimes being selfish and a bit distant.
lines.zh: 猫是美国另一种最常见的宠物。当然，猫也能给人关爱和陪伴，但它们也以有时自私、有点冷淡出名。

lines.en: I myself am a cat owner. My cat sleeps a lot, has no interest in exercise and gives a limited amount of affection. If I pet her too much, she will walk away.
lines.zh: 我自己就养猫。我的猫睡很多觉，对运动毫无兴趣，给的关爱也有限。我摸它摸多了，它就走开了。

lines.en: The coronavirus stay-at-home orders have led to many pet memes online. In them, dogs appear very happy that their owners are home all the time. The memes show dogs saying things like, "Yay! Another walk! That's 14 for today!"
lines.zh: 新冠居家令让网上出现了很多宠物段子。段子里，狗因为主人一直在家显得非常开心。这些段子里狗会说：“耶！又出去散步了！今天第 14 次了！”

lines.en: In the coronavirus cat memes, however, cats are saying things like, "Why is this human in my house so much?" and "Don't you have a job to go to?"
lines.zh: 可在新冠猫段子里，猫说的是：“这个人类怎么老待在我家？”还有“你不用去上班吗？”

lines.en: Dogs are known for being extra affectionate and loyal toward their owners. They like to go on walks, and they like the company of humans. And most experts agree that dogs became pets before cats. So perhaps they have simply had more time to perfect the art of being a pet!
lines.zh: 狗以对主人格外亲热、忠诚出名。它们喜欢散步，喜欢有人陪伴。大多数专家都同意，狗比猫更早成为宠物。所以也许它们只是有更多时间把“当宠物”这门艺术练到完美！

lines.en: Evan MacLean is a biological anthropologist at the University of Arizona. Biological anthropologists combine biological and social studies, often to better understand human evolution.
lines.zh: 埃文·麦克莱恩是亚利桑那大学的生物人类学家。生物人类学家结合生物学和社会学研究，常常是为了更好地理解人类进化。

lines.en: MacLean says that dogs may provide welcome emotional support during the current worldwide health crisis. He says that owning a dog not only makes a person feel good emotionally -- dogs also appear to help control "heart rate, blood pressure and cortisol – a hormone involved in stress responses."
lines.zh: 麦克莱恩说，在当前这场全球健康危机中，狗也许能提供令人欣慰的情感支持。他说，养狗不仅让人在情感上感觉良好——狗似乎还能帮助控制“心率、血压和皮质醇——一种与压力反应有关的激素”。

lines.en: MacLean adds that simply petting your dog in a soft, slow way may help you both feel more at ease.
lines.zh: 麦克莱恩还说，只要轻轻地、慢慢地抚摸你的狗，可能就会让你们俩都感到更放松。

lines.en: On its website, the CDC lists some health benefits of pet ownership (including cats!) They include:
lines.zh: CDC 在网站上列出了养宠物（包括猫！）对健康的一些好处，包括：

lines.en: Decreased blood pressure
lines.zh: 降低血压

lines.en: Decreased cholesterol levels
lines.zh: 降低胆固醇水平

lines.en: Decreased feelings of loneliness
lines.zh: 减少孤独感

lines.en: Increased opportunities for exercise and outdoor activities
lines.zh: 增加运动和户外活动的机会

lines.en: MacLean says dogs can give us support and help us "weather the storm." In other words, they help us get through a very bad time.
lines.zh: 麦克莱恩说，狗能给我们支持，帮我们“渡过风暴”。换句话说，它们帮我们熬过非常糟糕的时期。

lines.en: Dogs may provide support and be beside us "through thick and thin." If a pet or a person is with you "through thick and thin," they are with you through good times and bad. In other words, they are loyal. And this loyalty can be very comforting.
lines.zh: 狗也许能给我们支持，“不论顺境逆境”都陪在我们身边。如果一只宠物或一个人“through thick and thin”陪着你，就是说无论好时光还是坏时光都陪着你。换句话说，他们是忠诚的。这种忠诚能让人非常安心。

lines.en: Let's not forget that there is work involved in keeping a pet. Taking care of our pets may help give us a sense of purpose. A dog always needs to walk outside. In our current situation, this gives dog owners a reason to (safely) leave the house and get some fresh air. And, it makes them get a little exercise.
lines.zh: 别忘了养宠物也要付出劳动。照顾宠物也许能给我们一种目标感。狗总是需要出去散步。在目前的情况下，这给了养狗的人一个（安全地）出门、呼吸新鲜空气的理由，还让他们稍微活动一下。

lines.en: All of that is important and helpful.
lines.zh: 这一切都很重要，也很有帮助。

lines.en: "One thing we know is that sitting around worrying doesn't do much good for our mental health. So, refocusing our mental energy on something positive could bring relief at a time like this," MacLean says.
lines.zh: “我们知道的一点是，坐着发愁对心理健康没什么好处。所以，在这样的时候把精力重新集中到积极的事情上，可能会让人感到宽慰。”麦克莱恩说。

lines.en: And that's the Health & Lifestyle report. I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 以上就是《健康与生活》节目。我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: About what percent of American households have dogs?
qs.why: "around 38 percent of American households have one or more dogs."

qs.q: What does "through thick and thin" mean?
qs.why: "they are with you through good times and bad."

qs.q: How can dogs help their owners during quarantine?
opts: They give a reason to go outside and exercise.
qs.a: They give a reason to go outside and exercise.
qs.why: "this gives dog owners a reason to (safely) leave the house and get some fresh air."

lessons.title: Baking Is Good for Mental Health
lessons.zh: 烘焙有益心理健康
lessons.sum: 疫情中超市的面包常常最先被抢光，学做面包是一项“生存技能”。纽约的社工朱莉·奥哈纳用“烹饪疗法”帮助人们：烘焙需要按步骤专注当下，揉面擀面能让人放松；做出来的东西看得见、吃得着，送给别人还能让双方都开心。

lines.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle report.
lines.zh: 这里是 VOA 慢速英语《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: The world is experiencing a major health crisis.
lines.zh: 世界正在经历一场重大的健康危机。

lines.en: As the new coronavirus spreads, many countries are limiting their citizens' activities. Travel has been restricted. Many schools are closed. In major cities around the world, restaurants and other businesses are shut down.
lines.zh: 随着新冠病毒蔓延，许多国家在限制公民的活动。出行受到限制，很多学校停课，世界各大城市的餐馆和其他商家都关门了。

lines.en: Public emergencies bring out a certain type of person – the panic shopper. Some people fear not being able to find basic needs for survival. So, they buy everything off supermarket shelves in preparation for the days to come.
lines.zh: 公共紧急情况会催生某一类人——恐慌性抢购者。有些人担心买不到生存的基本必需品，于是把超市货架上的东西一扫而空，为接下来的日子做准备。

lines.en: Bread is often among the first products to disappear in emergency situations.
lines.zh: 在紧急情况下，面包常常是最先消失的商品之一。

lines.en: So, if you have never made bread, now may be good time to learn. Bread making is a survival skill. With very few simple things -- such as flour, salt and yeast -- you can bake a fresh loaf of bread for your family, neighbors or coworkers.
lines.zh: 所以，如果你从没做过面包，现在也许是学的好时机。做面包是一项生存技能。只需要面粉、盐和酵母这几样简单的东西，你就能为家人、邻居或同事烤一个新鲜的面包。

lines.en: Baking is not just a useful survival skill. It can make you feel better at stressful times. In fact, baking and cooking have been used to treat people with mental health issues.
lines.zh: 烘焙不只是一项有用的生存技能，它还能在压力大的时候让你感觉好些。事实上，烘焙和烹饪已经被用来治疗有心理健康问题的人。

lines.en: Julie Ohana is a social worker. She offers what she calls culinary therapy to her patients in New York City.
lines.zh: 朱莉·奥哈纳是一名社工。她在纽约市为病人提供她所说的“烹饪疗法”。

lines.en: "I say 'therapy' because to me cooking is so therapeutic. And 'therapeutic' really means something that makes you feel good, something that is helpful and beneficial to the person doing it ..."
lines.zh: “我说‘疗法’，是因为对我来说烹饪非常有疗愈作用。‘疗愈’的真正意思是让你感觉好、对做这件事的人有帮助、有益处的东西……”

lines.en: Julie Ohana uses culinary therapy to help people overcome many kinds of issues. She explains that culinary therapy works on many levels.
lines.zh: 朱莉·奥哈纳用烹饪疗法帮助人们克服各种各样的问题。她解释说，烹饪疗法在很多层面起作用。

lines.en: "So when you're in the kitchen – whether you're cooking or you're baking – it really requires a certain level of mindfulness, of being present in the moment. Specifically, when you're baking. And baking really requires step-by-step, following a recipe, being more precise. Kneading the dough or rolling something out, you really get the full benefit of being present in the moment and being able to relax and put aside all the other thoughts and just focus on the here-and-now. And there really are very strong benefits of being able to do that, to be able to relax, to decompress, destress, and really increase one's level of life satisfaction."
lines.zh: “所以当你在厨房里——不管是做饭还是烘焙——它确实需要一定程度的正念，要专注于当下。尤其是烘焙。烘焙真的需要一步一步来，照着食谱，更加精确。揉面或者擀面时，你真的能充分享受专注当下的好处，能够放松，把其他念头都放到一边，只专注于此时此地。能做到这一点真的有非常大的好处：能放松、减压、解压，真正提高一个人的生活满意度。”

lines.en: Ohana also says baking is a process filled with love. It not only makes you feel good, it produces something tangible -- something you can touch and eat! Ohana calls baking a labor of love.
lines.zh: 奥哈纳还说，烘焙是一个充满爱的过程。它不仅让你感觉好，还能做出实实在在的东西——你能摸得到、吃得到的东西！奥哈纳称烘焙是“爱的劳动”。

lines.en: "And when you bake, you go through this whole process and it really is a labor of love … and you end up with this finished product that - not only is it tangible - but it's edible and it's delicious."
lines.zh: “烘焙时，你走完整个过程，这真的是一种爱的劳动……最后你得到一个成品，它不仅实实在在，还能吃，而且很好吃。”

lines.en: Often our food experiences are tied to family memories and stories. We remember meals our grandmothers made. We teach our children important recipes for family favorites.
lines.zh: 我们的饮食经历常常与家庭记忆和故事联系在一起。我们记得外婆做的饭，我们把家人最爱的菜的重要做法教给孩子。

lines.en: Ohana says something that all bakers know -- giving delicious, baked goods makes the giver feel as good as the receiver. So, she calls baking a win-win.
lines.zh: 奥哈纳说了一件所有烘焙者都知道的事——送出美味的烘焙食品，送的人和收的人一样开心。所以她称烘焙是双赢。

lines.en: "To be able to pass that on to someone else certainly can make the day for the person receiving it. But It's also just as powerful for the person who's giving the baked goods. It's a win-win. It's not just something purely that you do for the other person. The baker, the cook really gets to benefit from the act as well."
lines.zh: “能把它送给别人，当然能让收到的人开心一整天。但它对送烘焙食品的人同样有力量。这是双赢。这不纯粹是你为别人做的事，烘焙的人、做饭的人也能从中受益。”

lines.en: And that's the Health & Lifestyle report. I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 以上就是《健康与生活》节目。我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: What simple things do you need to bake bread?
qs.why: "flour, salt and yeast"

qs.q: What is "culinary therapy"?
opts: using cooking to help people feel better
qs.a: using cooking to help people feel better
qs.why: Ohana uses cooking and baking as therapy.

qs.q: Why is baking a "win-win"?
opts: Both the giver and the receiver feel good.
qs.a: Both the giver and the receiver feel good.
qs.why: "giving delicious, baked goods makes the giver feel as good as the receiver."

lessons.title: Take Care of Your Teeth, Take Care of Your Heart
lessons.zh: 照顾好牙齿，就是照顾好心脏
lessons.sum: 一项对韩国 16 万多人的研究发现，每天刷牙三次或以上的人，心房颤动风险低 10%，心力衰竭风险低 12%。不清洁牙齿可能让细菌进入血液、引发炎症。不过这只说明“相关”而非“因果”。美国牙科协会建议每天用含氟牙膏刷牙两次、每次两分钟。

lines.en: Cleaning your teeth often, every day, is linked to a lower risk for heart problems. A new study found that brushing your teeth several times a day resulted in fewer cases of heart failure and atrial fibrillation— the term for an uneven heartbeat.
lines.zh: 每天经常清洁牙齿，与较低的心脏病风险有关。一项新研究发现，每天刷几次牙的人，心力衰竭和心房颤动——也就是心跳不规律——的病例更少。

lines.en: Heart failure happens when the heart cannot do its job of pumping blood through the body.
lines.zh: 心力衰竭是指心脏无法完成把血液泵送到全身的工作。

lines.en: What the research found is that brushing your teeth three times a day, or more, was linked to a ten percent lower risk of atrial fibrillation. It was also linked to a twelve percent lower risk of heart failure.
lines.zh: 研究发现，每天刷牙三次或以上，与心房颤动风险降低 10% 有关，也与心力衰竭风险降低 12% 有关。

lines.en: The study was published last Monday in the European Journal of Preventive Cardiology.
lines.zh: 这项研究上周一发表在《欧洲预防心脏病学杂志》上。

lines.en: The researchers examined information on more than 161,000 people in Korea with no history of heart problems.
lines.zh: 研究人员分析了韩国 16.1 万多名没有心脏病史的人的资料。

lines.en: They followed up ten and a half years later, and found that three percent had developed uneven heart rhythms and almost five percent had developed heart failure.
lines.zh: 十年半后他们进行了随访，发现 3% 的人出现了心律不齐，近 5% 的人出现了心力衰竭。

lines.en: All the participants in the study were part of the Korean National Health Insurance System, and aged 40 to 79. They had usual medical exams between 2003 and 2004. Information was collected on their height, weight, laboratory tests, sicknesses, and lifestyle. They also noted their mouth health in connection with cleaning.
lines.zh: 研究的所有参与者都属于韩国国民健康保险系统，年龄在 40 到 79 岁之间。他们在 2003 年到 2004 年间做过常规体检，研究收集了他们的身高、体重、化验结果、疾病和生活方式等信息，还记录了他们与清洁有关的口腔健康状况。

lines.en: You may wonder, how are teeth health and heart health connected?
lines.zh: 你也许会想，牙齿健康和心脏健康有什么关系？

lines.en: Earlier research suggests that not taking care to clean and brush teeth leads to bacteria in the blood. This can cause inflammation, and increases the risk for unusual heartbeat and heart failure.
lines.zh: 早先的研究表明，不注意清洁和刷牙会导致血液中出现细菌。这会引起炎症，增加心跳异常和心力衰竭的风险。

lines.en: A study last year by the American Heart Association showed that brushing your teeth twice a day for at least two minutes may lower the risk of cardiovascular, or heart, diseases.
lines.zh: 美国心脏协会去年的一项研究表明，每天刷牙两次、每次至少两分钟，可能降低心血管疾病——也就是心脏病——的风险。

lines.en: That study looked at a smaller group of fewer than 700 people. The AHA said that the researchers found that people who brushed less than twice a day for less than two minutes were three times more at risk, compared to those who brush at least twice a day for two minutes.
lines.zh: 那项研究的样本较小，不到 700 人。美国心脏协会说，研究人员发现，每天刷牙少于两次、每次不到两分钟的人，风险是每天至少刷两次、每次两分钟的人的三倍。

lines.en: Gums are the soft tissue structure that hold the teeth. They need to be cleaned as well. Experts say if gums are not cared for this way they can become inflamed. They say there is a connection between such inflammation, and future heart disease.
lines.zh: 牙龈是固定牙齿的柔软组织，也需要清洁。专家说，如果不这样护理，牙龈可能会发炎。他们说，这种炎症与日后的心脏病之间存在联系。

lines.en: The lead investigator of the new study is Tae-Jin Song, a doctor and professor at Mokdong Hospital at Ewha Womans University in Seoul, South Korea. He noted "we studied a large group over a long period, which adds strength to our findings."
lines.zh: 这项新研究的首席研究员是宋泰镇，他是韩国首尔梨花女子大学木洞医院的医生和教授。他指出：“我们长期研究了一个大群体，这增强了我们研究结果的说服力。”

lines.en: But he said that the research was limited to one country and as an observational study does not prove causation.
lines.zh: 但他说，这项研究只限于一个国家，而且作为观察性研究，并不能证明因果关系。

lines.en: The American Dental Association agrees. The organization said "this study is interesting, and while it may suggest an association between tooth brushing and heart health, it does not show a direct connection."
lines.zh: 美国牙科协会也同意这一点。该组织说：“这项研究很有意思，虽然它可能表明刷牙和心脏健康之间存在关联，但并没有显示直接的联系。”

lines.en: To have good oral health, the ADA advises people to:
lines.zh: 为了保持良好的口腔健康，美国牙科协会建议人们：

lines.en: Brush their teeth twice a day for two minutes each time with a fluoride toothpaste
lines.zh: 每天用含氟牙膏刷牙两次，每次两分钟

lines.en: Clean between their teeth once per day
lines.zh: 每天清洁牙缝一次

lines.en: Maintain a healthy diet
lines.zh: 保持健康饮食

lines.en: See a dentist regularly
lines.zh: 定期看牙医

lines.en: Mouth care companies have taken note. Some manufacture electric toothbrushes programmed to run for two minutes. That way, people do not have to watch the time while brushing their teeth.
lines.zh: 口腔护理公司也注意到了这一点。有些公司生产设定好运行两分钟的电动牙刷，这样人们刷牙时就不用盯着时间了。

lines.en: I'm Anne Ball.
lines.zh: 我是安妮·鲍尔。

qs.q: How often did people brush to have a lower heart risk in the Korean study?
opts: three times a day or more
qs.a: three times a day or more
qs.why: "brushing your teeth three times a day, or more, was linked to..."

qs.q: Why might dirty teeth affect the heart?
opts: Bacteria in the blood can cause inflammation.
Teeth are close to the heart.
Toothpaste is bad for the heart.
qs.a: Bacteria in the blood can cause inflammation.
qs.why: "not taking care to clean and brush teeth leads to bacteria in the blood. This can cause inflammation."

qs.q: Does the study prove that brushing causes better heart health?
opts: No, it shows an association, not causation.
qs.a: No, it shows an association, not causation.
qs.why: "as an observational study does not prove causation."

lessons.title: Should You Exercise While Sick?
lessons.zh: 生病时该运动吗？
lessons.sum: 美国心脏协会建议每周至少做 150 分钟中等强度运动。生病时能不能运动？专家的经验法则是：症状都在“脖子以上”（流鼻涕、鼻塞、打喷嚏、轻微喉咙痛）通常可以轻度运动；症状在“脖子以下”（胸闷、剧烈咳嗽、胃痛）或发烧、乏力、全身肌肉痛，就该休息。

lines.en: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle report.
lines.zh: 这里是 VOA 慢速英语《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: Exercise helps to keep us in good health. Doctors at the American Heart Association suggest getting at least 150 minutes of moderate physical activity every week.
lines.zh: 运动能帮助我们保持健康。美国心脏协会的医生建议，每周至少进行 150 分钟中等强度的身体活动。

lines.en: Many people have an exercise routine. They exercise for a few minutes every day or every other day. So, getting those 150 minutes is easier.
lines.zh: 很多人有固定的运动习惯，每天或隔一天运动几分钟，所以达到 150 分钟比较容易。

lines.en: But what about those times when you are sick? If you do not feel well, should you keep following your exercise routine? Will physical activity help you to feel better more quickly or will it delay the healing process?
lines.zh: 可是生病的时候怎么办？如果你感觉不舒服，还应该坚持运动习惯吗？身体活动会帮你更快好起来，还是会推迟康复？

lines.en: Health experts answer these and other questions on the Mayo Clinic website. The Mayo Clinic is a nonprofit medical center in the United States.
lines.zh: 健康专家在梅奥诊所网站上回答了这些问题和其他问题。梅奥诊所是美国的一家非营利医疗中心。

lines.en: Edward R. Laskowski is a doctor at the clinic. He notes that "mild to moderate physical activity is usually OK if you have a common cold."
lines.zh: 爱德华·R·拉斯科夫斯基是该诊所的一名医生。他指出：“如果你只是普通感冒，轻度到中度的身体活动通常没问题。”

lines.en: Dr. Laskowski and other experts have a general rule of thumb about exercising when you are sick. It is usually fine to exercise, he explains, if your symptoms are all "above the neck." These signs may include a runny nose, nasal congestion, sneezing or a minor sore throat.
lines.zh: 拉斯科夫斯基医生和其他专家对生病时运动有一条总的经验法则。他解释说，如果你的症状都在“脖子以上”，运动通常没问题。这些症状可能包括流鼻涕、鼻塞、打喷嚏或轻微的喉咙痛。

lines.en: In fact, Laskowski adds that exercise may make you feel better by "opening your nasal passages." This may temporarily reduce congestion and help you to breathe more easily.
lines.zh: 事实上，拉斯科夫斯基补充说，运动可能通过“打通鼻腔”让你感觉好些。这可能暂时减轻鼻塞，帮你呼吸更顺畅。

lines.en: The American health website WebMD offers similar advice.
lines.zh: 美国健康网站 WebMD 也给出了类似的建议。

lines.en: Geralyn Coopersmith is a physical fitness trainer who has written several books on exercise and nutrition. Coopersmith told WebMD: "The general rule is that if it is just a little sniffle and you take some medications and don't feel so sick, it's OK to work out."
lines.zh: 杰拉琳·库珀史密斯是一位健身教练，写过几本关于运动和营养的书。库珀史密斯告诉 WebMD：“一般规则是，如果只是有点流鼻涕，吃了些药，感觉不太难受，那锻炼是可以的。”

lines.en: However, both Coopersmith and Dr. Laskowski suggest taking a break from exercising if signs of your illness appear "below the neck." Be on guard for symptoms such as chest congestion, extreme cough or pain in the stomach.
lines.zh: 不过，库珀史密斯和拉斯科夫斯基医生都建议，如果病症出现在“脖子以下”，就暂停运动。要留意胸部充血、剧烈咳嗽或胃痛等症状。

lines.en: But there are other symptoms that can tell you to avoid exercise. They include:
lines.zh: 还有其他一些症状也在提醒你不要运动，包括：

lines.en: a higher than normal body temperature,
lines.zh: 体温比正常高，

lines.en: a sense of feeling extremely tired, also known as fatigue, and
lines.zh: 感到极度疲倦，也就是乏力，以及

lines.en: widespread muscle pain.
lines.zh: 全身肌肉疼痛。

lines.en: Coopersmith, the WebMD expert, adds that if you feel tightness in the chest, "it is not advisable to be working out."
lines.zh: WebMD 的专家库珀史密斯补充说，如果你感到胸闷，“就不建议锻炼”。

lines.en: Both she and Dr. Laskowski suggest listening to your body. If you feel really badly, take a break and let your body rest.
lines.zh: 她和拉斯科夫斯基医生都建议倾听身体的声音。如果你感觉非常难受，就休息一下，让身体恢复。

lines.en: If you don't feel too badly, these experts both suggest cutting back on the intensity of your exercise routine. For example, if you usually run, take a quick walk instead.
lines.zh: 如果感觉不太难受，这两位专家都建议降低运动强度。比如，如果你平时跑步，就改成快走。

lines.en: Experts at the Mayo Clinic add that a "few days off from exercise when you are sick shouldn't affect your performance."
lines.zh: 梅奥诊所的专家补充说，“生病时停几天运动不应该影响你的状态”。

lines.en: You can return to your usual intensity when you feel better. However, Dr. Laskowski warns that exercising when you have more than a common cold, could lead to "more-serious injury or illness."
lines.zh: 等你感觉好些了，就可以恢复平常的运动强度。不过拉斯科夫斯基医生提醒，如果你得的不只是普通感冒还去运动，可能会导致“更严重的损伤或疾病”。

lines.en: And that's the Health & Lifestyle Report.
lines.zh: 以上就是《健康与生活》节目。

lines.en: I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: How much exercise does the American Heart Association suggest each week?
qs.why: "at least 150 minutes of moderate physical activity every week."

qs.q: When is it usually fine to exercise while sick?
qs.why: "if your symptoms are all 'above the neck.'"

qs.q: If you usually run but feel a little sick, what should you do?
qs.why: "if you usually run, take a quick walk instead."

lessons.title: Museum Tells Stories of Arab Americans
lessons.zh: 讲述阿拉伯裔美国人故事的博物馆
lessons.sum: 密歇根州迪尔伯恩的阿拉伯裔美国人国家博物馆，用阿拉伯裔美国人自己的声音讲述他们自 19 世纪末以来的美国故事：发明“休闲裤”一词的黎巴嫩移民哈格，北达科他州的叙利亚、黎巴嫩移民，以及一面“名人墙”。博物馆也努力纠正人们的误解。

lines.en: Arab Americans have long been a part of life in the United States. A small museum in Dearborn, Michigan is trying to tell their stories.
lines.zh: 阿拉伯裔美国人长期以来一直是美国生活的一部分。密歇根州迪尔伯恩的一座小博物馆正在努力讲述他们的故事。

lines.en: Called the Arab American National Museum, it has an exhibit about Joseph Haggar. He was a Lebanese immigrant who founded Haggar's clothing company in 1926.
lines.zh: 这座名为“阿拉伯裔美国人国家博物馆”的博物馆有一个关于约瑟夫·哈格的展览。他是一位黎巴嫩移民，1926 年创立了哈格服装公司。

lines.en: Diana Abouali is the museum's director. Abouali said, "He settled in Texas, and he started this pant company that was extremely successful in the 20th century." She added, "He also revolutionized the way that pants and clothing were mass produced."
lines.zh: 黛安娜·阿布阿利是博物馆馆长。阿布阿利说：“他在德克萨斯州定居，创办了这家裤子公司，在 20 世纪非常成功。”她还说：“他还彻底改变了裤子和服装的大规模生产方式。”

lines.en: Haggar came up with the word "slacks" to describe pants that people would wear while relaxing. His slacks were worn by many American men including the 36th U.S. president, Lyndon Johnson.
lines.zh: 哈格创造了 slacks（休闲裤）这个词，用来指人们放松时穿的裤子。很多美国男人都穿过他的休闲裤，包括美国第 36 任总统林登·约翰逊。

lines.en: Stories like Haggar's are important to the museum's mission to show how Arab Americans have been part of American life since the late 19th century.
lines.zh: 像哈格这样的故事，对博物馆的使命很重要：展示阿拉伯裔美国人从 19 世纪末以来如何成为美国生活的一部分。

lines.en: "We communicate the American narrative in the voices of Arab Americans. They express their experiences in their own words," Abouali said. "This provides people with a more authentic and real representation of what it means to be Arab American."
lines.zh: “我们用阿拉伯裔美国人的声音讲述美国的故事。他们用自己的话表达自己的经历，”阿布阿利说，“这让人们更真实地了解做一个阿拉伯裔美国人意味着什么。”

lines.en: The museum attempts to share the Arab American experience, including the path to America, home and work life, and service in the U.S. Armed Forces.
lines.zh: 博物馆努力分享阿拉伯裔美国人的经历，包括来美国的道路、家庭和工作生活，以及在美国军队中服役。

lines.en: The offerings include an exhibit about the hundreds of Syrian and Lebanese immigrants in North Dakota between 1890 and World War I. Thousands of their descendants still live in the north central state today. Another exhibit includes lists of Arab American passengers on the Titanic, which sank in 1912.
lines.zh: 展品中有一个展览，介绍 1890 年到第一次世界大战期间来到北达科他州的几百名叙利亚和黎巴嫩移民，他们的几千名后代至今仍生活在这个中北部州。另一个展览列出了 1912 年沉没的泰坦尼克号上阿拉伯裔美国乘客的名单。

lines.en: The museum also tries to change religious misunderstandings.
lines.zh: 博物馆还努力改变人们在宗教上的误解。

lines.en: "Half of the Arab American community is Christian," Abouali said. "And in fact, the earlier immigrants, who came in the late 19th century, early 20th century, were predominantly Christian."
lines.zh: “阿拉伯裔美国人社区有一半是基督徒，”阿布阿利说，“事实上，19 世纪末 20 世纪初来的早期移民主要是基督徒。”

lines.en: A "wall of fame" shows other well-known Arab Americans. They include reporter Helen Thomas, known as the first woman to end a White House press conference by saying, "Thank you, Mr. President." Others are actress Kathy Najimy, former U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services Donna Shalala, and Candace Lightner, who founded Mothers Against Drunk Driving in 1980.
lines.zh: 一面“名人墙”展示了其他知名的阿拉伯裔美国人，包括记者海伦·托马斯——她以第一位用“谢谢您，总统先生”结束白宫记者会的女性而闻名；还有演员凯茜·纳吉米、前美国卫生与公众服务部部长唐娜·沙拉拉，以及 1980 年创立“母亲反酒驾”组织的坎迪丝·莱特纳。

lines.en: Stories of Arab immigrants are often misunderstood among Americans.
lines.zh: 阿拉伯移民的故事在美国人中常常被误解。

lines.en: Jasmine Hawamdeh is the director of arts and culture at the American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee. She said people often think of "the angry Arab, the terrorist Arab," or are "afraid of the Arab that comes from abroad." Another harmful idea, she said, is "the oppressed Arab woman."
lines.zh: 贾斯敏·哈瓦姆德是美国-阿拉伯反歧视委员会的艺术文化主任。她说，人们常常想到“愤怒的阿拉伯人、搞恐怖袭击的阿拉伯人”，或者“害怕来自国外的阿拉伯人”。她说，另一个有害的观念是“受压迫的阿拉伯女性”。

lines.en: The museum tries to correct these false narratives about Arab Americans. But Abouali said the museum also tries to present Arab Americans as "ourselves."
lines.zh: 博物馆努力纠正这些关于阿拉伯裔美国人的错误说法。但阿布阿利说，博物馆也努力把阿拉伯裔美国人呈现为“我们自己”。

lines.en: Although Arab Americans come from 22 countries, from northern Africa to western Asia, she said once they settle in the U.S., they become as American as they are Arab.
lines.zh: 她说，虽然阿拉伯裔美国人来自从北非到西亚的 22 个国家，但他们一旦在美国定居，就既是阿拉伯人，也同样是美国人。

lines.en: I'm Anna Matteo.
lines.zh: 我是安娜·马泰奥。

qs.q: What word did Joseph Haggar create?
qs.why: "Haggar came up with the word 'slacks.'"

qs.q: What was the religion of most early Arab immigrants?
qs.why: "the earlier immigrants... were predominantly Christian."

qs.q: How many countries do Arab Americans come from?
qs.why: "Arab Americans come from 22 countries."

lessons.title: Hollywood Is Finally Getting Its Own Film Museum
lessons.zh: 好莱坞终于有了自己的电影博物馆
lessons.sum: 90 多年前就有人提议，如今奥斯卡的主办方美国电影艺术与科学学院终于在洛杉矶建起电影博物馆：有一座带玻璃穹顶的千人影院，收藏 1200 万张照片、8 万部剧本和《卡萨布兰卡》等名片的道具服装，游客还能走红毯、“领”奥斯卡奖。

lines.en: More than 90 years have passed since Hollywood's official film organization first proposed plans to build its own museum.
lines.zh: 好莱坞的官方电影组织首次提出建造自己的博物馆，已经过去 90 多年了。

lines.en: Those plans are finally becoming a reality, with the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures set to open in 2019.
lines.zh: 这些计划终于要成为现实：美国电影艺术与科学学院博物馆定于 2019 年开放。

lines.en: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences is building the museum. The organization presents the yearly Academy Awards ceremony, also called the Oscars.
lines.zh: 美国电影艺术与科学学院正在建造这座博物馆。这个组织每年举办学院奖颁奖典礼，也就是奥斯卡。

lines.en: The Academy includes more than 8,000 members, including actors, directors and other professionals in the film industry.
lines.zh: 学院有 8000 多名成员，包括演员、导演和电影业的其他专业人士。

lines.en: Museum officials say visitors will be able to "experience the magic of cinema" by learning about all parts of the film-making process.
lines.zh: 博物馆官员说，参观者将通过了解电影制作过程的各个环节来“体验电影的魔力”。

lines.en: The almost 27,000-square-meter complex is expected to cost $388 million to complete. The project is underway at the site of an historic Los Angeles department store built in 1939. The Los Angeles County Museum of Art has used the building since 1994.
lines.zh: 这个近 2.7 万平方米的综合建筑预计耗资 3.88 亿美元。工程在洛杉矶一座建于 1939 年的历史悠久的百货大楼原址上进行。自 1994 年以来，洛杉矶县艺术博物馆一直在使用这座建筑。

lines.en: The Academy Museum will include a 1,000-seat theater inside a huge addition with a rounded glass cover. This so-called "Sphere" will provide extended views of the Hollywood Hills.
lines.zh: 学院博物馆将有一座千人影院，位于一个带圆形玻璃顶的巨大扩建部分里。这个所谓的“球体”将让人们远眺好莱坞山。

lines.en: Film historian Kerry Brougher has been named director of the museum. He told VOA the museum will open as Hollywood continues to seek new ways to entertainment audiences beyond the movie theater.
lines.zh: 电影史学家凯丽·布鲁厄被任命为博物馆馆长。他告诉 VOA，博物馆开放之际，好莱坞正在继续寻找在电影院之外娱乐观众的新方式。

lines.en: "Film is expanding," Brougher said. "It's in the theaters still, but it's also projected onto buildings. And it's also on your iPhone, it's on your computer." He added that movies often cross over into the art world too, with major exhibitions including film subjects.
lines.zh: “电影正在扩展，”布鲁厄说，“它仍然在电影院里，但也被投影到建筑上，还在你的 iPhone 上、在你的电脑上。”他还说，电影也常常跨界进入艺术世界，有些重要展览就以电影为主题。

lines.en: Brougher says the museum will include areas showing the Academy's collection of 12 million photographs and 80,000 screenplays. The collection also includes props, costumes and other objects from famous films, such as "Casablanca," "Psycho" and "The Ten Commandments."
lines.zh: 布鲁厄说，博物馆将设有展示学院收藏的 1200 万张照片和 8 万部剧本的区域。藏品还包括《卡萨布兰卡》《惊魂记》《十诫》等名片的道具、服装和其他物品。

lines.en: Special collections will also be shown from many film greats, such as Cary Grant, Katharine Hepburn and Alfred Hitchcock.
lines.zh: 博物馆还会展出许多电影巨星的特别收藏，比如加里·格兰特、凯瑟琳·赫本和阿尔弗雷德·希区柯克。

lines.en: The Academy Museum will also feature Oscar statuettes donated by actors who won the awards. Brougher said the museum is designed to make visitors feel like they, too, are in a movie, with many interactive experiences.
lines.zh: 学院博物馆还将展出获奖演员捐赠的奥斯卡小金人。布鲁厄说，博物馆的设计让参观者感觉自己也在电影里，有许多互动体验。

lines.en: "You won't necessarily know what's coming next," he added. "You'll be in environments sometimes that make you feel like you've gone back to the past – that you're in the era that you're actually exploring."
lines.zh: “你不一定知道接下来会发生什么，”他补充说，“有时你会身处一些环境中，让你觉得回到了过去——就在你正在探索的那个时代。”

lines.en: He added that visitors will even get the chance to walk down a red carpet and accept their own Academy Award.
lines.zh: 他还说，参观者甚至有机会走红毯，领取属于自己的奥斯卡奖。

lines.en: Currently, Hollywood only has a few possibilities for visitors interested in seeing film-related places.
lines.zh: 目前，对想看电影相关场所的游客来说，好莱坞只有几个去处。

lines.en: They can stroll the Walk of Fame, where actors are honored with stars on Hollywood sidewalks. They can also visit movie studios or see the Dolby Theater, where the Oscars are presented. But beyond these, movie fans have limited possibilities.
lines.zh: 他们可以漫步星光大道，那里的人行道上用星星纪念演员。他们也可以参观电影制片厂，或者去看颁发奥斯卡奖的杜比剧院。但除此之外，影迷们的选择很有限。

lines.en: Eric Garcetti is the mayor of Los Angeles. He says the Academy Museum will provide visitors the chance to experience many different parts of the film industry all in one place.
lines.zh: 埃里克·加希提是洛杉矶市长。他说，学院博物馆将让游客在一个地方体验电影业的许多方面。

lines.en: "I think they wander around wondering where they can experience this great golden ticket to the movies," he said. "Now they'll have a place."
lines.zh: “我想他们到处闲逛，想知道去哪儿才能体验这张通往电影世界的金色门票，”他说，“现在他们有地方去了。”

lines.en: Garcetti noted the museum will also serve the hundreds of thousands of local people working in film-related businesses. He said they, too, will finally be able to visit a place that celebrates their own Hollywood movie industry.
lines.zh: 加希提指出，这座博物馆也将服务于成千上万在电影相关行业工作的当地人。他说，他们也终于能参观一个颂扬他们自己好莱坞电影业的地方了。

lines.en: I'm Caty Weaver.
lines.zh: 我是凯蒂·韦弗。
